- Father curses two violent sons' anger and decrees they be scattered among the tribes (Gen 49:5, Gen 49:6, Gen 49:7)
- Tribes characterized by animal images (lion, ass, serpent, hind, wolf) (Gen 49:9, Gen 49:14, Gen 49:17, Gen 49:21, Gen 49:27)
- Judah likened to a lion's whelp crouching that none dare rouse (Gen 49:9)
- A tribe likened to a serpent by the road biting the horse's heels so the rider falls (Gen 49:17)
- Tribal sayings pun on each son's name (Gen 49:8, Gen 49:16, Gen 49:19)
- A brief prayer ('For your salvation I wait, YHWH') interrupts a poem (Gen 49:18)
- Blessings of heaven above, of the deep crouching below, and of breasts and womb (Gen 49:25)
- The favored son called 'nazir (consecrated/prince) among his brothers' (Gen 49:26)
- Patriarch dies and is 'gathered to his people' (Gen 49:33)

**Embalming and burial of Jacob; Joseph's last words and death**
- A great funeral procession with royal elders, chariots and horsemen escorts the patriarch's body (Gen 50:7, Gen 50:8, Gen 50:9)
- Locals name a place for the great mourning they witness (Abel-Mizraim) (Gen 50:11)
- Hero refuses to judge or avenge, asking 'Am I in the place of God?' (Gen 50:19)
- Great-grandchildren born on the hero's knees (Gen 50:23)
- Dying hero foretells 'God will surely visit you' (paqod yifqod) and bring you up (Gen 50:24, Gen 50:25)
- Embalmed hero laid in a coffin (aron) in Egypt (Gen 50:26)

**Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons**
- The people 'swarm' (sharats) and fill the land like creatures in creation (Exod 1:7)
- A new king arises who did not know the former benefactor (Exod 1:8)
- Ruler fears the immigrant people will grow numerous and join his enemies (Exod 1:9, Exod 1:10)
- Oppressed people forced to build store-cities with mortar and bricks (Exod 1:11, Exod 1:13, Exod 1:14)
- The more the people are oppressed, the more they multiply (Exod 1:12)
- Two named midwives fear God and disobey the king's order to kill boys (Exod 1:15, Exod 1:17)
- Midwives observe the newborn on the birthstool (ovnayim, 'the two stones') (Exod 1:16)
- Midwives excuse themselves: Hebrew women are vigorous and give birth before the midwife arrives (Exod 1:19)
- God rewards the God-fearing midwives by making them houses (families) (Exod 1:20, Exod 1:21)

**Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry**
- The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman (Exod 2:1)
- Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov) (Exod 2:2)
- The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion (Exod 2:6)
- Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land (Exod 2:22)

**The burning bush and the divine name**
- Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God (Exod 3:6)
- God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver (Exod 3:7, Exod 3:8, Exod 3:9)
- The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain (Exod 3:12)
- God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh) (Exod 3:14)
- God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews' (Exod 3:18)
- God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion (Exod 3:19, Exod 3:20)

**Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood**
- God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind (Exod 4:11, Exod 4:12)
- The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs (Exod 4:17, Exod 4:20)
- Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead (Exod 4:19)
- God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him (Exod 4:24)
- Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man (Exod 4:25)
- Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood' (Exod 4:25, Exod 4:26)
- Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God (Exod 4:27)
- The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship (Exod 4:31)

**First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw**
- Slaves must make the same quota of bricks while gathering their own straw (Exod 5:7, Exod 5:8, Exod 5:10, Exod 5:11, Exod 5:12, Exod 5:16, Exod 5:18)
- Foreign taskmasters over native foremen who are beaten for unmet quotas (Exod 5:6, Exod 5:10, Exod 5:14)
- Tyrant accuses the oppressed of idleness for wanting to worship (Exod 5:8, Exod 5:17)
- The oppressed blame the deliverer for making things worse (Exod 5:20, Exod 5:21)
- Prophet complains to God that his mission has only made things worse (Exod 5:22, Exod 5:23)

**'I am YHWH': the name not known to the patriarchs; genealogy of Moses and Aaron**
- God says he appeared to the ancestors under another name and did not make his proper name known (Exod 6:2, Exod 6:3)
- God's promise of redemption phrased in four verbs (bring out, deliver, redeem, take) (Exod 6:6, Exod 6:7)
- The people cannot listen to the prophet because of their broken spirit and hard labor (Exod 6:9)
- A genealogy interrupts a narrative at the hero's commissioning (Exod 6:14, Exod 6:15, Exod 6:16, Exod 6:17, Exod 6:18, Exod 6:19, Exod 6:20, Exod 6:21, Exod 6:22, Exod 6:23, Exod 6:24, Exod 6:25)
- Hero's father married his own aunt (Exod 6:20)

**Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs**
- God makes the prophet 'as God' to the king with his brother as his prophet (Exod 7:1)
- Wonders done so that Egypt shall know 'I am YHWH' (Exod 7:5)
- Hero is eighty (and his brother eighty-three) when they confront the king (Exod 7:7)

**Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice**
- Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water (Exod 7:24)
- Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power (Exod 8:5, Exod 8:6)
- The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks (Exod 8:10)

**Plagues 4-6: swarms, pestilence of livestock, boils**
- Israel's sacrifices would be an abomination to Egyptians who might stone them (Exod 8:22)
- Pestilence kills the oppressors' livestock while sparing the oppressed's (Exod 9:3, Exod 9:6)
- God sets a fixed time ('tomorrow') for a plague (Exod 9:5)
- Soot from a kiln thrown skyward becomes boils on men and beasts (Exod 9:8, Exod 9:9, Exod 9:10)
- The magicians themselves are struck and cannot stand before the prophet (Exod 9:11)

**Plague 7: hail and fire**
- Plagues sent so the king will know there is none like God in all the earth (Exod 9:14)
- God has kept the tyrant alive to show his power and make his name known in all the earth (Exod 9:15, Exod 9:16)
- A plague unlike any since the nation was founded, or ever again (Exod 9:18, Exod 9:24)
- Some of the king's servants fear God's word and bring their slaves and cattle indoors (Exod 9:19, Exod 9:20, Exod 9:21)
- Narrator dates a plague by the growth stage of named crops (barley in ear, flax in bud, wheat late) (Exod 9:31, Exod 9:32)

**Plagues 8-9: locusts and darkness**
- The king's own servants urge him to let the people go (Exod 10:7)
- A west wind carries the locusts into the Sea of Reeds (Exod 10:19)
- During the plague of darkness the Israelites have light in their dwellings (Exod 10:23)
- King tells the prophet never to see his face again or he will die (Exod 10:28, Exod 10:29)

**Announcement of the death of the firstborn**
- God announces one final plague after which the king will drive them out (Exod 11:1)
- The prophet becomes very great in the eyes of the king's servants and the people (Exod 11:3)
- God goes out through the land at midnight to strike (Exod 11:4)
- Not even a dog will growl at the Israelites on the night of the plague (Exod 11:7)

**Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt**
- The spring exodus month becomes the first month of the year (Exod 12:2)
- An unblemished yearling lamb selected on the tenth and slaughtered at twilight on the fourteenth (Exod 12:3, Exod 12:5, Exod 12:6)
- Small households join neighbors to share one sacrificial lamb (Exod 12:4)
- Sacrificial blood daubed on the doorposts and lintel protects the household (Exod 12:7, Exod 12:13, Exod 12:22, Exod 12:23)
- Sacrificial lamb roasted whole, head, legs and innards, eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs (Exod 12:8, Exod 12:9)
- Leaven must be removed from houses; whoever eats it is cut off (Exod 12:15, Exod 12:19)
- Festival days are holy convocations on which no work is done except preparing food (Exod 12:16)
- No one may leave the house until morning on the night of the destroyer (Exod 12:22)
- Defeated king asks the departing prophet to bless him too (Exod 12:32)
- The people carry their unleavened dough in kneading-troughs on their shoulders (Exod 12:34, Exod 12:39)
- About 600,000 men on foot leave Egypt, besides children (Exod 12:37)
- A mixed multitude (erev rav) of non-Israelites leaves Egypt with Israel (Exod 12:38)
- Israel's stay in Egypt lasts 430 years to the very day (Exod 12:40, Exod 12:41)
- No uncircumcised foreigner may eat the Passover; circumcised slaves and converts may (Exod 12:43, Exod 12:44, Exod 12:45, Exod 12:48)
- No bone of the paschal sacrifice may be broken (Exod 12:46)

**Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire**
- The exodus month is Aviv, the month of ripening grain (Exod 13:4)
- Firstborn sons must be redeemed (Exod 13:13, Exod 13:15)
- God leads the people by a roundabout route so they will not see war and turn back (Exod 13:17, Exod 13:18)

**The pursuit and the parting of the sea**
- Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth (Exod 14:2, Exod 14:9)
- God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him (Exod 14:3, Exod 14:4, Exod 14:17, Exod 14:18)
- The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness (Exod 14:11, Exod 14:12)
- God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward' (Exod 14:15)
- God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers (Exod 14:19, Exod 14:20)
- At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy (Exod 14:24)
- God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots (Exod 14:25)
- The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore (Exod 14:30)
- After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant (Exod 14:31)

**The Song of the Sea and Miriam's song**
- By the blast of God's nostrils the waters pile up and the deeps congeal (Exod 15:8, Exod 15:10)
- The earth swallows the enemy at God's outstretched right hand (Exod 15:12)
- God leads the redeemed people to his holy abode (Exod 15:13)
- Neighboring nations and chieftains tremble on hearing of God's deeds (Exod 15:14, Exod 15:15, Exod 15:16)

**Bitter water sweetened at Marah; Elim's twelve springs and seventy palms**
- Three days in the wilderness without finding water (Exod 15:22)
- At a desert stop God gives statute and ordinance and tests the people (Exod 15:25)

**Manna and quail; the first Sabbath**
- Food is given daily, a day's portion at a time, to test obedience (Exod 16:4, Exod 16:16, Exod 16:21)
- Manna appears as a fine flaky layer like hoarfrost when the dew lifts (Exod 16:13, Exod 16:14)
- Each gathers an omer per person; the one who gathers much has no excess, the one who gathers little no lack (Exod 16:16, Exod 16:17, Exod 16:18)
- Manna kept overnight breeds worms and stinks (Exod 16:19, Exod 16:20)
- Ungathered manna melts when the sun grows hot (Exod 16:21)
- A double portion of manna falls or is gathered on the sixth day (Exod 16:5, Exod 16:22, Exod 16:29)
- Seventh-day rest declared holy to God, with no gathering or going out (Exod 16:23, Exod 16:25, Exod 16:26, Exod 16:29, Exod 16:30)
- Manna kept for the Sabbath does not spoil or breed worms (Exod 16:24)
- Those who go out to gather on the Sabbath find nothing (Exod 16:27, Exod 16:28)
- Explanatory gloss defining a measure (an omer is a tenth of an ephah) (Exod 16:36)

**Water from the rock at Massah and Meribah**
- God stands upon a rock before the prophet (Exod 17:6)
- The people put God to the test (Exod 17:2, Exod 17:7)

**Battle with Amalek; Moses' raised hands**
- Joshua leads Israel's fighting men (Exod 17:9, Exod 17:13)
- Battle outcome depends on the leader keeping his hands raised (Exod 17:11)
- Two men hold up the leader's tired arms, one on each side (Exod 17:12)
- God vows to blot out the memory of Amalek (Exod 17:14)

**Jethro's visit and the appointment of judges**
- The hero's wife and sons were sent away and are brought back to him (Exod 18:2)
- A father names his sons after events in his own life (Exod 18:3, Exod 18:4)
- A foreign priest offers sacrifice to Israel's God and shares a meal with the elders (Exod 18:12)
- The leader judges the people alone from morning to evening and is overburdened (Exod 18:13, Exod 18:14, Exod 18:18)
- Judges must be capable, God-fearing, truthful and hate bribes (Exod 18:21)
- Minor cases are judged by subordinates; hard cases go to the leader (Exod 18:22, Exod 18:26)
- The prophet adopts an administrative reform suggested by a foreigner (Exod 18:24)

**Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany**
- Israel arrives at Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exod 19:1)
- God carried Israel on eagles' wings (Exod 19:4)
- God comes to the prophet in a thick cloud so the people may hear (Exod 19:9)
- God descends or reveals himself on the third day (Exod 19:11, Exod 19:16)
- A ram's horn blast signals that the people may go up the mountain (Exod 19:13)
- Men must not approach a woman before a holy encounter (Exod 19:15)
- Moses speaks and God answers him with a voice (thunder) (Exod 19:19)
- Priests are mentioned before the Aaronic priesthood is instituted (Exod 19:22, Exod 19:24)

**The Ten Words and the people's fear**
- God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves (Exod 20:2)
- Do not take God's name in vain (Exod 20:7)
- The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation (Exod 20:18)
- The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is (Exod 20:21)

**Altar law**
- God declares that he spoke from heaven (Exod 20:22)
- Altar to be made of earth (Exod 20:24)
- God will come and bless in every place where he causes his name to be remembered (Exod 20:24)
- No steps up to the altar, lest nakedness be exposed (Exod 20:26)

**Covenant Code - Hebrew slaves**
- A wife given by the master and her children stay with the master when the slave goes free (Exod 21:4)
- A daughter sold as a slave-wife keeps rights to food, clothing and conjugal relations or goes free (Exod 21:7-11)

**Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox**
- Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall be put to death (Exod 21:12)
- Striking or cursing father or mother is a capital crime (Exod 21:15, Exod 21:17)
- One who injures another pays for his lost time and his healing (Exod 21:18, Exod 21:19)
- A master who beats his slave to death is punished, unless the slave survives a day or two (Exod 21:20, Exod 21:21)
- Men fighting strike a pregnant woman and she miscarries (Exod 21:22, Exod 21:23)
- A slave whose eye or tooth the master destroys goes free (Exod 21:26, Exod 21:27)
- Laws of the goring ox and the warned owner (Exod 21:28-32, Exod 21:35, Exod 21:36)
- An animal that kills a person is stoned and its flesh not eaten (Exod 21:28)
- The owner of an uncovered pit pays for an animal that falls in (Exod 21:33, Exod 21:34)

**Covenant Code - theft, deposits, seduction**
- Killing a burglar caught breaking in at night incurs no bloodguilt, but by day it does (Exod 22:1, Exod 22:2)
- A thief who cannot pay is sold for his theft (Exod 22:2)
- A thief pays double (Exod 22:3, Exod 22:6, Exod 22:8)
- A dispute over deposited goods is brought before God (ha-elohim) for decision (Exod 22:7, Exod 22:8)
- An oath by YHWH settles a dispute without witnesses (Exod 22:10)
- A herdsman brings the remains of a torn animal as evidence and is not liable (Exod 22:12)
- Liability for a borrowed animal that dies when the owner is absent (Exod 22:13, Exod 22:14)

**Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn**
- Lying with an animal is a capital crime (Exod 22:18)
- Whoever sacrifices to other gods is devoted to destruction (Exod 22:19)
- Flesh torn by beasts in the field is not eaten but thrown to dogs (Exod 22:30)

**Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals**
- Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit (Exod 23:3, Exod 23:6)
- Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey (Exod 23:4, Exod 23:5)

**The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest**
- Obedience is rewarded with health, fertility and full lifespan (Exod 23:25, Exod 23:26)
- The promised borders run from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines and to the River (Exod 23:31)

**Covenant ratified in blood; the elders see God**
- Only the prophet may approach God; the others stay at a distance (Exod 24:2)
- The prophet writes down all of God's words (Exod 24:4)
- Young men, not priests, offer the covenant sacrifices (Exod 24:5)
- Sacrificial blood splashed on altar and people seals the covenant ('blood of the covenant') (Exod 24:6, Exod 24:8)
- People see God and are not harmed (Exod 24:11)
- A meal eaten in God's presence seals a covenant (Exod 24:11)

**Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days**
- Joshua serves as Moses' attendant (Exod 24:13)
- The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh (Exod 24:16)
- God's glory appears as a devouring fire (Exod 24:17)

**The high priest's vestments**
- Aaron and his sons are designated as priests (Exod 28:1)
- Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty (Exod 28:2, Exod 28:40)

**Ordination of the priests**
- A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered (Exod 29:2, Exod 29:3, Exod 29:23)
- The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days (Exod 29:29, Exod 29:30)
- An outsider may not eat holy food (Exod 29:33)

**The daily offering and God's dwelling**
- A drink offering of wine accompanies a sacrifice (Exod 29:40)
- The tent of meeting is where God meets Israel and speaks with Moses (Exod 29:42, Exod 29:43)

**Incense altar, half-shekel ransom and bronze laver**
- Incense is burned every morning and evening (Exod 30:7, Exod 30:8)
- Unauthorized ('strange') incense or offerings are forbidden on the altar (Exod 30:9)
- Once a year atonement is made on the altar's horns with blood (Exod 30:10)
- Atonement money funds the sanctuary as a memorial before God (Exod 30:16)

**Recipes of the holy anointing oil and incense**
- Copying the sacred oil or incense for private use is forbidden on pain of being cut off (Exod 30:32, Exod 30:33, Exod 30:37, Exod 30:38)
- Sacred incense of stacte, onycha, galbanum and frankincense in equal parts, salted (Exod 30:34, Exod 30:35, Exod 30:36)

**The golden calf**
- The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith (Exod 32:1)
- Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH (Exod 32:5)
- The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol (Exod 32:6)
- Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Exod 32:13)

**Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer**
- The tablets are written on both sides by God (Exod 32:15, Exod 32:16)
- The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle (Exod 32:17, Exod 32:18)
- Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire (Exod 32:22, Exod 32:23, Exod 32:24)
- The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies (Exod 32:25)
- The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies (Exod 32:26)
- The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven (Exod 32:32, Exod 32:33)
- God strikes the people with plague for idolatry (Exod 32:35)

**Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back**
- God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way (Exod 33:3, Exod 33:5)
- The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence (Exod 33:4, Exod 33:5, Exod 33:6)
- A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go (Exod 33:7)
- The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God (Exod 33:8, Exod 33:10)
- Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent (Exod 33:11)
- God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor (Exod 33:12, Exod 33:17)

**New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue**
- The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time (Exod 34:21)
- God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage (Exod 34:24)

**Moses' shining face and the veil**
- The prophet's face shines (or is 'horned') after speaking with God (Exod 34:29, Exod 34:30, Exod 34:35)
- The people fear to approach the prophet after his encounter with God (Exod 34:30)
- The prophet covers his radiant face with a veil (Exod 34:33, Exod 34:34, Exod 34:35)

**Sabbath fire ban and the people's donations**
- No fire may be kindled in any dwelling on the Sabbath (Exod 35:3)
- Men and women donate their jewelry to the sanctuary (Exod 35:22)
- Skilled women spin yarn and goat hair for the sanctuary (Exod 35:25, Exod 35:26)
- The tribal chieftains bring the gemstones, spices and oil (Exod 35:27, Exod 35:28)

**Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames**
- God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others (Exod 35:34)
- The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving (Exod 36:5, Exod 36:6, Exod 36:7)

**Altar, laver of mirrors, court and the metal inventory**
- The bronze laver is made from the mirrors of the women (Exod 38:8)
- Women who serve at the entrance of the tent of meeting (Exod 38:8)
- Ithamar son of Aaron supervises the Levites' work (Exod 38:21)
- The count of Israelite men is 603,550 (Exod 38:26)
- One hundred silver talents make one hundred sockets, a talent each (Exod 38:27)

**The vestments made; the work completed and blessed**
- Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving (Exod 39:3)
- The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers (Exod 39:43)

**The tabernacle erected; cloud and glory fill it**
- The sanctuary is erected on the first day of the first month (Exod 40:2, Exod 40:17)
- Anointing confers an everlasting priesthood on the line (Exod 40:15)
- When the cloud lifts from the tabernacle the people set out; otherwise they stay (Exod 40:36, Exod 40:37)

**The burnt offering of cattle, flock and birds**
- God calls to Moses and speaks from the tent of meeting (Lev 1:1)
- The victim is flayed and cut into its pieces (Lev 1:6, Lev 1:12)
- The entrails and legs are washed with water before burning (Lev 1:9, Lev 1:13)
- The bird's crop and feathers are thrown on the ash heap east of the altar (Lev 1:16)
- The bird is torn open by its wings but not divided in two (Lev 1:17)

**The grain offering; no leaven or honey; salt of the covenant**
- A grain offering of fine flour with oil and frankincense (Lev 2:1, Lev 2:15)
- Grain offerings baked in an oven, on a griddle or in a pan (Lev 2:4, Lev 2:5, Lev 2:6, Lev 2:7)
- No leaven or honey may be burned on the altar (Lev 2:11)
- First-fruit offerings are brought but not burned on the altar (Lev 2:12)
- First-fruits grain offering of fresh ears roasted in fire (Lev 2:14)

**The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood**
- The sacrifice is called God's food (lehem) (Lev 3:11, Lev 3:16)
- All the fat belongs to YHWH (Lev 3:16)

**The purification (hattat) offering for unintentional sin**
- An offering is required for sins committed unintentionally (Lev 4:2, Lev 4:13, Lev 4:22, Lev 4:27)
- The required sacrifice is graded by the sinner's rank: priest, community, chieftain, commoner (Lev 4:3, Lev 4:14, Lev 4:23, Lev 4:28, Lev 4:32)
- The anointed priest's sin brings guilt on the whole people (Lev 4:3)
- The priest sprinkles blood seven times before the veil (Lev 4:6, Lev 4:17)
- The elders lay hands on the offering on behalf of the community (Lev 4:15)

**Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering**
- Touching an unclean carcass or human impurity makes one guilty (Lev 5:2, Lev 5:3)
- The poorest bring a flour sin offering without oil or frankincense (Lev 5:11)
- Sacrilege (me'ilah) against the holy things of YHWH (Lev 5:15, Lev 5:16)
- One is guilty even for a sin committed without knowing (Lev 5:17, Lev 5:18)
- Defrauding a neighbor with a false oath is a trespass against God (Lev 5:21, Lev 5:22)
- Restitution to the wronged person precedes the atonement offering (Lev 5:23, Lev 5:24, Lev 5:25)

**Priestly instructions for burnt, grain and sin offerings; the perpetual fire**
- The altar fire must burn continually and never go out (Lev 6:2, Lev 6:5, Lev 6:6)
- The priest removes the ashes in linen garments and changes clothes to take them out (Lev 6:3, Lev 6:4)
- The anointed priest offers a daily griddle-cake grain offering, half morning half evening (Lev 6:13, Lev 6:14, Lev 6:15)
- A priest's own grain offering is wholly burned and not eaten (Lev 6:15, Lev 6:16)
- A garment spattered with sin-offering blood is washed in a holy place (Lev 6:20)
- An earthen vessel that held sacred meat is broken; a bronze one is scoured and rinsed (Lev 6:21)
- A sin offering whose blood is brought inside the sanctuary is burned, not eaten (Lev 6:23)

**Guilt and well-being offerings; priests' portions; fat and blood bans**
- The officiating priest receives the hide of the burnt offering (Lev 7:8)
- The thanksgiving offering is accompanied by leavened loaves (Lev 7:12, Lev 7:13)
- Sacrificial meat must be eaten within a fixed time and leftovers burned (Lev 7:15, Lev 7:16, Lev 7:17)
- An impure person who eats sacred meat is cut off (Lev 7:19, Lev 7:20, Lev 7:21)
- Fat of a carcass or torn animal may be used for work but not eaten (Lev 7:24)
- The offerer must bring the offering with his own hands (Lev 7:30)

**Moses ordains Aaron and his sons**
- The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite (Lev 8:3, Lev 8:4)
- Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination (Lev 8:15, Lev 8:19, Lev 8:29)

**The eighth day - Aaron's first offerings and the divine fire**
- Cult inaugurated on the eighth day after a seven-day ordination (Lev 9:1)
- High priest's own sin offering is a calf (Lev 9:2, Lev 9:8)
- The breast and right thigh are waved before God and given to the priests (Lev 9:21)
- The glory (kavod) of God appears to all the people (Lev 9:4, Lev 9:6, Lev 9:23)
- The people shout and fall on their faces at the theophany (Lev 9:24)

**Strange fire - death of Nadab and Abihu; priestly rules**
- God says he is sanctified through those who are near him, after a fatal cultic error (Lev 10:3)
- Father remains silent on the death of his sons (Lev 10:3)
- Bodies of priests struck by God carried out of the camp in their tunics by relatives (Lev 10:4, Lev 10:5)
- Moses is angry that the priests burned the sin offering instead of eating it (Lev 10:16, Lev 10:17, Lev 10:18)
- The bereaved priest declines to eat the sin offering on the day of his sons' death, and Moses accepts this (Lev 10:19, Lev 10:20)

**Clean and unclean animals; carcass impurity**
- The camel is unclean because it does not have a split hoof (Lev 11:4)
- The hyrax and the hare are described as chewing the cud (Lev 11:5, Lev 11:6)
- Certain kinds of locust with jointed legs for hopping may be eaten (Lev 11:21, Lev 11:22)
- Touching or carrying a carcass makes one unclean until evening (Lev 11:24, Lev 11:25, Lev 11:27, Lev 11:28, Lev 11:39, Lev 11:40)
- A list of eight swarming creatures (mole, mouse, lizards, chameleon) whose carcasses defile (Lev 11:29, Lev 11:30, Lev 11:31)
- Food or seed becomes susceptible to impurity only once water has come on it (Lev 11:34, Lev 11:37, Lev 11:38)
- A spring or cistern collecting water remains clean even if a carcass falls in (Lev 11:36)
- Creatures that go on their belly or have many legs are forbidden as food (Lev 11:41, Lev 11:42)

**Impurity after childbirth**
- Mother's impurity after a daughter's birth lasts twice as long as after a son's (Lev 12:2, Lev 12:4, Lev 12:5)
- Woman after childbirth may not touch holy things or enter the sanctuary until her days are complete (Lev 12:4)
- Mother brings a burnt offering and sin offering at the end of her purification (Lev 12:6, Lev 12:7)

**Diagnosis of tsara'at in skin, scalp and fabric**
- Priest inspects and declares a skin affliction clean or unclean (Lev 13:2, Lev 13:3)
- Hair turned white in the affected spot is a sign of skin disease (Lev 13:3, Lev 13:10, Lev 13:20, Lev 13:25)
- Priest shuts up a suspected affliction for seven days and re-examines it (Lev 13:4, Lev 13:5, Lev 13:21, Lev 13:26, Lev 13:31, Lev 13:33, Lev 13:50, Lev 13:54)
- Raw (living) flesh in a swelling is a sign of skin disease (Lev 13:10, Lev 13:14, Lev 13:15)
- A person whose skin disease covers the whole body and turns white is declared clean (Lev 13:12, Lev 13:13)
- Skin disease diagnosed in a healed boil or burn scar (Lev 13:18, Lev 13:19, Lev 13:23, Lev 13:24, Lev 13:28)
- Skin disease of the scalp or beard (neteq) judged by yellow or black hair (Lev 13:29, Lev 13:30, Lev 13:37)
- Ordinary baldness of the head or forehead is declared clean (Lev 13:40, Lev 13:41)
- Fabric or leather with spreading green or red 'leprous' mold is burned (Lev 13:47, Lev 13:48, Lev 13:49, Lev 13:51, Lev 13:52, Lev 13:55, Lev 13:57)

**Purification of the healed leper; plague in houses**
- Priest goes out of the camp to examine the healed person (Lev 14:3)
- Two birds: one slaughtered, the other dipped in its blood and set free over the field (Lev 14:4, Lev 14:5, Lev 14:6, Lev 14:7, Lev 14:49, Lev 14:50, Lev 14:51, Lev 14:52, Lev 14:53)
- Bird slaughtered over running water in an earthenware vessel (Lev 14:5, Lev 14:50)
- Oil poured on the head of the person being purified (Lev 14:18, Lev 14:29)
- God himself puts a 'leprous' plague in houses of the land (Lev 14:34)
- House is emptied before the priest inspects it so its contents are not defiled (Lev 14:36)
- Infected stones and plaster removed to an unclean place outside the city (Lev 14:40, Lev 14:41, Lev 14:42, Lev 14:45)
- House whose 'leprous' plague returns after repair is torn down (Lev 14:43, Lev 14:44, Lev 14:45)

**Impurity of bodily discharges, semen and menstruation**
- A man with a genital discharge is unclean (Lev 15:2, Lev 15:3)
- Impurity passes to the bed, seat or saddle of the unclean person and to whoever touches them (Lev 15:4, Lev 15:5, Lev 15:6, Lev 15:9, Lev 15:10, Lev 15:20, Lev 15:21, Lev 15:22, Lev 15:23, Lev 15:26)
- Spittle of an unclean person defiles the person it falls on (Lev 15:8)
- Person with a discharge who has rinsed his hands does not transmit impurity by touch (Lev 15:11)
- After a discharge ends, seven clean days are counted and the person bathes in living water (Lev 15:13, Lev 15:28)
- Menstruating woman is unclean seven days and defiles what she lies or sits on (Lev 15:19, Lev 15:24)
- Woman with bleeding beyond her menstrual period is unclean all the days of the flow (Lev 15:25, Lev 15:26, Lev 15:27)
- Human impurity defiles God's dwelling in their midst and endangers them (Lev 15:31)

**The Day of Atonement and the goat for Azazel**
- High priest may enter the inner sanctuary behind the veil only on the annual day of atonement (Lev 16:2, Lev 16:34)
- High priest wears plain linen garments to enter the holy of holies (Lev 16:4, Lev 16:23, Lev 16:32)
- Lots cast over two goats to decide their roles (Lev 16:8)
- A goat is designated by lot 'for Azazel', a named wilderness recipient (Lev 16:8, Lev 16:10, Lev 16:26)
- Cloud of incense covers the ark cover so the priest does not die (Lev 16:12, Lev 16:13)
- Blood rites purge the sanctuary and altar of the people's impurities and transgressions (Lev 16:16, Lev 16:18, Lev 16:19, Lev 16:20, Lev 16:33)
- No one may be in the tent while the high priest makes atonement in the sanctuary (Lev 16:17)
- Living goat bears the people's sins away into the wilderness (Lev 16:10, Lev 16:21, Lev 16:22)
- Priest confesses the people's sins over the head of a live animal (Lev 16:21)
- The man who led away the scapegoat or burned the remains washes before re-entering the camp (Lev 16:26, Lev 16:28)

**Slaughter only at the tent; the blood is the life**
- Animals may be slaughtered only as offerings at the sanctuary entrance (Lev 17:3, Lev 17:4, Lev 17:5, Lev 17:8, Lev 17:9)
- Eating blood is forbidden because the life (nefesh) of the flesh is in the blood (Lev 17:10, Lev 17:11, Lev 17:12, Lev 17:14)
- God gives blood on the altar to make atonement for lives (Lev 17:11)
- The law applies to the resident alien (ger) as to the Israelite (Lev 17:8, Lev 17:10, Lev 17:12, Lev 17:13, Lev 17:15)

**Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants**
- Do not follow the practices of Egypt where you lived or of Canaan where you are going (Lev 18:3)
- Marrying or lying with a brother's wife is forbidden (Lev 18:16)
- Sexual relations of a man or a woman with an animal are forbidden (Lev 18:23)

**Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor**
- Each person must revere mother and father (Lev 19:3)
- Do not stand idly by the blood of your neighbor (Lev 19:16)
- Do not hate your brother in your heart; rebuke your neighbor instead (Lev 19:17)
- Do not take vengeance or bear a grudge against your people (Lev 19:18)

**Mixtures, orlah fruit, mourning cuttings, alien and just weights**
- Prohibition of cross-breeding animals, sowing mixed seed and wearing mixed cloth (Lev 19:19)
- Fruit of a new tree is 'uncircumcised' for three years, holy in the fourth, eaten in the fifth (Lev 19:23, Lev 19:24, Lev 19:25)
- Gashes in the flesh for the dead and tattoo marks are forbidden (Lev 19:28)
- Rise before the gray-haired and honor the elderly (Lev 19:32)

**Penalties for Molech worship, necromancy and sexual offenses**
- One who curses father or mother is put to death (Lev 20:9)
- In bestiality the animal is killed together with the human offender (Lev 20:15, Lev 20:16)
- Sibling incest is called 'hesed' (normally 'kindness'), here a disgrace (Lev 20:17)
- God separated Israel from the peoples as clean animals are separated from unclean (Lev 20:24, Lev 20:25, Lev 20:26)

**Priests' mourning and marriage limits; blemished priests**
- High priest may not defile himself even for father or mother (Lev 21:11, Lev 21:12)
- Priest with a bodily defect may not approach the altar or veil (Lev 21:17, Lev 21:18, Lev 21:19, Lev 21:20, Lev 21:21, Lev 21:23)
- Blemished priest still eats the holy and most holy food (Lev 21:22)

**Who may eat holy food; unblemished sacrificial animals**
- Priest in a state of impurity may not eat holy food until he washes and the sun sets (Lev 22:3, Lev 22:4, Lev 22:5, Lev 22:6, Lev 22:7)
- Impure person becomes clean when the sun sets (Lev 22:7)
- A priest's purchased or house-born slave eats holy food, but a hired worker or lodger does not (Lev 22:10, Lev 22:11)
- Widowed or divorced childless priest's daughter returns to eat of her father's holy food (Lev 22:12, Lev 22:13)
- Animal with an overgrown or stunted limb accepted as a freewill offering but not for a vow (Lev 22:23)
- Animals with crushed or cut testicles may not be offered, nor may such be done in the land (Lev 22:24)
- Blemished animals may not be accepted as offerings from a foreigner either (Lev 22:25)
- An animal and its young may not be slaughtered on the same day (Lev 22:28)
- Thanksgiving offering eaten the same day with nothing left till morning (Lev 22:29, Lev 22:30)

**The appointed times - sabbath and annual festivals**
- First sheaf (omer) of the harvest waved by the priest on the morrow after the sabbath (Lev 23:10, Lev 23:11, Lev 23:12)
- New bread, parched grain or fresh ears may not be eaten until the first sheaf is offered (Lev 23:14)
- Two leavened loaves of new grain offered as first fruits (Lev 23:17, Lev 23:20)
- A holy day is kept from evening to evening (Lev 23:32)

**Perpetual lamp, showbread, and the blasphemer stoned**
- Son of an Israelite mother and Egyptian father blasphemes the Name in a quarrel (Lev 24:10, Lev 24:11)
- Pronouncing or pricking 'the Name' of God in blasphemy is a capital offense (Lev 24:11, Lev 24:16)
- Offender held in custody until God's ruling is given (Lev 24:12)
- Those who heard the blasphemy lay their hands on the offender's head before stoning (Lev 24:14)
- Killing a person is capital; killing an animal is compensated life for life (Lev 24:17, Lev 24:18, Lev 24:21)

**Sabbatical year and the jubilee; the land is mine**
- Every seventh year the land rests: no sowing, pruning or harvesting (Lev 25:2, Lev 25:3, Lev 25:4, Lev 25:5)
- Spontaneous growth of the fallow year is food for owner, slaves, hired men, aliens, livestock and wild animals (Lev 25:6, Lev 25:7)
- Fiftieth year after seven sabbatical cycles is the jubilee (Lev 25:8, Lev 25:10, Lev 25:11, Lev 25:12, Lev 25:13)
- The shofar is sounded throughout the land on the Day of Atonement to begin the jubilee (Lev 25:9)
- Land is sold by the number of harvests remaining until the jubilee (Lev 25:14, Lev 25:15, Lev 25:16, Lev 25:17)
- God promises the sixth year will yield enough for three years (Lev 25:20, Lev 25:21, Lev 25:22)

**Redemption of land, interest-free loans, and Israelite bondmen**
- A house in a walled city can be redeemed only within a year and does not return at the jubilee (Lev 25:29, Lev 25:30)
- Houses in Levite cities can always be redeemed and their fields never sold (Lev 25:32, Lev 25:33, Lev 25:34)
- An impoverished Israelite sold to a brother serves as a hired worker, not a slave, until the jubilee (Lev 25:39, Lev 25:40, Lev 25:41, Lev 25:53)
- Do not rule over a fellow Israelite with harshness (perekh) (Lev 25:43, Lev 25:46, Lev 25:53)
- Permanent slaves may be bought from surrounding nations and resident aliens and bequeathed (Lev 25:44, Lev 25:45, Lev 25:46)

**Covenant blessings for obedience**
- No idols, carved image, pillar or figured stone set up to bow down on (Lev 26:1)
- God promises to walk about in the midst of the people (Lev 26:11, Lev 26:12)

**Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant**
- Punishments escalate sevenfold each time the people do not listen (Lev 26:18, Lev 26:21, Lev 26:24, Lev 26:28)
- Curse of consumption and fever that waste the eyes and the soul (Lev 26:16)
- Curse: you will flee though no one pursues, chased by the sound of a driven leaf (Lev 26:17, Lev 26:36, Lev 26:37)
- Curse: the sky like iron and the earth like bronze (Lev 26:19)
- God answers the people's 'walking contrary' (qeri) by walking contrary to them (Lev 26:21, Lev 26:24, Lev 26:27, Lev 26:28, Lev 26:40, Lev 26:41)
- Curse: ten women bake bread in one oven and it is doled out by weight (Lev 26:26)
- Curse: your corpses will be heaped on the corpses of your idols (Lev 26:30)
- Curse: God will not smell the pleasing odor of their offerings (Lev 26:31)

**Valuation of vowed persons, animals, houses, fields; herem and tithes**
- A person vowed to God is valued in silver by age and sex (Lev 27:2, Lev 27:3, Lev 27:4, Lev 27:5, Lev 27:6, Lev 27:7)
- A poor person who vows is assessed by the priest according to his means (Lev 27:8)
- A vowed animal may not be exchanged; if it is, both become holy (Lev 27:10, Lev 27:33)
- Value of a dedicated field set by the amount of seed it takes (a homer of barley = 50 shekels) (Lev 27:16, Lev 27:17, Lev 27:18)
- A dedicated field not redeemed becomes the priest's holding at the jubilee (Lev 27:20, Lev 27:21)
- A firstborn animal already belongs to God and cannot be dedicated by vow (Lev 27:26)
- Anything devoted (herem) to God cannot be sold or redeemed; a devoted person is put to death (Lev 27:28, Lev 27:29)
- Every tenth animal passing under the shepherd's rod is holy as tithe (Lev 27:32)

**The census of fighting men in the wilderness of Sinai**
- Divine speech dated to a precise day, month and year after the exodus (Num 1:1)
- Census of all males twenty years and older able to go to war (Num 1:2, Num 1:3, Num 1:18, Num 1:20)
- Twelve tribal leaders listed by name and patronymic (Num 1:4, Num 1:5, Num 1:6, Num 1:7, Num 1:8, Num 1:9, Num 1:10, Num 1:11, Num 1:12, Num 1:13, Num 1:14, Num 1:15, Num 1:16, Num 1:44)

**The camp in four standards around the tent**
- Tribes camp in four groups of three under standards on the four sides of the sanctuary (Num 2:2, Num 2:3, Num 2:10, Num 2:18, Num 2:25)
- Each tribe camps by its standard with ensigns of its ancestral house (Num 2:2)
- The tent and Levite camp march in the middle of the tribal columns (Num 2:17)

**Aaron's sons; Levite clans counted and taken in place of the firstborn**
- Priests who died for a cultic offense left no sons (Num 3:4)
- Levites taken in place of all the firstborn of Israel (Num 3:12, Num 3:13, Num 3:41, Num 3:45)
- Levite males are counted from one month old (Num 3:15, Num 3:22, Num 3:28, Num 3:34)
- Levite clans camp on three sides of the sanctuary and the priests on the east (Num 3:23, Num 3:29, Num 3:35, Num 3:38)
- Kohathite Levites carry the ark, table, lampstand and altars (Num 3:31)

**Wrapping and carrying the sanctuary; Levites aged 30 to 50**
- Before marching, priests cover the ark with the screening veil and further wrappings (Num 4:5, Num 4:6)
- Holy objects covered with tahash skins for transport (Num 4:6, Num 4:8, Num 4:10, Num 4:11, Num 4:12, Num 4:14)
- Each holy vessel wrapped in a cloth of a specified color (blue, scarlet, purple) for transport (Num 4:6, Num 4:7, Num 4:8, Num 4:9, Num 4:11, Num 4:12, Num 4:13)
- Bread stays perpetually on the table of the presence (Num 4:7)
- Bearers of the sanctuary objects die if they touch or even look at them uncovered (Num 4:15, Num 4:18, Num 4:19, Num 4:20)
- Priest's son Eleazar is in charge of lamp oil, incense, daily meal offering and anointing oil (Num 4:16)
- Priest's son Ithamar supervises the Gershonite and Merarite Levites (Num 4:28, Num 4:33)
- Each item to be carried is assigned to a bearer by name (Num 4:32)

**Unclean sent out of the camp; confession and restitution**
- People with skin disease, discharge or corpse impurity are sent out of the camp (Num 5:2, Num 5:3, Num 5:4)
- Wrongdoer must confess his sin and repay what he took (Num 5:6, Num 5:7)
- If the wronged party has no kinsman, restitution goes to God, to the priest (Num 5:8)
- Holy donations given to a priest belong to that priest (Num 5:9, Num 5:10)

**The suspected adulteress and the bitter water**
- A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife (Num 5:14, Num 5:30)
- Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy' (Num 5:15, Num 5:18, Num 5:25, Num 5:26)
- Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor (Num 5:17)
- Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God (Num 5:18)
- Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls (Num 5:21, Num 5:22, Num 5:27)
- Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen' (Num 5:22)
- Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks (Num 5:23, Num 5:24)
- Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children (Num 5:28)
- Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result (Num 5:31)

**The Nazirite vow**
- A man or a woman may take the vow of a Nazirite (Num 6:2)
- Nazirite may not become unclean even for the corpse of father, mother, brother or sister (Num 6:6, Num 6:7)
- Sudden death of someone beside a Nazirite voids his vow and he must start again (Num 6:9, Num 6:10, Num 6:11, Num 6:12)
- Priest places the boiled shoulder and cakes in the hands of the shaved Nazirite and waves them (Num 6:19, Num 6:20)
- After the vow's completion rite the Nazirite may drink wine (Num 6:20)

**The priestly blessing**
- Blessing: may God lift up his face to you and give you peace (Num 6:26)
- Priests 'put God's name' upon the people by blessing them (Num 6:27)

**The chieftains' covered wagons and oxen**
- The sanctuary and its vessels anointed and consecrated on its completion (Num 7:1)
- Twelve leaders give six covered wagons and twelve oxen for transporting the sanctuary (Num 7:3)
- Wagons and oxen allotted to Levite clans according to their loads (Num 7:6, Num 7:7, Num 7:8)
- Most holy objects must be carried on the shoulders, not on wagons (Num 7:9)

**Altar dedication gifts, days seven to twelve; totals; the voice from between the cherubim**
- After itemized gifts, the grand totals of silver, gold and animals are summed (Num 7:84, Num 7:85, Num 7:86, Num 7:87, Num 7:88)

**Lighting the lampstand**
- Sacred object made after a pattern shown by God (Num 8:4)

**Purification and dedication of the Levites**
- Community lays hands on persons to transfer or consecrate (Num 8:10)
- Persons themselves 'waved' or presented as an offering to God (Num 8:11, Num 8:13, Num 8:21)
- A priestly class is taken in place of the firstborn owed to God (Num 8:16, Num 8:17, Num 8:18)
- Sacred service bounded by fixed ages (start and retirement) (Num 8:24, Num 8:25, Num 8:26)
- A ritual or class prevents a plague when people approach the holy (Num 8:19)

**Silver trumpets and departure from Sinai**
- Blowing trumpets in battle makes God 'remember' and save (Num 10:9, Num 10:10)
- Tribes march under banners in a fixed order around the shrine (Num 10:14, Num 10:18, Num 10:22, Num 10:25)

**Hobab invited as guide; the Song of the Ark**
- Hero asks his foreign father-in-law to be the people's 'eyes' in the desert (Num 10:29, Num 10:30, Num 10:31)
- The sacred chest goes ahead to scout a resting place (Num 10:33)

**Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail**
- Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint (Num 11:1)
- A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin (Num 11:4)
- Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically) (Num 11:25, Num 11:26)
- Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets' (Num 11:26, Num 11:27, Num 11:28, Num 11:29)

**Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses**
- Prophet's own siblings challenge his unique authority (Num 12:2)
- Hero called the humblest man on earth (Num 12:3)
- Ordinary prophets receive revelation in visions and dreams (Num 12:6)
- Father spitting in a daughter's face brings seven days' shame (Num 12:14)
- Afflicted person shut outside the camp seven days (Num 12:14, Num 12:15)

**The twelve spies and their report**
- Leader renames a disciple (Hoshea to Joshua) (Num 13:16)
- Founding of a city dated relative to an Egyptian city (Hebron seven years before Zoan) (Num 13:22)
- Single grape cluster so large two men carry it on a pole (Num 13:23, Num 13:24)

**Rebellion after the spies' report and the forty-year sentence**
- Intercessor argues the nations would say God was unable (Num 14:13, Num 14:14, Num 14:15, Num 14:16)
- People have tested God 'ten times' (Num 14:22)
- Those who slandered the land die by plague (Num 14:36, Num 14:37)

**Grain and drink offerings, dough offering, inadvertent sin**
- First of the dough given as a gift (challah) (Num 15:20, Num 15:21)
- Inadvertent sin atoned by sacrifice; 'high-handed' sin unforgivable (Num 15:24, Num 15:27, Num 15:28, Num 15:30, Num 15:31)

**The Sabbath wood-gatherer; the law of tassels**
- Man gathering wood on the Sabbath is stoned by divine ruling (Num 15:32, Num 15:35, Num 15:36)
- Tassels (tzitzit) with a blue cord on garment corners as reminder (Num 15:38, Num 15:39)

**Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel; the earth swallows them**
- Rebels claim all the people are holy and challenge the priest-leader's monopoly (Num 16:1, Num 16:2, Num 16:3, Num 16:10)
- Rival claimants offer incense in fire-pans so God may choose the holy one (Num 16:6, Num 16:7, Num 16:17, Num 16:18)
- Prophet stakes his mission on an unprecedented sign ('if these die a common death, YHWH has not sent me') (Num 16:28, Num 16:29, Num 16:30)

**Censers as altar plating, Aaron stops the plague, Aaron's rod blossoms**
- Rebels' censers beaten into altar plating as a memorial (Num 17:3, Num 17:4, Num 17:5)
- Priest with incense stands between the dead and the living and stops the plague (Num 17:11, Num 17:12, Num 17:13)
- Chosen leader's rod sprouts, blossoms and bears almonds overnight (Num 17:17, Num 17:18, Num 17:20, Num 17:23)

**The red heifer and corpse impurity**
- Those who prepare the purifying agent are themselves rendered impure (Num 19:7, Num 19:8, Num 19:10, Num 19:21)
- Ash mixed with running ('living') water sprinkled to cleanse (Num 19:9, Num 19:17)
- A corpse defiles everyone and every open vessel in the tent (Num 19:14, Num 19:15)

**Miriam's death; water from the rock at Meribah**
- Death and burial of the hero's sister (Num 20:1)
- Leader strikes the rock (twice) instead of speaking to it (Num 20:10, Num 20:11)

**Edom refuses passage; death of Aaron at Mount Hor**
- Messengers appeal to a neighboring nation as 'your brother' (Num 20:14)
- An angel sent to bring the people out of Egypt (Num 20:16)
- Dying high priest is stripped and his vestments put on his son (Num 20:26, Num 20:28)

**Hormah; the fiery serpents and the bronze serpent**
- War vow to devote an enemy's cities to destruction (herem) if God gives victory (Num 21:2, Num 21:3)
- People call the miraculous food 'worthless bread' (Num 21:5)
- God sends fiery (saraph) serpents that bite the people (Num 21:6)

**Stations to Moab; Book of the Wars of YHWH; Song of the Well**
- Citation of a lost source, the 'Book of the Wars of YHWH' (Num 21:14, Num 21:15)
- Song to a well dug by princes with their staffs ('Spring up, O well') (Num 21:16, Num 21:17, Num 21:18)

**Defeat of Sihon and Og; the Heshbon ballad**
- A national god (Chemosh) gives up his sons as fugitives and daughters as captives (Num 21:29)
- Enemy smitten until no survivor (sarid) remained (Num 21:35)

**Balak sends for Balaam**
- Simile: the horde will lick up everything as an ox licks up grass (Num 22:4)
- A king hires a foreign seer to curse an enemy people (Num 22:5, Num 22:6, Num 22:11, Num 22:17)
- Envoys come with the fees of divination in hand (Num 22:7)
- God comes to a non-Israelite at night to speak with him (Num 22:8, Num 22:9, Num 22:12, Num 22:19, Num 22:20)

**Balaam's donkey and the angel**
- The angel stands in the road 'as a satan' (adversary) against the traveler (Num 22:22, Num 22:32)
- An animal sees an angel that its human rider cannot (Num 22:23, Num 22:25, Num 22:27, Num 22:33)
- Rider beats his animal three times as it swerves from the hidden angel (Num 22:23, Num 22:25, Num 22:27, Num 22:28)
- A donkey speaks with a human voice to its rider (Num 22:28, Num 22:29, Num 22:30)
- God uncovers a man's eyes to see an angel (Num 22:31)

**Balaam's first and second oracles**
- Seven altars with seven bulls and seven rams (Num 23:1, Num 23:2, Num 23:4, Num 23:14, Num 23:29, Num 23:30)
- 'A people that dwells alone, not reckoned among the nations' (Num 23:9)
- Descendants innumerable as the dust (Num 23:10)
- Seer wishes to die the death of the upright (Num 23:10)
- Curse attempted again from a different mountain/vantage point (Num 23:13, Num 23:14, Num 23:27, Num 23:28)
- 'God is not a man that he should lie, nor a son of man that he should repent' (Num 23:19)
- 'There is no augury in Jacob, no divination in Israel' (Num 23:23)

**Balaam's third and fourth oracles; the Star from Jacob; oracles against nations**
- The spirit of God comes upon a non-Israelite seer (Num 24:2)
- Oracle of 'the man whose eye is opened', falling down with eyes uncovered (Num 24:3, Num 24:4, Num 24:15, Num 24:16)
- 'How goodly are your tents, O Jacob' (Mah tovu) (Num 24:5)
- Israel likened to gardens by a river, aloes planted by YHWH, cedars by water (Num 24:6, Num 24:7)
- King strikes his hands together in anger (Num 24:10)
- A star shall come forth from Jacob, a scepter rise from Israel (Num 24:17, Num 24:18, Num 24:19)
- Ships from Kittim shall afflict Asshur and Eber (Num 24:24)

**Baal Peor and the zeal of Phinehas**
- Foreign women invite the people to their gods' sacrifices, leading to idolatry (Num 25:1, Num 25:2)
- Zealous priest spears an Israelite man and foreign woman together in the act (Num 25:6, Num 25:7, Num 25:8)
- Zealous act rewarded with a 'covenant of peace' and eternal priesthood (Num 25:11, Num 25:12, Num 25:13)
- The transgressing couple named with their noble lineage (Zimri, Cozbi) (Num 25:14, Num 25:15)

**Census of the second generation on the plains of Moab**
- A second census counts the new generation by clans (Num 26:2, Num 26:4, Num 26:51, Num 26:63)
- The sons of the rebel did not die with him (Num 26:11)

**Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned**
- Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan (Num 27:4)
- Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod) (Num 27:18, Num 27:20, Num 27:23)
- Decisions sought through the priest's Urim (Num 27:21)

**Calendar of public offerings**
- Tenth of the seventh month: day to 'afflict your souls' (fast) (Num 29:7, Num 29:11)
- Diminishing series of bulls over Booths (13 down to 7, totaling 70) (Num 29:13, Num 29:17, Num 29:20, Num 29:23, Num 29:26, Num 29:29, Num 29:32)
- A concluding eighth-day assembly ('atseret) after the feast (Num 29:35, Num 29:36)

**Vows of men and women**
- Silence on hearing counts as confirmation (Num 30:5, Num 30:8, Num 30:12, Num 30:15)
- Vows of a widow or divorced woman stand on their own (Num 30:10)

**War against Midian and division of the spoils**
- Leader given a final task to complete before he is 'gathered to his people' (Num 31:2)
- Army of a thousand from each tribe (12,000) (Num 31:4, Num 31:5)
- Priest accompanies the army with holy vessels and trumpets (Num 31:6)
- Five named kings slain together (Num 31:8)
- Warriors and captives purified outside camp seven days after battle (Num 31:19, Num 31:20, Num 31:24)
- Metal spoils purified by passing through fire, others through water (Num 31:22, Num 31:23)
- Commanders report that not one man of the army is missing (Num 31:49)
- Captured gold jewelry offered to atone for the soldiers' lives (Num 31:50, Num 31:52, Num 31:54)

**Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh settle east of the Jordan**
- Tribes pledge to fight in the vanguard before returning home (Num 32:16, Num 32:17, Num 32:18, Num 32:27, Num 32:32)
- 'Know that your sin will find you' (Num 32:23)

**The stages of Israel's journey from Egypt to Moab**
- Moses writes down the stages of the journey by God's command (Num 33:2)
- Itinerary of about forty-two encampments from Egypt to Moab (Num 33:5, Num 33:48, Num 33:49)
- Aaron dies aged 123 on the first of the fifth month of the fortieth year (Num 33:38, Num 33:39)

**Borders of Canaan and the land commission**
- Named commission of a priest, a leader and one chieftain per tribe to apportion land (Num 34:17, Num 34:18, Num 34:19, Num 34:29)

**Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers**
- The Jubilee year considered in tribal land transfers (Num 36:4)

**Setting of Moses' speech; appointment of judges**
- Eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea (yet it took forty years) (Deut 1:2)
- Moses 'expounds this Torah' in Moab on the first of the eleventh month of the fortieth year (Deut 1:3, Deut 1:5)
- People multiplied 'like the stars of heaven' (Deut 1:10)
- Blessing: may God make you a thousand times as many (Deut 1:11)

**The spies episode retold**
- Children 'who do not yet know good and evil' will inherit (Deut 1:39)

**Passing Edom, Moab and Ammon; the giant aboriginal peoples**
- The rebellious generation dies out before entering the land (Deut 2:14, Deut 2:15, Deut 2:16)

**Defeat of Og of Bashan and allotment of Transjordan**
- Kingdom of sixty walled cities with gates and bars (Deut 3:4, Deut 3:5)
- A giant king's oversized bed (Og's iron bed, nine cubits) displayed as a relic (Deut 3:11)

**Moses pleads to cross the Jordan and is refused**
- God is angry with the leader on account of the people (Deut 3:26)

**Exhortation at Horeb's memory; no image; exile and return**
- Keeping the law will make the nations call Israel wise (Deut 4:6, Deut 4:8)
- No other nation has a god so near whenever they call on him (Deut 4:7)

**The Shema and the instruction to teach**
- Swear only by God's name (Deut 6:13)
- When your son asks what the laws mean, recite the exodus story (Deut 6:20, Deut 6:21)

**Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people**
- God chose Israel not for their numbers, being the fewest of peoples, but from love (Deut 7:7, Deut 7:8)
- Silver and gold on idols must not be taken; it is abomination and herem (Deut 7:25, Deut 7:26)

**Lessons of the wilderness; the good land; beware of pride**
- Man does not live by bread alone but by every word from God's mouth (Deut 8:3)
- Land whose stones are iron and from whose hills copper is dug (Deut 8:9)
- When you eat and are satisfied, bless God for the land (Deut 8:10)
- Wilderness of fiery serpents and scorpions (Deut 8:15)

**Not for your righteousness; the golden calf and Moses' intercession recalled**
- Land given not for Israel's righteousness but for the nations' wickedness (Deut 9:4, Deut 9:5, Deut 9:6)
- Intercession appeals to what the nations would say of God (Deut 9:28)

**Second tablets and ark; Levites set apart; what God requires**
- Wooden ark made to hold the stone tablets (Deut 10:1, Deut 10:2, Deut 10:3, Deut 10:5)
- Aaron dies and his son Eleazar becomes priest in his place (Deut 10:6)

**The land that drinks rain; blessing and curse; Gerizim and Ebal**
- Egypt watered by foot like a vegetable garden; the promised land drinks rain from heaven (Deut 11:10, Deut 11:11)
- God's eyes are on the land continually from the beginning to the end of the year (Deut 11:12)
- Oaks (terebinths) of Moreh near Shechem as a landmark (Deut 11:30)

**The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition**
- Every man doing what is right in his own eyes (Deut 12:8)
- Meat may be slaughtered and eaten anywhere, like gazelle and deer, when far from the sanctuary (Deut 12:15, Deut 12:20, Deut 12:21, Deut 12:22)
- Do not inquire how the nations served their gods in order to imitate them (Deut 12:30)

**False prophet, enticing kin, and the apostate city**
- Prophet or dreamer whose sign comes true but who urges other gods must be rejected (Deut 13:2, Deut 13:3)
- Relative or friend who secretly entices to other gods must be stoned, your hand first (Deut 13:7, Deut 13:9, Deut 13:10, Deut 13:11)
- A city that turns to other gods is put under the ban, burned and left a mound forever (Deut 13:13, Deut 13:15, Deut 13:16, Deut 13:17)

**Mourning rites forbidden; clean and unclean food; tithes**
- Animal that died of itself may be given to the resident alien or sold to a foreigner (Deut 14:21)
- Annual tithe eaten by the owner before God at the chosen place (Deut 14:22, Deut 14:23)
- If the place is far, convert the tithe to silver and buy what you desire there, wine and strong drink included (Deut 14:24, Deut 14:25, Deut 14:26)

**Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings**
- There will be no poor among you, yet the poor will never cease from the land (Deut 15:4, Deut 15:11)
- Base thought refusing a loan as the release year nears; the poor man cries to God against you (Deut 15:9)

**Passover, Weeks, Booths; judges; no Asherah**
- Passover in the month of Aviv, at evening, at the chosen place (Deut 16:1, Deut 16:2, Deut 16:5, Deut 16:6)
- Unleavened bread, bread of affliction, because you left Egypt in haste (Deut 16:3, Deut 16:4)
- Feast of Weeks counted seven weeks from the first sickle in the standing grain (Deut 16:9, Deut 16:10)
- Justice, justice shall you pursue (Deut 16:20)
- No Asherah tree planted beside God's altar and no standing stone (Deut 16:21, Deut 16:22)

**Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king**
- Hand of the witnesses first against the condemned, then the people's (Deut 17:7)
- King must be chosen by God from among brothers, not a foreigner (Deut 17:14, Deut 17:15)
- King writes a copy of the Torah and reads it all his days (Deut 17:18, Deut 17:19, Deut 17:20)

**Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses**
- Priest's due: shoulder, two cheeks and stomach of the sacrifice, and first of the fleece (Deut 18:3, Deut 18:4)
- Be wholehearted (tamim) with God (Deut 18:13)
- A prophecy that does not come true shows the prophet spoke presumptuously (Deut 18:21, Deut 18:22)

**Cities of refuge, boundary stones, false witnesses**
- Axe head slips off the handle while cutting wood and kills a companion (accidental homicide) (Deut 19:5)
- Deliberate murderer who flees to refuge is handed over by the elders to the avenger (Deut 19:11, Deut 19:12, Deut 19:13)

**Broken-necked heifer; captive bride; firstborn; rebellious son; hanged body**
- Elders wash their hands over the heifer: our hands did not shed this blood (Deut 21:6, Deut 21:7)
- Captive woman shaves her head, pares her nails, mourns her parents a month before marriage (Deut 21:11, Deut 21:12, Deut 21:13)
- Captive wife who is no longer wanted must be freed, not sold (Deut 21:14)
- Body hanged on a tree must be buried the same day; the hanged is a curse of God (Deut 21:22, Deut 21:23)

**Lost property, bird's nest, mixtures, tassels, virginity and sexual offences**
- Return a brother's lost animal or property; you may not hide yourself (Deut 22:1, Deut 22:2, Deut 22:3)
- Help lift a brother's fallen ox or donkey (Deut 22:4)
- Woman must not wear man's gear, nor man a woman's garment (Deut 22:5)
- Send away the mother bird before taking the young, for long life (Deut 22:6, Deut 22:7)
- Build a parapet on a new roof so no one falls (Deut 22:8)
- Prohibition of mixed seeds in a vineyard (Deut 22:9)
- Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together (Deut 22:10)
- Tassels (gedilim) on the four corners of the garment (Deut 22:12)
- Parents display the bride's virginity cloth before the elders (Deut 22:15, Deut 22:17)
- Bride found not a virgin stoned at the door of her father's house (Deut 22:20, Deut 22:21)
- Betrothed girl lain with in the city dies for not crying out; in the field only the man dies (Deut 22:23, Deut 22:24, Deut 22:25, Deut 22:26, Deut 22:27)
- Man who lies with an unbetrothed virgin pays her father fifty silver and must marry her without divorce (Deut 22:28, Deut 22:29)

**Admission to the assembly; camp purity; slaves, interest, vows**
- Edomites (brothers) and Egyptians (hosts) admitted in the third generation (Deut 23:8, Deut 23:9)
- Man unclean from a nocturnal emission stays outside the camp until evening and washes (Deut 23:11, Deut 23:12)
- Latrine outside the war camp; dig with a spade and cover excrement because God walks in the camp (Deut 23:13, Deut 23:14, Deut 23:15)
- Escaped slave not returned to his master; he may live where he chooses (Deut 23:16, Deut 23:17)
- Harlot's hire and the price of a dog may not be brought to the temple for a vow (Deut 23:19)

**Divorce, newlyweds, pledges, wages, gleanings**
- Newly married man exempt from army for one year to gladden his wife (Deut 24:5)
- Millstones may not be taken in pledge, for that is taking a life (Deut 24:6)
- Remember what God did to Miriam (skin disease) on the way (Deut 24:8, Deut 24:9)

**Forty lashes, muzzled ox, levirate and halitzah, weights, Amalek**
- Flogging limited to forty stripes so your brother is not degraded (Deut 25:2, Deut 25:3)
- Do not muzzle the ox while it threshes (Deut 25:4)
- Widow removes the refusing brother-in-law's sandal and spits in his face (Deut 25:7, Deut 25:8, Deut 25:9, Deut 25:10)
- Woman who seizes a man's genitals in a brawl has her hand cut off (Deut 25:11, Deut 25:12)
- Remember Amalek who attacked the stragglers; blot out his memory (Deut 25:17, Deut 25:18, Deut 25:19)

**First-fruits creed, tithe declaration, mutual covenant**
- First fruits brought in a basket to the priest at the chosen place (Deut 26:2, Deut 26:3, Deut 26:4, Deut 26:10)
- Historical creed: a wandering Aramean was my father, went down to Egypt... (Deut 26:5, Deut 26:6, Deut 26:7, Deut 26:8, Deut 26:9)
- Tithe declaration: I did not eat it in mourning nor give any of it to the dead (Deut 26:13, Deut 26:14)
- Look down from your holy habitation in heaven and bless your people (Deut 26:15)

**Inscribed stones and altar on Ebal; the twelve curses**
- Six tribes stand on one mountain to bless, six on the other to curse (Deut 27:12, Deut 27:13)
- Levites pronounce twelve curses on secret crimes and all the people answer Amen (Deut 27:14, Deut 27:15, Deut 27:26)
- Cursed is he who misleads a blind man on the road (Deut 27:18)
- Curses on lying with father's wife, a beast, a sister, a mother-in-law (Deut 27:20, Deut 27:21, Deut 27:22, Deut 27:23)

**Blessings and the great curses**
- Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough (Deut 28:3, Deut 28:4, Deut 28:5, Deut 28:6, Deut 28:16, Deut 28:17, Deut 28:18, Deut 28:19)
- Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways (Deut 28:7, Deut 28:25)
- God will make you the head and not the tail (Deut 28:13, Deut 28:44)
- The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust (Deut 28:23, Deut 28:24)
- Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed (Deut 28:27, Deut 28:35)
- Futility curse: betroth a wife another lies with, build a house and not live in it, plant a vineyard and not enjoy it (Deut 28:30, Deut 28:31, Deut 28:32, Deut 28:33)
- King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone (Deut 28:36, Deut 28:64)
- The stranger in your midst rises higher and higher while you sink (Deut 28:43, Deut 28:44)
- God puts an iron yoke on your neck (Deut 28:48)
- Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege (Deut 28:56, Deut 28:57)
- As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you (Deut 28:63)
- In the morning you will say: would it were evening; in the evening: would it were morning (Deut 28:66, Deut 28:67)
- God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy (Deut 28:68)
- Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb (Deut 28:69)

**Covenant at Moab; the secret apostate; the land like Sodom**
- All ranks stand before God, from the hewer of wood to the drawer of water (Deut 29:9, Deut 29:10)
- A root bearing poison and wormwood among you (secret apostate) (Deut 29:17)

**Return from exile; the near commandment; choose life**
- God himself will circumcise your heart and your offspring's heart (Deut 30:6)

**Joshua commissioned; Torah written and deposited; the Song commanded**
- Torah read before all the people, men, women, children and strangers, every seventh year at Sukkot (Deut 31:10, Deut 31:11, Deut 31:12, Deut 31:13)
- God foretells to the dying prophet that the people will go astray after him (Deut 31:16, Deut 31:20, Deut 31:27, Deut 31:29)
- God knows the people's inclination (yetzer) before he brings them in (Deut 31:21)
- Book of the Torah placed beside the ark as a witness (Deut 31:25, Deut 31:26)

**The Song of Moses (Ha'azinu)**
- Teaching falls like rain and distils like dew (Deut 32:2)
- God like an eagle stirring its nest and bearing its young on its pinions (Deut 32:11)
- God nursed Israel with honey from the rock and oil from flint (Deut 32:13, Deut 32:14)
- Jeshurun grew fat and kicked, forsaking the God who made him (Deut 32:15)
- God as the Rock that bore you and the God who writhed in labor with you (Deut 32:18)
- God will provoke Israel to jealousy with a no-people, a foolish nation (Deut 32:21)
- Fire kindled in God's anger burns to the depths of Sheol and the foundations of the mountains (Deut 32:22)
- God refrains from annihilating Israel lest the enemy boast it was their own hand (Deut 32:26, Deut 32:27)
- Their vine is from the vine of Sodom; grapes of poison, wine of serpents' venom (Deut 32:32, Deut 32:33)
- Nations called to rejoice as God avenges his servants' blood and atones for his land (Deut 32:43)

**Song delivered; Moses ordered up Mount Nebo to die**
- Prophet told to ascend a mountain, see the land, and die there, gathered to his people (Deut 32:49, Deut 32:50)
- Moses and Aaron's breach of faith at the waters of Meribah (Deut 32:51)

**The Blessing of Moses on the tribes**
- Dying patriarch or leader blesses each tribe in turn (Deut 33:1, Deut 33:6, Deut 33:7)
- A fiery law (esh dat) from God's right hand (Deut 33:2)
- God dwells between Benjamin's shoulders (Deut 33:12)
- Zebulun and Issachar suck the abundance of the seas and treasures hidden in the sand (Deut 33:19)
- A tribe likened to a lion or lion's whelp (Deut 33:20, Deut 33:22)
- Asher dips his foot in oil; sandals of iron and bronze (Deut 33:24, Deut 33:25)
- Underneath are the everlasting arms (Deut 33:27)
- Happy are you, Israel, who is like you, a people saved by YHWH (Deut 33:29)

**Death and burial of Moses**
- From Nebo/Pisgah God shows Moses the whole land from Gilead to Dan to the western sea (Deut 34:1, Deut 34:2, Deut 34:3, Deut 34:4)
- Moses dies 'by the mouth of YHWH' (al pi YHWH) (Deut 34:5)
- God (he) buries the prophet; no one knows his grave to this day (Deut 34:6)
- At death his eye was not dim nor his vigor abated (Deut 34:7)
- Successor filled with spirit of wisdom through laying on of hands (Deut 34:9)
- No prophet arose again like Moses whom God knew face to face (Deut 34:10, Deut 34:11, Deut 34:12)

**God commissions Joshua; Transjordan tribes pledged**
- People pledge to obey the successor as they obeyed his predecessor; rebels to die (Josh 1:16, Josh 1:17, Josh 1:18)

**Rahab hides the spies in Jericho**
- A prostitute (Rahab) shelters the spies in her house (Josh 2:1, Josh 2:4)
- Host deceives pursuers to protect the hidden guests (Josh 2:4, Josh 2:5)
- Spies hidden under stalks of flax on the roof (Josh 2:6)
- Spies swear to spare the helper's whole family in return for her kindness (Josh 2:12, Josh 2:13, Josh 2:14, Josh 2:17, Josh 2:20)
- Spies let down by a rope through a window in the city wall (Josh 2:15)
- Scarlet cord tied in the window as the sign of protection (Josh 2:18, Josh 2:21)
- Whoever goes out of the door, his blood is on his own head (Josh 2:19)
- Fugitives hide three days in the hills until pursuers give up (Josh 2:16, Josh 2:22)

**The ark goes before; the Jordan stands in a heap**
- People follow the ark at a distance of 2000 cubits (Josh 3:3, Josh 3:4, Josh 3:6)
- Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow God will do wonders (Josh 3:5)
- The ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth (Josh 3:11, Josh 3:13)
- Twelve men chosen, one from each tribe (Josh 3:12)
- The Jordan overflows its banks all the days of harvest (Josh 3:15)
- Priests bearing the ark stand on dry ground in the middle of the river until all have crossed (Josh 3:15, Josh 3:17)

**Twelve memorial stones from the Jordan; the river returns**
- Twelve stones, one per tribe, taken from the riverbed as a memorial of the crossing (Josh 4:3, Josh 4:8, Josh 4:20)
- Stones set up in the middle of the river where the priests stood, visible 'to this day' (Josh 4:9)
- The crossing into the land is dated to the tenth day of the first month (Josh 4:19)
- Gilgal as the first camp and sanctuary in the land (Josh 4:19-20)
- A miracle is done so that all the peoples of the earth may know God's power (Josh 4:24)

**Mass circumcision at Gilgal, Passover, end of manna, the commander of YHWH's army**
- Circumcision performed with flint knives (Josh 5:2-3)
- A place called the Hill of Foreskins, where mass circumcision took place (Josh 5:3)
- The generation born in the wilderness was not circumcised (Josh 5:4-7)
- Passover kept at a decisive turning point (entry into the land) (Josh 5:10)
- The manna stops the day after the people eat the produce of the land (Josh 5:11-12)
- A figure with a sword reveals himself as commander of YHWH's army (Josh 5:14)

**Fall of Jericho; Rahab spared; curse on the rebuilder**
- A besieged city is circled once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh (Josh 6:3-4, Josh 6:14-15)
- Seven priests blow seven rams' horns before the ark (Josh 6:4, Josh 6:6, Josh 6:8, Josh 6:13)
- The ark goes before the army in battle or procession (Josh 6:6-9, Josh 6:11)
- The army must keep total silence until the leader gives the signal to shout (Josh 6:10)
- City walls collapse at a trumpet blast and a great shout (Josh 6:5, Josh 6:20)
- Captured silver, gold, bronze and iron are holy, for the treasury of YHWH (Josh 6:19, Josh 6:24)
- The harlot who hid the spies is spared with her family when the city falls (Josh 6:17, Josh 6:22-23, Josh 6:25)
- A conquered city is burned with fire (Josh 6:24)

**Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan**
- Leader complains to God after a defeat: would that we had stayed where we were (Josh 7:7-9)
- The culprit is urged to 'give glory to God' by confessing (Josh 7:19-20)
- The sinner's children, animals and property are destroyed with him (Josh 7:24-25)

**Ambush and capture of Ai; altar and Torah inscribed on Mount Ebal**
- Leader holds out his javelin and does not lower his hand until victory is complete (Josh 8:18, Josh 8:26)

**The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty**
- Locals disguise themselves with worn clothes and old provisions to pass as travelers from a far country (Josh 9:4-6, Josh 9:12-13)
- Dry, crumbled bread shown as proof of a long journey (Josh 9:5, Josh 9:12)
- Leaders make a decision without asking the oracle of YHWH (Josh 9:14)
- The congregation grumbles against its chiefs over a decision (Josh 9:18)
- A subject people made perpetual woodcutters and water-drawers for the sanctuary (Josh 9:21, Josh 9:23, Josh 9:27)
- A people is cursed to perpetual slavery (Josh 9:23)

**Battle of Gibeon, hailstones, sun and moon stand still, five kings in the cave, southern campaign**
- Five kings form an alliance and are defeated together (Josh 10:3-5)
- A king of Jerusalem bears a name with 'tsedeq' (Adoni-zedek, Melchizedek) (Josh 10:1, Josh 10:3)
- The army marches all night and attacks the enemy by surprise (Josh 10:9)
- God heeds the command of a man, a unique event (Josh 10:14)
- Defeated kings hide in a cave, which is sealed with great stones (Josh 10:16-18)
- Idiom: no one 'sharpened his tongue' against Israel (Josh 10:21)
- Captains put their feet on the necks of captured kings (Josh 10:24)
- Summary of a sweeping conquest of the whole south from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza (Josh 10:40-42)

**Northern coalition under Jabin of Hazor; hamstrung horses; Anakim destroyed**
- An enemy army as numerous as the sand on the seashore (Josh 11:4)
- The enemy is pursued as far as Great Sidon (Josh 11:8)
- Hazor, 'head of all those kingdoms', is the only city burned in the north (Josh 11:10-11, Josh 11:13)

**List of the kings defeated by Moses and Joshua (thirty-one kings)**
- A numbered list of conquered city-kings (thirty-one) (Josh 12:9-24)
- A 'king of the nations (Goiim)' among the conquered kings (Josh 12:23)

**Land still to be conquered; Transjordanian allotments; Balaam's death**
- God tells the aged leader that much land remains to be possessed (Josh 13:1)
- The Shihor 'before Egypt' as the land's southern limit (Josh 13:3)
- Five named Midianite princes (Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, Reba) (Josh 13:21)

**Allotment by lot begins; Caleb at eighty-five claims Hebron**
- The sons of Joseph count as two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim (Josh 14:4)
- The faithful spy receives the land his foot trod on (Josh 14:6-9, Josh 14:14)
- An old hero says he is as strong as on the day he was sent out forty-five years before (Josh 14:10-11)

**The boundaries of Judah**
- The 'Ascent of Scorpions' (Ma'aleh Aqrabbim) on the border (Josh 15:3)
- The Brook (Wadi) of Egypt as the southwestern border (Josh 15:4)

**City list of Judah by districts; Jebusites remain in Jerusalem**
- The City of Salt and En-gedi listed in the Judean wilderness (Josh 15:62)
- Philistine cities listed with their 'daughters' (dependent villages) (Josh 15:45-47)

**Manasseh's lot; the daughters of Zelophehad receive land**
- Machir, the warrior firstborn of Manasseh, receives Gilead and Bashan (Josh 17:1)
- Daughters of a man without sons receive an inheritance among their kin (Josh 17:3-4, Josh 17:6)

**Joseph's complaint of one lot; clear the forest; iron chariots**
- A tribe complains that its allotment is too small for its numbers (Josh 17:14)
- A tribe is told to clear forest to make more land (Josh 17:15, Josh 17:18)

**Tent of meeting set up at Shiloh; land surveyed in a book; seven lots cast**
