- Milcom (their 'king') dispossessed the tribe of Gad and will go into exile (Jer 49:1, Jer 49:3)
- Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, God will bring you down (Jer 49:16)
- The cry at a nation's fall is heard as far as the Red Sea (Jer 49:21)
- Fire kindled in the wall of Damascus devours the palaces of Ben-hadad (Jer 49:27)
- Desert peoples described as those with the corners of their hair clipped (Jer 49:32)
- A people at ease that dwells alone with neither gates nor bars (Jer 49:31)
- A ruined city becomes a haunt of jackals, desolate forever (Jer 49:33)
- God breaks the bow of Elam, the chief of their might (Jer 49:35)
- God brings the four winds from the four ends of heaven to scatter a people (Jer 49:36)
- God sets his own throne in a conquered foreign land (Jer 49:38)

**Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken**
- Babylon's gods Bel and Merodach are put to shame and its idols dismayed (Jer 50:2)
- God's people are lost sheep whose shepherds led them astray on the mountains (Jer 50:6-7, Jer 50:17)
- Repay the city according to her deeds: do to her as she has done (Jer 50:15, Jer 50:29)
- Israel a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured it, last Babylon gnawed its bones (Jer 50:17-18)
- Israel's iniquity will be sought and not found, for God pardons the remnant (Jer 50:20)
- Babylon addressed by wordplay names: Merathaim ('double rebellion') and Pekod ('punishment') (Jer 50:21)
- Babylon called the 'hammer of the whole earth' is broken (Jer 50:23)
- God opens his armory and brings out the weapons of his indignation (Jer 50:25)
- Repeated 'A sword upon...' litany against every class of a city (Jer 50:35-38)
- Babylon is a land of idols, mad over their terrors (Jer 50:38)
- Desert creatures or demons (tsiyyim, iyyim) and ostriches inhabit the ruined city (Jer 50:39)

**Oracle against Babylon (II): golden cup, destroying mountain, Sheshach, the scroll sunk in the Euphrates**
- Names hidden by the atbash letter cipher (Sheshach for Babel, Leb-qamai for Kasdim) (Jer 51:1, Jer 51:41)
- God stirs up a destroying wind (or spirit) against the empire (Jer 51:1, Jer 51:11)
- Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God (Jer 51:5)
- Babylon is a golden cup in God's hand that made all the earth drunk (Jer 51:7)
- Ironic call to bring balm for a fallen city that cannot be healed (Jer 51:8-9)
- God stirs up the spirit of the kings of the Medes against Babylon (Jer 51:11, Jer 51:28)
- The doomed imperial city 'dwells on many waters' rich in treasures (Jer 51:13)
- 'The Portion of Jacob' is not like idols, but the former of all things (Jer 51:19)
- God calls a nation his war-club with which he shatters nations, horses, chariots and people (Jer 51:20-23)
- The empire as a 'destroying mountain' to be rolled down and made a burnt mountain (Jer 51:25-26)
- The northern kingdoms Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz are summoned against Babylon (Jer 51:27)
- Runner after runner and messenger after messenger bring the king news of his city's fall (Jer 51:31)
- The city is like a threshing floor at treading time; soon her harvest comes (Jer 51:33)
- The conqueror swallowed the city like a dragon (tannin) and filled his belly (Jer 51:34)
- God dries up Babylon's 'sea' and makes her fountain dry (Jer 51:36)
- God prepares a feast for the empire's leaders, makes them drunk, and they sleep an eternal sleep (Jer 51:39, Jer 51:57)
- The sea rises over Babylon and covers her with its roaring waves (Jer 51:42, Jer 51:55)
- God punishes Bel and makes him vomit out what he swallowed (Jer 51:44)
- Heaven and earth and all in them sing for joy over the empire's fall (Jer 51:48)
- Though Babylon should climb to heaven and fortify its height, destroyers will reach it (Jer 51:53)
- A scroll of oracles is tied to a stone and thrown into a river as a sign the city will sink (Jer 51:59-64)

**Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release**
- The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city (Jer 52:4)
- Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile (Jer 52:28-30)
- A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table (Jer 52:31-34)
- A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him (Jer 52:31)

**Lamentations 1: 'How lonely sits the city', Zion as a widow with no comforter**
- The ruined city sits alone like a widow (Lam 1:1)
- She who was a princess among provinces has become a forced laborer (Lam 1:1)
- She weeps bitterly in the night with tears on her cheek (Lam 1:2, Lam 1:16)
- Refrain that the city has no one to comfort her (Lam 1:2, Lam 1:9, Lam 1:16-17, Lam 1:21)
- The roads to Zion mourn because none come to the festivals (Lam 1:4)
- The princes became like deer that find no pasture and flee without strength (Lam 1:6)
- The fallen city is likened to a menstruant (niddah) whose impurity is in her skirts (Lam 1:8-9, Lam 1:17)
- Nations forbidden to enter the assembly invade the sanctuary (Lam 1:10)
- The starving people trade their treasures for food to keep alive (Lam 1:11)
- 'Is it nothing to you, all who pass by? Look and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow' (Lam 1:12)
- From on high God sent fire into the sufferer's bones (Lam 1:13)
- God spread a net for the sufferer's feet and turned him back (Lam 1:13)
- The yoke of the sinner's transgressions is knotted by God's hand onto her neck (Lam 1:14)
- The Lord trod the virgin daughter of Judah as in a winepress (Lam 1:15)
- The sufferer confesses 'YHWH is righteous, for I rebelled against his word' (Lam 1:18)
- The sufferer's bowels churn and heart turns over within her (Lam 1:20)
- Outside the sword bereaves, inside it is like death (Lam 1:20)
- The ruined city, personified as a woman, speaks in the first person (Lam 1:9, Lam 1:11-22)

**Lamentations 2: the Lord became like an enemy; children faint in the streets**
- God did not remember his footstool (Zion or the ark) on the day of his anger (Lam 2:1)
- God cast down the splendor of Israel from heaven to earth (Lam 2:1)
- The Lord has become like an enemy to his own people (Lam 2:4-5)
- God himself spurns his altar and destroys his own sanctuary and festivals (Lam 2:6-7)
- Enemies raise a shout in the temple as on a festival day (Lam 2:7)
- The city's gates sink into the ground and their bars are broken (Lam 2:9)
- There is no torah, and the prophets find no vision from YHWH (Lam 2:9)
- The mourner's liver is poured out on the ground (Lam 2:11)
- Infants and sucklings faint from hunger in the city squares, asking their mothers for bread and wine (Lam 2:11-12, Lam 2:19)
- The city's ruin is as vast as the sea; who can heal it? (Lam 2:13)
- Passers-by clap hands, hiss and wag their heads at the ruined city (Lam 2:15-16)
- Let tears run down like a torrent day and night with no rest (Lam 2:18)
- Arise and cry out in the night at the beginning of the watches, pour out your heart like water (Lam 2:19)
- Priest and prophet are slain in the sanctuary of the Lord (Lam 2:20)
- The day of YHWH's anger on which none escape (Lam 2:1, Lam 2:21-22)

**Lamentations 3: 'I am the man who has seen affliction'; mercies new every morning**
- Acrostic in which each letter begins three consecutive verses (Lam 3:1-3, Lam 3:64-66)
- God like a bear or lion lying in wait, bending his bow and shooting arrows into the sufferer (Lam 3:10-13)
- God has walled the sufferer in, blocked his ways with hewn stones and weighted his chains (Lam 3:5, Lam 3:7, Lam 3:9)
- God makes the sufferer dwell in darkness like those long dead (Lam 3:2, Lam 3:6)
- God shuts out the sufferer's prayer or wraps himself in a cloud so no prayer passes (Lam 3:8, Lam 3:44)
- The sufferer becomes the laughing-stock and mocking song of all his people (Lam 3:14, Lam 3:63)
- God sates the sufferer with bitterness and makes him drunk with wormwood (Lam 3:15, Lam 3:19)
- God made the sufferer's teeth grind on gravel and cowered him in ashes (Lam 3:16)
- God's mercies are not ended; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness (Lam 3:22-23)
- It is good to wait silently for the salvation of YHWH (Lam 3:25-26)
- It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth (Lam 3:27)
- Let him put his mouth in the dust; perhaps there is hope (Lam 3:29)
- Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him and be filled with reproach (Lam 3:30)
- God does not willingly afflict or grieve human beings (Lam 3:31-33)
- Let us search and examine our ways and return to YHWH (Lam 3:40)
- Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in heaven (Lam 3:41)
- God made his people offscouring and refuse among the nations (Lam 3:45)
- The mourner's eyes run down with streams of water ceaselessly (Lam 3:48-49)
- Enemies hunted the sufferer like a bird without cause (Lam 3:52)
- Enemies cast the sufferer into a pit and throw stones on him; waters close over his head (Lam 3:53-55)
- God pleads the sufferer's cause and redeems his life (Lam 3:58-59)

**Lamentations 4: gold grown dim, ostrich-cruel mothers, the anointed captured**
- The holy stones lie scattered at the head of every street (Lam 4:1)
- Zion's precious sons, worth fine gold, now counted as clay pots (Lam 4:2)
- Even jackals nurse their young, but the people have become cruel like ostriches (Lam 4:3)
- The suckling's tongue cleaves to its palate from thirst (Lam 4:4)
- Those raised in scarlet now embrace dunghills (Lam 4:5)
- The people's iniquity is greater than the sin of Sodom, overthrown in a moment (Lam 4:6)
- The city's nazirites (princes) were purer than snow, whiter than milk, ruddier than coral; now blacker than soot (Lam 4:7-8)
- Those slain by the sword are better off than those wasting from hunger (Lam 4:9)
- The kings of the earth did not believe an enemy could enter Jerusalem's gates (Lam 4:12)
- The city fell for the sins of its prophets and priests who shed the blood of the righteous (Lam 4:13-14)
- Our eyes failed watching for help from a nation that could not save (Lam 4:17)
- Pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven, chasing over mountains and desert (Lam 4:19)
- The captured king is called 'the breath of our nostrils, YHWH's anointed, in whose shadow we would live' (Lam 4:20)
- Daughter Edom, dwelling in the land of Uz, will drink the cup and strip herself (Lam 4:21-22)

**Lamentations 5: communal prayer 'Remember, O LORD', renew our days as of old**
- A poem of twenty-two lines matching the alphabet count but not acrostic (Lam 5:1-22)
- Our inheritance is turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners (Lam 5:2)
- The people have become orphans without a father, their mothers like widows (Lam 5:3)
- The conquered must pay for their own water and buy their wood (Lam 5:4)
- Slaves rule over the conquered with no one to deliver them (Lam 5:8)
- Our skin is hot as an oven from the burning of famine (Lam 5:10)
- Women are raped in Zion and virgins in the towns of Judah (Lam 5:11)
- Princes hanged up by their hands by the enemy (Lam 5:12)
- The crown has fallen from our head; woe to us for we have sinned (Lam 5:16)
- Foxes (jackals) prowl over desolate Mount Zion (Lam 5:18)
- YHWH sits enthroned forever; his throne endures from generation to generation (Lam 5:19)
- A book closes on the fear that God has utterly rejected his people (Lam 5:22)

**Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory**
- The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God (Ezek 1:1)
- A prophet receives visions beside a river in the land of exile (Ezek 1:1, Ezek 1:3)
- A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era (Ezek 1:1-2)
- The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family (Ezek 1:3)
- The vision begins with a storm wind, great cloud and flashing fire coming from the north (Ezek 1:4)
- The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum) (Ezek 1:4, Ezek 1:27)
- Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle (Ezek 1:10)
- The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings (Ezek 1:7-8)
- Each creature has wings touching its neighbor's and wings covering its body (Ezek 1:9, Ezek 1:11, Ezek 1:23)
- The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning (Ezek 1:9, Ezek 1:12, Ezek 1:17)
- Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it (Ezek 1:13-14)
- The rims of the wheels are full of eyes all around (Ezek 1:18)
- A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads (Ezek 1:22)
- The creatures' wings sound like many waters, like the voice of Shaddai (Ezek 1:24)
- God's throne appears like sapphire (lapis lazuli) above the firmament (Ezek 1:26)
- On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man' (Ezek 1:26-27)
- The radiance around the enthroned figure is like the rainbow in the cloud (Ezek 1:28)
- The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...' (Ezek 1:5, Ezek 1:26, Ezek 1:28)

**Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey**
- God addresses the prophet as 'son of man' (ben adam) (Ezek 2:1, Ezek 2:3, Ezek 3:1)
- The prophet lives among briers, thorns and scorpions, yet must not fear (Ezek 2:6)
- The prophet is made to eat a heavenly scroll (Ezek 2:8-3:3)
- A hand is stretched out to the prophet holding a scroll (Ezek 2:9)
- A scroll written on front and back with laments, mourning and woe (Ezek 2:10)
- The eaten scroll tastes sweet as honey in the prophet's mouth (Ezek 3:3)
- Foreign peoples of strange speech would heed the prophet, but Israel will not (Ezek 3:5-7)
- God makes the prophet's forehead as hard as diamond against a hard-faced people (Ezek 3:8-9)
- The spirit lifts and carries the prophet away (Ezek 3:12, Ezek 3:14)
- Heavenly voice cries 'Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place' (Ezek 3:12)
- A great rushing sound of the creatures' wings and the wheels behind the prophet (Ezek 3:12-13)
- After his vision the prophet sits stunned among the people for seven days (Ezek 3:15)

**Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house**
- If the watchman fails to warn the wicked, God requires their blood from him (Ezek 3:18-21)
- The glory seen by the river appears again to the prophet in a valley/plain (Ezek 3:22-23)
- The prophet is told to shut himself in his house (Ezek 3:24-25)

**Sign-acts of the siege: the brick, the iron griddle, lying on his sides, rationed bread baked on dung**
- The prophet draws the city on a clay brick and lays a model siege against it (Ezek 4:1-2)
- The prophet sets an iron griddle as an iron wall between himself and the city (Ezek 4:3)
- The prophet symbolically bears the iniquity of the people in his body (Ezek 4:4-6)
- The prophet lies on his left side 390 days and his right side 40 days bearing the iniquity of Israel and Judah (Ezek 4:4-6)
- Prophetic time reckoned a day for each year (Ezek 4:6)
- The prophet is bound with cords so he cannot turn from side to side (Ezek 4:8)
- Siege bread made of wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt mixed in one vessel (Ezek 4:9)
- Bread eaten by weight and water drunk by measure, as in a siege (Ezek 4:10-11, Ezek 4:16)
- The prophet is told to bake his bread over human excrement as a sign of unclean exile food (Ezek 4:12-13)
- Israel will eat unclean bread among the nations (Ezek 4:13)
- The prophet protests that he has never eaten carrion, torn meat or foul flesh (Ezek 4:14)
- After the prophet protests, God allows cow dung instead of human dung for baking (Ezek 4:15)
- The besieged will waste away in their iniquity, appalled at one another (Ezek 4:17)

**The shaven hair divided in thirds; Jerusalem in the midst of the nations**
- Prophet shaves head and beard with a sword as razor, weighs the hair on scales and divides it into thirds (burned, struck with sword, scattered to the wind) (Ezek 5:1, Ezek 5:2)
- A few hairs are kept back and bound in the prophet's garment hem (remnant), yet some of these are thrown into fire (Ezek 5:3, Ezek 5:4)
- God set Jerusalem in the center of the nations with countries all around her (Ezek 5:5)
- God will do to the city what he has never done and will never do again (Ezek 5:9)
- Fathers will eat their sons and sons will eat their fathers in the besieged city (Ezek 5:10)
- God shoots 'evil arrows of famine' at the people (Ezek 5:16)

**Oracle against the mountains of Israel and their high places**
- God lays the slain before their idols and scatters their bones around their altars (Ezek 6:4, Ezek 6:5, Ezek 6:13)

**The end has come upon the four corners of the land**
- Proclamation 'An end has come, the end has come' upon the land (qets ba) (Ezek 7:2, Ezek 7:3, Ezek 7:6)
- Survivors on the mountains moan like doves of the valleys, each for his iniquity (Ezek 7:16)
- God's 'treasured place' (tsefuni) is profaned by robbers when he turns his face away (Ezek 7:22)
- In disaster people seek a vision from the prophet, but instruction perishes from the priest and counsel from the elders (Ezek 7:26)

**Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship**
- A human-like figure of fire from the waist down and gleaming like hashmal (amber/electrum) from the waist up (Ezek 8:2)
- A hand seizes the prophet by a lock of his hair and the spirit carries him between earth and heaven to a distant place (Ezek 8:3)
- An idol called 'the image (semel) of jealousy that provokes jealousy' stands at the north gate of the temple (Ezek 8:3, Ezek 8:5)
- Prophet is told to dig through a wall and enters through the opening (Ezek 8:7, Ezek 8:8)
- Hidden temple chamber whose walls are engraved all around with creeping things, loathsome beasts and idols (Ezek 8:10)
- Seventy elders stand with censers in hand offering incense in the dark, each in his chamber of images (Ezek 8:11, Ezek 8:12)
- Women sit at the north gate of the temple weeping for Tammuz (Ezek 8:14)
- Idolaters 'put the branch (zemorah) to their nose', an obscure cultic gesture (Ezek 8:17)
- Though they cry in God's ears with a loud voice, he will not listen (Ezek 8:18)

**The six executioners and the man in linen who marks the foreheads**
- Six men (angelic executioners), each with a weapon of destruction, come from the north gate to slay the city (Ezek 9:1, Ezek 9:2)
- Divine slaughter is to begin at God's sanctuary, with the elders before the temple (Ezek 9:6, Ezek 9:7)
- The angelic agent returns and reports 'I have done as you commanded me' (Ezek 9:11)

**Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple**
- Above the firmament over the living creatures appears something like sapphire in the likeness of a throne (Ezek 10:1)
- Burning coals are taken from between the cherubim / wheels and scattered over the city (Ezek 10:2, Ezek 10:6, Ezek 10:7)
- The sound of the cherubim's wings is heard like the voice of El Shaddai when he speaks (Ezek 10:5)
- The bodies, backs, hands, wings and wheels of the throne-creatures are full of eyes all around (Ezek 10:12)
- The wheels are called by the name 'galgal' ('whirl') in the prophet's hearing (Ezek 10:2, Ezek 10:13)

**The cauldron saying, death of Pelatiah, God as little sanctuary, the new heart, the glory on the Mount of Olives**
- Proverb 'the city is the cauldron and we are the meat', turned against its speakers (Ezek 11:3, Ezek 11:7, Ezek 11:11)
- A man dies suddenly while the prophet is still prophesying against him (Ezek 11:13)
- God himself becomes 'a little sanctuary' (miqdash me'at) for the exiles in the lands of dispersion (Ezek 11:16)
- The spirit carries the prophet back to the exiles and the vision lifts from him (Ezek 11:1, Ezek 11:24, Ezek 11:25)

**The exile's baggage, eating with trembling, and the end of delayed visions**
- The people are a 'rebellious house' that have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear (Ezek 12:2, Ezek 12:3, Ezek 12:9)
- Prophet packs an exile's bag by day, digs through the wall and goes out at dusk with covered face as a sign of exile (Ezek 12:3, Ezek 12:4, Ezek 12:5, Ezek 12:6, Ezek 12:7)
- A few are spared from sword, famine and plague so they may recount their abominations among the nations (Ezek 12:16)
- Prophet eats his bread with quaking and drinks water with trembling as a sign of the coming desolation (Ezek 12:18, Ezek 12:19)
- God abolishes the saying 'the days drag on and every vision fails': his word will no longer be delayed (Ezek 12:22, Ezek 12:23, Ezek 12:25, Ezek 12:27, Ezek 12:28)

**Against the false prophets and the women who hunt souls**
- The prophets of Israel are like foxes (jackals) among ruins (Ezek 13:4)
- The true prophet's task is to go up into the breaches and build a wall for the people on the day of battle; false prophets did not (Ezek 13:5)
- False prophets will not be in the council of God's people nor written in the register of the house of Israel (Ezek 13:9)
- False prophets mislead the people saying 'Peace' when there is no peace (Ezek 13:10, Ezek 13:16)
- Women prophetesses sew bands (kesatot) on wrists and make veils (mispahot) for heads to hunt souls, killing and keeping alive by magic (Ezek 13:17, Ezek 13:18, Ezek 13:20, Ezek 13:21)
- Diviners profane God for handfuls of barley and crumbs of bread (Ezek 13:19)
- God tears off the magic bands and lets the trapped souls go free 'like birds' (leporhot) (Ezek 13:20)

**Idols in the heart; Noah, Daniel and Job could not save the land**
- Inquirers have 'set up their idols in their hearts' and put the stumbling-block of iniquity before their faces (Ezek 14:3, Ezek 14:4, Ezek 14:7)
- God himself will answer the idolater who inquires of a prophet, making him a sign and a byword and cutting him off (Ezek 14:4, Ezek 14:7, Ezek 14:8)
- If a prophet is enticed to speak, 'I YHWH have enticed that prophet' and will destroy him (Ezek 14:9, Ezek 14:10)
- Even if Noah, Daniel (Dan'el) and Job were in the land, their righteousness would save only themselves, not sons or daughters (Ezek 14:14, Ezek 14:16, Ezek 14:18, Ezek 14:20)
- God's 'four evil judgments': sword, famine, evil beasts and pestilence (Ezek 14:21)
- Survivors from the doomed city will come to the exiles, who will be consoled on seeing their deeds that the punishment was not without cause (Ezek 14:22, Ezek 14:23)

**Parable of the useless vine-wood**
- Parable of the vine-wood: useless for any work, not even for a peg, fit only for the fire; so are Jerusalem's inhabitants (Ezek 15:2, Ezek 15:3, Ezek 15:4, Ezek 15:5, Ezek 15:6)

**Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot**
- A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth (Ezek 16:4, Ezek 16:5)
- God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!' (Ezek 16:6)
- God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her (Ezek 16:7, Ezek 16:8, Ezek 16:9)
- The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by (Ezek 16:14, Ezek 16:15, Ezek 16:25)
- The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them (Ezek 16:17, Ezek 16:18, Ezek 16:19)
- Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food (Ezek 16:20, Ezek 16:21, Ezek 16:36)
- Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh') (Ezek 16:26, Ezek 16:28, Ezek 16:29)
- Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them (Ezek 16:31, Ezek 16:33, Ezek 16:34)

**Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant**
- Proverb 'like mother, like daughter' (Ezek 16:44, Ezek 16:45)
- Samaria (elder, on the left/north) and Sodom (younger, on the right/south) are Jerusalem's sisters, and she is worse than both (Ezek 16:46, Ezek 16:47, Ezek 16:48, Ezek 16:51, Ezek 16:52)
- God will restore the fortunes of Sodom and Samaria along with Jerusalem (Ezek 16:53, Ezek 16:55)
- When God atones for her she will remember, be ashamed and never again open her mouth (Ezek 16:61, Ezek 16:63)

**Riddle of the two eagles, the cedar and the vine; the messianic cedar shoot**
- A great eagle with long pinions and many-colored plumage comes to Lebanon, plucks the top of the cedar and carries it to a land of merchants (Ezek 17:3, Ezek 17:4)
- A low spreading vine planted by one great eagle turns its roots toward a second great eagle (vassal turning from Babylon to Egypt) (Ezek 17:5, Ezek 17:6, Ezek 17:7, Ezek 17:8)
- The vassal king who despised his oath and broke his covenant will not escape but die in the overlord's land (Ezek 17:15, Ezek 17:16, Ezek 17:18)
- God himself takes a tender shoot from the cedar's top and plants it on Israel's high mountain, where it becomes a noble cedar (Ezek 17:22, Ezek 17:23)

**Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance**
- Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them (Ezek 18:10, Ezek 18:14, Ezek 18:18)
- Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die? (Ezek 18:31)

**Dirge for the princes of Israel - the lioness and her cubs, the uprooted vine**
- Dirge: the mother lioness among lions raises cubs who learn to devour men and are caught in pits and led away with hooks to Egypt and Babylon (Ezek 19:2, Ezek 19:3, Ezek 19:4, Ezek 19:5, Ezek 19:6, Ezek 19:7, Ezek 19:8, Ezek 19:9)
- The mother was a fruitful vine by many waters with strong rods for sceptres; plucked up in fury, dried by the east wind and burned, now planted in the desert (Ezek 19:10, Ezek 19:11, Ezek 19:12, Ezek 19:13, Ezek 19:14)

**Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt; the second exodus into the wilderness of the peoples**
- God swears he will not be inquired of by the elders who come to consult him (Ezek 20:3, Ezek 20:31)
- Israel already worshipped the idols of Egypt in Egypt and would not cast them away (Ezek 20:7, Ezek 20:8)
- God refrains from destroying the people 'for the sake of my name', lest it be profaned in the sight of the nations (Ezek 20:9, Ezek 20:14, Ezek 20:22, Ezek 20:44)
- Wordplay etiology: 'What is the high place (bamah) to which you go (ha-ba'im)?' and its name is Bamah to this day (Ezek 20:29)
- The people's wish 'We will be like the nations, serving wood and stone' will never come to pass (Ezek 20:32)
- God swears 'with a mighty hand, outstretched arm and poured-out wrath I will be king over you' (Ezek 20:33, Ezek 20:34)
- God will bring the exiles into 'the wilderness of the peoples' and judge them face to face as he judged the fathers in Egypt's wilderness (Ezek 20:35, Ezek 20:36)
- God makes the people pass under the shepherd's rod and brings them into the bond (masoret) of the covenant, purging out rebels (Ezek 20:37, Ezek 20:38)
- On God's holy mountain, the height of Israel, all Israel will serve him and he will accept their offerings as a pleasing odor (Ezek 20:40, Ezek 20:41)

**Fire in the southern forest; the song of the sword; Babylon's divination at the crossroads; against Ammon**
- God kindles an unquenchable fire in the forest of the south that devours every green tree and every dry tree (Ezek 21:3, Ezek 21:4)
- God draws his sword from its sheath against righteous and wicked alike, and it will not return (Ezek 21:8, Ezek 21:9, Ezek 21:10)
- Prophet commanded to groan with breaking loins before the people; when asked why, he announces coming news (Ezek 21:11, Ezek 21:12)
- Incantatory song of the sharpened and polished sword, flashing like lightning, given to the slayer (Ezek 21:14, Ezek 21:15, Ezek 21:16, Ezek 21:19, Ezek 21:20, Ezek 21:21)
- At the fork of two roads the king of Babylon divines: he shakes arrows, consults teraphim and inspects the liver (Ezek 21:24, Ezek 21:25, Ezek 21:26, Ezek 21:27)
- Divination by inspecting the liver (hepatoscopy) (Ezek 21:26)
- Remove the turban and take off the crown: the low exalted, the high brought low (Ezek 21:30, Ezek 21:31)
- 'A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it ... until he comes to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him' (Ezek 21:32)
- The sword is returned to its sheath and Ammon is judged in the land of its origin and forgotten (Ezek 21:33, Ezek 21:34, Ezek 21:35, Ezek 21:36, Ezek 21:37)

**The city of blood; the dross in the furnace; no man in the breach**
- Catalogue of social, sexual and cultic sins in the city: contempt of parents, oppression of stranger, orphan and widow, slander, incest, bribery, interest (Ezek 22:6, Ezek 22:7, Ezek 22:8, Ezek 22:9, Ezek 22:10, Ezek 22:11, Ezek 22:12)
- Israel has become dross: copper, tin, iron and lead in the furnace, gathered into Jerusalem to be melted by God's wrath (Ezek 22:18, Ezek 22:19, Ezek 22:20, Ezek 22:21, Ezek 22:22)
- The land is not cleansed and not rained upon on the day of indignation (Ezek 22:24)
- Princes are wolves tearing prey and prophets a roaring lion devouring souls (Ezek 22:25, Ezek 22:27)
- Priests do violence to the torah and fail to distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean, hiding their eyes from the sabbaths (Ezek 22:26)
- God seeks a man to build up the wall and stand in the breach before him for the land, and finds none (Ezek 22:30)

**Oholah and Oholibah, the two harlot sisters**
- Two sisters, Oholah ('her tent') and Oholibah ('my tent is in her'), daughters of one mother, are Samaria and Jerusalem, wives of God who play the harlot (Ezek 23:2, Ezek 23:4, Ezek 23:36, Ezek 23:44)
- The sisters' harlotry began in their youth in Egypt where their breasts were pressed (Ezek 23:3, Ezek 23:8, Ezek 23:19, Ezek 23:21, Ezek 23:27)
- The harlot lusts after Assyrian governors and officers clothed in blue, all handsome young horsemen (Ezek 23:5, Ezek 23:6, Ezek 23:12, Ezek 23:23)
- Seeing men portrayed on a wall in vermilion (images of Chaldeans with belts and turbans), the woman lusts and sends messengers to them (Ezek 23:14, Ezek 23:15, Ezek 23:16)
- Egyptian paramours described with 'flesh of donkeys and issue of stallions' (Ezek 23:20)
- Enemy peoples named Pekod, Shoa and Koa come with the Babylonians and Assyrians (Ezek 23:23)
- The adulteress's nose and ears are cut off as punishment (Ezek 23:25)
- The younger sister must drink her sister's deep and wide cup of horror and desolation, drain it, gnaw its sherds and tear her breasts (Ezek 23:31, Ezek 23:32, Ezek 23:33, Ezek 23:34)
- Having slaughtered their children to idols, they enter God's sanctuary the same day to profane it (Ezek 23:37, Ezek 23:38, Ezek 23:39)
- The harlot bathes, paints her eyes, puts on ornaments and sits on a splendid couch with a table set with God's incense and oil (Ezek 23:40, Ezek 23:41)
- Drunkards (sove'im/Sabeans) brought from the desert put bracelets on the women's hands and crowns on their heads (Ezek 23:42)
- All women will be warned by the punishment of the lewd sisters and not imitate them (Ezek 23:48)

**The rusted cauldron; death of the prophet's wife without mourning**
- Prophet told to write down 'the name of this very day' on which the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem (clairvoyant dating) (Ezek 24:2)
- Parable of the pot set on the fire with choice pieces of meat and bones, its rust (hel'ah) never removed (Ezek 24:3, Ezek 24:4, Ezek 24:5, Ezek 24:6)
- The city put its blood on the bare rock, not pouring it on the earth to cover it with dust, so God leaves it uncovered to cry for vengeance (Ezek 24:7, Ezek 24:8)
- The empty pot is set on the coals to glow so its impurity melts and its rust is consumed, yet the rust will not go out (Ezek 24:11, Ezek 24:12, Ezek 24:13)
- God takes the prophet's wife, 'the delight of your eyes', at a stroke and forbids him to weep or perform mourning rites, as a sign (Ezek 24:16, Ezek 24:17, Ezek 24:18)
- Mourning customs listed: removing the turban and sandals, covering the upper lip (mustache), eating the 'bread of men' (mourners' meal) (Ezek 24:17, Ezek 24:22, Ezek 24:23)
- The temple called 'the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes and the desire of your soul' (Ezek 24:21, Ezek 24:25)

**Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia**
- God gives Ammon and Moab to the 'sons of the east' who will pitch their encampments there; Rabbah becomes a pasture for camels (Ezek 25:4, Ezek 25:5, Ezek 25:10)
- Philistines acted with 'eternal enmity'; God will cut off the Cherethites (pun hikhratti et keretim) and the remnant of the seacoast (Ezek 25:15, Ezek 25:16, Ezek 25:17)

**Oracle on the fall of Tyre and the princes of the sea**
- Tyre gloats over Jerusalem: 'Aha, the gate of the peoples is broken; it has turned to me' (Ezek 26:2)
- God brings many nations against the city as the sea brings up its waves (Ezek 26:3)
- Tyre will be scraped to bare rock, a place for spreading fishing nets in the midst of the sea, never rebuilt (Ezek 26:4, Ezek 26:5, Ezek 26:14)
- Nebuchadrezzar, 'king of kings', comes from the north with horses, chariots and siege works (Ezek 26:7, Ezek 26:8, Ezek 26:9, Ezek 26:10, Ezek 26:11)
- The noise of the city's songs and the sound of its lyres will be heard no more (Ezek 26:13)
- Princes of the sea step down from their thrones, strip off embroidered robes, sit on the ground trembling and raise a lament (Ezek 26:15, Ezek 26:16, Ezek 26:17, Ezek 26:18)
- God brings up the deep (tehom) over the city and the great waters cover it (Ezek 26:19)

**Lament over Tyre the great merchant ship**
- Tyre portrayed as a magnificent ship of perfect beauty built from Senir cypress, Lebanon cedar mast, Bashan oak oars, ivory deck, Egyptian linen sail, crewed by Sidon, Arvad and Gebal (Ezek 27:4, Ezek 27:5, Ezek 27:6, Ezek 27:7, Ezek 27:8, Ezek 27:9)
- Long catalogue of nations trading with Tyre and their goods (Tarshish metals, Javan-Tubal-Meshech slaves and bronze, Togarmah horses, Dedan ivory and ebony, Sheba spices, Judah wheat and balm, Damascus Helbon wine) (Ezek 27:12, Ezek 27:13, Ezek 27:14, Ezek 27:15, Ezek 27:16, Ezek 27:17, Ezek 27:18, Ezek 27:19, Ezek 27:20, Ezek 27:21, Ezek 27:22, Ezek 27:23, Ezek 27:24, Ezek 27:25)
- Trade in 'souls of men' (slaves) among the goods of commerce (Ezek 27:13)
- The laden ship is shattered by the east wind in the heart of the seas and sinks with all its crew and cargo (Ezek 27:26, Ezek 27:27, Ezek 27:34)
- Sailors come ashore, cry bitterly, throw dust on their heads, roll in ashes, shave themselves bald and gird sackcloth (Ezek 27:28, Ezek 27:29, Ezek 27:30, Ezek 27:31)
- Lament question 'Who was like Tyre, like one silenced in the midst of the sea?' (Ezek 27:32)

**The prince of Tyre who said 'I am a god'**
- A ruler's heart is proud and he says 'I am a god (El); I sit in the seat of the gods in the heart of the seas', but he is a man and not a god (Ezek 28:2, Ezek 28:6, Ezek 28:9)
- The king of Tyre is 'wiser than Daniel (Dan'el); no secret is hidden from you' (Ezek 28:3)
- The proud ruler will 'die the death of the uncircumcised' at the hand of strangers (dishonorable death and burial) (Ezek 28:10)

**Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain**
- The king of Tyre is called 'the seal of perfection (hotem toknit), full of wisdom and perfect in beauty' (Ezek 28:12)
- A primal figure was in Eden, the garden of God, covered with every precious stone (sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, emerald) and gold settings prepared on the day of his creation (Ezek 28:13)
- 'You were an anointed guardian cherub; I placed you on the holy mountain of God' (Ezek 28:14, Ezek 28:16)
- The primal being walked among the 'stones of fire' on God's mountain (Ezek 28:14, Ezek 28:16)
- The being was blameless from the day he was created until iniquity was found in him (Ezek 28:15)
- God brings out a fire from within the sinner that consumes him and turns him to ashes on the ground (Ezek 28:18)

**Against Sidon; Israel gathered to dwell securely**
- There will no longer be a pricking brier or painful thorn for Israel from contemptuous neighbors (Ezek 28:24)
- Restored Israel will dwell securely, build houses and plant vineyards (Ezek 28:26)

**Pharaoh the great dragon of the Nile; Egypt as a reed; Egypt given as Nebuchadnezzar's wages**
- Pharaoh boasts 'My Nile is my own; I made it (or made myself)' (Ezek 29:3, Ezek 29:9)
- God puts hooks in the monster's jaws, makes the fish of its rivers stick to its scales and hauls it out of the water (Ezek 29:4)
- Nebuchadnezzar's army labored at Tyre till every head was bald and shoulder rubbed, without reward, so God gives him Egypt as wages (Ezek 29:18, Ezek 29:19, Ezek 29:20)
- On that day God will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel (Ezek 29:21)
- God gives the prophet 'an opening of the mouth' among the people (Ezek 29:21)

**The day of YHWH on Egypt; the cities of Egypt; Pharaoh's broken arms**
- On that day messengers go out from God in ships to terrify complacent Cush (Ezek 30:9)
- God destroys the idols and puts an end to the false gods of Memphis (Ezek 30:13)
- Catalogue of doomed Egyptian cities: Noph (Memphis), Pathros, Zoan, No (Thebes), Sin (Pelusium), Aven (On), Pi-beseth (Bubastis), Tehaphnehes (Ezek 30:13, Ezek 30:14, Ezek 30:15, Ezek 30:16, Ezek 30:17, Ezek 30:18)
- At Tehaphnehes the day grows dark when God breaks the yokes of Egypt; a cloud covers her (Ezek 30:18)
- God breaks Pharaoh's arm (unbandaged, unhealed) and both his arms, and strengthens the arms of the king of Babylon, putting his own sword in his hand (Ezek 30:21, Ezek 30:22, Ezek 30:24, Ezek 30:25)

**The great cedar of Eden felled and sent down to Sheol**
- Assyria/Pharaoh as a towering cedar of Lebanon nourished by the deep (tehom), its top among the clouds, all birds nesting and beasts bearing young under it, all nations in its shade (Ezek 31:3, Ezek 31:4, Ezek 31:5, Ezek 31:6, Ezek 31:7)
- No tree in the garden of God, Eden, equalled the great tree's beauty; all the trees of Eden envied it (Ezek 31:8, Ezek 31:9, Ezek 31:18)
- Because it grew proud of its height, foreigners cut the great tree down; its boughs fall on mountains and valleys and the peoples leave its shade (Ezek 31:10, Ezek 31:11, Ezek 31:12, Ezek 31:13, Ezek 31:14)
- When the tree goes down to Sheol God makes the deep mourn, holds back its rivers and darkens Lebanon (Ezek 31:15)
- The trees of Eden already in the netherworld are comforted when the great tree descends to join them (Ezek 31:16, Ezek 31:17)

**Dirge over Pharaoh the sea dragon caught in God's net**
- Pharaoh likened to a young lion of the nations yet a dragon (tannin) in the seas, thrashing in his rivers and muddying the waters with his feet (Ezek 32:2)
- God spreads his net over the sea monster with a company of many peoples and hauls it up in his dragnet (Ezek 32:3)
- The slain monster's flesh is spread on the mountains, its carrion fills the valleys and its blood waters the land up to the mountains (Ezek 32:5, Ezek 32:6)
- When the monster is extinguished God covers the heavens, darkens the stars, covers the sun with cloud and the moon gives no light (Ezek 32:7, Ezek 32:8)
- God makes the waters settle clear and the rivers run like oil (Ezek 32:13, Ezek 32:14)

**Egypt's descent to the Pit among the uncircumcised nations**
- The mightiest heroes (elei gibborim) speak to the newcomer from the midst of Sheol (Ezek 32:21)
- Tour of the netherworld: Assyria, Elam, Meshech-Tubal, Edom, the princes of the north and the Sidonians lie with their hordes around their graves in the recesses of the Pit (Ezek 32:22, Ezek 32:24, Ezek 32:26, Ezek 32:29, Ezek 32:30)
- Graves set in the farthest recesses (yarketei) of the Pit (Ezek 32:23)
- Refrain: those who spread terror in the land of the living now bear their shame with those who go down to the Pit (Ezek 32:23, Ezek 32:24, Ezek 32:25, Ezek 32:26, Ezek 32:27, Ezek 32:30, Ezek 32:32)
- The fallen mighty ones of old went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, swords laid under their heads (Ezek 32:27)
- Pharaoh will see the other slain kings in Sheol and be consoled for his horde (Ezek 32:31)

**The watchman; turn and live; the fugitive's news; Abraham was one; the prophet as love-singer**
- The watchman who sees the sword coming blows the shofar to warn the people; whoever ignores it, his blood is on his own head (Ezek 33:2, Ezek 33:3, Ezek 33:4, Ezek 33:5, Ezek 33:6)
- Exiles despair: 'Our transgressions are upon us and we rot away in them; how then shall we live?' (Ezek 33:10)
- Call 'Turn back, turn back from your evil ways; why will you die, O house of Israel?' (Ezek 33:11)
- A fugitive arrives in exile announcing 'the city has been struck', and the prophet's mouth is opened (Ezek 33:21, Ezek 33:22)
- Survivors in the ruins argue 'Abraham was only one and inherited the land; we are many, so the land is given to us' (Ezek 33:24)
- People come to hear the prophet as one hears a lovely singer of love songs with a fine instrument, but do not do his words (Ezek 33:30, Ezek 33:31, Ezek 33:32)
- When the word comes true, 'they shall know that a prophet has been among them' (Ezek 33:33)

**The bad shepherds; God the shepherd; one shepherd David; the covenant of peace**
- Woe to the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves, eat the fat, wear the wool, slaughter the fatlings and do not tend the flock (Ezek 34:2, Ezek 34:3, Ezek 34:8, Ezek 34:10)
- The shepherd's neglected duties: strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind up the injured, bring back the strayed, seek the lost (Ezek 34:4, Ezek 34:16)
- Without a shepherd the flock is scattered over every mountain and hill and becomes food for wild beasts, with no one to search for them (Ezek 34:5, Ezek 34:6, Ezek 34:8)
- God declares 'I myself will search for my sheep and seek them out' and shepherd them on the mountains of Israel (Ezek 34:11, Ezek 34:12, Ezek 34:13, Ezek 34:14, Ezek 34:15, Ezek 34:16)
- God judges between sheep and sheep, fat and lean, rams and goats who trample the pasture, foul the water and butt the weak with their horns (Ezek 34:17, Ezek 34:18, Ezek 34:19, Ezek 34:20, Ezek 34:21, Ezek 34:22)
- God raises up for them 'a plantation of renown' (matta' leshem) so they are no longer consumed by famine (Ezek 34:29)
- 'You are my flock, the flock of my pasture; you are men (adam), and I am your God' (Ezek 34:31)

**Against Mount Seir**
- Mount Seir (Edom) is condemned for its 'eternal enmity', delivering Israel to the sword at the time of their calamity (Ezek 35:2, Ezek 35:3, Ezek 35:5)
- 'Since you did not hate blood, blood shall pursue you' (Ezek 35:6)
- Edom says 'these two nations and two lands will be mine' although YHWH was there (Ezek 35:10)
- As the nation rejoiced over Israel's desolate inheritance, so God will make it desolate (measure for measure) (Ezek 35:11, Ezek 35:14, Ezek 35:15)

**Prophecy to the mountains of Israel - restoration after the nations' mockery**
- The mountains of Israel, mocked by the nations, will again put forth branches and bear fruit for God's returning people, and be tilled and sown (Ezek 36:8, Ezek 36:9, Ezek 36:10)
- The land that was said to devour men and bereave its nations will devour and bereave no more (Ezek 36:12, Ezek 36:13, Ezek 36:14, Ezek 36:15)

**For my holy name - clean water, new heart, my spirit within; the land like Eden**
- Israel's conduct defiled the land 'like the uncleanness of a menstruous woman' (Ezek 36:17)
- The exiles profane God's holy name among the nations, who say 'These are YHWH's people, yet they had to leave his land' (Ezek 36:20, Ezek 36:21)
- God declares 'Not for your sake do I act, O house of Israel, but for my holy name which you profaned' (Ezek 36:22, Ezek 36:32)
- God will sprinkle clean water upon them and purify them from all their uncleanness and idols (Ezek 36:25)
- Onlookers say 'This desolate land has become like the garden of Eden' (Ezek 36:35)
- God will multiply the people like flocks of men, like the holy flocks of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts (Ezek 36:37, Ezek 36:38)

**The valley of dry bones**
- The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them (Ezek 37:1, Ezek 37:2)
- The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live (Ezek 37:9, Ezek 37:10)
- The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off' (Ezek 37:11)
- God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel (Ezek 37:12, Ezek 37:13)

**The two sticks joined - one kingdom under David, an everlasting covenant and sanctuary**
- Prophet writes 'For Judah' and 'For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim' on two sticks and joins them into one in his hand: the reunited kingdom (Ezek 37:16, Ezek 37:17, Ezek 37:19, Ezek 37:20)
- Israel will be one nation with one king, never again divided into two kingdoms (Ezek 37:22)
- 'David my servant shall be their prince (nasi) forever' (Ezek 37:25)
- God sets his sanctuary in their midst forever and his dwelling (mishkan) is over them (Ezek 37:26, Ezek 37:27, Ezek 37:28)

**Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth**
- God turns the invader around and puts hooks in his jaws to drag him out with all his army (Ezek 38:4)
- Gog's coalition: Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer with all its hordes, Beth-togarmah from the far north, many peoples (Ezek 38:5, Ezek 38:6)
- Gog is summoned 'after many days', 'in the latter years / end of days', against a land restored from the sword (Ezek 38:8, Ezek 38:16)
- The invading host comes up like a storm, like a cloud covering the land (Ezek 38:9, Ezek 38:16)
- The invader plots to attack a quiet people dwelling securely in unwalled villages without bars or gates, to seize plunder (Ezek 38:10, Ezek 38:11, Ezek 38:12)
- Restored Israel dwells 'on the navel of the earth' (tabbur ha-arets) (Ezek 38:12)
- Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask the invader 'Have you come to take plunder?' (Ezek 38:13)
- God asks 'Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants the prophets?' (Ezek 38:17)
- Every man's sword is turned against his brother in the enemy host (Ezek 38:21)
- God judges Gog with pestilence, blood, torrential rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur (Ezek 38:22)

**Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds**
- God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand (Ezek 39:3)
- God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands (Ezek 39:6)
- Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest (Ezek 39:9, Ezek 39:10)
- Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them (Ezek 39:10)
- Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah (Ezek 39:11, Ezek 39:15, Ezek 39:16)
- All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers (Ezek 39:12, Ezek 39:13, Ezek 39:14, Ezek 39:15, Ezek 39:16)
- God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood (Ezek 39:17, Ezek 39:18, Ezek 39:19)
- The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war (Ezek 39:20)
- The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak (Ezek 39:23, Ezek 39:24)
- God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel (Ezek 39:29)

**The new temple vision begins - the man of bronze with the measuring reed on a very high mountain**
- The temple vision is dated 'in the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year (rosh ha-shanah), on the tenth of the month, the fourteenth year after the city fell, on that very day' (Ezek 40:1)
- In visions of God the prophet is set on a very high mountain on which there is something like a city structure to the south (Ezek 40:2)
- A man whose appearance is like bronze stands in the gate with a linen cord and a measuring reed, guiding the visionary (Ezek 40:3)
- Visionary told: 'look with your eyes, hear with your ears, set your heart on all I show you, and declare it all to the house of Israel' (Ezek 40:4)

**Measuring the gates and courts of the visionary temple**
- The measuring reed is six cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth (the long cubit) (Ezek 40:5)
- The visionary temple is measured part by part: wall, three-sided gatehouses with three guard chambers each, porches, jambs, windows and palm ornaments (Ezek 40:5, Ezek 40:6, Ezek 40:7, Ezek 40:8, Ezek 40:9, Ezek 40:10, Ezek 40:11, Ezek 40:12, Ezek 40:13, Ezek 40:14, Ezek 40:15, Ezek 40:16)
- Thirty chambers stand on the stone pavement around the outer court (Ezek 40:17, Ezek 40:18)
- Three identical gatehouses (east, north, south), 50 by 25 cubits, with seven steps to the outer court and eight to the inner (Ezek 40:20, Ezek 40:21, Ezek 40:22, Ezek 40:24, Ezek 40:25, Ezek 40:26, Ezek 40:28, Ezek 40:29, Ezek 40:30, Ezek 40:31, Ezek 40:32, Ezek 40:33, Ezek 40:34, Ezek 40:35, Ezek 40:36, Ezek 40:37)

**Slaughtering tables, the priests' chambers, the Zadokites, the inner court and the porch**
- Eight tables at the inner gate for slaughtering burnt, sin and guilt offerings, and four hewn-stone tables for the implements, with hooks a handbreadth long (Ezek 40:38, Ezek 40:39, Ezek 40:40, Ezek 40:41, Ezek 40:42, Ezek 40:43)
- Chambers in the inner court for the (singers/)priests who keep the charge of the house and those who keep the charge of the altar (Ezek 40:44, Ezek 40:45, Ezek 40:46)
- Only the sons of Zadok among the Levites may come near to YHWH to minister at the altar (Ezek 40:46)
- The porch of the house is reached by steps and has pillars beside its jambs, one on each side (Ezek 40:48, Ezek 40:49)

**Ezekiel's visionary temple, the house and its carvings**
- Temple ringed by side chambers (tsela'ot) in three stories, thirty-three rooms, widening upward (Ezek 41:6-7)
- Temple walls carved with alternating palm trees and cherubim having a human face and a lion face (Ezek 41:18-20, Ezek 41:25)
- A wooden altar is explained as 'the table that is before YHWH' (Ezek 41:22)

**The priests' chambers and the outer measurement**
- The sacred precinct is a perfect square of 500 by 500, walled to separate holy from profane (Ezek 42:16-20)

**The glory of God returns to the temple**
- The divine glory returns to the temple from the east through the east gate (Ezek 43:2, Ezek 43:4)
- God's voice (or the sound of his coming) is like the sound of many waters (Ezek 43:2)
- The temple is called the place of God's throne and the soles of his feet, where he will dwell forever (Ezek 43:7)
- Kings' corpses or memorials (pigre malkehem) beside the temple defile God's holy name (Ezek 43:7-9)
- The prophet is to describe the temple's plan so that Israel will be ashamed of its sins (Ezek 43:10-11)
- The temple stands on the top of a (very high) mountain whose whole territory is most holy (Ezek 43:12)

**The altar and its seven-day consecration**
- The altar rises in diminishing ledges from a 'bosom of the earth' base, with steps facing east (Ezek 43:13-17)
- The altar's top hearth is called har'el/ari'el ('mountain of God' or 'lion of God') (Ezek 43:15-16)
- The altar is purged and consecrated by sacrifices over seven days before regular worship begins on the eighth (Ezek 43:25-27)

**The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests**
- The east gate stays shut forever because YHWH the God of Israel entered by it (Ezek 44:1-2)
- Only the prince (nasi) may sit in the shut gate to eat bread before YHWH (Ezek 44:3)
- Levites who went astray after idols are demoted to gatekeepers and slaughterers, barred from priestly service (Ezek 44:10-14)
- Priests serve in linen only, with no wool, and must not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat (Ezek 44:17-18)
- Priests may neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long, but must trim it (Ezek 44:20)
- Priests stand as judges in disputes, judging by God's ordinances (Ezek 44:24)
- The first of the dough (reshit arisot) is given to the priest so that blessing rests on the house (Ezek 44:30)

**The sacred allotment, the prince's duties, measures and feasts**
- Weights and measures are fixed by decree (ephah, bath, homer, shekel of twenty gerahs, mina) (Ezek 45:11-14)
- The ruler (prince) provides the offerings for the feasts, new moons and sabbaths on behalf of the people (Ezek 45:16-17, Ezek 45:22)
- On the first day of the first month the sanctuary is purged with blood on the doorposts and altar (Ezek 45:18-19)
- Rite of atonement for anyone who sins inadvertently or through simplicity (Ezek 45:20)

**The prince's worship, gate rules, land gifts and temple kitchens**
- The inner east gate is shut on the six working days and opened on the sabbath and the new moon (Ezek 46:1-3)
- Worshippers who enter by the north gate must leave by the south gate, and vice versa, not returning the way they came (Ezek 46:9)
- A prince's gift of land to a servant reverts to him in the year of liberty (deror) (Ezek 46:16-17)
- Kitchens in the corners of the temple courts where the sacrifices are boiled (Ezek 46:19-24)

**The river from the temple and the healing of the sea**
- The temple river heals the salt waters of the Dead Sea so they teem with fish (Ezek 47:8-9)
- Fishermen spread nets from En-gedi to En-eglaim on the healed sea (Ezek 47:10)
- The swamps and marshes are left unhealed, given over to salt (Ezek 47:11)
- Trees along the river bear fruit every month and their leaves are for healing (Ezek 47:12)

**Borders and tribal allotment of the land; the city 'YHWH is there'**
- Joseph receives two portions in the allotment of the land (Ezek 47:13)
- Resident aliens with children born in the land receive an inheritance among the tribes like citizens (Ezek 47:22-23)
- The twelve tribes receive equal parallel east-west strips of land, seven north and five south of the sacred portion (Ezek 48:1-7, Ezek 48:23-28)
- The holy city has twelve gates, three on each side, named after the twelve tribes (Ezek 48:31-34)
- The city's new name is 'YHWH is there' (YHWH shammah) (Ezek 48:35)

**Daniel and his companions at Nebuchadnezzar's court refuse the king's food**
- The conqueror carries the vessels of God's temple into the treasury of his own god (Dan 1:2)
- Flawless, handsome, learned youths of royal or noble blood are taken to be trained in the conqueror's court and language (Dan 1:3-5)
- Pious exiles refuse the king's food and wine so as not to defile themselves (Dan 1:8)
- God grants the hero favor and compassion in the eyes of the foreign official in charge of him (Dan 1:9)
- A ten-day test on vegetables and water leaves the pious youths healthier than those who eat the king's food (Dan 1:12-16)
- The exiled youths are found ten times wiser than all the court magicians and enchanters (Dan 1:20)

**Nebuchadnezzar demands his dream be told; the mystery revealed to Daniel**
- The king demands that his experts tell him the dream itself as well as its meaning, on pain of death (Dan 2:3, Dan 2:5-9)
- The magicians say only the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh, could reveal such a thing (Dan 2:11)
- The enraged king orders all the wise men of the capital killed (Dan 2:12-13)
- A hidden mystery (raz) is revealed to the seer in a night vision (Dan 2:18-19)
- God knows what is in darkness and light dwells with him (Dan 2:22)

**The statue of four metals and the stone cut without hands**
- There is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries (gale razin) and makes known what will be at the end of days (Dan 2:28-29)
- Dream of a great statue with head of gold, chest of silver, belly of bronze, legs of iron and feet of iron mixed with clay (Dan 2:31-33)
- A stone cut out without hands strikes the statue and becomes a great mountain filling the earth (Dan 2:34-35, Dan 2:45)
- Destroyed kingdoms become like chaff from the summer threshing floors carried away by the wind (Dan 2:35)
- Successive kingdoms or ages symbolized by declining metals (gold, silver, bronze, iron) (Dan 2:38-43)
- Iron mixed with clay signifies kingdoms mingling by intermarriage ('the seed of men') yet not holding together (Dan 2:41-43)
- The pagan king falls on his face before the Jewish seer and orders offerings and incense for him (Dan 2:46)
- A foreign king confesses Israel's God as 'God of gods and Lord of kings, revealer of mysteries' (Dan 2:47)

**The golden image and the fiery furnace**
- The king sets up a golden image sixty cubits high and six wide on the plain of Dura (Dan 3:1)
- Long repeated list of imperial officials (satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates) (Dan 3:2-3, Dan 3:27)
- A listed orchestra of instruments (horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, symphonia) signals the moment to bow to the idol (Dan 3:5, Dan 3:7, Dan 3:10, Dan 3:15)
- All are commanded to bow to the king's image on pain of being thrown into a blazing furnace (Dan 3:6, Dan 3:11, Dan 3:15)
- Envious courtiers 'eat the pieces' (slander) of the Jews and denounce their non-compliance to the king (Dan 3:8-12)
- The faithful declare that God can save them, but even if he does not, they will not serve the king's gods (Dan 3:16-18)
- The furnace is heated seven times more than usual (Dan 3:19)
- The flames kill the men who throw the heroes into the furnace (Dan 3:22)
- A fourth figure appears walking in the fire, looking like a son of the gods (bar elahin) (Dan 3:25)
- The rescued have not a hair singed, their garments unchanged, and no smell of fire on them (Dan 3:27)
- God sends his angel to rescue his servants from death (Dan 3:28)
- The pagan king decrees that anyone who blasphemes or fails to fear the Jewish God will be punished (Dan 3:29)

**Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness**
- Dream of an immense tree whose top reaches heaven, visible to the ends of the earth, sheltering beasts and birds (Dan 4:7-9, Dan 4:17-19)
- A 'watcher' ('ir), a holy one, descends from heaven and decrees the judgment (Dan 4:10, Dan 4:20)
- The felled tree's stump is left in the earth bound with a band of iron and bronze (Dan 4:12, Dan 4:20, Dan 4:23)
- 'Seven times' (periods) pass over the punished king (Dan 4:13, Dan 4:20, Dan 4:22, Dan 4:29)
- The sentence is 'by the decree of the watchers and the word of the holy ones' (Dan 4:14)
- The seer is dismayed and terrified when he grasps the meaning of the dream (Dan 4:16)
- The king boasts 'Is not this great Babylon which I have built by my might?' (Dan 4:27)
- While the words are still in his mouth a voice falls from heaven pronouncing the king's sentence (Dan 4:28)
- The king's reason returns when he lifts his eyes to heaven and he is restored to his throne after praising God (Dan 4:31, Dan 4:33)
- No one can stay God's hand or say to him 'What are you doing?' (Dan 4:32)

**Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall**
- A king holds a great feast for a thousand nobles and drinks wine before them (Dan 5:1)
- The king and his concubines drink from the vessels taken from God's temple while praising idols (Dan 5:2-3, Dan 5:23)
- Idols listed as gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone that neither see nor hear nor know (Dan 5:4, Dan 5:23)
- Fingers of a human hand appear and write on the plaster of the palace wall opposite the lampstand (Dan 5:5, Dan 5:24)
- The king's face blanches, his hip-joints loosen and his knees knock together in terror (Dan 5:6, Dan 5:9)
- Reward offered to the interpreter: purple robe, gold chain and rule as third in the kingdom (Dan 5:7, Dan 5:16, Dan 5:29)
- The queen (mother) reminds the king of a forgotten sage who solved riddles in his father's day (Dan 5:10-12)
- The sage is renowned for interpreting dreams, explaining riddles and 'loosing knots' (Dan 5:12, Dan 5:16)
- The prophet tells the king to keep his gifts for himself (Dan 5:17)
- The writing 'Mene, mene, tekel, u-pharsin' is read as numbered, weighed and divided (Dan 5:25-28)
- That very night the king is killed and his kingdom passes to another people (Dan 5:30)

**Daniel in the lions' den**
- Darius the Mede receives the kingdom at age sixty-two (Dan 6:1)
- The king appoints 120 satraps over the kingdom with three presidents above them, one of them the hero (Dan 6:2-4)
- Rivals can find no fault in the hero except in the matter of the law of his God (Dan 6:5-6)
- For thirty days no one may petition any god or man except the king (Dan 6:8, Dan 6:13)
- A royal decree written by the law of the Medes and Persians cannot be revoked, even by the king (Dan 6:9, Dan 6:13, Dan 6:16)
- The faithful prays facing Jerusalem through open windows (Dan 6:11)
- The pious kneels on his knees to pray (Dan 6:11)
- The hero is thrown into a pit of lions (Dan 6:17)
- A stone is placed on the mouth of the pit and sealed with the king's signet and those of his nobles (Dan 6:18)
- The king spends a sleepless night fasting, without entertainment, worrying over the hero (Dan 6:19)
- God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths so they do not harm the innocent (Dan 6:23)
- The accusers, with their wives and children, are thrown to the lions and crushed before they reach the bottom (Dan 6:25)

**The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man**
- The four winds of heaven stir up the great sea, out of which monstrous beasts arise (Dan 7:2)
- Four great beasts rise from the sea, each different, symbolizing successive kingdoms (Dan 7:3, Dan 7:17)
- A lion with eagle's wings has its wings plucked, is made to stand like a man and given a human heart (Dan 7:4)
- A bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth is told 'Arise, devour much flesh' (Dan 7:5)
- A leopard with four wings and four heads is given dominion (Dan 7:6)
- A terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth and ten horns devours and tramples the rest with its feet (Dan 7:7, Dan 7:19, Dan 7:23-24)
- A little horn with human eyes and a mouth speaking great things uproots three horns (Dan 7:8, Dan 7:11, Dan 7:20)
- Thrones are set and the Ancient of Days sits, his garment white as snow and his hair like pure wool (Dan 7:9, Dan 7:13, Dan 7:22)
- God's throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire (Dan 7:9)
- A river of fire flows out from before the divine throne (Dan 7:10)
- Thousands of thousands serve God and myriads of myriads stand before him (Dan 7:10)
- The arch-enemy beast is slain and its body given over to burning fire (Dan 7:11)
- A heavenly figure or the holy ones are given everlasting dominion, glory and kingdom which all peoples serve (Dan 7:14, Dan 7:27)
- The seer asks one of the attendants or an angel, who explains the vision to him (Dan 7:16)
- The holy ones of the Most High (qaddishe 'elyonin) receive and possess the kingdom forever (Dan 7:18, Dan 7:22, Dan 7:27)
- The horn makes war against the holy ones and prevails until the Ancient of Days comes (Dan 7:21, Dan 7:25)
- The tyrant plans to change the times (festivals) and the law (Dan 7:25)
- The seer is troubled, his face changes, and he keeps the matter in his heart (Dan 7:15, Dan 7:28)

**The ram, the he-goat and the little horn; Gabriel explains**
- The seer finds himself in a vision at Susa the citadel by the river Ulai (Dan 8:2, Dan 8:16)
- A two-horned ram (Media-Persia) is trampled by a he-goat with one great horn (Greece) coming from the west without touching the ground (Dan 8:3-7, Dan 8:20-21)
- A small horn grows up to the host of heaven, casts down some of the stars and tramples them (Dan 8:9-10)
- The tyrant magnifies himself against the Prince of the host / Prince of princes (Dan 8:11, Dan 8:25)
- Desolation reckoned as 2,300 evenings and mornings before the sanctuary is restored (Dan 8:14, Dan 8:26)
- The vision concerns the time of the end (et qets) (Dan 8:17, Dan 8:19)
- A king 'fierce of face' and understanding riddles arises, destroys the holy people, and is broken without human hand (Dan 8:23-25)
- The seer is exhausted and sick for days after the vision (Dan 8:27)

**Daniel's penitential prayer and the seventy weeks**
- The seer studies the books (sefarim) to understand a prophecy (Dan 9:2)
- Communal confession: 'To you, Lord, belongs righteousness and to us shame of face' (Dan 9:7-8)
- The curse and oath written in the Torah of Moses has been poured out on the people (Dan 9:11-13)
- We present our pleas not because of our righteous deeds but because of your great mercy (Dan 9:18)
- The angel arrives in swift flight at the time of the evening offering, while the seer is still praying (Dan 9:21)
- Seventy 'weeks' (seventy sevens) decreed to finish transgression, atone iniquity, bring everlasting righteousness and anoint a most holy (Dan 9:24-27)
- An anointed one (mashiah) is cut off and has nothing (Dan 9:26)

**The vision by the Tigris and the angelic princes of the nations**
- The seer mourns three weeks, eating no delicacies, meat or wine and not anointing himself (Dan 10:2-3)
- The seer receives a vision standing by the great river Tigris (Hiddeqel) (Dan 10:4)
- A man clothed in linen with a gold belt, body like chrysolite, face like lightning, eyes like torches, limbs like burnished bronze (Dan 10:5-6)
- The seer's companions do not see the vision but are seized with terror and flee (Dan 10:7)
- The angel was opposed twenty-one days by the 'prince of the kingdom of Persia' until Michael came to help (Dan 10:12-13)
- Nations have heavenly 'princes' (patron angels): the prince of Persia, prince of Greece, and Michael 'your prince' (Dan 10:13, Dan 10:20-21)
- A figure in human likeness touches the seer's lips so he can speak (Dan 10:16)
- What is inscribed in the 'book of truth' is revealed (Dan 10:21)

**The wars of the kings of the north and south and the arrogant king**
- Detailed veiled prophecy of wars between the 'king of the north' and the 'king of the south' (Dan 11:5-15, Dan 11:25-29, Dan 11:40)
- A king's daughter given in marriage to seal an alliance between rival kings, but the alliance fails (Dan 11:6, Dan 11:17)
- A victorious king carries off the enemy's gods, molten images and precious vessels to Egypt (Dan 11:8)
- Ships of Kittim come against the king of the north and turn him back (Dan 11:30)
- The wise (maskilim) instruct the many and some fall to sword, flame and captivity to refine and purify them (Dan 11:33-35)
- The king exalts himself above every god, speaks monstrous things against the God of gods, and honors a 'god of fortresses' (Dan 11:36-39)
- The tyrant disregards the gods of his fathers and 'the one desired by women' (Dan 11:37)
- The final tyrant pitches his palace tents between the seas and the holy mountain and comes to his end with none to help (Dan 11:45)

**Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book**
- A time of trouble such as never was since nations existed (Dan 12:1)
- The wise shine like the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars forever (Dan 12:3)
- Many shall run to and fro and knowledge shall increase (Dan 12:4)
- Two figures stand on either bank of the river, with a linen-clad figure above the waters (Dan 12:5-6)
- Secret reckonings: 1,290 days from the abolition of the daily offering, and blessed is he who waits for 1,335 days (Dan 12:11-12)
- The seer is told he will rest and rise to his allotted portion at the end of days (Dan 12:13)

**Hosea marries Gomer; the children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi**
- God commands the prophet to marry a 'woman of harlotry' as a sign of the land's unfaithfulness (Hos 1:2-3)
- The prophet's children receive symbolic names announcing judgment or salvation (Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi) (Hos 1:4, Hos 1:6, Hos 1:9)
- God will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu (Hos 1:4-5)

**The unfaithful wife and the new betrothal**
- The unfaithful wife is threatened with being stripped naked as on the day she was born (Hos 2:5, Hos 2:12)
- God hedges her way with thorns and a wall so she cannot find her lovers' paths (Hos 2:8)
- The straying wife resolves 'I will go back to my first husband, for it was better then' (Hos 2:9)
- God will end the land's festivals, new moons and sabbaths (Hos 2:13)
- God will allure his people into the wilderness and speak to her heart, as in the days of youth (Hos 2:16-17)
- The Valley of Achor ('trouble') becomes a door of hope (Hos 2:17)
- She will call God 'my husband (ishi)' and no longer 'my baal'; the names of the Baals removed from her mouth (Hos 2:18-19)
- God betroths his people to himself forever in righteousness, justice, steadfast love, mercy and faithfulness (Hos 2:21-22)
- Chain of responses: God answers the heavens, the heavens the earth, the earth grain-wine-oil, and they answer Jezreel (Hos 2:23-24)

**Hosea buys back an adulterous woman**
- Lovers of raisin cakes (ashishe anavim), offerings associated with other gods (Hos 3:1)
- The prophet buys back a woman for fifteen shekels and a homer and a half of barley (Hos 3:2)
- Israel will dwell many days without king, prince, sacrifice, pillar, ephod or teraphim (Hos 3:3-4)

**YHWH's lawsuit; priests, divination and cultic harlotry**
- Prophet lists violations echoing the Decalogue: swearing, lying, murder, theft, adultery (Hos 4:2)
- My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; the priest who rejected knowledge is rejected (Hos 4:6)
- 'Like people, like priest': both punished alike (Hos 4:9)
- Men sacrifice with qedeshot (cult women) and go aside with harlots (Hos 4:14)
- Israel is like a stubborn heifer (Hos 4:16)

**Judgment on priests and kings; 'on the third day he will raise us'**
- The leaders have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread on Tabor (Hos 5:1)
- God is like a moth (or pus) to Ephraim and like rot to Judah (Hos 5:12)
- Ephraim sees its sickness and goes to the great king of Assyria, who cannot heal it (Hos 5:13)
- God returns to his place until the people acknowledge guilt and seek his face (Hos 5:15)
- 'After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up' (Hos 6:1-2)
- The people's love is like a morning cloud and the dew that vanishes early (Hos 6:4)
- 'I desire steadfast love (hesed) and not sacrifice, knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings' (Hos 6:6)
- 'Like Adam they transgressed the covenant' (Hos 6:7)
- A band of priests murders on the road to Shechem (Hos 6:9)

**The heated oven, the silly dove and the calf of Samaria**
- Court conspirators are like a heated oven; they devour their judges and their kings fall (Hos 7:4-7)
- Ephraim is a cake not turned (half-baked) (Hos 7:8)
- Grey hairs are sprinkled on him and he does not know it (Hos 7:9)
- Ephraim is like a silly dove, calling to Egypt and going to Assyria (Hos 7:11)
- God spreads his net over the people and brings them down like birds of the sky (Hos 7:12)
- The people are like a deceitful (slack) bow (Hos 7:16)
- They made kings, but not by me; princes, but I did not know it (Hos 8:4)
- The calf of Samaria, made by a craftsman, is no god and will be broken to pieces (Hos 8:5-6)
- They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind (Hos 8:7)
- Ephraim like a wild ass wandering alone, hiring lovers (Hos 8:9)
- Though God writes for him the many things of his Torah, they are counted as something strange (Hos 8:12)

**No rejoicing for Israel; exile, the mad prophet, Baal-peor**
- Israel loves a harlot's hire on every threshing floor of grain (Hos 9:1)
- In exile (Assyria) they will eat unclean food (Hos 9:3)
- Their sacrifices are like the bread of mourners: all who eat it are defiled (Hos 9:4)
- Egypt gathers them and Memphis (Moph) buries them; thorns in their tents (Hos 9:6)
- 'The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad' (Hos 9:7)
- God found Israel like grapes in the wilderness, like the first fig (Hos 9:10)
- The apostasy at Baal-peor (Hos 9:10)
- Prayer/curse: 'Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts' (Hos 9:11-16)

**The luxuriant vine, the calves of Beth-aven, sow righteousness**
- Israel a luxuriant vine: the more fruit, the more altars and pillars (Hos 10:1-2)
- The idol-priests (kemarim) mourn as the calf is carried off as tribute to Assyria (Hos 10:5-6)
- Thorns and thistles grow up on their altars (Hos 10:8)
- Ephraim a trained heifer that loves to thresh, now yoked to plow (Hos 10:11)
- Sow for yourselves righteousness, reap steadfast love, break up your fallow ground (Hos 10:12-13)

**'Out of Egypt I called my son'; God's compassion overturns his anger**
- 'When Israel was a child I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' (Hos 11:1)
- God taught Ephraim to walk, took them in his arms and drew them with cords of love (Hos 11:3-4)
- God's heart turns over within him: 'How can I give you up? I am God and not man' (Hos 11:8-9)
- Admah and Zeboiim, destroyed with Sodom, cited as the fate God refuses to inflict (Hos 11:8)
- God roars like a lion and his children come trembling back from the west, Egypt and Assyria like birds and doves (Hos 11:10-11)

**Jacob's story as indictment; Canaan's false scales**
- Oil carried to Egypt as tribute while a covenant is made with Assyria (Hos 12:2)
- Jacob strove with the angel, prevailed, wept and sought his favor; found God at Bethel (Hos 12:5)
- God will make Israel dwell in tents again, as in the days of the appointed feast (Hos 12:10)
- God has spoken through the prophets, multiplied visions and given parables by them (Hos 12:11)
- By a prophet God brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet it was guarded (Hos 12:14)

**Ephraim's idols, God as predator, 'O Death, where are your plagues?'**
- 'Those who sacrifice men kiss calves' (Hos 13:2)
- The wicked vanish like the morning cloud, dew, chaff whirled from the threshing floor, and smoke from a window (Hos 13:3)
- God attacks like a bear robbed of her cubs (Hos 13:8)
- God gives a king in his anger and takes him away in his wrath (Hos 13:10-11)
- Ephraim's iniquity is bound up and his sin stored away (Hos 13:12)
- Birth pangs come but he is an unwise son who does not present himself at the opening of the womb (Hos 13:13)
- 'Shall I ransom them from Sheol? O Death, where are your plagues? O Sheol, where is your sting?' (Hos 13:14)
- An east wind, the wind of YHWH, comes from the desert and dries up his spring (Hos 13:15)

**'Return, O Israel'; God as dew and evergreen**
- Take words with you and return; we will pay the bulls (fruit) of our lips (Hos 14:3)
- Penitent renounces reliance on Assyria and horses and calling handiwork 'our gods' (Hos 14:4)
- God will be like dew to Israel (Hos 14:6)
- Restored Israel blossoms like a lily, roots like Lebanon, beauty like the olive, fragrance like Lebanon (Hos 14:6-8)
- God compares himself to an evergreen cypress from whom Israel's fruit comes (Hos 14:9)
- Wisdom colophon: 'Whoever is wise, let him understand; the ways of YHWH are right' (Hos 14:10)

**The locust plague and the call to lament**
- Tell this to your children, and they to theirs, and theirs to the next generation (Joel 1:2-3)
- Successive kinds of locust (gazam, arbeh, yeleq, hasil) each eat what the previous one left (Joel 1:4)
- Invading horde (locusts) has the teeth of a lion and fangs of a lioness (Joel 1:6)
- Lament like a virgin in sackcloth for the husband of her youth (Joel 1:8)
- Grain offering and libation are cut off from God's house and the priests mourn (Joel 1:9, Joel 1:13)
- Even the beasts of the field long for / cry out to God in the drought (Joel 1:18, Joel 1:20)

**The locust army of the Day of YHWH; 'rend your hearts'; restoration**
- Blow the shofar in Zion, sound the alarm on God's holy mountain (Joel 2:1, Joel 2:15)
- The land is like the Garden of Eden before the invader and a desolate wilderness after (Joel 2:3)
- The locusts look like horses and run like cavalry, leaping on mountaintops with a noise like chariots (Joel 2:4-8)
- The invaders climb walls and enter houses through windows like a thief (Joel 2:9)
- 'Rend your hearts and not your garments' (Joel 2:12-13)
- 'Who knows? He may turn and relent' (mi yodea) (Joel 2:14)
- Even bridegroom and bride must leave the wedding chamber for the public fast (Joel 2:16)
- Priests weep between the porch and the altar (Joel 2:17)
- The northern one (ha-tsefoni) is driven into the desert and seas, and its stench rises (Joel 2:20)
- God sends the early and latter rain (moreh and malqosh) and restores abundance (Joel 2:23-24)
- God will repay the years the locust has eaten (Joel 2:25-26)

**The spirit poured on all flesh and signs before the Day**
- God pours out his spirit on all flesh: sons and daughters prophesy, old men dream dreams, young men see visions (Joel 3:1)
- The spirit is poured out even on male and female slaves (Joel 3:2)
- Portents in heaven and earth: blood, fire and columns of smoke (Joel 3:3)
- The sun turns to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrible Day (Joel 3:4)
- Everyone who calls on the name of YHWH will be delivered (Joel 3:5)
- On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be survivors (peletah) whom God calls (Joel 3:5)

**Judgment of the nations in the Valley of Jehoshaphat; the fountain from the temple**
- God gathers all nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat ('YHWH judges') to judge them (Joel 4:2, Joel 4:12)
- The nations cast lots for God's people, trading a boy for a harlot and a girl for wine (Joel 4:3)
- Tyre, Sidon and Philistia sold Judeans to the Ionians (Greeks) (Joel 4:6)
- Measure for measure: the slave-traders' children will be sold to the Sabeans (Joel 4:4, Joel 4:7-8)
- Beat your plowshares into swords and pruning hooks into spears (call to war) (Joel 4:9-10)
- Put in the sickle, the harvest is ripe; the winepress is full and the vats overflow with wickedness (Joel 4:13)
- Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision (emeq he-harus) (Joel 4:14)
- Jerusalem will be holy and strangers will pass through it no more (Joel 4:17)
- A spring issues from the house of YHWH and waters the Wadi of Shittim (Acacias) (Joel 4:18)

**Amos's oracles against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab and Judah**
- The prophecy is dated 'two years before the earthquake' (Amos 1:1)
- At God's roar the shepherds' pastures mourn and the top of Carmel withers (Amos 1:2)
- Refrain: 'I will send fire on (the wall of) X and it shall devour its palaces' (Amos 1:4, Amos 1:7, Amos 1:10, Amos 1:12, Amos 1:14, Amos 2:2, Amos 2:5)
- War crime: threshing Gilead with iron threshing sledges (Amos 1:3)
- War crime: deporting an entire population and handing it over to Edom (Amos 1:6, Amos 1:9)
- Tyre did not remember the 'covenant of brothers' (Amos 1:9)
- Edom pursued his brother with the sword and kept his wrath forever (Amos 1:11)
- Moab burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime (desecration of the dead) (Amos 2:1)

**The oracle against Israel; sandals, pledged garments and silenced prophets**
- A man and his father go in to the same young woman, profaning God's name (Amos 2:7)
- They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge and drink wine of the fined (Amos 2:8)
- The Amorite was tall as cedars and strong as oaks, yet God destroyed his fruit above and roots below (Amos 2:9)
- The people made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy (Amos 2:11-12)
- In that day even the bravest warrior will flee away naked (Amos 2:14-16)

**'You only have I known'; the lion has roared**
