- 'You only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities' (Amos 3:2)
- Chain of rhetorical questions of cause and effect (do two walk together unless agreed? does a lion roar without prey?) (Amos 3:3-6)
- God does nothing without revealing his secret (sod) to his servants the prophets (Amos 3:7)
- 'The lion has roared, who will not fear? The Lord has spoken, who will not prophesy?' (Amos 3:8)
- As a shepherd rescues two legs or a piece of ear from the lion's mouth, so a remnant of Israel will be rescued (Amos 3:12)
- The horns of the altar of Bethel will be cut off and fall to the ground (Amos 3:14)
- God will strike the winter house with the summer house, and the houses of ivory will perish (Amos 3:15)

**Cows of Bashan; 'yet you did not return'; prepare to meet your God**
- The wealthy women of Samaria are called 'cows of Bashan' who oppress the poor and say to their husbands 'Bring, let us drink' (Amos 4:1)
- Captives will be dragged away with hooks and fishhooks (Amos 4:2-3)
- Ironic summons: 'Come to Bethel and transgress, to Gilgal and multiply transgression' (Amos 4:4-5)
- God makes it rain on one city and not on another, one field and not another (Amos 4:7-8)
- 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel' (Amos 4:12)
- Hymnic doxology: he who forms the mountains, creates the wind, makes dawn into darkness, treads the heights; YHWH of hosts is his name (Amos 4:13)

**Lament for virgin Israel; seek me and live; the Day of YHWH is darkness**
- Dirge: 'Fallen, no more to rise, is the virgin Israel' (Amos 5:1-2)
- The city that marched out a thousand will have a hundred left, and the hundred ten (Amos 5:3)
- 'Seek me and live'; do not seek Bethel, Gilgal or Beersheba (Amos 5:4-6, Amos 5:14)
- They hate the one who reproves in the gate and abhor the one who speaks the truth (Amos 5:10)
- Futility curse: you built houses of hewn stone but will not live in them, planted vineyards but will not drink their wine (Amos 5:11)
- The prudent will keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time (Amos 5:13)
- Farmers and professional wailers are summoned to lamentation in every street and vineyard (Amos 5:16-17)
- As if a man fled from a lion and met a bear, entered the house, leaned on the wall and was bitten by a snake (Amos 5:19)
- 'I hate, I despise your feasts'; God rejects offerings and the noise of their songs and harps (Amos 5:21-23)
- 'Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream' (Amos 5:24)
- Rhetorical question: did you bring me sacrifices in the wilderness forty years? (Amos 5:25)
- Israel carried Sakkuth their king and Kaiwan their images, the star of their god (Amos 5:26)
- God will exile them beyond Damascus (Amos 5:27)

**Woe to the complacent; the marzeah ends; the plague-house**
- Woe to those at ease in Zion and secure on Mount Samaria (Amos 6:1-3)
- The marzeah (revelry banquet) of the sprawlers shall pass away (Amos 6:7)
- Survivor of a plague-struck house says 'Hush! We must not mention the name of YHWH' (Amos 6:10)
- A kinsman who burns (mesaref) the bodies carries the bones out of the house (Amos 6:10)
- Do horses run on rock? Does one plow the sea with oxen? (absurdity questions) (Amos 6:12)
- Those who rejoice in Lo-debar ('nothing') and boast of taking Karnaim ('horns') by their strength (Amos 6:13)

**Visions of locusts, fire and plumb line; Amos and Amaziah**
- Vision of locusts after the king's mowing; the prophet intercedes 'Forgive! How can Jacob stand, for he is small?' and God relents (Amos 7:1-3)
- Vision of a cosmic fire that devours the great deep (tehom rabbah); the prophet intercedes and God relents (Amos 7:4-6)
- Vision of the Lord standing on a wall with an anakh (plumb line or tin) in his hand (Amos 7:7-8)
- The high places of Isaac (yishaq, spelled with sin) will be desolate (Amos 7:9, Amos 7:16)
- The priest of the royal sanctuary at Bethel reports the prophet to the king and orders him back to Judah: 'Go, seer, flee' (Amos 7:10-13)
- 'I am no prophet nor a prophet's son; I am a herdsman, and YHWH took me from following the flock' (Amos 7:14-15)
- Prophet's curse on the opposing priest: his wife will be a harlot, his children fall by sword, he will die in an unclean land (Amos 7:17)

**The basket of summer fruit; cheating merchants; famine of the word**
- Vision of a basket of summer fruit (qayits) means 'the end (qets) has come' (Amos 8:1-2)
- God will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight (Amos 8:9)
- A famine not of bread or thirst for water, but of hearing the words of YHWH; they wander from sea to sea seeking it (Amos 8:11-12)
- Those who swear by the Ashimah of Samaria, 'As your god lives, O Dan', and 'As the way of Beersheba lives' (Amos 8:14)

**The Lord at the altar, no escape, the sieve, and the fallen booth of David**
- The prophet sees the Lord standing by the altar commanding 'Strike the capitals so the thresholds shake' (Amos 9:1)
- God commands the serpent at the bottom of the sea to bite those who hide there (Amos 9:3)
- God builds his upper chambers (ma'alot) in the heavens and founds his vault (aguddah) on the earth (Amos 9:6)
- 'Are you not like the Cushites to me, O Israel?' (Amos 9:7)
- God brought up Israel from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor and Aram from Kir (Amos 9:7)
- God will shake Israel among the nations as grain is shaken in a sieve, yet no pebble will fall to the ground (Amos 9:9)
- In that day God will raise up the fallen booth (sukkah) of David and repair its breaches (Amos 9:11)
- All the nations over whom God's name is called will be possessed (Amos 9:12)
- The plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes the sower (Amos 9:13)
- God will plant them on their land and they will never again be uprooted (Amos 9:14-15)

**Obadiah's vision against Edom's pride**
- A nation's treaty partners and table companions deceive and overpower it (Obad 1:7)

**Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH**
- Edom condemned for violence against its brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's fall (Obad 1:10)
- Prohibition of gloating over, looting or handing over one's brother on the day of his calamity (Obad 1:12, Obad 1:13)
- The enemy stands at the crossroads to cut off and hand over the fleeing survivors (Obad 1:14)
- On Mount Zion there will be escape (peletah) and holiness in the coming judgment (Obad 1:17)
- The house of Jacob will be fire and the house of Esau stubble consumed without survivor (Obad 1:18)
- Exiles of Jerusalem in Sepharad and of Israel as far as Zarephath will repossess the land (Obad 1:20)
- Saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingship shall be YHWH's (Obad 1:21)

**Jonah flees to Tarshish and is thrown into the sea**
- The wickedness of a great city rises up before God, who sends a prophet to cry against it (Jonah 1:2)
- Hero goes down to Joppa, pays the fare and boards a ship bound for Tarshish (Jonah 1:3)
- God hurls a great wind on the sea and the ship is about to break up (Jonah 1:4)
- In the storm the sailors each cry out to their own god (Jonah 1:5)
- Sailors throw the cargo overboard to lighten the ship in a storm (Jonah 1:5)
- A man of God lies fast asleep in the hold while the storm threatens the ship, and is woken by others (Jonah 1:5)
- The ship's captain wakes the sleeper and urges him to call on his god that they may not perish (Jonah 1:6)
- Strangers question the hero: your occupation, where you come from, your land and your people (Jonah 1:8)
- Confession of the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land (Jonah 1:9)
- A man is thrown into the sea at his own request so that the storm will cease, and the sea grows calm (Jonah 1:12, Jonah 1:15)
- The sailors row hard to bring the ship back to land but cannot against the storm (Jonah 1:13)
- Those about to kill a man pray that God not hold his innocent blood against them (Jonah 1:14)
- Gentile sailors, saved from the storm, fear YHWH, offer sacrifice and make vows (Jonah 1:16)

**Jonah swallowed by the great fish and his psalm**
- Hero stays three days and three nights in the belly of a fish or in the underworld (Jonah 2:1)
- The speaker cries from 'the belly of Sheol' (beten sheol) (Jonah 2:3)
- The speaker is cast into the deep, the heart of the seas, with the current around him (Jonah 2:4)
- The dying man remembers God and his prayer reaches God's holy temple; he looks again toward the temple (Jonah 2:5, Jonah 2:8)
- Reeds or seaweed (suf) are wrapped round the drowning man's head (Jonah 2:6)
- The speaker goes down to the roots (or cut-offs) of the mountains where the earth's bars close behind him forever (Jonah 2:7)
- Declaration 'Salvation belongs to YHWH' (Jonah 2:10)

**Jonah preaches and Nineveh repents down to its animals**
- Nineveh is an exceedingly great city of three days' walk (Jonah 3:3)
- A prophet announces: 'Forty more days and the city will be overturned' (Jonah 3:4)
- The king rises from his throne, removes his robe, covers himself with sackcloth and sits in ashes (Jonah 3:6)
- By royal decree even the cattle and flocks fast, drink no water and are covered in sackcloth (Jonah 3:7, Jonah 3:8)
- Each is to turn from his evil way and from the violence (hamas) in his hands (Jonah 3:8)
- 'Who knows? God may turn and relent' as a ground for repentance (Jonah 3:9)
- God sees the people's repentance and does not carry out the announced destruction (Jonah 3:10)

**Jonah's anger, the qiqayon plant and God's question**
- Prophet asks God to take his life: 'my death is better than my life' (Jonah 4:3, Jonah 4:8)
- The prophet sits in a booth east of the city to see what will become of it (Jonah 4:5)
- God sends a scorching east wind (ruah qadim harishit) and the sun beats on the man's head till he faints (Jonah 4:8)
- God argues from the prophet's pity for a plant that grew and perished in a night to his own pity for a city (Jonah 4:10, Jonah 4:11)
- God's compassion extends to the many animals of the city (Jonah 4:11)

**YHWH comes down against Samaria; the prophet wails naked**
- God comes forth from his place, descends and treads on the high places of the earth (Mic 1:3)
- A city's idols and cult objects were gathered from a harlot's hire and will return to a harlot's hire (Mic 1:7)
- The prophet goes stripped and barefoot, wailing like jackals and mourning like ostriches (Mic 1:8)

**Punning lament over the towns of the Shephelah**
- Mourners shave themselves bald like the vulture (nesher) for exiled children (Mic 1:16)

**Woe to those who seize fields; the breaker goes before the flock**
- The wicked devise evil on their beds and carry it out at morning light (Mic 2:1)
- The powerful covet and seize fields and houses, oppressing a man and his inheritance (Mic 2:2)
- The people tell the prophets: 'Do not preach (drip) these things' (Mic 2:6)
- The people want a lying prophet who preaches of wine and strong drink (Mic 2:11)
- 'The breaker' (ha-porets) goes up before the gathered flock, their king passes before them, YHWH at their head (Mic 2:13)

**Cannibal rulers, hireling prophets and Zion plowed as a field**
- Rulers flay the people, break their bones and chop them like meat in a cauldron (Mic 3:2, Mic 3:3)
- Prophets cry 'Peace' when fed and declare holy war on whoever puts nothing in their mouths (Mic 3:5)
- False seers will have night without vision; the sun sets on the prophets and there is no answer from God (Mic 3:6, Mic 3:7)
- Shamed seers cover their upper lip (mustache), a mourning or leper's gesture (Mic 3:7)
- The true prophet is filled with power by the spirit of YHWH to declare Israel's sin (Mic 3:8)
- The corrupt leaders say 'Is not YHWH among us? No evil will come on us' (Mic 3:11)

**Nations stream to Zion; swords into plowshares**
- All peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we walk in the name of YHWH (Mic 4:5)
- Migdal Eder, 'tower of the flock', hill of daughter Zion, to which the former dominion returns (Mic 4:8)

**Daughter Zion in labor, exiled to Babylon, threshing the nations**
- Daughter Zion writhes like a woman in labor (Mic 4:9, Mic 4:10)
- Zion will go to Babylon and there be rescued and redeemed (Mic 4:10)
- God gathers the nations like sheaves to the threshing floor without their knowing his plan (Mic 4:12)
- Daughter Zion threshes the peoples with a horn of iron and hooves of bronze, devoting their wealth to God (Mic 4:13)
- The judge (ruler) of Israel is struck on the cheek with a rod (Mic 4:14)

**The ruler from Bethlehem and the remnant among the nations**
- From little Bethlehem Ephrathah will come a ruler whose origins are from of old, from ancient days (Mic 5:1)
- Israel is given up until she who is in labor has given birth (Mic 5:2)
- Seven shepherds and eight princes of men will be raised against Assyria (Mic 5:4)
- Assyria is called the land of Nimrod (Mic 5:5)
- The remnant of Jacob among the peoples is like dew from YHWH that waits for no man (Mic 5:6)
- The remnant of Jacob among the nations is like a lion among the beasts of the forest (Mic 5:7)

**God cuts off horses, sorcery and idols**
- In that day God cuts off horses, chariots, fortresses, sorceries, soothsayers, idols, pillars and asherim from his own people (Mic 5:9, Mic 5:10, Mic 5:11)

**YHWH's lawsuit with his people; what YHWH requires**
- God's plea: 'My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me' (Mic 6:3)
- God sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before the people (Miriam named as a leader) (Mic 6:4)
- Remember what Balak king of Moab plotted and how Balaam son of Beor answered him (Mic 6:5)
- Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression? Thousands of rams and rivers of oil do not please God (Mic 6:6, Mic 6:7)

**False scales and futility curses**
- The people keep the statutes of Omri and all the works of the house of Ahab (Mic 6:16)

**No godly man left; who is a God like you?**
- The godly have vanished from the land like a vineyard after gleaning with no cluster to eat (Mic 7:1, Mic 7:2)
- Trust no neighbor or friend; guard your mouth even from the wife in your bosom (Mic 7:5)
- 'Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: though I fall I shall rise; though I sit in darkness YHWH is my light' (Mic 7:8)
- God will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea (Mic 7:19)
- God will show truth to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham as he swore to the fathers (Mic 7:20)

**The jealous and avenging God against Nineveh**
- YHWH is an avenging God (noqem), 'lord of wrath' (ba'al hemah), keeping anger for his enemies (Nah 1:2)
- God's way is in whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet (Nah 1:3)
- God rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all rivers fail; Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon wither (Nah 1:4)
- One who plots evil against YHWH comes out of the enemy city, a counselor of Belial (beliyya'al) (Nah 1:11)

**The herald of peace and the sack of Nineveh**
- Attacking warriors with red shields and scarlet clothes; chariots flash like torches and dart like lightning (Nah 2:4, Nah 2:5)
- The river gates are opened and the palace melts away (Nah 2:7)
- The captive queen's maids moan like doves, beating their breasts (Nah 2:8)
- The empire is a lions' den where the lion tore prey for his cubs and lionesses and filled his lairs (Nah 2:12, Nah 2:13)

**Woe to the bloody city, harlot and sorceress**
- Onomatopoeic battle scene: crack of whip, rumble of wheel, galloping horse, bounding chariot, heaps of corpses (Nah 3:2, Nah 3:3)
- The enemy city is a graceful harlot and mistress of sorceries who sells nations by her harlotries (Nah 3:4)
- God lifts the city's skirts over her face and shows the nations her nakedness (Nah 3:5, Nah 3:6)
- Are you better than No-Amon (Thebes), surrounded by water, which still went into exile? (Nah 3:8, Nah 3:9, Nah 3:10)
- Infants are dashed to pieces at the head of every street (Nah 3:10)
- Fortresses are like first-ripe figs that fall into the eater's mouth when shaken (Nah 3:12)
- The enemy's troops are women; the gates of the land stand wide open (Nah 3:13)
- Merchants and officials are like locusts that camp in the hedges in the cold and fly off when the sun rises (Nah 3:15, Nah 3:16, Nah 3:17)
- All who hear of the tyrant's downfall clap their hands, for who has not suffered his evil? (Nah 3:19)

**Habakkuk's complaint and the Chaldean fisherman**
- Torah grows numb and justice goes out crooked because the wicked surround the righteous (Hab 1:3, Hab 1:4)
- God raises up the Chaldeans, a bitter and hasty nation, as his instrument of judgment (Hab 1:5, Hab 1:6)
- The invader's horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than evening wolves; his horsemen fly like an eagle (Hab 1:8)
- The conqueror makes his own strength his god (Hab 1:11)
- A verse traditionally counted among the scribal corrections (tiqqunei soferim) where 'you do not die' was altered to 'we shall not die' (Hab 1:12)
- God's eyes are too pure to look on evil; why then does he look on the treacherous? (Hab 1:13)
- God makes humans like fish of the sea; the conqueror hauls them up with hook, net and seine (Hab 1:14, Hab 1:15)
- The conqueror sacrifices and burns incense to his net because it makes him rich (Hab 1:16)

**The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes**
- The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint (Hab 2:1)
- Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it (Hab 2:2)
- The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come (Hab 2:3)
- 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)' (Hab 2:4)
- The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations (Hab 2:5)
- A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor (Hab 2:6, Hab 2:9, Hab 2:12, Hab 2:15, Hab 2:19)
- The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork (Hab 2:11)
- Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness (Hab 2:15)

**Habakkuk's prayer; God marches from Teman**
- A prayer headed 'on shigionoth', an obscure musical or genre term (Hab 3:1)
- Plea: 'in wrath remember mercy' (Hab 3:2)
- Brightness like light, with rays (qarnayim, horns) coming from God's hand, where his power is hidden (Hab 3:4)
- God stands and measures (or shakes) the earth; the eternal mountains shatter and the everlasting hills sink (Hab 3:6)
- The tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian tremble at the theophany (Hab 3:7)
- God rides his horses and chariots of salvation, angry at River and Sea, and treads the sea with his horses (Hab 3:8, Hab 3:15)
- God goes out to save his anointed and crushes the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck (Hab 3:13, Hab 3:14)
- Though fig and vine fail, olive and fields yield nothing and the folds are empty, yet I will rejoice in YHWH (Hab 3:17, Hab 3:18)

**Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah**
- A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah) (Zeph 1:1)
- God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed) (Zeph 1:2, Zeph 1:3)
- People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom) (Zeph 1:5)
- The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated (Zeph 1:7, Zeph 1:8)
- God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments (Zeph 1:8)
- Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail (Zeph 1:10, Zeph 1:11)
- God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent (Zeph 1:12)
- Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil' (Zeph 1:12)
- Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm (Zeph 1:15, Zeph 1:16)

**Seek humility; oracles on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush and Assyria**
- Seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of YHWH's anger (Zeph 2:3)
- God starves the gods of the earth and all the coastlands bow to him each from its own place (Zeph 2:11)
- A ruined city becomes a lair for flocks and wild creatures; owls and hedgehogs lodge in its capitals and a voice sings in the window (Zeph 2:14)
- The exultant city says in her heart 'I am, and there is none besides me' (Zeph 2:15)

**The oppressing city, a pure speech for the peoples and God's song over Zion**
- The city's officials are roaring lions and its judges evening wolves that leave nothing for morning (Zeph 3:3)
- A verse noted by tradition as containing every letter of the Hebrew alphabet (Zeph 3:8)
- God will change the peoples to a pure speech (safah berurah) so all call on his name and serve him shoulder to shoulder (Zeph 3:9)
- From beyond the rivers of Cush God's worshipers, his dispersed daughter, bring him offerings (Zeph 3:10)
- God leaves in Zion a humble and poor people who do no wrong, speak no lies, and lie down with none to frighten (Zeph 3:12, Zeph 3:13)
- God in Zion's midst rejoices over her with gladness, is silent in his love, and exults over her with song (Zeph 3:14, Zeph 3:17)

**Haggai rouses Zerubbabel and Joshua to rebuild**
- The people say it is not yet time to rebuild YHWH's house (Hag 1:2)
- The people live in paneled houses while God's house lies in ruins (Hag 1:4, Hag 1:9)
- The wage earner puts his wages into a bag with holes (Hag 1:6)
- Heaven withholds dew and earth its produce because God's house lies waste (Hag 1:10, Hag 1:11)
- A human prophet is called 'the messenger (malakh) of YHWH' (Hag 1:13)
- God stirs up the spirit of the leaders and people to build (Hag 1:14)

**The glory of this latter house**
- Those who saw the first temple in its glory find the new one as nothing (Hag 2:3)
- The glory of the latter house will be greater than the former, and in this place God will give peace (Hag 2:9)

**A priestly ruling on holiness and impurity; blessing from this day**
- Priestly ruling: holy meat in a garment's fold does not sanctify food the garment touches, but corpse impurity does defile it (Hag 2:11, Hag 2:12, Hag 2:13)
- God struck their labor with blight, mildew and hail, yet they did not return to him (Hag 2:16, Hag 2:17)
- From the day the temple's foundation is laid, God promises to bless the harvest (Hag 2:18, Hag 2:19)

**Zerubbabel as God's signet ring**
- God will overturn the thrones of kingdoms and chariots and their riders (Hag 2:22)
- God will take Zerubbabel his servant and make him like a signet ring, for he has chosen him (Hag 2:23)

**Zechariah's call to return**
- 'Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?' Yet God's words overtook them (Zech 1:5, Zech 1:6)

**First night vision, the horsemen among the myrtles**
- A prophet sees a series of night visions, each explained by an angel (Zech 1:8)
- A man on a red horse stands among the myrtles in the deep (metsulah), with horses behind him (Zech 1:8, Zech 1:10, Zech 1:11)
- The angel of YHWH intercedes: 'How long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem?' (Zech 1:12)

**Second night vision, four horns and four craftsmen**
- Vision of four horns, the powers that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem (Zech 2:1, Zech 2:2)
- Four craftsmen (harashim) come to terrify and cast down the horns of the nations (Zech 2:3, Zech 2:4)

**Third night vision, the measuring line and the wall of fire**
- A man with a measuring line goes to measure the length and breadth of Jerusalem (Zech 2:5, Zech 2:6)
- Jerusalem will be unwalled for its multitude; God will be a wall of fire around it and glory within (Zech 2:8, Zech 2:9)
- Call to the exiles: 'Flee from the land of the north; escape, Zion, who dwells with daughter Babylon' (Zech 2:10, Zech 2:11)
- Judah called God's portion in 'the holy land' (admat ha-qodesh) (Zech 2:16)

**Fourth vision, the high priest, the satan and the Branch**
- 'YHWH rebuke you, Satan!': the accuser is rebuked in the heavenly court (Zech 3:2)
- The high priest's filthy garments are removed and replaced with festal robes and a pure turban, signifying removal of guilt (Zech 3:3, Zech 3:4, Zech 3:5)
- If faithful, the high priest is granted a place to walk among the heavenly attendants who stand there (Zech 3:7)
- A stone set before the high priest with seven eyes on it, which God will engrave (Zech 3:9)

**Fifth vision, the lampstand, the two olive trees and Zerubbabel**
- The angel rouses the prophet like a man woken from sleep before the vision (Zech 4:1)
- 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit', says YHWH (Zech 4:6)
- 'Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you become a plain' (Zech 4:7)
- The headstone is brought out with shouts of 'Grace, grace to it' (Zech 4:7)
- 'Who has despised the day of small things?' (small beginnings of the rebuilding) (Zech 4:9, Zech 4:10)
- Two 'sons of oil' (anointed ones) stand by the Lord of all the earth (Zech 4:14)

**Sixth vision, the flying scroll**
- A huge flying scroll, twenty by ten cubits, is seen in a vision (Zech 5:1, Zech 5:2)
- A curse goes out over the land, enters the house of the thief and the false swearer, lodges there and consumes its timber and stones (Zech 5:3, Zech 5:4)

**Seventh vision, the woman in the ephah carried to Shinar**
- A woman sitting inside an ephah measure is identified as Wickedness (ha-rish'ah) (Zech 5:6, Zech 5:7, Zech 5:8)
- Wickedness is thrust back into the ephah and a lead weight is thrown over its mouth (Zech 5:7, Zech 5:8)
- Two women with wind in their wings like the wings of a stork lift the ephah between earth and heaven (Zech 5:9)
- Wickedness is carried off to Shinar (Babylonia) where a house is built for it and it is set on its base (Zech 5:10, Zech 5:11)

**Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains**
- Four chariots come out from between two mountains of bronze (Zech 6:1)
- The chariots are the four winds (spirits) of heaven that go out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth (Zech 6:5)
- The horses going to the north country have set God's spirit at rest there (Zech 6:8)

**Crowns for Joshua; the man named Branch**
- Crowns made from the exiles' silver and gold are set on the head of the high priest (Zech 6:10, Zech 6:11)
- A ruler on his throne and a priest by (or on) his throne with 'counsel of peace between the two of them' (Zech 6:13)
- The crowns are kept in the temple as a memorial for named donors (Zech 6:14)

**The Bethel delegation's question about fasting**
- A delegation asks the priests whether to keep weeping and abstaining in the fifth month now the temple is rebuilt (Zech 7:2, Zech 7:3)
- 'When you fasted and mourned these seventy years, was it for me that you fasted?' (Zech 7:5, Zech 7:6)
- The people made their hearts like shamir (adamant or flint) so as not to hear the Torah (Zech 7:11, Zech 7:12)
- As God called and they would not hear, so they will call and he will not hear (Zech 7:13)

**Ten promises for Zion; fasts become feasts; ten men grasp a Jew's garment**
- Jerusalem will be called 'the city of truth' and Zion 'the holy mountain' (Zech 8:3)
- Old men and women with staffs sit again in Jerusalem's squares and boys and girls play in its streets (Zech 8:4, Zech 8:5)
- The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become joy and festivals (Zech 8:19)
- Ten men of every tongue will grasp the corner of a Jew's garment: 'Let us go with you, for we have heard God is with you' (Zech 8:23)

**Oracle against Hadrach, Tyre and Philistia**
- Tyre builds a fortress and heaps up silver like dust and gold like street mud, yet will be burned (Zech 9:3, Zech 9:4)
- A mixed or illegitimate people (mamzer) will dwell in Ashdod (Zech 9:6)
- God removes blood and abominations from the Philistine's mouth; the remnant becomes like a clan in Judah, Ekron like the Jebusites (Zech 9:7)

**Zion's humble king on a donkey; sons of Zion against Javan**
- Zion's king comes righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt the foal of a she-ass (Zech 9:9)
- The king speaks peace to the nations and rules from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth (Zech 9:10)
- By the blood of the covenant God frees the prisoners from the waterless pit; 'prisoners of hope' return to the stronghold (Zech 9:11, Zech 9:12)
- God rouses the sons of Zion against the sons of Javan (Greece) (Zech 9:13)
- God's warriors trample sling-stones, drink and roar as with wine, and are filled like sacrificial basins at the altar corners (Zech 9:15)

**Rain from YHWH, false teraphim and the regathering of Judah and Joseph**
- Ask YHWH for rain in the season of the latter rain; he makes the storm clouds (Zech 10:1)
- Teraphim speak deceit, diviners see lies and tell false dreams (Zech 10:2)
- From Judah will come the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler (Zech 10:4)
- God whistles (sharaq) for his scattered people to gather them (Zech 10:8)
- A new exodus: God passes through the sea of distress, strikes the waves and dries the depths of the Nile, bringing them back from Egypt and Assyria (Zech 10:11)

**The shepherd of the flock of slaughter, two staffs and thirty pieces of silver**
- Lebanon opens its doors to fire; cypresses and oaks of Bashan are told to wail because the cedar has fallen (Zech 11:1, Zech 11:2, Zech 11:3)
- The prophet is told to shepherd 'the flock of slaughter' whose buyers kill them guiltless and sellers say 'Blessed be YHWH, I am rich' (Zech 11:4, Zech 11:5, Zech 11:7)
- The shepherd takes two staffs named Favor (No'am) and Union (Hovlim) and later breaks them to annul a covenant and the brotherhood of Judah and Israel (Zech 11:7, Zech 11:10, Zech 11:14)
- The shepherd destroys three shepherds in one month (Zech 11:8)
- The shepherd's wage of thirty silver pieces, 'the lordly price', is thrown to the potter (or treasury) in the house of YHWH (Zech 11:13)
- Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock: a sword on his arm and right eye, his arm withered and eye blinded (Zech 11:15, Zech 11:16, Zech 11:17)

**Jerusalem a cup of reeling; mourning for the one they pierced**
- God who stretches out the heavens, founds the earth and forms the spirit of man within him (Zech 12:1)
- Jerusalem becomes a heavy stone that wounds all the nations who try to lift it (Zech 12:3)
- God strikes the enemy's horses with panic and blindness and their riders with madness (Zech 12:4)
- The feeblest in Jerusalem will be like David, and the house of David like God, like the angel of YHWH before them (Zech 12:8)
- God pours on the house of David and Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication (Zech 12:10)
- They look on 'me (or him) whom they pierced' and mourn him as for an only son, bitterly as for a firstborn (Zech 12:10)
- The great mourning is compared to the mourning of (or for) Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo (Zech 12:11)
- The land mourns family by family, each apart, and the men apart from the women (David, Nathan, Levi, Shimei) (Zech 12:12, Zech 12:13, Zech 12:14)

**A cleansing fountain, the end of prophecy, and the struck shepherd**
- A fountain is opened for the house of David and Jerusalem to cleanse sin and menstrual impurity (niddah) (Zech 13:1)
- In that day God cuts off the names of idols and removes the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land (Zech 13:2)
- If anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother will pierce him through for speaking falsely in God's name (Zech 13:3)
- Prophets wear a hairy mantle (adderet se'ar) as a mark of office, here to deceive (Zech 13:4)
- Disclaimer: 'I am no prophet; I am a tiller of the soil' (Zech 13:5)
- Asked about the wounds 'between your hands', the man says 'I was struck in the house of my friends (lovers)' (Zech 13:6)
- 'Awake, sword, against my shepherd, the man who is my fellow; strike the shepherd and the sheep will scatter' (Zech 13:7)
- Two-thirds perish and one third is brought through fire, refined like silver and tested like gold (Zech 13:8, Zech 13:9)

**The final day on the Mount of Olives; living waters; Sukkot for the nations**
- God gathers all nations to battle against Jerusalem: the city is taken, houses plundered, women raped, half exiled (Zech 14:2)
- God's feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits east to west into a great valley, half moving north and half south (Zech 14:4, Zech 14:5)
- The great earthquake in the days of King Uzziah is remembered as a reference point (Zech 14:5)
- A unique day known to YHWH, neither day nor night, without light, cold and frost; at evening there will be light (Zech 14:6, Zech 14:7)
- Living waters flow out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, summer and winter (Zech 14:8)
- The whole land is leveled like the Arabah while Jerusalem is raised up on its site (Zech 14:10)
- Plague on Jerusalem's attackers: their flesh, eyes and tongues rot while they stand on their feet (Zech 14:12, Zech 14:15)
- Survivors of the nations go up yearly to Jerusalem to bow to the King, YHWH of hosts, and keep the feast of Booths (Zech 14:16)
- Families of the earth that do not go up for Sukkot get no rain; Egypt is struck with plague (Zech 14:17, Zech 14:18, Zech 14:19)
- In that day 'Holy to YHWH' is inscribed on the horses' bells and every pot in Jerusalem becomes holy (Zech 14:20, Zech 14:21)
- There will no longer be a Canaanite (trader) in the house of YHWH (Zech 14:21)

**I loved Jacob, Esau I hated**
- A prophetic book is headed 'by the hand of Malakhi' ('my messenger'), a name or title (Mal 1:1)
- God says 'I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated', laying Edom's mountains waste (Mal 1:2, Mal 1:3)
- If Edom rebuilds its ruins God will tear down; it will be called 'territory of wickedness' (Mal 1:4)

**Priests who despise God's name with blemished offerings**
- A son honors his father and a servant his master: 'If I am a father, where is my honor?' (Mal 1:6)
- The altar is called 'the table of YHWH' and the offering 'bread' (lehem) (Mal 1:7, Mal 1:12)
- 'Offer that to your governor; would he accept you?': sarcastic comparison of God and a human ruler (Mal 1:8)
- God wishes someone would shut the temple doors rather than kindle the altar in vain (Mal 1:10)
- God calls himself 'a great king' (melekh gadol) whose name is feared among the nations (Mal 1:14)

**The covenant with Levi and the corrupt priests**
- God will send the curse on the priests and curse their blessings if they do not give glory to his name (Mal 2:2)
- God will spread the dung of the festival sacrifices on the priests' faces (Mal 2:3)
- God's covenant of life and peace with Levi, who revered God, had true Torah in his mouth and turned many from iniquity (Mal 2:4, Mal 2:5, Mal 2:6)
- The priest's lips guard knowledge and people seek Torah from his mouth, for he is the messenger (malakh) of YHWH of hosts (Mal 2:7)

**One father, one God; foreign wives and the wife of one's youth**
- The people cover God's altar with tears, weeping and groaning because he no longer accepts their offering (Mal 2:13)
- God is witness between a man and the wife of his youth, his companion and 'wife of your covenant' (Mal 2:14)
- 'I hate sending away (divorce)', says YHWH, and covering one's garment with violence (Mal 2:15, Mal 2:16)

**Where is the God of justice? The messenger who prepares the way**
- The people weary God saying 'Everyone who does evil is good in his eyes' or 'Where is the God of justice?' (Mal 2:17)
- The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple, the messenger of the covenant in whom you delight (Mal 3:1)
- The coming one is like a refiner's fire and fuller's lye; he sits refining and purifies the sons of Levi like gold and silver (Mal 3:2, Mal 3:3)
- God draws near for judgment as a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers and those who cheat the hired worker, widow, orphan and stranger (Mal 3:5)

**Return to me; will a man rob God? Test me with the tithe**
- 'I YHWH do not change; therefore you sons of Jacob are not consumed' (Mal 3:6)
- 'Will a man rob God? Yet you rob me' in tithes and offerings (Mal 3:8, Mal 3:9)

**The book of remembrance and the sun of righteousness**
- Complaint: 'It is vain to serve God; what profit that we kept his charge? The arrogant are blessed and the wicked test God and escape' (Mal 3:13, Mal 3:14, Mal 3:15)
- God will spare the faithful as a man spares the son who serves him, on the day he makes his treasured possession (Mal 3:17)
- The day comes burning like an oven; the arrogant and evildoers become stubble, left neither root nor branch (Mal 3:19)
- For those who fear God the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings (kenafeha) (Mal 3:20)
- The righteous go out leaping like stall-fed calves and tread the wicked like ashes under their feet (Mal 3:20, Mal 3:21)

**Remember Moses; Elijah sent before the great day**
- Remember the Torah of Moses my servant, commanded at Horeb for all Israel (Mal 3:22)
- God will send Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of YHWH (Mal 3:23)
- Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to their sons and of sons to their fathers, lest God strike the land with a ban (herem) (Mal 3:24)
- A book ends on a harsh word, so synagogue reading repeats the previous verse (Isaiah, Malachi, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes) (Mal 3:24)

**The Opening (al-Fatiha)**
- Text or act opened with the formula 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' (1:1)
- Communal confession 'You alone we worship, you alone we ask for help' (1:5)
- Three ways contrasted: those God favored, those under wrath, and those gone astray (1:7)

**Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites**
- The scripture announces itself as 'the Book' in which there is no doubt, guidance for the God-fearing (2:2)
- The faithful defined as those who believe in the unseen (al-ghayb) (2:3)
- Parable: one kindles a fire, and when it lights his surroundings God takes away the light, leaving him in darkness (2:17)
- Parable: travelers in a rainstorm of darkness, thunder and lightning put fingers in their ears for fear of death (2:19, 2:20)
- Unbelievers called 'deaf, dumb, blind' (summun bukmun umyun) (2:18)

**Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat**
- Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before' (2:25)
- God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller (2:26)

**Adam, the angels and Iblis**
- God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth (2:30)
- God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot (2:31, 2:32, 2:33)
- The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time (2:36)

**Exodus, the calf and the wilderness**
- Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death (2:55, 2:56)

**The cow and the slain man**
- Moses commands a cow be slaughtered; the people repeatedly ask its age, color and nature before complying (2:67, 2:68, 2:69, 2:70, 2:71)
- The sacrificial cow is bright yellow, pleasing to beholders (2:69)
- A slain man is struck with part of the slaughtered cow and revived to reveal his killer (2:72, 2:73)
- Hearts harder than stones, yet some stones gush rivers, split for water or fall down in fear of God (2:74)

**Polemic with the People of the Book**
- The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts (2:93)
- If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will (2:94, 2:95)
- Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years (2:96)
- Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart (2:97)
- Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God (2:97, 2:98)

**Solomon, the devils and Harut and Marut**
- Devils (shayatin) taught sorcery in Solomon's reign; Solomon himself did not disbelieve (2:102)
- Two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut, teach magic while warning 'we are only a trial' (2:102)
- Magic is learned that separates a man from his wife, harming only by God's leave (2:102)

**Ra'ina, abrogation, rival claims and the face of God**
- Believers told not to say 'ra'ina' (a word twisted by opponents) but 'unzurna' (2:104)
- Claim that none enters paradise unless Jew or Christian, rebutted by surrender of the face to God (2:111, 2:112)
- Jews say the Christians stand on nothing, Christians say the same of the Jews (2:113)

**Abraham, Ishmael and the House**
- God tests Abraham with words, he fulfills them and is made an imam for mankind; the covenant excludes the wrongdoers among his seed (2:124)
- Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House while praying (2:125, 2:127)
- Abraham told 'Submit' answers 'I submit to the Lord of the worlds' (aslamtu) (2:128, 2:131)
- Dying Jacob asks his sons 'What will you worship after me?' and they confess the God of their fathers (2:133)
- The 'dye' or baptism (sibgha) of God: who has a better dye than God? (2:138)
- That was a community that has passed; it has what it earned and you what you earned (2:134, 2:141)

**The change of qibla**
- The direction of prayer (qibla) is changed toward the Sacred Mosque; fools ask why (2:142, 2:143, 2:144, 2:149, 2:150)
- God sees the prophet turning his face toward heaven and grants him a qibla he is pleased with (2:144)
- Believers made a middle community (umma wasat), witnesses over mankind, with the messenger a witness over them (2:143)
- To each a direction he faces: so race toward good deeds (2:148)

**Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation**
- Formula of the afflicted: 'To God we belong and to him we return' (2:156)
- Safa and Marwa are among God's waymarks; circuit between them permitted on pilgrimage (2:158)
- On seeing the punishment, those followed disown their followers, who wish for a return to disown them in turn (2:166, 2:167)

**Lawful food and true piety**
- Refusal of revelation in favor of what was found with the fathers is rebuked (2:170)
- Unbelievers are like beasts shouted at by a herdsman, hearing only a call and a cry (2:171)
- Those who conceal scripture for gain eat only fire into their bellies (2:174)
- Wealth given for (freeing) necks, i.e. ransoming slaves and captives (2:177)

**Retaliation and bequests**
- Retaliation (qisas) for the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female (2:178)
- Kin of the slain may pardon and accept compensation (diya) instead of retaliation, a lightening from God (2:178)
- 'In retaliation there is life for you' (2:179)

**The fast of Ramadan**
- Fasting prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you (2:183)
- The sick and the traveler may make up missed fast days later (2:184, 2:185)
- Those able only with hardship may ransom fast days by feeding a poor person (fidya) (2:184)
- Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down (2:185)
- Marital relations permitted on fast nights; spouses are garments for one another (2:187)
- Eat and drink until the white thread is distinguished from the black thread at dawn (2:187)
- Spouses not approached while in retreat (i'tikaf) in the mosques (2:187)

**New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites**
- Piety is not entering houses from their backs but from their doors (2:189)
- Fight in God's way those who fight you, but do not transgress (2:190)
- Do not fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there (2:191)
- The sacred month for the sacred month; violations are subject to retaliation (2:194)
- Complete the pilgrimage (hajj) and visitation (umra) for God (2:196)
- Do not shave heads until the sacrificial offering (hady) reaches its place (2:196)
- Who cannot find an offering fasts three days on pilgrimage and seven on return: ten complete (2:196)
- No sexual talk, wickedness or quarreling during the pilgrimage (2:197)
- Take provision, but the best provision is God-consciousness (taqwa) (2:197)
- When you pour down from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) (2:198, 2:199)
- Remember God as you remember your fathers, or more (2:200)
- Prayer 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next, and guard us from the fire' (2:201)
- Remember God on the counted days; no sin whether one hastens in two days or delays (2:203)

**The corrupter, God in clouds, one community, fighting in the sacred month**
- Will they wait until God comes to them in canopies of cloud with the angels? (2:210)
- Mankind was one community; God sent prophets as bearers of good news and warners with the Book (2:213)
- Fighting is prescribed though you hate it; you may hate what is good for you (2:216)
- Who turns from his religion and dies an unbeliever, his deeds are void in this world and the next (2:217)

**Wine, gambling, orphans, mixed marriage and menstruation**
- What to spend? 'The surplus' (al-'afw) (2:219)
- Mixing with orphans' affairs permitted: they are your brothers (2:220)
- A believing slave woman (or man) is better for marriage than an attractive polytheist (2:221)
- Your wives are a tilth for you; come to your tilth as you wish (2:223)

**Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood**
- Oath of abstention from wives (ila'): a four-month waiting period (2:226, 2:227)
- Divorced women wait three menstrual periods (quru') and may not conceal what is in their wombs (2:228)
- Divorce is twice; then retain honorably or release with kindness (2:229)
- No blame if the wife ransoms herself (khul') when they fear not keeping God's bounds (2:229)
- Husband may not take back what he gave the wife except in fear of transgressing God's bounds (2:229)
- After a third divorce she may not return to the first husband until she marries another (2:230)
- Do not retain divorced wives to harm them (2:231)
- Do not prevent divorced women from remarrying their husbands when agreed (2:232)
- Widows wait four months and ten days ('idda) before remarriage (2:234)
- Proposal may be hinted during the waiting period but no secret promise or contract until it ends (2:235)
- If divorced before consummation with dower fixed, half the dower is due (2:236, 2:237)
- In fear, pray on foot or riding (2:239)
- Bequest of a year's provision to widows without expelling them (2:240)
- Divorced women are due a provision (mut'a) according to the husband's means (2:236, 2:241)

**The thousands who died and were revived; a loan to God**
- Thousands who left their homes fearing death are told by God 'Die' and then revived (2:243)

**Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath)**
- The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship (2:247)
- God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth (2:247)
- The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron (2:248)
- Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand (2:249)
- 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave' (2:249)
- David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom (2:251)
- Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted (2:251)

**Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse**
- Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes God (2:255)
- God's footstool or seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth (2:255)
- No compulsion in religion (2:256)

**Abraham disputes with the king**
- Abraham challenges the king: God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west; the king is confounded (2:258)

**The man who passed a ruined town**
- A man passing a ruined town is made to die for a hundred years, then revived, thinking he slept a day or part of a day (2:259)
- After a century the sleeper's food and drink have not spoiled (2:259)
- The sleeper is shown his donkey's bones assembled and clothed with flesh (2:259)

**Abraham and the four birds**
- Abraham, asking to see how God revives the dead, takes four birds, places parts on each hill, calls them and they come flying (2:260)

**Parables of charity**
- Spending in God's way is like a grain sprouting seven ears with a hundred grains each (2:261)
- Charity voided by reminders of generosity and injury, like dust on a rock washed bare by rain (2:262, 2:263, 2:264)
- Spending for God's pleasure is like a garden on a height that yields double with heavy rain or even with dew (2:265)
- Satan threatens you with poverty and commands indecency (2:268)
- Deserving poor, restrained in God's way, thought rich by the ignorant for their restraint, known by their mark (2:273)

**Usury**
- Those who consume usury rise like one driven mad by Satan's touch (2:275)
- Trade is like usury, they say; but God permitted trade and forbade usury (riba) (2:275)
- God blots out usury and makes charity grow (2:276)
- Those who do not give up usury are warned of war from God and his messenger; they keep their principal (2:279)
- A debtor in hardship is given respite until ease; remitting it as charity is better (2:280)

**The debt verse**
- A debt for a fixed term must be written by a just scribe, dictated by the debtor or his guardian (2:282)
- Two male witnesses, or one man and two women so that if one errs the other reminds her (2:282)

**Closing confession and prayer**
- Prayer not to be laid with a burden (isr) like that laid on those before us (2:286)

**The two hosts, worldly lures, God's witness**
- Sign in two hosts that met: one saw the other as twice their number (3:13)
- God bears witness there is no god but he, and so do the angels and those of knowledge (3:18)

**Owner of sovereignty**
- O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase (3:26)
- God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living (3:27)
- Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat) (3:28)
- God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu) (3:28, 3:30)
- On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil (3:30)

**The family of Imran, Mary and Zechariah**
- Mother who vowed her unborn child finds she has borne a girl: 'the male is not like the female' (3:36)
- Mother names her daughter Mary and commits her and her offspring to God's protection from the accursed Satan (3:36)
- Zechariah is made Mary's guardian (3:37, 3:44)
- Angels call to Zechariah while he stands praying in the sanctuary, announcing John (Yahya) (3:39)
- John (Yahya) foretold as noble, chaste (hasur) and a prophet, confirming a word from God (3:39)
- Sign given to the doubting father: he will not speak to people for three days except by gestures (3:41)
- Angels tell Mary that God chose and purified her above the women of the worlds (3:42)

**The annunciation and the mission of Jesus**
- Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (3:45)
- Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses (3:49)
- Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden (3:50)
- God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you' (3:55)

**The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian**
- Argument: Torah and Gospel were revealed only after Abraham, so he cannot be Jew or Christian (3:65)
- Some People of the Book plot to believe at the start of the day and disbelieve at its end (3:72)
- Some People of the Book return a heap of gold entrusted; others not even a dinar (3:75)
- Claim 'there is no obligation on us concerning the unlettered (ummiyyin)' (3:75)
- Some twist their tongues with the book so you think it is from the book (3:78)
- No human given book and prophethood would tell people to be his servants instead of God's (3:79, 3:80)

**The covenant of the prophets and the apostates**
- God took the covenant of the prophets to believe in and help a later confirming messenger (3:81)

**Israel's self-imposed food law and the House at Bakka**
- All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel (Jacob) forbade himself before the Torah (3:93)
- The first House appointed for mankind was the one at Bakka, blessed (3:96)
- Pilgrimage to the House is a duty to God for whoever is able to find a way (3:97)

**Hold fast to the rope of God**
- Hold fast all together to the rope of God and do not be divided (3:103)
- You were on the brink of a pit of fire and God rescued you (3:103)
- 'You are the best community brought forth for mankind' (3:110)
- Spending of unbelievers is like an icy wind that destroys the tillage of a wrongdoing people (3:117)
- When alone they bite their fingertips at you in rage: 'Die in your rage' (3:119)

**Badr and Uhud**
- God helped you at Badr when you were weak (3:123)
- Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled (3:130)
- Those who restrain anger and pardon people (3:134)
- Such days God alternates among people (3:140)
- Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken (3:146, 3:147)
- Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils) (3:152, 3:153)
- After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters (3:154)
- Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds (3:154, 3:156, 3:168)
- The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter (3:159)
- Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection (3:161)
- The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them (3:170, 3:171)
- It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me (3:175)

**Misers, those who called God poor, and the fire-consumed offering**
- God grants the unbelievers respite only that they may increase in sin (3:178)
- Misers will have what they hoarded hung round their necks as a collar on the Day of Resurrection (3:180)
- Those who said 'God is poor and we are rich' are recorded and will taste the burning (3:181)
- Some demand that a messenger bring an offering consumed by fire as his credential (3:183)
- God took the covenant of those given the Book to make it clear to people and not conceal it (3:187)

**Signs for people of understanding; closing prayer**
- 'We heard a caller calling to faith: believe in your Lord' (3:193)
- God does not waste the work of any worker, male or female; you are of one another (3:195)
- Be patient, vie in patience, stand guard (rabitu) (3:200)

**One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift**
- Fear God, by whom you ask of one another, and the wombs (kinship ties, al-arḥām) (4:1)
- Property is not handed to the feeble-minded (sufahāʾ); they are fed and clothed from it (4:5)
- Women as well as men receive a fixed share of what parents and kin leave (4:7)
- Kin, orphans and the poor present at the division of an estate are given something from it (4:8)
- Those who devour orphans' property devour fire into their bellies (4:10)

**The fixed shares of inheritance**
- Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds) (4:11, 4:12)
- Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other (4:12)
- Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid (4:11, 4:12)

**Indecency, four witnesses, and the limits of repentance**
- Four witnesses are required to establish sexual indecency (fāḥisha) (4:15)
- Women guilty of indecency are confined to houses until death or until God makes a way (4:15)
- Offenders who repent and reform are to be left alone (4:16)
- Repentance is not accepted from one who repents only when death comes (4:18)

**Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees**
- It is forbidden to inherit women against their will or to hold them back to recover gifts (4:19)
- A husband exchanging one wife for another may not take back anything he gave, even a qinṭār (4:20, 4:21)
- Foster mothers and foster sisters by nursing are forbidden in marriage (4:23)
- One who cannot afford a free wife may marry a believing slave woman with her people's leave (4:25)
- A married slave woman who commits indecency receives half the punishment of a free woman (4:25)
- God wishes to lighten your burden, for the human was created weak (4:28)

**Wealth by consent, major sins, and discord in marriage**
- Command: do not kill yourselves (or one another) (4:29)
- If the major sins (kabāʾir) are avoided, God expiates lesser misdeeds (4:31)
- Those bound to you by oath-alliance receive their share (4:33)
- Men are maintainers (qawwāmūn) of women by God's preference and their spending (4:34)
- A wife whose rebellion (nushūz) is feared is admonished, left alone in bed, then struck (4:34)
- In marital discord an arbiter is sent from his family and one from hers (4:35)

**The circle of kindness, misers, and the atom's weight**
- Misers who urge stinginess and hide what God gave them of his bounty (4:37)
- On that day the disbelievers wish the earth were leveled over them (4:42)

**Prayer not while drunk; bathing and dry ablution**
- Do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until you know what you say (4:43)

**Shifted words, 'we hear and disobey', and the people of the Sabbath**
- Opponents twist an ambiguous address ('rāʿinā') with their tongues to mock (4:46)
- Threat to obliterate faces and turn them backward (4:47)
- God gave the family of Abraham the book, wisdom and a great kingdom (4:54)
- In hellfire, whenever the skins are burnt through, they are replaced with new skins (4:56)
- The blessed enter a deep, lasting shade (ẓill ẓalīl) (4:57)

**Trusts, obedience to authority, and the hypocrites who seek other judges**
- Obey God, obey the Messenger and those in authority; refer disputes to God and the Messenger (4:59)
- Had they been commanded 'kill yourselves or leave your homes', few would have done it (4:66)
- Companions of the obedient: prophets, the truthful (ṣiddīqūn), martyrs and the righteous (4:69)

**Fighting for the oppressed; death in lofty towers**
- Fight for the oppressed men, women and children who cry 'take us out of this town of wrongdoers' (4:75)
- The plot of Satan is weak (4:76)
- Death will reach you wherever you are, even in lofty towers (4:78)
- All comes from God; yet good befalling you is from God and evil from yourself (4:78, 4:79)
- Were the Quran from other than God they would find much contradiction in it (4:82)
- Whoever intercedes for good shares in it; whoever intercedes for evil bears a part of it (4:85)
- When greeted, return a better greeting or the same (4:86)

**The hypocrites, deserters and those who offer peace**
- Believers are split into two factions over the hypocrites, whom God has overturned (4:88)

**Accidental and deliberate killing of a believer**
- Accidental killing of a believer: free a believing slave and pay blood money (diya) to the family unless they remit it (4:92)
- Whoever cannot pay the expiation fasts two consecutive months (4:92)
- Deliberate killing of a believer is punished by hell forever, God's wrath and curse (4:93)
- Do not tell one who greets you with peace 'you are not a believer' to seize booty (4:94)

**Those who strive and those who sit; the angels' question at death**
- Those with disabilities (ulū l-ḍarar) are excepted from the duty to fight (4:95)
- Angels taking a soul ask 'what state were you in?'; excuses of weakness are tested (4:97)
- Whoever leaves home as an emigrant to God and dies on the way has his reward with God (4:100)

**Shortened prayer and prayer in shifts under arms**
- Prayer may be shortened when travelling in danger (4:101)
- Prayer is prescribed for believers at fixed times (kitāban mawqūtan) (4:103)
- If you suffer, they suffer as you do, but you hope from God what they do not (4:104)

**Guilt cast on the innocent and the Prophet who must not defend traitors**
- The Prophet is told not to argue on behalf of those who betray themselves (4:105, 4:107, 4:109)
- No good in most secret counsels except enjoining charity, kindness or reconciliation (4:114)

**Female deities, Satan's vow, slit cattle ears, and Abraham the friend**
- Idolaters invoke only female beings besides God, and only a rebellious Satan (4:117)
- Cursed Satan vows to take an appointed share (naṣīb mafrūḍ) of God's servants (4:118)
- Satan commands people to slit the ears of cattle (a pagan dedication rite) (4:119)
- Satan commands people to alter God's creation (4:119)
- Salvation is not by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book: whoever does evil is requited (4:123)

**Orphan girls, reconciliation, the suspended wife, and justice against oneself**
- A wife who fears her husband's aversion may make a settlement with him; settlement is best (4:128)
- You will never be able to be equally just among wives, however eager (4:129)

**Articles of faith; hypocrites wavering between two sides**
- Belief in God, his angels, his books, his messengers and the last day (4:136)
- Those who believe, then disbelieve, then believe, then disbelieve and increase in disbelief (4:137)
- The hypocrites are in the lowest depth (al-dark al-asfal) of the fire (4:145)
- God does not love public evil speech except by one who has been wronged (4:148)
- Those who believe in some messengers and reject others, making distinctions among them (4:150, 4:151, 4:152)

**The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised**
- Israel demands 'show us God openly' and is seized by the thunderbolt (4:153)
- The Jews' grave slander (buhtān) against Mary (4:156)
- They did not kill the Messiah Jesus nor crucify him (4:157)
- It was only made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum) (4:157)
- Every one of the People of the Book will believe in him before his (or their) death (4:159)
- Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book on resurrection day (4:159)

**The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three'**
- God spoke to Moses directly (kallama taklīman) (4:164)
- Jesus is God's word cast to Mary and a spirit from him (4:171)
- The angels brought near (al-muqarrabūn) to God (4:172)

**Contracts, pilgrim sanctity and the forbidden foods**
- Fulfil your contracts and covenants (ʿuqūd) (5:1)
- The sacred month and God's rites must not be profaned (5:2)
- Sacrificial animals (hady) marked with garlands (qalāʾid) are inviolable (5:2)
- Forbidden: the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen and the gored animal (5:3)
- 'Today I have perfected your religion and completed my favor' (5:3)
- What trained hunting animals (dogs, birds of prey) catch is lawful, with God's name pronounced (5:4)
- The food of the People of the Book is lawful to believers and theirs to them (5:5)
- Believers may marry chaste women of the People of the Book (5:5)

**Ablution, the covenant 'we hear and obey', and justice despite hatred**
- Before prayer wash the face, hands to the elbows, wipe the head and wash feet to the ankles (5:6)
- God restrained a people who meant to stretch out their hands against the believers (5:11)

**Israel's covenant and twelve chiefs; the Christians' forgotten portion**
- The Messenger makes clear much of the scripture they used to hide (5:15)
- A messenger comes after an interval (fatra) without messengers (5:19)

**The refusal to enter the holy land and forty years of wandering**
- God set prophets among Israel and made them kings, giving them what he gave no other (5:20)
- Enter the holy land (al-arḍ al-muqaddasa) which God has ordained for you (5:21)
- The people tell the leader 'go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here' (5:24)
- Moses: 'I control only myself and my brother; separate us from the rebellious people' (5:25)

**The two sons of Adam, the raven, and whoever saves one life**
- The threatened brother refuses to raise his hand to kill in return, out of fear of God (5:28)
- The victim wishes the murderer to bear both the victim's sin and his own (5:29)
- God sends a raven scratching the earth to show how to hide a brother's corpse (5:31)
- Whoever kills one soul is as if he killed all humanity; whoever saves one, as if he saved all (5:32)

**Penalty for waging war on God; the ransom of the earth; the thief's hand**
- Those who wage war on God and spread corruption: killed, crucified, hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or exiled (5:33)
- Those who repent before they are overpowered are pardoned (5:34)
- Seek a means of approach (al-wasīla) to God (5:35)
- Cut off the hands of the male and female thief as recompense (5:38, 5:39)

**Judging by the Torah, the Gospel and the Quran; eye for eye**
- Why do they seek the Prophet's judgment when they have the Torah with God's judgment? (5:43)
- The prophets, rabbis (rabbāniyyūn) and scholars (aḥbār) judged by the Torah they were entrusted to guard (5:44)
- Whoever remits retaliation as charity, it is expiation for him (5:45)
- The book confirms the scripture before it and is a guardian (muhaymin) over it (5:48)
- For each community God made a law (shirʿa) and a way; had he willed he would have made one nation (5:48)
- Do they seek the judgment of the Age of Ignorance (jāhiliyya)? (5:50)

**Allies, apostates replaced, the mocked call to prayer, apes and swine**
- A people whom God loves and who love him (5:54)
- When you call to prayer they take it as mockery and play (5:58)

**'God's hand is fettered'; the blessings of observing the Torah**
- Whenever they kindle the fire of war, God extinguishes it (5:64)
- Believers, Jews, Sabians and Christians who believe in God and the last day and do good need not fear (5:69)

**Against the deification of Jesus; the weeping Christians**
- The Messiah and his mother both ate food (proof of their humanity) (5:75)
- Mary called truthful (ṣiddīqa) (5:75)
- The unbelievers of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and of Jesus son of Mary (5:78)
- Hearing the revelation, their eyes overflow with tears at the truth they recognize (5:83)

**Lawful good things, oath expiation, wine and gambling, game in iḥrām**
- Do not forbid the good things God has made lawful (against self-imposed abstinence) (5:87, 5:88)
- Expiation for a broken oath: feed or clothe ten poor, free a slave, or fast three days (5:89)
- Wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are abomination of Satan's work (5:90, 5:91)
- Killing game in iḥrām is compensated by an equivalent domestic animal judged by two just men and brought to the Kaʿba (5:95)
- Game of the sea and its food are lawful, also for travellers (5:96)
- God made the Kaʿba, the sacred house, a support (qiyām) for people (5:97)

**Questions not to ask; the freed camels of the pagans**
- Do not ask about things which, if made plain, would trouble you; a people before you asked and disbelieved (5:101, 5:102)
- God did not institute the baḥīra, sāʾiba, waṣīla or ḥām (camels set free by pagan dedication) (5:103)

**Witnesses to a bequest made far from home**
- Two just witnesses attend a bequest at death; on a journey two outsiders may serve (5:106)
- Doubted witnesses are detained after prayer and swear by God they will not sell their testimony (5:106)
- If the witnesses are found guilty, two of the wronged heirs swear in their place (5:107, 5:108)

**Jesus' miracles, the table from heaven, and Jesus questioned at judgment**
- God gathers the messengers and asks what response they received; they say 'we have no knowledge' (5:109)
- The disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) declare 'we believe; bear witness that we submit (muslimūn)' (5:111)
- At the disciples' request Jesus prays and God sends down a table (māʾida) from heaven (5:112, 5:113, 5:114, 5:115)
- The heavenly table is to be a festival (ʿīd) for the first and last of them and a sign (5:114)
- Whoever disbelieves after the sign will be punished as no one else in the worlds (5:115)
- At judgment Jesus denies telling people to take him and his mother as gods (5:116, 5:117)
- Polemic against taking Mary, with Jesus, as gods besides God (5:116)
- Jesus: 'If you punish them they are your servants; if you forgive them, you are the Mighty, the Wise' (5:118)

**Darkness and light, clay and two terms, and those who would not believe**
- Praise God who created heaven and earth and made the darknesses and the light (6:1)
- God decreed a term (ajal) for each person, and another term named with him (6:2)
- God destroyed earlier generations though he had established them more firmly and given them rain and rivers (6:6)
- Even a book on parchment they could touch would be called magic (6:7)
- Had God sent an angel he would have made him a man (6:9)
- Earlier messengers were mocked, and what the mockers mocked surrounded them (6:10)

**Mercy written on himself; the idolaters' denial at the gathering**
- God feeds and is not fed (6:14)
- The idolaters swear 'by God our Lord, we were not idolaters' (6:23, 6:24)
- Unbelievers say there is only this worldly life and no raising (6:29)
- Standing before the fire the damned wish to be sent back; were they sent back they would return to sin (6:27, 6:28)
- On the day of the Hour they carry their burdens (awzār) on their backs (6:31)

**The Prophet consoled; a ladder to the sky; animals as communities**
- The Prophet is consoled: messengers before him were denied and patient until help came (6:33, 6:34)
- If you could seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign... (6:35)
- Every beast on earth and bird flying with its wings are communities (umam) like you, gathered to their Lord (6:38)
- We have neglected nothing in the Book (6:38)
- God opened the gates of everything to them, and when they rejoiced he seized them suddenly (6:42, 6:43, 6:44, 6:45)

**Do not drive away the poor; the keys of the unseen and the falling leaf**
- Do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking his face (6:52, 6:53)
- Not a leaf falls but he knows it, nor a grain in the darkness of the earth (6:59)
- God takes your souls by night (sleep) and raises you by day until the appointed term (6:60)
- God sends guardians (ḥafaẓa) over people (6:61)

**Rescue in the darkness of land and sea; the bewildered man; the trumpet**
- God can send punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or split you into factions (6:65)
- Parable: one lured by devils, bewildered in the land, while companions call him to guidance (6:71)

**Abraham, Azar and the star, moon and sun**
- Abraham's father is named Āzar (6:74)
- God showed Abraham the kingdom (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth (6:75)
- Abraham: 'I do not love things that set' (lā uḥibbu l-āfilīn) (6:76, 6:77, 6:78)
- Abraham's people dispute with him; he fears none of their gods (6:80, 6:81)
- Which of the two parties has more right to security? Those who believe without mixing in wrong (6:81, 6:82)

**Abraham's line of eighteen prophets; Torah in sheets; the false claimant**
- Opponents say 'God has sent down nothing to any human' (6:91)
- They make Moses' book into sheets (qarāṭīs), showing some and hiding much (6:91)
- The intercessors they claimed as partners are not seen with them; ties are cut (6:94)

**Splitter of seed and dawn; stars for navigation; do not revile their gods**
- God splits the grain and the date-stone (6:95)
- God is the splitter of the dawn (fāliq al-iṣbāḥ); night for rest (6:96)
- Humans have a lodging place and a repository (mustaqarr wa-mustawdaʿ) (6:98)
- Rain brings forth vegetation: clustered grain, hanging date clusters, vineyards, olives and pomegranates (6:99)
- They made the jinn partners of God, though he created them (6:100)
- Vision does not grasp him, but he grasps all vision (6:103)
- Opponents say to the Prophet 'you have studied' (darasta) (6:105)
- Do not revile those they invoke besides God, lest they revile God in ignorance (6:108)

**Sworn oaths for a sign; even the dead speaking would not convince**
- They swear solemnly they would believe if a sign came (6:109)
- Even if angels came down and the dead spoke to them, they would not believe (6:111)
- Most on earth follow only conjecture (ẓann) and guess (6:116)

**Eat what God's name is spoken over; the opened breast; jinn and humans judged**
- Parable: one who was dead whom God revived and gave a light to walk among people (6:122)
- In every town God placed its great criminals to plot there (6:123)
- God knows best where to place his message (6:124)
- Jinn led many humans astray; their human allies say 'we profited from one another' (6:128)
- Messengers came to both jinn and humans 'from among you' (6:130)

**Pagan portions and taboos; eight pairs; what is forbidden to all and to the Jews**
- Pagans assign a portion of crops and cattle to God and a portion to their partners (6:136)
- Pagans declare certain cattle and crops taboo (ḥijr), to be eaten only by whom they will (6:138)
- Pagans set apart cattle whose backs may not be ridden or burdened (6:138)
- Pagans reserve what is in the wombs of cattle for males, forbidden to wives unless stillborn (6:139)
- Give its due on the day of harvest (6:141)
- Do not be wasteful; God does not love the wasteful (musrifīn) (6:141)
- Eight in pairs: sheep, goats, camels and cattle, male and female; which did God forbid? (6:143, 6:144)
- For the Jews God forbade every animal with claws/undivided hoof and the fat of cattle and sheep except on backs, entrails or bone (6:146)
- Idolaters say 'had God willed we would not have associated partners nor forbidden anything' (6:148, 6:149)

**The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue)**
- List of commandments introduced 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you' (6:151, 6:152, 6:153)
- This is my straight path; follow it and not other ways that scatter you (6:153)
- God gave Moses the book complete and detailing everything (6:154)
- Lest you say scripture was sent only to two groups before us (6:156, 6:157)

**Tenfold reward; my life and death for God; no bearer bears another's burden**
- On the day some of the signs come, faith not believed before will not avail (6:158)
- My prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds (6:162)
- God made you successors (khalāʾif) on the earth and raised some above others in rank to test you (6:165)

**Opening letters, destroyed towns and the weighing of deeds**
- On judgment day both the peoples and the messengers sent to them are interrogated (7:6, 7:7)

**The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall**
- The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left (7:17)
- Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out (7:19, 7:20, 7:22)
- The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals (7:20)
- The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser (7:21)
- The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness (7:23)
- The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time (7:24)
- On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out (7:25)

**Children of Adam - clothing, Satan's enmity, what God forbids**
- God sends down clothing to cover nakedness, and the 'garment of piety' is better (7:26)
- Satan pulled off the first couple's garments to show them their nakedness (7:27)
- Satan and his tribe see humans from where humans cannot see them (7:27)
- Wear your adornment (clothing) at every place of prostration (7:29, 7:31)
- Eat and drink but do not be excessive (7:31)
- God's adornments and good provisions are not forbidden to believers (7:32)
- Short list of what God truly forbids: indecencies open and hidden, sin, oppression, associating partners, false speech about God (7:33)

**Hell's quarrels, the camel and the needle, the people of the Heights**
- Each nation entering hell curses its sister nation (7:38)
- The gates of heaven are not opened for those who arrogantly deny the signs (7:40)
- Impossibility proverb: entering paradise is as possible as a camel (or rope) passing through the eye of a needle (7:40)
- Hell is the damned's bed below and covering above (7:41)
- The people of paradise and the people of hell call out to each other across the divide (7:44, 7:50)
- A herald proclaims between paradise and hell: God's curse is on the wrongdoers (7:44)
- A partition (hijab) separates paradise from hell (7:46)
- Men on the heights (al-A'raf) between paradise and hell recognize all by their marks, hoping to enter (7:46, 7:47, 7:48, 7:49)
- The damned beg the blessed to pour some water on them and are refused (7:50)
- The damned ask for intercessors or to be sent back to do differently (7:53)
- The damned find no intercessors to plead for them (7:53)

**Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection**
- Call on God humbly and in secret / not aloud (7:55, 7:56)
- Parable: good land yields its plants by God's leave, bad land yields only scantily (7:58)

**Noah warns his people**
- The drowned/destroyed were a blind people (7:64)

**Hud and the people of Ad**
- The people of Ad are given increased stature (bastatan fi l-khalq) (7:69)
- False gods are only names the people and their fathers invented, with no authority from God (7:71)

**Lot and his people**
- A people commit an indecency no one in the world did before them (7:80)
- Lot's people come to men with desire instead of women (7:81)
- The townspeople resolve to expel the righteous family because 'they keep themselves pure' (7:82)

**Shu'ayb and Midian**
- The prophet forbids his people to lie in wait on every road, threatening and turning people from God's way (7:86)

**The pattern of the destroyed towns**
- If the towns had believed God would have opened blessings from heaven and earth (7:96)

**Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues**
- The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw (7:115, 7:116)
- The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them (7:116)
- The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts (7:124)
- Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon (7:127)
- Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues (7:130)
- Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God (7:131)
- One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan) (7:133)

**Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets**
- The appointed time on the mountain is thirty nights completed with ten more, making forty (7:142)
- When God manifests himself to the mountain it is crushed to dust (7:143)
- The prophet falls down unconscious at the theophany and repents on waking (7:143)
- The tablets contain an exhortation and an explanation of all things (7:145)

**The lowing calf and the seventy**
- The angry prophet seizes his brother by the head (and beard), dragging him (7:150)
- Aaron pleads 'son of my mother, the people overpowered me and almost killed me' (7:150)
- When his anger subsides the prophet takes up the cast-down tablets again, their text intact (7:154)
- The seventy chosen men are seized by a tremor at the appointed meeting (7:155)

**The unlettered prophet foretold in Torah and Gospel**
- The new prophet removes the burdens and fetters (isr, aghlal) laid on the earlier community (7:157)

**Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate**
- Twelve springs gush from the struck rock, one drinking place for each tribe (7:160)

**The Sabbath-breaking seaside town turned into apes**
- Fish come openly to a seaside town on the Sabbath but not on other days, as a test (7:163)
- Transgressors are turned into despised apes (7:166)

**The primordial covenant ("Am I not your Lord?")**
- God takes all Adam's descendants from their loins and makes them testify 'Am I not your Lord?' ('Yes') (7:172)
