**The man who sloughed off God's signs (the panting dog)**
- A man given God's signs sloughs them off, clings to the earth and follows his desire (7:175, 7:176)
- Parable: like a dog that pants whether you chase it or leave it (7:176)

**Made for hell, the beautiful names, the unknown Hour**
- God has created many jinn and humans for hell (7:179)

**The single soul, the couple's vow, and powerless idols**
- A couple vow thanks for a sound child, then ascribe partners to God in what he gave (7:189, 7:190)
- Those you call on besides God are servants like yourselves (7:194)

**Forbearance, refuge from Satan, and the prostration of the near ones**
- When the Quran is recited, listen and be silent (7:204)
- A verse at which reciters customarily prostrate (sajda) (7:206)

**The question of spoils and the marks of true believers**
- True believers' hearts tremble when God is mentioned and their faith grows when his verses are recited (8:2, 8:3, 8:4)

**Badr - angels, slumber, rain and God's throw**
- Some believers dispute the call to battle as if driven to death with their eyes open (8:5, 8:6)
- God covers the fighters with slumber as a security from him before battle (8:11)
- Rain is sent down before battle to purify the fighters, remove Satan's filth and make their feet firm (8:11)
- Angels are told to strike the enemy above the necks and on every finger-tip (8:12)

**Deaf and dumb beasts, heart and trial**
- God comes between a man and his heart (8:24)
- God gives the God-fearing a furqan (criterion / deliverance) (8:29)

**The plot against the prophet and the worship of the pagans**
- God separates the bad from the good, heaps the bad on one another and casts them into hell (8:36, 8:37)
- If unbelievers desist, what is past is forgiven (8:38)
- Fight them until there is no persecution (fitna) and religion is wholly God's (8:39, 8:40)

**The fifth of the spoils, the dream of few, Satan's desertion**
- The day the two hosts met is the 'day of the criterion' (yawm al-furqan) (8:41)
- God shows the prophet the enemy as few in a dream so the believers will not lose heart (8:43)
- God makes each army appear few in the other's eyes so that the battle takes place (8:44)

**Angels at the death of unbelievers; the custom of Pharaoh's people**
- Unbelievers follow 'the custom of Pharaoh's people' and those before them (8:52, 8:54)

**Treaty-breakers, deterrence and peace**
- If a treaty partner is feared treacherous, throw the treaty back to them on equal terms (8:58)
- Prepare against the enemy whatever force and tethered war horses you can, to deter them (8:60)
- If the enemy inclines to peace, incline to it and trust God (8:61, 8:62)
- God united the believers' hearts, which all the wealth on earth could not have done (8:63)

**The ratio of the steadfast, captives and ransom**
- Twenty steadfast defeat two hundred, a hundred a thousand; later eased to one against two (8:65, 8:66)
- Only a prior decree from God averted punishment for taking ransom (8:68)
- Captives with good in their hearts are promised better than what was taken from them (8:70, 8:71)

**Emigrants, helpers and kin**
- Believers who emigrated and those who sheltered them are each other's allies; non-emigrants are not, unless they ask help in religion (8:72, 8:73, 8:74)

**The disavowal - treaties, sacred months and asylum**
- A surah begins without the formula 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' (9:1)
- God and his messenger proclaim their disavowal (bara'a) of the polytheists at the greater pilgrimage (9:1, 9:3)
- Treaty partners are given four months to move freely in the land before hostilities (9:2)
- If enemies repent, pray and give alms, let them go their way: they are brothers in religion (9:5, 9:11)
- A polytheist who seeks protection is given asylum to hear God's word, then escorted to safety (9:6)

**Who maintains the mosques; God above family**
- Giving water to pilgrims and tending the Sacred Mosque are not equal to faith and striving (9:19, 9:20)

**Hunayn, the impurity of polytheists, the jizya**
- Polytheists are impure (najas) and may not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year (9:28)
- People of the Book who do not follow the true religion are fought until they pay the jizya, subdued (9:29)

**'Uzayr and the Messiah called sons of God; rabbis and monks as lords**
- Polemic: the Jews are said to call 'Uzayr (Ezra?) son of God (9:30)
- People of the Book took their rabbis (ahbar) and monks as lords besides God (9:31)

**The excuses of those who stayed behind**
- God pardons the prophet, asking why he gave the shirkers leave before the truthful were clear (9:43)
- Nothing will befall us except what God has written for us (9:51)
- Believers expect one of two good things, victory or martyrdom (9:52)
- Alms given grudgingly by unbelievers will not be accepted (9:53, 9:54)

**Hypocrites who mock and the destroyed peoples**
- Hypocrites mock the prophet as 'all ear' (udhun), credulous (9:61)
- Hypocrites fear a surah will be revealed exposing what is in their hearts (9:64)

**The broken vow of charity; seventy prayers in vain**
- Men vow to give alms if God enriches them, then turn miserly, and God sets hypocrisy in their hearts (9:75, 9:76, 9:77)
- Hypocrites mock believers who give voluntarily and those who can give only their effort (9:79)

**Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin**
- Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter (9:81)
- Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them (9:92)
- The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy (9:97, 9:98)

**The forerunners, alms that purify, and the mosque of harm**
- The first forerunners (al-sabiqun al-awwalun) among emigrants and helpers: God is pleased with them and they with him (9:100)
- Hardened hypocrites will be punished twice, then given to great punishment (9:101)
- A rival mosque built for harm, unbelief and division (masjid al-dirar) (9:107, 9:108)
- A mosque founded on piety from the first day, with men who love to purify themselves (9:108, 9:109)

**The bargain of lives for paradise; Abraham's prayer for his father**
- God has bought from the believers their lives and wealth for paradise; a promise in Torah, Gospel and Quran (9:111)
- Believers may not pray for forgiveness for polytheists, even close kin (9:113)

**The three who were left behind; every step recorded**
- The three who stayed behind are forgiven after the earth grew narrow for them and they found no refuge but God (9:117, 9:118)

**Prayer in distress, a changed Quran, the storm at sea**
- Deniers ask the prophet to bring a different Quran or change it; he may not alter it of himself (10:15)
- The prophet argues he had lived a lifetime among them before receiving revelation (10:16)

**Life like a crop, the abode of peace, darkened faces**
- The doers of good get the best reward 'and more' (ziyada) (10:26)

**Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith**
- Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh (10:83)
- Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment (10:88, 10:89)
- As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late (10:90, 10:91)
- Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him (10:92)

**Ask the readers of scripture; the people of Jonah**
- If in doubt, ask those who read the scripture before you (10:94)
- Had God willed all on earth would believe; will you compel people to believe? (10:99, 10:100)

**The hanif creed and patience**
- Set your face toward religion as a hanif (pure monotheist) (10:105)

**The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs**
- Every creature on earth has its provision from God, who knows its resting place and depository (11:6)
- Before creation God's throne was upon the water (11:7)
- Those who want only this life are paid in full here and have nothing in the hereafter but fire (11:15, 11:16)
- On judgment day witnesses (al-ashhad) testify against those who lied about God (11:18)

**Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi**
- The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him (11:27)
- Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring' (11:41)
- The ark sails through waves like mountains (11:42)
- God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides (11:44)
- Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true (11:45)
- God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous' (11:46, 11:47)
- The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before (11:49)

**Hud and Ad**
- The people say one of their gods has struck the prophet with madness (11:53, 11:54)
- There is no creature but God holds it by its forelock (11:56)

**Salih, the she-camel and the Shout**
- The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this (11:62)
- After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction (11:65)

**Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife**
- Abraham's angelic guests do not stretch their hands to the food, and he is afraid (11:70)
- The annunciation names Isaac 'and after Isaac, Jacob' (11:71)
- Abraham is forbearing, sighing (awwah) and penitent (11:75)

**Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil**
- Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in (11:80)
- The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?' (11:81)

**Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan**
- What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain (11:86)
- The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?' (11:87)
- The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform (11:88)

**Pharaoh leads his people into the fire; the towns standing and mown**
- On judgment day Pharaoh will lead his people down into the fire, an evil watering place (11:97, 11:98)
- Of the destroyed towns some still stand, some are mown down (11:100)

**The witnessed day; the wretched and the blessed**
- On that day no soul speaks except by God's leave (11:105)
- In the fire the damned have sighing and sobbing (zafir wa-shahiq) (11:106)
- Hell and paradise last as long as heavens and earth endure, except as God wills (11:107, 11:108)
- Moses was given the Book and people differed over it (11:110)

**Stand firm; prayer times; good deeds remove bad**
- Only a few in past generations forbade corruption, and they were saved (11:116)
- The stories of the messengers are told to make the prophet's heart firm (11:120)

**Prologue to the Joseph surah (the best of stories)**
- God tells the prophet 'the best of stories', of which he was unaware before (12:3)

**Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)**
- The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God (12:18, 12:83)
- Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door (12:25)
- The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (12:38)
- 'The soul is ever inciting to evil' (al-nafs al-ammara bi-l-su') except whom God shows mercy (12:53)
- A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor (12:72)
- The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed (12:76)
- Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before (12:77)
- Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story (12:82)
- Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away (12:84, 12:85, 12:86)
- The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know (12:86, 12:96)
- Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms (12:88)
- The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them (12:91, 12:97)
- Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later (12:97, 12:98)

**Epilogue to the Joseph surah**
- A past story is called 'news of the unseen' revealed to a prophet who was not present (12:102)
- People pass by countless signs in the heavens and earth and turn away from them (12:105)
- When the messengers despair and think they were lied to, divine help comes and the chosen are saved (12:110)

**The signs of creation, thunder and the parable of the foam (Surah 13:1-17)**
- Neighboring plots watered with one water give different fruits: a sign (13:4)
- To every people there is a guide (13:7)
- God knows what every female carries and how wombs shrink or swell (13:8)
- Each person has angels in succession (mu'aqqibat) before and behind guarding him by God's command (13:11)
- The thunder glorifies God with his praise, and the angels too in awe of him (13:13)
- Praying to idols is like stretching one's palms to water hoping it will reach one's mouth (13:14)
- Parable: torrents and smelted metal throw up foam that vanishes, while what benefits people remains (13:17)

**Those who keep God's covenant and the abode of Eden (Surah 13:18-29)**
- The righteous enter paradise together with the righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring (13:23)
- Angels enter upon the blessed from every gate saying 'Peace be upon you for your patience' (13:23, 13:24)
- In the remembrance of God hearts find rest (13:28)
- 'Tuba' (blessedness, later a tree of paradise) for those who believe and do good (13:29)

**Messengers, the Mother of the Book and the witness of scripture (Surah 13:30-43)**
- Even a recitation that moved mountains, cleft the earth or made the dead speak would not convince the deniers (13:31)
- Messengers were mocked; God gave the deniers respite, then seized them (13:32)
- Challenge to the polytheists: 'Name them!' (the partners they ascribe to God) (13:33)
- Some to whom the Book was given rejoice at the new revelation while factions deny part of it (13:36)
- For every term there is a book (a written decree) (13:38)
- The messenger's duty is only to deliver the message; the reckoning belongs to God (13:40)
- Those with knowledge of the earlier Book are invoked as witnesses to the prophet's mission (13:43)

**Messengers in their people's tongue; Moses and the days of God; the threatened messengers (Surah 14:1-17)**
- Every messenger is sent speaking the language of his own people to make things clear (14:4)
- God proclaims: if you are grateful I will give you more; if ungrateful, my punishment is severe (14:7)
- If you and all on earth disbelieve, God is free of need and praiseworthy (14:8)
- The rejecting peoples thrust their hands into their mouths at the messengers (14:9)
- The people reject their messengers: 'you are only humans like us' (14:10, 14:11)
- In hell death comes from every side, yet the damned does not die (14:17)

**Ashes in the wind, Satan disowns his followers, the good and bad tree (Surah 14:18-34)**
- On judgment day Satan disowns his followers: 'I only called you; blame yourselves' (14:22)
- Parable: a good word is like a good tree, its root firm, its branches in the sky, yielding fruit every season (14:24, 14:25)
- God makes the believers firm with the firm word in this life and the hereafter (14:27)
- God has subjected ships, rivers, sun, moon, night and day to human use (14:32, 14:33)

**Abraham's prayer at the sacred house (Surah 14:35-41)**
- Abraham prays that he and his sons be kept from worshipping idols (14:35, 14:36)
- Abraham settles some of his offspring in a barren valley by God's sacred House (14:37)
- Abraham prays that people's hearts yearn toward his offspring at the sanctuary (14:37)
- Abraham thanks God for giving him Ishmael and Isaac in old age (14:39)

**The day eyes stare and the earth is changed (Surah 14:42-52)**
- God is not heedless; he only delays the wrongdoers to a day when eyes stare (14:42)
- On that day eyes stare fixed, heads upraised, hearts empty as air (14:42, 14:43)
- The wrongdoers beg for a short respite to answer the call and follow the messengers (14:44)
- They lived in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves and saw what God did to them (14:45)
- The opponents' scheme was such that mountains might be moved by it (14:46)
- God is swift in reckoning (14:51)

**The guarded reminder, the guarded heaven and the fertilizing winds (Surah 15:1-25)**
- No town is destroyed without a known written decree; no nation outstrips its term (15:4, 15:5)
- Opponents demand that the prophet bring the angels if he is truthful (15:7, 15:8)
- God declares that he sent down the Reminder and will himself guard it (15:9)
- Even if a door of heaven were opened and they ascended, they would say their eyes were bewitched (15:14, 15:15)
- God sends the winds as fertilizers (lawaqih), then rain to drink (15:22)

**Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)**
- The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire (15:27)
- Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned (15:44)
- The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security (15:45, 15:46)
- In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it (15:48)

**Abraham's guests and the destruction of Lot's people (Surah 15:51-77)**
- The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you' (15:52, 15:53)
- The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people (15:57, 15:58)
- The rescued family leaves by night, the leader following behind them (15:65)
- God swears by the prophet's life (la-'amruka) (15:72)
- The ruins of the destroyed towns lie on a road still traveled (15:76)

**The Thicket, al-Hijr, the seven oft-repeated and the close of the surah (Surah 15:78-99)**
- The people of the Thicket (ashab al-ayka) were wrongdoers and were punished (15:78, 15:79)
- Heavens and earth were created only with truth, and the Hour is surely coming (15:85)
- The prophet is given 'seven of the oft-repeated' (mathani) and the great recitation (15:87)
- The prophet is told to lower his wing (be gentle) to the believers (15:88)
- Those who divide scripture into fragments, accepting parts and rejecting others, are condemned (15:90, 15:91)
- The prophet is commanded to proclaim openly what he is ordered and turn from the polytheists (15:94)
- Worship your Lord until the certainty (death) comes to you (15:99)

**The command has come; cattle, rain, sea and stars as blessings (Surah 16:1-23)**
- God sends down the angels with the spirit of his command upon whom he wills (16:2)
- Man was created from a drop, yet he becomes an open adversary (16:4)
- Cattle were created for human warmth, food, burden-bearing and the beauty of herds coming and going (16:5, 16:6, 16:7)
- God made horses, mules and donkeys to ride and for adornment, and creates what you do not know (16:8)
- Night, day, sun, moon and stars are subjected by God's command (16:12)
- The subjected sea gives fresh meat and ornaments to wear, and ships cleave it (16:14)

**Legends of the ancients, the fallen roof, the angels who take souls (Surah 16:24-50)**
- Those who mislead bear their own full burdens and some of the burdens of those they misled (16:25)
- God came at the plotters' building from its foundations and the roof fell on them (16:26)
- The arrogant are told to enter the gates of hell to abide in it (16:29)
- Polytheists excuse themselves: had God willed we would not have worshipped others nor forbidden anything (16:35)
- Deniers swear their strongest oaths that God will not raise the dead (16:38)
- Those who emigrate for God after being wronged will be settled well in this world and rewarded more in the next (16:41, 16:42)
- The angels are not arrogant; they fear their Lord above them and do as commanded (16:49, 16:50)

**Not two gods; daughters ascribed to God and buried alive; milk, wine and the bee (Surah 16:51-70)**
- God says: do not take two gods; he is only one God (16:51)
- The polytheists assign daughters to God while wishing sons for themselves (16:57, 16:62)
- When told of a daughter's birth the father's face darkens and he hides from people in shame (16:58, 16:59)
- Burying a newborn daughter in the dust is condemned (16:59)
- Pure milk issues from cattle's bellies from between dung and blood: a sign (16:66)
- God reveals (awha) to the bee to build in mountains, trees and trellises and follow his paths (16:68, 16:69)
- Some are returned to the feeblest age (ardhal al-'umur), knowing nothing after knowledge (16:70)

**The slave and the free, the mute man, the woman who unravels her yarn (Surah 16:71-100)**
- Masters will not share their provision equally with their slaves (argument against partners to God) (16:71)
- God made spouses for you from yourselves and from them sons and grandsons (16:72)
- Parable: a slave owning nothing compared with a free man who spends secretly and openly (16:75)
- Parable: a mute, helpless man who is a burden to his master compared with one who commands justice (16:76)
- The coming of the Hour is like the blink of an eye, or nearer (16:77)
- God brought you from your mothers' wombs knowing nothing and gave you hearing, sight and hearts (16:78)
- God gave tents of hides light for travel, wool for furnishings, shade, mountain shelters and garments against heat and violence (16:80, 16:81)
- God commands justice, kindness and giving to kin, and forbids indecency, wrong and oppression (16:90)
- What you have runs out; what is with God remains (16:96)
- Before reciting scripture, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan (16:98)

**Abrogation, the foreign teacher, coerced unbelief, food law, Abraham the hanif and the Sabbath (Surah 16:101-128)**
- The Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus) brings the revelation down from God (16:102)
- Opponents claim a foreign-tongued man teaches the prophet; answer: this is clear Arabic (16:103)
- Parable of a secure town supplied from everywhere which was ungrateful and was made to taste the garment of hunger and fear (16:112, 16:113)
- The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it (16:124)
- Call to God's way with wisdom and good counsel and argue in the best way (16:125)

**The Night Journey and the two corruptions of the Children of Israel (Surah 17:1-8)**
- God takes his servant on a journey to show him some of his signs (17:1)
- Israel addressed as descendants of those carried with Noah, who was a grateful servant (17:3)
- It is decreed in the Book that Israel will work corruption on earth twice (17:4)
- Divine warning 'if you return (to sin), we will return (to punishment)' (17:8)

**The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21)**
- Man prays for evil as he prays for good; man is ever hasty (17:11)
- Every human's 'bird' (ta'ir, fate or omen) is fastened to his neck (17:13)
- When God would destroy a town he commands its affluent ones; they transgress and it is destroyed (17:16)
- How many generations God destroyed after Noah (17:17)
- Those who want the hasty world get some of it and then hell; those who strive for the hereafter are thanked (17:18, 17:19, 17:20)
- The hereafter is greater in degrees and in preference than this world (17:21)

**The code of commandments (Surah 17:22-39)**
- A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content (17:22, 17:39)
- Do not say even 'uff' to aged parents nor rebuke them; speak to them gently (17:23)
- Lower the wing of humility to parents and pray 'Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when small' (17:24)
- Squanderers are brothers of the devils (17:26, 17:27)
- Do not keep your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it out fully: moderation in spending (17:29)
- Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right (17:33)
- Do not walk the earth exultantly: you cannot split the earth nor reach the mountains in height (17:37)

**Daughters of God, all things glorify him, bones and dust, the cursed tree (Surah 17:40-60)**
- When the prophet recites, God places a hidden veil between him and those who deny the hereafter (17:45, 17:46)
- Answer to the deniers: even if you were stone or iron, the one who made you first will raise you (17:50, 17:51)
- Those whom the polytheists invoke themselves seek a means (wasila) of nearness to God (17:57)
- Every town will be destroyed or severely punished before the Day of Resurrection, as inscribed in the Book (17:58)
- The prophet's vision and the cursed tree in the Quran are made a trial for people (17:60)

**Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)**
- God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children (17:64)
- Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea (17:68, 17:69)
- On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam) (17:71)
- Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray (17:72)

**Near compromise, prayer times, the praised station, the spirit, the challenge and the demanded signs (Surah 17:73-100)**
- Prayer is fixed from the sun's decline to the dark of night, with the dawn recitation (17:78)
- Keep vigil (tahajjud) with recitation in part of the night as an extra devotion (17:79)
- The prophet may be raised to a 'praised station' (maqam mahmud), later read as intercession (17:79)
- Prayer: 'Lord, make my entrance and my exit true and grant me a helping authority' (17:80)
- Scripture is sent down as healing and mercy for believers but only loss for wrongdoers (17:82)
- Asked about the spirit, the prophet answers 'The spirit is of my Lord's command' (17:85)
- Opponents demand a spring gushing from the earth or a garden of palms and vines with rivers (17:90, 17:91)
- Opponents demand that the sky fall on them in pieces or God and the angels appear (17:92)
- Opponents demand that the prophet have a house of gold ornament (17:93)
- Were angels walking the earth, God would have sent them an angel as messenger (17:95)
- The astray are gathered on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf (17:97)
- Whenever the fire of hell abates, God increases its blaze (17:97)
- The creator of heavens and earth is able to create the like of them (resurrection argument) (17:99)
- Even owning the treasuries of God's mercy, humans would hold back for fear of spending (17:100)

**Moses' nine signs, the drowning of Pharaoh, the Quran sent in portions (Surah 17:101-111)**
- The prophet answers the accusing king: 'I think you are doomed' (17:102)
- After Pharaoh's drowning Israel is told to dwell in the land; at the last promise they are gathered in a mixed crowd (17:104)
- Those given knowledge before fall on their chins prostrate and weeping when the scripture is recited (17:107, 17:108, 17:109)
- Call on God as Allah or as al-Rahman: to him belong the most beautiful names (17:110)
- Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between (17:110)

**Prologue to the surah of the Cave (Surah 18:1-8)**
- The Book is sent down without any crookedness, straight and upright (18:1, 18:2)
- What is on earth is made its adornment to test who is best in deeds (18:7)
- God will reduce all that is on earth to barren dust (18:8)

**The Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (Surah 18:9-31)**
- The companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (an inscription or tablet) (18:9)
- Believing youths stand against their idolatrous people and take refuge in a cave (18:10, 18:14, 18:15, 18:16)
- The sleepers are awakened to show which party best reckoned how long they stayed (18:12)
- The sun inclines away from the sleepers' cave at rising and passes them at setting (18:17)
- The sleepers seem awake though asleep, and God turns them from side to side (18:18)
- The sleepers' dog lies stretching its forelegs at the cave's threshold (18:18, 18:22)
- Whoever looked upon the sleepers would flee filled with terror (18:18)
- Woken after centuries, the sleepers think they slept a day or part of a day (18:19)
- One sleeper is sent to town with their silver coin to buy food discreetly (18:19)
- The sleepers fear the townspeople will stone them or force them back to their religion (18:20)
- The prevailing party builds a place of worship over the sleepers (18:21)
- People dispute the sleepers' number (three, five or seven, plus their dog); only God knows (18:22)
- The sleepers stayed in their cave three hundred years and nine more (18:25)
- Keep company with those who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking his face (18:28)
- Hell's walls (suradiq) enclose the damned; they are given water like molten metal that scalds faces (18:29)
- In paradise the blessed wear gold bracelets and green silk and brocade, reclining on couches (18:31)

**The parable of the two gardens; this life as rain-fed plants; the book of deeds (Surah 18:32-49)**
- The rich man boasts of having more wealth and a mightier following (18:34)
- On entering one's garden one should say 'What God wills; there is no power except in God' (18:39)
- The proud man's garden is destroyed and he wrings his hands over what he spent on it (18:40, 18:41, 18:42)
- The ruined man says 'Would that I had associated no one with my Lord' (18:42)
- On the last day the earth is seen laid bare and all are gathered, none left out (18:47)

**Iblis was of the jinn; the partners do not answer (Surah 18:50-59)**
- Iblis was one of the jinn and transgressed his Lord's command (18:50)
- Iblis has offspring (dhurriyya) whom people take as protectors (18:50)
- Called on at the judgment, the false partners do not answer; a place of perdition is set between them (18:52)
- Man is the most contentious of all things (18:54)
- Messengers are sent only as bearers of good news and warners (18:56)

**Moses and the servant of God at the meeting of the two seas (Surah 18:60-82)**
- Moses vows to travel until he reaches the meeting of the two seas (18:60, 18:61)
- The travelers' provision fish comes to life and slips away into the sea at the destined place (18:61, 18:63)
- A forgetting is blamed on Satan (18:63)
- The travelers rest at a rock where the sign occurs (18:63)
- Realizing the sign, the travelers retrace their footsteps (18:64)
- A servant of God given mercy and knowledge from God's presence (ilm ladunni) (18:65)
- The sage holes the boat that carries them (18:71)
- The sage kills a boy they meet (18:74)
- The sage repairs a wall about to collapse in the inhospitable town without payment (18:77)
- After the third objection master and disciple part (18:72, 18:75, 18:76, 18:78)
- The sage explains the hidden reasons for his shocking acts (18:78, 18:79, 18:80, 18:81, 18:82)
- A king ahead seizes every sound ship by force, so the damaged boat is spared (18:79)
- A boy is killed lest he burden his believing parents with rebellion; God will give them a better child (18:80, 18:81)
- A wall shelters a treasure belonging to two orphans until they come of age (18:82)

**Dhul-Qarnayn, the setting and rising sun, and the barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-101)**
- At the place of sunset the conqueror finds the sun setting in a muddy (or hot) spring (18:86)
- The conqueror is given the choice to punish the people at the sunset or treat them kindly (18:86, 18:87, 18:88)
- At the sun's rising the conqueror finds a people with no shelter from it (18:90)
- Between two mountain barriers the conqueror finds a people who scarcely understand speech (18:93)
- A people complain that Gog and Magog spread corruption in the land (18:94)
- The people offer tribute for a barrier; the conqueror declines payment and asks for their labor (18:94, 18:95)
- A barrier of iron blocks filling the gap between two cliffs, heated with bellows and sealed with molten copper, shuts out Gog and Magog (18:95, 18:96, 18:97)
- When God's promise comes the barrier is leveled to the ground (18:98)
- At the end peoples surge into one another like waves (18:99)

**Those whose works are weightless; the sea as ink (Surah 18:102-110)**
- Hell is prepared as the unbelievers' hospitality (nuzul) (18:102)
- The greatest losers are those whose efforts went astray while they thought they did good (18:103, 18:104)
- The gardens of Firdaws (paradise) are the believers' hospitality (18:107)

**Zechariah's secret prayer and the birth of John (Surah 19:1-15)**
- A petitioner calls to God in a hidden, secret voice (19:3)
- Old man's prayer: 'my bones have weakened and my head is aflame with gray' (19:4)
- The childless priest fears for his kinsmen after him and asks for an heir to the family of Jacob (19:5, 19:6)
- The announced son receives a name never given to anyone before (19:7)
- The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old (19:8)
- As a sign of the promised son the father cannot speak to people for three days or nights (19:10, 19:11)
- The mute priest comes out of the sanctuary and signals to the people to glorify God (19:11)
- The child is given judgment and wisdom while still a boy (19:12)

**Mary, the spirit in human form, the birth under the palm, the speaking infant (Surah 19:16-40)**
- Mary withdraws from her family to an eastern place behind a screen (19:16, 19:17)
- The woman seeks refuge in God from the mysterious visitor (19:18)
- A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man (19:19, 19:20, 19:21)
- Labor pains drive the mother to the trunk of a palm tree (19:23)
- A voice from beneath her consoles the mother: 'do not grieve' (19:24)
- The mother returns with the child and her people accuse her of an enormity (19:27, 19:28)
- Mary is addressed as 'sister of Aaron' (19:28)
- The infant Jesus declares himself God's servant, given the Book and made a prophet (19:30)
- 'That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute' (19:34)
- The Day of Regret (yawm al-hasra) when the matter is decided (19:39)

**Abraham pleads with his father (Surah 19:41-50)**
- The son repeatedly and tenderly pleads with his idolatrous father ('O my father') (19:42, 19:43, 19:44, 19:45)
- The son tells his father that knowledge has come to him that has not come to the father (19:43)
- Worshipping idols is worshipping Satan, who rebelled against the Merciful (19:44)
- The idolatrous father threatens to stone his son and banishes him (19:46)
- Abraham withdraws from his people and their gods and is given descendants (19:48, 19:49)
- God grants the patriarchs a lofty 'tongue of truth' (lasting renown) (19:50)

**Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65)**
- Ishmael was true to his promise and enjoined prayer and alms on his family (19:54, 19:55)
- When the Merciful's verses are recited the prophets fall prostrate and weeping (19:58)
- In paradise the blessed receive their provision morning and evening (19:62)
- The angels say 'We descend only by your Lord's command' (19:64)
- God has no namesake or equal (samiyy) (19:65)

**Kneeling around hell, all will come to it; 'al-Rahman has taken a son' (Surah 19:66-98)**
- The deniers and the devils are gathered and brought kneeling around hell (19:68, 19:72)
- From every faction God draws out the one most insolent against the Merciful (19:69)
- Unbelievers boast that their side has the better station and finer assembly (19:73, 19:74)
- God lengthens the term of those in error until they see what they were promised (19:75)
- A denier boasts he will surely be given wealth and children (in the hereafter) (19:77, 19:78, 19:79, 19:80)
- Each person comes to God alone on the Day of Resurrection (19:80, 19:95)
- God sends devils against the unbelievers to goad them on (19:83)
- The pious are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation while the guilty are driven to hell like thirsty herds (19:85, 19:86)
- They say 'al-Rahman has taken a son'; it is not fitting for the Merciful (19:88, 19:91, 19:92)
- Everyone in the heavens and earth comes to the Merciful only as a servant (19:93, 19:94)
- The Merciful will appoint love (wudd) for those who believe and do good (19:96)
- God made the scripture easy in the prophet's own tongue to give good news and warn (19:97)
- Of the destroyed generations not one can be perceived nor a whisper heard (19:98)

**Ta Ha, the purpose of the revelation and the throne**
- The revelation was not sent down to make the prophet miserable but as a reminder (20:2, 20:3)

**Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa**
- The Hour is coming; God almost keeps it hidden so each soul is repaid for its striving (20:15)
- Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs (20:17, 20:18)
- Prophet prays for his chest to be expanded and the knot of his tongue untied (20:25, 20:26, 20:27, 20:28)

**God recalls his favors to Moses from infancy to Midian**
- Moses stays years among the people of Midian before his call (20:40)

**Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians**
- The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear (20:44)
- Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance' (20:47)
- Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book (20:51, 20:52)
- From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again (20:55)
- The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled (20:59)

**Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf**
- God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment (20:83, 20:84)
- Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns (20:90, 20:91)
- In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother' (20:92, 20:93, 20:94)
- Aaron explains he feared being blamed for dividing the children of Israel (20:94)
- The calf-maker took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger and cast it in (20:96)
- The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast (20:97)
- The calf is burned and its remains scattered in the sea (yamm) (20:97)

**The trumpet, the leveled mountains and the hushed judgment**
- The guilty are gathered on that day blue-eyed or bleary (zurq) (20:102)
- On the last day God scatters the mountains as dust and leaves a level, featureless plain (20:105, 20:106, 20:107)

**Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent**
- God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve (20:115)
- In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat (20:118, 20:119)
- The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' (20:120)
- Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten (20:124, 20:125, 20:126)

**Destroyed generations, patience, prayer times and waiting**
- Appeal to 'the former scrolls' (al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā) as evidence (20:133)

**The reckoning approaches; mortal messengers and destroyed towns**
- The doomed townsfolk run from God's onslaught and are told mockingly to return to their luxuries; they become mown stubble (21:12, 21:13, 21:14, 21:15)

**The split heavens, water of life, orbits, mortality and the scales**
- The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) (21:30)
- Man was created of haste (21:37)

**Abraham breaks the idols and is cast into the fire**
- God commands the fire: 'Be coolness and peace upon Abraham' (21:69)
- Abraham and Lot are rescued to the land God blessed for all peoples (21:71)

**Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind**
- David and Solomon judge a case of sheep that strayed by night into a field; Solomon is given the right understanding (21:78, 21:79)

**One community, Gog and Magog, the rolled heaven and the Zabur's promise**
- The idolaters and what they worship are fuel (ḥaṣab) for hell (21:98, 21:99)
- On the day of the great terror the angels meet the righteous: 'This is your day that you were promised' (21:103)
- The prophet was sent only as a mercy to the worlds (21:107)

**The quake of the Hour and the proofs from embryo and rain**
- Some are returned to the most abject age so that after knowing they know nothing (22:5)

**Those who dispute about God and those who worship on an edge**
- Some worship God 'on an edge': content in good fortune, turning away when tested (22:11)
- Taunt: whoever thinks God will not help him, let him stretch a rope to the sky, then cut it, and see if his rage is removed (22:15)

**Six communities judged; all things prostrate; garments of fire and bracelets of gold**
- God will judge between believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magians and polytheists on resurrection day (22:17)
- Hooked maces of iron (maqāmiʿ) drive back those who try to escape hell (22:21, 22:22)

**Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice**
- The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert (22:25)
- Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine (22:27)
- Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq) (22:29, 22:33)
- Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind (22:31)
- Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them (22:36)
- Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer (22:37)

**Permission to fight; the houses of worship protected**
- Permission to fight is given to those wronged and expelled from their homes for saying 'Our Lord is God' (22:39, 22:40)
- Were God not to check people by others, monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques would be destroyed (22:40)

**Rejected prophets, ruined towns, the thousand-year day and Satan's insertion**
- Destroyed towns lie fallen on their roofs, with an abandoned well and a lofty palace (22:45)
- It is not the eyes that are blind but the hearts within the breasts (22:46)
- Satan casts something into every prophet's recitation or wish; God abrogates it and confirms his verses (22:52, 22:53)

**Migrants provided for; the night and day, the held sky, a rite for every nation**
- Those who emigrated for God and were killed or died will receive a fine provision (22:58, 22:59)
- God holds back the sky from falling onto the earth except by his leave (22:65)

**The parable of the fly; messengers from angels and men; the religion of Abraham**
- Parable: those invoked besides God could not create a fly even together, nor recover what a fly snatches from them (22:73, 22:74)
- God chooses messengers from among the angels and from among humans (22:75)

**The successful believers who inherit Firdaws**
- The righteous inherit al-Firdaws (paradise, from Persian pairidaēza) forever (23:10, 23:11)

**Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships**
- God called 'the best of creators' (aḥsan al-khāliqīn) (23:14)
- A tree springing from Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Saynāʾ) yields oil and a relish for eaters (23:20)
- Cattle are a lesson: God gives drink from what is in their bellies (23:21)

**Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven**
- God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned (23:27)
- The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place (23:28, 23:29)

**A later generation's messenger, the Cry, and messengers in succession**
- A people is seized by the Cry (al-ṣayḥa) and made like flood-scum (23:41)
- God sent his messengers one after another; each was denied and each nation became a tale (23:42, 23:43, 23:44)

**Moses and Aaron rejected; the son of Mary and his mother on a height**
- God gave Mary and her son refuge on a height (rabwa) with a resting place and a flowing spring (23:50)

**Repel evil with good; the deathbed plea, the barzakh and the scales**
- Seek refuge in God from the goadings of the devils and from their presence (23:97, 23:98)
- At death the sinner begs 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do good'; it is refused (23:99, 23:100)
- Behind the dead is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised (23:100)
- When the trumpet is blown there will be no ties of kinship between them, nor will they ask after one another (23:101)
- God tells the damned pleading to leave hell: 'Be driven away into it and do not speak to me' (23:106, 23:107, 23:108)
- The damned had taken the believers as a laughingstock; now the believers triumph (23:109, 23:110, 23:111)

**Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath**
- The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers (24:2)
- A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers (24:3)
- A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath (24:6, 24:7, 24:8, 24:9)

**The affair of the lie (ifk) against a chaste woman**
- A band spreads a lie (ifk) against a chaste believing woman; the community is rebuked for not dismissing it (24:11, 24:12, 24:15, 24:16)
- The wealthy must not swear to stop giving to kin, the poor and emigrants, but pardon and overlook (24:22)
- Corrupt women are for corrupt men and good women for good men (24:26)

**Entering houses, lowering the gaze, head-coverings, marriage and manumission**
- Do not enter others' houses until you have asked leave and greeted the household; if told to go back, go back (24:27, 24:28, 24:29)
- Believing men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard their private parts (24:30, 24:31)
- Believing women draw their head-coverings (khumur) over their bosoms and do not show adornment except to listed kin (24:31)
- Marry off the unmarried among you and your righteous slaves; God will enrich the poor (24:32, 24:33)
- Grant slaves who ask a written manumission contract (kitāba) and give them of God's wealth (24:33)

**The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures**
- God is the light of the heavens and the earth (24:35)
- God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light (24:35)
- In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening (24:36, 24:37)
- The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there (24:39)
- Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand (24:40)
- God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight (24:43)

**Hypocrites and the call to judgment; 'we hear and obey'; the promise of succession**
- God promises the believers succession (istikhlāf) in the land as he gave it to those before them, exchanging fear for security (24:55)

**Times of privacy, elderly women, eating in kin houses, leave from the messenger**
- Slaves and children must ask permission at three times of undress: before dawn prayer, at noon and after the night prayer (24:58, 24:59)
- Elderly women past hope of marriage may lay aside their outer garments without displaying adornment (24:60)
- No blame on the blind, lame, sick or anyone eating in the houses of listed relatives or friends, together or apart (24:61)
- Do not address the messenger as you address one another, nor slip away without his leave (24:62, 24:63)

**The Criterion sent down; charges of forgery and the prophet who eats in markets**
- Opponents claim the prophet had old tales written down and dictated to him morning and evening, with others helping him (25:4, 25:5)
- Opponents object that the messenger eats food and walks in the markets, with no angel, treasure or garden (25:7, 25:8)

**Raging hell, the disowning of false gods, the split sky and the regretful wrongdoer**
- Thrown chained into a narrow place of hell, the damned cry for annihilation (thubūr) (25:13, 25:14)
- Unbelievers demand that angels be sent down or that they see their Lord (25:21)
- God turns the unbelievers' deeds into scattered dust (habāʾ manthūr) (25:23)
- On that day the wrongdoer bites his hands, wishing he had not taken so-and-so as a friend (25:27, 25:28, 25:29)
- God appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the guilty (25:31)
- Unbelievers ask why the Quran was not sent down all at once; it is sent in stages to strengthen the prophet's heart (25:32)
- The damned are gathered on their faces to hell (25:34)

**Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town**
- The 'People of the Rass' (aṣḥāb al-rass, the well) named among destroyed peoples (25:38)
- Most unbelievers are like cattle, or even further astray (25:44)

**The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations**
- God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently (25:45, 25:46)
- God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage (25:54)
- Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?' (25:60)

**The virtues of the servants of the Merciful**
- The servants of the Merciful walk humbly on the earth and answer the ignorant with 'Peace' (25:63)
- The righteous spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord (25:64)
- When they spend they are neither extravagant nor stingy, but in between (25:67)
- For the repentant God changes their evil deeds into good deeds (25:70, 25:71)
- Prayer: grant us from our spouses and offspring the comfort of our eyes (25:74)
- The righteous are rewarded with the lofty chamber (al-ghurfa) and greeted with peace (25:75, 25:76)

**Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains**
- Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?' (26:18, 26:19)
- Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear (26:20, 26:21)
- Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh (26:29)
- Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān) (26:32)
- The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh' (26:44)
- Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him (26:54, 26:55)
- God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them (26:57, 26:58, 26:59)

**Abraham's argument against idols and his prayer**
- Abraham's creed: the God who created and guides me, feeds and gives drink, heals me when sick, causes me to die and revives me, and will forgive me (26:78, 26:79, 26:80, 26:81, 26:82)
- Abraham prays for 'a tongue of truthfulness' (good repute) among later generations (26:84)
- The deluded and all the hosts of Iblis are hurled headlong into hell (26:94, 26:95)
- In hell the damned dispute with the gods they equated with God and wish for another chance (26:96, 26:97, 26:98, 26:99, 26:100, 26:101, 26:102)

**Noah, the lowly followers and the laden ark**
- The people threaten to stone the prophet if he does not desist (26:116)

**Hud and the monument-building people of Ad**
- The people of ʿĀd build a monument on every height and take fortresses (maṣāniʿ) hoping to live forever (26:128, 26:129)

**Lot and his people**
- Lot's family is saved except an old woman among those who stayed behind (26:171)

**Shuayb and the People of the Thicket; the day of the canopy**
- Shuʿayb commands full measure and weighing with the straight balance, and not defrauding people (26:181, 26:182, 26:183)
- Unbelievers challenge the prophet to make pieces of the sky fall on them (26:187)
- The People of the Thicket are destroyed by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy/Shadow (yawm al-ẓulla) (26:189)

**The Trustworthy Spirit, the scriptures of the ancients, devils, kin and poets**
- The Trustworthy Spirit (al-rūḥ al-amīn) brought the revelation down upon the prophet's heart (26:193, 26:194)
- The Quran is in the scriptures (zubur) of the ancients and known to the learned of the Children of Israel (26:196, 26:197)
- Devils did not bring down the revelation; they are barred from overhearing heaven (26:210, 26:211, 26:212)
- The prophet is told to warn his nearest kinsfolk (26:214)
- The devils descend upon every sinful liar, passing on what they overhear, mostly lies (26:221, 26:222, 26:223)
- Poets are followed by the deluded, wander in every valley and say what they do not do, except the believing poets (26:224, 26:225, 26:226, 26:227)

**Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs**
- At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it' (27:8)

**Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba**
- Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship) (27:15, 27:16)
- Solomon announces 'We have been taught the speech of birds (manṭiq al-ṭayr)' (27:16)
- Solomon's hosts of jinn, men and birds are mustered in ordered ranks (27:17)
- In the Valley of the Ants an ant warns the ants to enter their dwellings lest Solomon's army crush them unawares; Solomon smiles and laughs (27:18, 27:19)
- Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous (27:19)
- Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse (27:20, 27:21)
- The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked (27:22)
- The hoopoe found a woman ruling Sheba, given everything, with a mighty throne (27:23)
- The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God (27:24)
- Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply (27:28)
- Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission (27:29, 27:30, 27:31)
- The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion (27:35, 27:36, 27:37)
- An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat (27:38, 27:39)
- One with knowledge of the Book brings the throne before Solomon's glance returns to him (27:40)
- Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it' (27:41, 27:42)
- Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs (27:44)
- The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds (27:44)

**Salih, the evil omen and the nine plotters of Thamud**
- The people say they augur ill (iṭṭayyarnā) of the prophet; he answers that their omen (ṭāʾir) is with God (27:47)

**Lot and the people who expel the pure**
- Lot's people mock his family as 'people who keep themselves pure' and order their expulsion (27:56)

**The Quran and Israel's disputes; the beast of the earth, the trumpet and the sacred town**
- The Quran relates to the Children of Israel most of what they differ about (27:76)
- At the end God brings forth a beast from the earth that speaks to people (27:82)
- At the trumpet all in heaven and earth are terrified except whom God wills (27:87)
- You think the mountains firm, yet they pass like clouds (27:88)
- The prophet worships the Lord of 'this town' which God made sacred (27:91)

**Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water**
- Pharaoh exalted himself and divided the land's people into factions, oppressing one group (28:4)
- God wills to favor the oppressed and make them leaders (aʾimma) and inheritors (28:5, 28:6)
- Moses' mother's heart becomes empty and she nearly discloses him, but God steadies her heart (28:10)

**Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian**
- When Moses reached his full strength God gave him judgment and knowledge (28:14)
- Moses calls his killing 'the work of Satan' and asks forgiveness, which is granted (28:15, 28:16, 28:17)
- A man comes running from the far end of the city to warn the hero that the chiefs plot to kill him (28:20)

**At the water of Midian; the two women, their old father and the marriage contract**
- One of the women comes walking shyly to invite the hero to her father, who will reward him (28:25)
- The daughter advises: 'The best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy' (28:26)
- The father offers one of his two daughters in marriage for eight years' service, ten if the groom wishes (28:27, 28:28)

**The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper**
- Moses is called from the tree on the right bank of the valley, in the blessed spot (28:30)
- Moses says his brother Aaron is more eloquent of tongue and asks for him as a helper to confirm him (28:34)

**Pharaoh, 'no god but me', Haman's tower of fired brick, and the drowning**
- Pharaoh's people are made leaders who call to the Fire and are cursed in this world (28:41, 28:42)

**The prophet was not there; the two books; believing People of the Book**
- The prophet was not present on the western side of the mount or among the Midianites; the knowledge is a mercy from God (28:44, 28:45, 28:46)
- Opponents call the Torah and the Quran 'two sorceries supporting each other' (28:48)
- Challenge: bring a book from God more guiding than these two and I will follow it (28:49)
- Those given the Book before who believe in the Quran, being muslims already, receive their reward twice (28:52, 28:53, 28:54)
- 'To us our deeds and to you yours; peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant' (28:55)
- The prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God guides whom he wills (28:56)
- God established a safe sanctuary (ḥaram) to which fruits of every kind are brought (28:57)

**Towns destroyed for ingratitude; 'Where are my partners?'; perpetual night and day**
- God does not destroy towns until he sends a messenger to their mother-town (28:59)
- If God made the night or the day perpetual until resurrection, what god could bring the other? (28:71, 28:72, 28:73)

**Qarun's treasures and his swallowing by the earth; closing**
- Qārūn (Korah) of Moses' people was given treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men (28:76)
- Qārūn says his wealth came to him through knowledge he possesses (28:78)
- God who imposed the Quran will bring the prophet back to a place of return (maʿād) (28:85)

**Believers tested; parents and idolatry; the false offer to carry sins**
- Unbelievers offer to carry the believers' sins if they follow their way; they cannot, and will carry their own loads and others' besides (29:12, 29:13)

**Abraham preaches against idols, is saved from the fire, and Lot believes**
- The idols own no provision (rizq) for their worshippers; seek provision from God (29:17)
- Idols are taken only as a bond of affection among people in this life; on the Day they will disown and curse one another (29:25)

**Lot and the destruction of his town**
- Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi) (29:29)
- The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them (29:33)

**Midian, Ad, Thamud, Korah, Pharaoh and Haman punished**
- The prophet Shu'ayb is sent to his kin, the people of Midian (Madyan) (29:36)

**Recite the Book; dispute with the People of the Book; the unlettered prophet**
- Prayer (salat) restrains from indecency and wrongdoing, and remembrance of God is greater (29:45)
- Argue with the People of the Book only in the best manner; say 'our God and your God is one' (29:46)

**God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary**
- God made a secure sanctuary (haram amin) while people around are snatched away (29:67)

**The Romans defeated and the promise of their victory**
- Prophecy: the Romans (al-Rum) have been defeated in the nearest land but will triumph within a few years (30:2, 30:3, 30:4)

**The Hour, the times of praise, and the signs of God**
- God created mates for humans from their own selves so they may find rest in them, with love and mercy between them (30:21)
- The diversity of human languages and colors is one of God's signs (30:22)
- Everything in the heavens and the earth is devoutly obedient (qanit) to God (30:26)

**The slave-partner parable, the fitra, and the social duties**
- Parable: you would not make your slaves equal partners in your wealth; how then make God's creatures his partners? (30:28)
- The fitra: God's original pattern on which he created humankind, the upright (hanif) religion; no change to God's creation (30:30)
- Usury (riba) given to increase people's wealth does not increase with God, but alms (zakat) seeking his face are multiplied (30:39)
- Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned (30:41)

**Luqman's advice to his son**
- Luqman, a sage given wisdom by God, instructs his son (31:12, 31:13)
- Associating partners with God (shirk) is a tremendous wrong (31:13)
- The mother carried the child in weakness upon weakness and his weaning is in two years (31:14)
- Even a deed the weight of a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or in heaven or earth, God will bring it forth (31:16)
- Do not turn your cheek away from people in scorn or walk proudly on the earth; be modest in your walk (31:18, 31:19)
- Lower your voice: the most repugnant of voices is the braying of donkeys (31:19)

**God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows**
- If all trees were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, were ink, God's words would not be exhausted (31:27)
- Creating and resurrecting all of you is for God like a single soul (31:28)
- Waves overwhelm the ship like canopies (zulal) (31:32)

**Al-Sajda: creation, the angel of death, and the two fates**
- A divine day whose measure is a thousand (or fifty thousand) years of human reckoning (32:5)
- Whenever the damned try to get out of the fire they are driven back into it (32:20)
- God makes people taste the nearer punishment before the greater one, that they may return (32:21)
- On the Day of the Opening/Victory (al-fath) the unbelievers' faith will not benefit them (32:28, 32:29)

**Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers**
- God took a solemn covenant (mithaq) from the prophets: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary (33:7, 33:8)

**The confederates besiege Medina; hypocrites and the faithful**
- Hypocrites ask leave to quit the battle line saying 'our houses are exposed', wanting only to flee (33:12, 33:13, 33:14)
- Fleeing will not save you from death or killing; you would enjoy life only a little (33:16)
- In the messenger of God you have an excellent example (uswa hasana) (33:21)
- Among the believers are men who fulfilled their covenant with God; some have met their end (qada nahbah) and some still wait (33:23)

**The prophet's wives, the people of the House, and the believers men and women**
- The prophet's wives are given the choice between worldly adornment (with release and gift) and God and the hereafter (33:28, 33:29)

**Zayd's wife, the seal of the prophets, and the prophet as a lamp**
- The greeting of the righteous in the hereafter is 'Peace' (salam) (33:44)

**Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks**
- A wife divorced before consummation owes no waiting period ('idda); give her a gift and release her gracefully (33:49)
- Special marriage rules for the prophet: lawful wives, captives, named cousins who emigrated, and a woman who gives herself; afterwards no more wives (33:50, 33:51, 33:52)
- Enter the prophet's houses only when invited to a meal and leave after; ask his wives from behind a curtain (hijab) (33:53)

**The Hour, the blaming of leaders, Moses cleared, and the Trust**
- In hell the faces of the damned are turned over in the fire (33:66)
- Those who hurt Moses: God cleared him of what they said (33:69)

**Praise, the atom's weight, and mockery of resurrection**
- Praise belongs to God in this world and the hereafter (34:1)

**David's mountains and mail; Solomon's wind, copper, jinn and staff**
- God made a spring of molten copper (or brass) flow for Solomon (34:12)
- Solomon dies leaning on his staff; only a creature of the earth gnawing the staff reveals his death when he falls (34:14)
- The jinn did not know the unseen, else they would not have stayed in humiliating labor (34:14)

**Sheba's two gardens and the bursting of the dam**
- Sheba (Saba') had a sign in their dwelling: two gardens to the right and left, a good land (34:15)
- Between Sheba and the blessed towns God set visible towns and measured stages for safe travel by night and day (34:18)
- Sheba asks 'Lengthen the distances between our journeys', and God makes them bygone tales and scatters them utterly (34:19)
- Iblis found his opinion of humans to be true; they followed him except a party of believers (34:20, 34:21)

**Partners own nothing; intercession; the weak and the arrogant at judgment**
- When terror is lifted from their hearts they ask 'what did your Lord say?' and answer 'The truth' (34:23)

**The affluent reject warners; angels disown jinn-worshippers; the prophet is not mad**
- Wealth and children do not bring you near to God, only faith and good works (34:37)
- On the Day God asks the angels whether people worshipped them; they disown them: 'they worshipped the jinn' (34:40, 34:41)
- Stand up for God in twos or singly, then reflect: your companion is not mad (34:46)

**The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas**
- God made the angels messengers with wings in twos, threes and fours, adding to creation what he wills (35:1)
- Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he calls his party to the blaze (35:6)
- To God ascends the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up (35:10)

**No soul bears another's burden; the blind and the seeing; the colors of creation**
- There was no community but a warner passed among it (35:24)
- God brings forth fruits of varied colors, streaks in the mountains white, red and raven-black, and varied colors in people and beasts (35:27, 35:28)
- Only those of his servants who have knowledge truly fear God (35:28)

**The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned**
- Heirs of the Book are of three kinds: one who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one foremost in good deeds (35:32)
- God made humans successors (khala'if) on the earth (35:39)

**The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running**
- A man comes running from the farthest part of the city urging his people to follow the messengers (36:20, 36:21, 36:22, 36:23, 36:24, 36:25)
- The believer is told 'enter the Garden' and says 'Would that my people knew how my Lord forgave me' (36:26, 36:27)

**Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship**
- The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness (36:37)
- God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk (36:39)
- A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride (36:41, 36:42)
- Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?' (36:47)

**The trumpet, the sleepers raised, the Garden and the witnessing limbs**
- The people of the Garden recline with their spouses in shade on couches (ara'ik), with fruit and whatever they ask (36:55, 36:56, 36:57)
- 'Peace': a word from a merciful Lord to the blessed (36:58)
- 'Separate yourselves today, you guilty ones!' (36:59)
- God's covenant with the children of Adam: do not serve Satan; serve me, this is a straight path (36:60, 36:61, 36:62)
- Whomever God gives long life he reverses in creation (returns to weakness) (36:68)
- God did not teach the prophet poetry, nor is it fitting for him; it is a reminder and a clear Quran (36:69, 36:70)

**Who revives rotten bones? Fire from the green tree; Be and it is**
- The skeptic asks 'Who will give life to bones when they have rotted?'; the answer: he who produced them the first time (36:78, 36:79)

**The ranks, the guarded heaven and the shooting stars**
- Opening oath by those ranged in ranks, those who drive (or rebuke), and those who recite the reminder (37:1, 37:2, 37:3)
- Devils cannot listen to the Exalted Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la); any who snatch a word are pursued by a piercing flame (shihab) (37:8, 37:9, 37:10)
- 'This is the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din), the Day of Sorting (yawm al-fasl) which you denied' (37:20, 37:21)

**The damned questioned; the blessed on facing couches; the tree of Zaqqum**
- Gather the wrongdoers, their mates and what they worshipped and lead them to the path of hell; stop them, they will be questioned (37:22, 37:23, 37:24)
- The blessed sit on couches facing one another (37:44)
- Beside them are wide-eyed maidens of restrained glance, as if they were sheltered eggs (37:48, 37:49)
- The blessed will not die except their first death and will not be punished (37:58, 37:59)

**Noah called and was answered**
- Noah called to God and God answered, saving him and his family from the great distress (37:75, 37:76)

**Abraham, the stars, the smashed idols and the fire**
- Abraham glances at the stars and says 'I am sick', so his people leave him behind (37:88, 37:89, 37:90)
- Abraham asks the idols 'Will you not eat? Why do you not speak?' and strikes them with his right hand (37:91, 37:92, 37:93)
- The people build a structure (bunyan) and cast Abraham into the blaze, but God makes them the lowest (37:97, 37:98)

**Abraham's dream and the near-sacrifice of his son**
- The father sees in a dream that he is sacrificing his son (37:102)
- When both had submitted he laid him on his forehead (talla-hu li-l-jabin) (37:103)
- God ransomed the son with a great sacrifice (dhibh 'azim) (37:107)
- The son of the sacrifice is not named; Isaac's birth is announced only after the episode (read as Ishmael by many exegetes) (37:112, 37:113)

**Moses and Aaron; Elias against Ba'l**
- The prophet's name appears in variant form ('Il Yasin') for rhyme (37:130)

**Lot's old woman; Jonah and the fish**
- The hearers pass by the ruins of Lot's people morning and night (37:137, 37:138)
- Jonah ran away (abaqa, as a runaway slave) to the laden ship (37:140)
- Had Jonah not been among those who glorify God he would have stayed in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection (37:144)
- The fish casts the prophet onto a barren shore while he is sick (37:145)
- Jonah is sent to a hundred thousand or more; they believe and are granted enjoyment for a while (37:148)

**Daughters of God denied; the angels' stations; closing doxology**
- Idolaters claim a kinship (nasab) between God and the jinn; the jinn know they will be brought to judgment (37:158)

**Sad: the chiefs marvel at one God; the confederates of old**
- Opponents say 'We did not hear of this in the latest religion (al-milla al-akhira); it is a fabrication' (38:7)

**David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes**
- Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him (38:21, 38:22)
- A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument (38:23)

**Solomon's steeds, the body on his throne, and the unmatched kingdom**
- Fine steeds shown to Solomon in the evening distract him from remembrance of God until the sun hides; he has them brought back and strokes (or slashes) their legs and necks (38:31, 38:32, 38:33)
- God tested Solomon by placing a body (jasad) on his throne; then he repented (38:34)
- Solomon asks for a kingdom such as no one after him should have (38:35)
- Devils serve Solomon as builders and divers, and others are bound together in fetters (38:37, 38:38)

**Job, the spring and the bundle of twigs**
- Job calls to his Lord: 'Satan has touched me with weariness and torment' (38:41)
- Job is told to stamp with his foot: a cool spring to wash in and drink appears (38:42)
- God gives Job back his family and as many again with them (38:43)
- Job is told to take a bundle of grass or twigs (dighth) in his hand and strike with it, so as not to break his oath (38:44)

**The chosen patriarchs; the Gardens of Eden and the quarrel of the damned**
- Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are 'possessors of hands and sight' (power and insight) (38:45, 38:46, 38:47)
- Ishmael is named among the chosen prophets (38:48)
- Elisha (al-Yasa') is named among the excellent (38:48)
- The provision of paradise never runs out (38:54)
- The damned ask 'Why do we not see men we counted among the wicked, whom we mocked?' (38:62, 38:63, 38:64)
- The prophet had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed (over Adam) (38:69)

**Adam made from clay; Iblis refuses and is granted respite**
- Iblis swears by God's might to lead all humans astray except God's sincere servants (38:82, 38:83)
- The prophet asks no wage and is not one of the pretenders (mutakallifin) (38:86)

**Pure religion; no son for God; creation from one soul in three darknesses**
- Idolaters say 'we worship them only that they may bring us near to God' (39:3)
- Had God wished to take a son he would have chosen from what he creates whatever he willed; glory be to him, the One (39:4)
- God sent down for you eight pairs of livestock (39:6)

**The first of those who submit; canopies of fire; chambers above chambers**
- The damned have canopies (zulal) of fire above them and below them (39:16)
- For the godfearing are lofty chambers with built chambers above them, beneath which rivers flow (39:20)
- An Arabic Quran without any crookedness (39:28)

**The prophet's mortality; souls taken in sleep; intercession belongs to God**
- All intercession belongs to God (39:43, 39:44)
- When God alone is mentioned the hearts of unbelievers shrink with aversion; at mention of others they rejoice (39:45)

**Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden**
- Lest a soul say 'Alas for my neglect of God' or 'If only I had another chance (karra)' (39:56, 39:57, 39:58)
- If you associate partners with God your deeds will come to nothing (39:65)
- At the first trumpet blast all in heaven and earth swoon (sa'iqa) except whom God wills; at the second they stand looking (39:68)
- The Book (record) is laid down, the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed with truth (39:69, 39:70)
- Unbelievers are driven to hell in throngs (zumar) and the godfearing to the Garden in throngs; the gates open and the keepers address each (39:71, 39:73)
- The keepers of the Garden greet the righteous 'Peace be upon you, you have been good; enter' (39:73)
- The blessed praise God who gave them the land (ard) as inheritance to settle in the Garden where they will (39:74)
- The angels are seen surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord (39:75)

**Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers**
- God as Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty (string of divine epithets) (40:3)
- The damned say 'Lord, you caused us to die twice and gave us life twice; we confess our sins; is there a way out?' (40:11)
- God casts the Spirit (al-ruh) of his command upon whom he wills of his servants to warn of the Day of Meeting (40:15)
- The Day of the Approaching (al-azifa) when hearts reach the throats, choking (40:18)

**Moses, Pharaoh, Haman and the believer of Pharaoh's family**
- Moses is sent to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, who call him 'a lying sorcerer' (40:23, 40:24)
- After Moses comes, Pharaoh's people order: kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women (40:25)
- Pharaoh says 'Let me kill Moses and let him call on his Lord; I fear he will change your religion' (40:26)
- Argument of caution: if he is a liar his lie is upon him; if truthful, some of what he threatens will strike you (40:28)
- The Day of Mutual Calling (yawm al-tanad) (40:32, 40:33)
- Joseph had come to the Egyptians with clear proofs; when he died they said God would send no messenger after him (40:34)
- Pharaoh's people are exposed to the Fire morning and evening (before the Hour), then made to enter the severest punishment (40:45, 40:46)
- The damned ask the keepers of hell to pray their Lord to lighten the punishment by a day; they are told 'then pray yourselves' (40:49, 40:50)

**Ha-Mim Fussilat: the veil between; creation in days; heaven as smoke**
- Rejecters say 'our hearts are in coverings, in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a veil (hijab)' (41:5)
- 'I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God' (41:6)
- God created the earth in two days, set mountains and measured its provisions in four days, then made the seven heavens in two days (41:9, 41:10, 41:12)
- God turned to the heaven while it was smoke (dukhan) (41:11)

**The thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud**
- Warning of a thunderbolt (sa'iqa) like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud (41:13, 41:17)
- God sent upon 'Ad a howling cold wind (sarsar) on ill-omened days (ayyam nahisat) (41:16)
- Thamud were guided but preferred blindness to guidance, and the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them (41:17)

**Skins testify; evil companions; the misled ask to trample their misleaders**
- At the fire their hearing, sight and skins testify against them; the skins answer 'God who gave speech to all things made us speak' (41:20, 41:21, 41:22)
- God assigned to them companions (quarana') who made their deeds seem fair (41:25)
- Unbelievers say 'Do not listen to this Quran; make noise (laghw) during it so you may prevail' (41:26)
- The damned ask to be shown the jinn and humans who misled them so they may put them beneath their feet (41:29)

**Angels descend on the steadfast; repel evil with good; signs on the horizons**
- Angels descend on those who say 'Our Lord is God' and stand firm: 'Fear not, grieve not, rejoice in the Garden' (41:30, 41:31, 41:32)
- Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon but to God who created them (41:37)
- Falsehood cannot approach the Book from before it or behind it (41:42)
- The Quran is guidance and healing (shifa') for believers; for others deafness and blindness (41:44)
- No fruit comes out of its sheath and no female conceives or gives birth but with God's knowledge (41:47)
- On the Day God calls 'Where are my partners?', they answer 'We declare to you none of us is a witness' (41:47, 41:48)
- Given relief, man says 'This is mine; I do not think the Hour will come, and if returned to my Lord I will have the best with him' (41:50)
- 'We will show them our signs on the horizons and in themselves until it is clear to them that it is the truth' (41:53)

**Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf: revelation, the angels' intercession and the one religion of the prophets**
- 'There is nothing like him' (laysa ka-mithlihi shay'), yet he is the Hearing, the Seeing (42:11)
- Perhaps the Hour is near; unbelievers mock and ask to hasten it, believers fear it (42:17, 42:18)
