- Whoever seeks the tillage (harth) of the hereafter has it increased; whoever seeks the tillage of this world gets some of it and no share hereafter (42:20)
- The prophet's only requested 'wage' is affection among kin (al-mawadda fi l-qurba) (42:23)

**Provision in measure, rain, ships like mountains and the ethics of consultation and pardon**
- God accepts repentance from his servants and pardons evil deeds (42:25)
- God has dispersed living creatures (dabba) in both the heavens and the earth and can gather them (42:29)
- The believers conduct their affairs by mutual consultation (shura) (42:38)
- Retaliation in kind is permitted, but whoever pardons and makes peace has his reward with God (42:40, 42:43)

**The damned seek a way back; God gives children as he wills; three ways God speaks to man**
- The damned, seeing the punishment, ask whether there is any way of return (to the world) (42:44)
- The wrongdoers are presented to the Fire humbled, looking with a stealthy glance (42:45)
- When man tastes mercy he exults; when evil strikes him for his deeds he is ungrateful (42:48)
- God speaks to a human only by inspiration (wahy), from behind a veil (hijab), or by sending a messenger (42:51)
- Before revelation the prophet did not know what the Book or faith was (42:52)
- The revelation is a spirit (ruh) from God's command and a light by which he guides (42:52)

**Ha-Mim: the Mother of the Book, the riding prayer and the 'daughters' of God**
- A formula of praise when mounting ship or beast: 'Glory to him who subjected this to us; we could not have done it' (43:12, 43:13, 43:14)
- When one of them is told of a daughter's birth, his face darkens and he chokes with grief (43:17)

**Abraham disowns his father's worship; the great man of the two towns; silver roofs; the devil-companion**
- But for fear all would become one community, God would give unbelievers houses with silver roofs, stairways, doors, couches and gold ornament (43:33, 43:34, 43:35)
- The damned wishes that between him and his companion lay 'the distance of the two easts' (43:38)

**Moses before Pharaoh: the laughing courtiers, the rivers beneath Pharaoh and the drowning**
- Each sign shown to Pharaoh's people was greater than the one before it (43:47, 43:48)
- Pharaoh scorns Moses as contemptible, barely able to speak, without gold bracelets or attending angels (43:52, 43:53)

**The son of Mary as an example and sign of the Hour; the Garden with golden dishes; Malik of hell**
- When the son of Mary is cited as an example, the opponents clamor and ask whether their gods or he are better (43:57, 43:58)
- Jesus is only a servant whom God favored and made an example for the Children of Israel (43:59)
- Jesus (or the revelation) is knowledge/a sign of the Hour (43:61)
- Jesus came with wisdom to make clear some of what they disputed and called them to worship God, 'my Lord and your Lord' (43:63, 43:64)
- On that day intimate friends become enemies to one another, except the God-fearing (43:67)
- The righteous enter the Garden with their spouses, made joyful (43:70)
- In paradise they are served with golden platters and cups, with all that souls desire and eyes delight in (43:71)
- The guilty remain in the punishment of Gehenna forever; it is not lightened for them and they despair (mublisun) (43:74, 43:75)
- The damned call on Malik, the keeper of hell, to ask God to end them, and he answers 'You will remain' (43:77)
- 'If the Merciful had a son, I would be the first of worshippers' (43:81)
- Those invoked besides God have no power of intercession, except one who bore witness to the truth (43:86)
- The prophet is told to turn away from the scoffers and say 'Peace' (salam), for they will come to know (43:89)

**Ha-Mim: the blessed night and the day of the smoke**
- The Book was sent down on a blessed night in which every wise matter is decreed/distinguished (cf. the Night of Decree) (44:3, 44:4, 44:5)
- Opponents call the prophet 'one taught (by others), a madman' (mu'allam majnun) (44:14)
- God lifts the punishment a little, but they revert; then comes 'the greatest assault' (al-batsha al-kubra) (44:15, 44:16)

**Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep**
- Moses is told to leave the sea parted and still (rahwan), for Pharaoh's host will be drowned (44:24)
- The drowned Egyptians left gardens, springs, crops and noble dwellings, which God gave another people to inherit (44:25, 44:26, 44:27, 44:28)
- Neither heaven nor earth wept over the destroyed people (44:29)

**Deniers demand their fathers; the people of Tubba'; the tree of Zaqqum; silk, brocade and the houris**
- The Day of Sorting/Decision (yawm al-fasl) is the appointed time for all (44:40)
- The blessed wear fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), facing one another on couches (44:53)
- God has made the revelation easy in the prophet's own tongue so they may remember (44:58)

**Ha-Mim: the signs, the scornful liar, Israel's book and the Prophet's shari'a**
- God has subjected (sakhkhara) to humans the sea and all that is in the heavens and on the earth (45:12, 45:13)
- Believers are to forgive those who do not look for 'the days of God'; God himself will requite (45:14)
- God gave the Children of Israel the Book, judgment (hukm) and prophethood, good provision, and preferred them over the worlds (45:16)
- God set the Prophet upon a clear way (shari'a) of the command, to follow and not the desires of the ignorant (45:18)

**Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book**
- God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did' (45:29)

**Ha-Mim: the idols created nothing; a witness from Israel; the Book of Moses**
- 'I am no novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you' (46:9)
- A witness from the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it and believes (46:10)
- Before it was the Book of Moses as a guide (imam) and mercy; this Arabic book confirms it (46:12)

**Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff'**
- God enjoins humans to be good to their parents (46:15)
- His mother bore him with hardship and delivered him with hardship; bearing and weaning take thirty months (46:15)
- On reaching full strength at forty, a man prays to be grateful for favor on himself and his parents and for righteous offspring (46:15)
- A son says 'Uff!' to his parents who plead with him, scorning resurrection as 'tales of the ancients' (46:17)

**Hud warns 'Ad at the dunes; the cloud that was not rain; the jinn listen to the Quran**
- The brother of 'Ad (Hud) warns his people at al-Ahqaf (the wind-curved sand dunes) (46:21)
- A destroyed people see a cloud approaching their valleys and say 'this cloud will give us rain', but it is the wind of punishment (46:24)
- A destroying wind wipes out everything at its Lord's command; in the morning only their dwellings are seen (46:24, 46:25)
- God destroyed the towns around the hearers, which serve as warning (46:27)
- A band of jinn listens to the Quran in silence and returns to warn their people (46:29)
- The jinn declare they heard a book sent down after Moses confirming what was before it (46:30, 46:31)
- The Prophet is told to be patient like 'the messengers of resolve' (ulu l-'azm) (46:35)
- On the day they see what was promised, it will seem they had tarried only an hour of a day (46:35)

**Muhammad: deeds nullified, striking necks and freeing captives, and the four rivers of the Garden**
- In battle, strike the necks of unbelievers; when they are subdued bind them, then free them as favor or for ransom until war lays down its burdens (47:4)
- Those killed in God's way: their deeds are not lost; he guides them and admits them to a Garden he has made known to them (47:4, 47:5, 47:6)
- The Garden has rivers of unstaling water, of milk unchanged in taste, of wine delightful to drinkers, and of purified honey (47:15)
- The damned are given boiling water to drink which tears their bowels apart (47:15)
- Some listen to the prophet and on leaving ask the learned 'What did he say just now?'; God has sealed their hearts (47:16)
- The signs/portents (ashrat) of the Hour have already come (47:18)
- The prophet is told to ask forgiveness for his own sin and for the believing men and women (47:19)

**The sick-hearted faint at the call to fight; locks on hearts; the twist of speech; God rich, you poor**
- When a decisive surah mentions fighting, those with sickness in their hearts look at the prophet like one fainting at death (47:20)
- Would you, if you turned away, cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship (arham)? (47:22)
- 'Do they not ponder the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?' (47:24)
- The hypocrites could be recognized by their marks (sima) and by the twist of their speech (lahn al-qawl) (47:29, 47:30)
- Do not weaken and call for peace when you are uppermost; God is with you (47:35)

**Al-Fath: the clear opening, the sakina, the hand of God over their hands and the bedouin who stayed behind**
- God forgives the prophet his past and future sins (48:2)
- To God belong the hosts (junud) of the heavens and the earth (48:4, 48:7)
- Those who pledge allegiance to the prophet pledge to God; 'the hand of God is over their hands' (48:10)
- The bedouin who stayed behind plead that wealth and families kept them busy and ask for forgiveness insincerely (48:11, 48:12)
- Those who stayed behind ask to follow when spoils are in prospect and are refused (48:15)
- No blame on the blind, the lame or the sick (for not going out to fight) (48:17)

**The pledge under the tree, the hidden believers in Mecca, the dream of entering the sanctuary, and the seed parable from Torah and Gospel**
- The unbelievers barred the believers from the Sacred Mosque and kept the sacrificial animals from reaching their place (48:25)
- But for unknown believing men and women in the city, whom you might have trampled unawares, God would have punished its unbelievers (48:25)
- The unbelievers set in their hearts fierce pride, 'the zealotry of the Jahiliyya', while God sent tranquillity on the believers (48:26)
- God fulfilled the prophet's vision: you will enter the Sacred Mosque in safety, heads shaved or hair cut short (48:27)
- The believers bear on their faces the mark (sima) from the traces of prostration (48:29)
- Their likeness in the Torah and the Gospel: a seed that puts forth its shoot, strengthens, grows stout and stands on its stem, delighting the sowers (48:29)

**Al-Hujurat: lowering voices, verifying reports, reconciling believers, backbiting and the peoples and tribes**
- Those who call the prophet from outside his private chambers (hujurat) lack understanding; they should wait until he comes out (49:4, 49:5)
- If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them; fight the one that transgresses until it returns to God's command (49:9)
- Let no people mock another, nor women other women, nor defame one another or insult with nicknames (49:11)
- The bedouin say 'we believe'; rather say 'we have submitted (aslamna)', for faith has not yet entered your hearts (49:14)
- They count their submission a favor to the prophet; rather God has done them a favor in guiding them (49:17)

**Qaf: wonder at the warner, the earth that consumes the dead, the sky without rifts and the destroyed peoples**
- The unbelievers marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves (50:2)
- Tall palm trees with spathes of layered dates (tal' nadid) as provision (50:10)
- The companions of al-Rass (the well/pit), a destroyed people (50:12)

**Nearer than the jugular vein; the two recorders; driver and witness; Gehenna says 'Is there more?'; creation in six days without weariness**
- Two receivers sit on the right and the left recording every word a person utters (50:17, 50:18)
- The stupor (sakra) of death comes with the truth: 'this is what you tried to avoid' (50:19)
- Every soul comes with a driver (sa'iq) and a witness (shahid) (50:21)
- At judgment the covering is removed from a person and his sight that day is sharp as iron (50:22)
- The damned man's companion (qarin) disputes before God: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress' (50:27, 50:28)
- The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing, not far off (50:31)
- 'Enter it in peace': the day of eternity; they have what they wish and more (mazid) with God (50:34, 50:35)
- God created the heavens and earth in six days and no weariness (lughub) touched him (50:38)
- On the day the caller calls from a place near at hand, and they hear the Cry (al-sayha): the day of coming forth (50:41, 50:42)
- The earth splits open from them and they hasten forth to the gathering (50:44)

**Al-Dhariyat: the oath by the winds, the conjecturers, the night-wakeful righteous and the beggar's due**
- Oath 'By the sky with its tracks/weaves (dhat al-hubuk)' (51:7)
- 'Perish the conjecturers (al-kharrasun)' who are heedless in a flood of ignorance (51:10, 51:11)
- God swears by the Lord of heaven and earth that it is as true as the fact that you speak (51:23)

**Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah**
- The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)' (51:24, 51:25)
- Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them (51:27, 51:28)
- The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim) (51:28)
- Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!' (51:29)
- On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones (51:41, 51:42)
- Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on (51:43, 51:44, 51:45)

**The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship**
- Of everything God created pairs (zawjayn) (51:49)
- 'So flee to God; I am to you a clear warner from him' (51:50)
- God created jinn and humans only to worship him; he wants no provision or food from them (51:56, 51:57, 51:58)
- The wrongdoers have a portion (dhanub, a bucketful) of punishment like that of their fellows (51:59)

**Al-Tur: the oath by the Mount, the inscribed parchment and the frequented House; the sky heaves**
- The sea 'set aflame' or 'filled to overflowing' (al-bahr al-masjur) at the end (52:6)
- The deniers are shoved into the Fire and asked 'Is this sorcery, or do you not see?'; patience or impatience is the same for them (52:13, 52:14, 52:15, 52:16)

**The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges**
- In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin (52:23)
- The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum) (52:25, 52:26, 52:27, 52:28)
- Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof (52:38)
- If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds' (52:44)
- 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes' (52:48)
- Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn) (52:48, 52:49)

**Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary**
- Oath 'By the star when it sets/falls (idha hawa)' (53:1)
- The heavenly figure came within two bow-lengths or nearer (qaba qawsayn aw adna) and revealed to his servant (53:9, 53:10)
- The heart did not falsify what it saw; the gaze did not swerve nor transgress (53:11, 53:17)
- He saw him at a second descent by the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), near the Garden of Refuge (53:13, 53:14, 53:15)
- When there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered it (an ineffable phenomenon) (53:16)

**Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius**
- The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected (53:19, 53:20)
- 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division' (53:21, 53:22)
- The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority (53:23)
- They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth (53:28)
- Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide (53:32)
- God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity (53:32)
- To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha) (53:42)
- God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted (53:45, 53:46)
- God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs (53:49)
- God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad) (53:50)
- 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?' (53:55)
- A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse) (53:62)

**Al-Qamar: the moon split, the dead like locusts, and Noah's ark of planks and fibres**
- Whenever they see a sign they turn away and say 'continuous/passing sorcery' (sihr mustamirr) (54:2)
- Noah, called a madman and driven off, prays 'I am overcome, so help me!' (54:9, 54:10)
- God opens the gates of heaven with pouring water and makes the earth burst with springs; the waters meet for a decreed matter (54:11, 54:12)
- Noah carried on a thing of planks and nails/fibres (dhat alwah wa-dusur), running under God's eyes (54:13, 54:14)
- God left the ark (or the event) as a sign: is there anyone who will remember? (54:15)

**Refrains over 'Ad, Thamud's she-camel, Lot's guests and Pharaoh; everything by measure; the seat of truth**
- A single Cry (sayha) is sent and they become like the dry stubble of a pen-builder (54:31)
- When they solicited Lot's guests, God obliterated their eyes (54:37)
- 'The host will be routed and turn their backs' (applied to Badr) (54:45)
- The guilty are dragged on their faces into the Fire: 'Taste the touch of Saqar' (54:48)
- God's command is but one, like a blink of the eye (54:50)
- The God-fearing are in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth with an all-powerful King (54:54, 54:55)

**Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier**
- The Merciful (al-Rahman) taught the Quran, created man and taught him clear speech (bayan) (55:1, 55:2, 55:3, 55:4)
- God raised the sky and set the Balance: do not transgress in the balance; weigh with justice and do not skimp (55:7, 55:8, 55:9)
- Lord of the two easts and the two wests (the solstitial sunrises and sunsets) (55:17)
- From the two seas come pearls and coral (marjan) (55:22)

**Passing the regions of heaven, the rose-red sky, forelocks and feet, and the two pairs of gardens with secluded maidens**
- 'We shall attend to you, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalan)' (55:31)
- When the sky is split open and becomes rose-red like (red) leather/oil dregs (55:37)
- The damned go round between Gehenna and seething boiling water (55:43, 55:44)
- For whoever fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens, with branches, two flowing springs and every fruit in pairs (55:46, 55:48, 55:50, 55:52)
- 'Is the reward of excellence anything but excellence?' (55:60)
- Below those, two further gardens, dark green (mudhammatan), with gushing springs, fruit, palms and pomegranates (55:62, 55:64, 55:66, 55:68)
- Houris secluded in pavilions/tents (khiyam) (55:72)
- Reclining on green cushions (rafraf) and beautiful 'abqari carpets (55:76)

**Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden**
- Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near (56:7, 56:8, 56:9, 56:10, 56:11)
- The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later (56:13, 56:14, 56:39, 56:40)
- Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring (56:17, 56:18)
- In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire (56:21)
- In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace' (56:25, 56:26)
- The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water (56:28, 56:29, 56:30, 56:31)
- God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age (56:35, 56:36, 56:37)

**The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat**
- The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind (56:41, 56:42, 56:43, 56:44)
- The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim) (56:45, 56:46)
- The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him) (56:54, 56:55)
- The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell (56:56, 56:93, 56:94)
- Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj) (56:68, 56:69, 56:70)
- 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew' (56:75, 56:76)
- A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified (56:77, 56:78, 56:79, 56:80)
- For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss (56:88, 56:89)

**Al-Hadid: First and Last, Outward and Inward; stewards of wealth; the goodly loan**
- God is the First and the Last, the Outward (al-zahir) and the Inward (al-batin) (57:3)
- God has taken your covenant (mithaq) (57:8)
- Those who spent and fought before the Victory are higher in rank than those who did so after (57:10)

**The believers' light, the hypocrites who would borrow it, and the wall with a gate; hearts hardened by long time**
- The hypocrites beg the believers 'Wait for us, that we may borrow some of your light' and are told 'Go back and seek light' (57:13)
- A wall with a gate is set between them: inside it mercy, outside it, facing, the punishment (57:13)
- Believers must not be like those given the Book before, whose term grew long and whose hearts hardened (57:16)

**Life like withering plants; the Garden as wide as heaven and earth; every calamity written; iron sent down; Jesus' followers and invented monasticism**
- Worldly life is play, adornment, boasting and rivalry in wealth and children, like rain whose growth pleases the sowers, then withers yellow and becomes chaff (57:20)
- God sent down iron, with mighty force and benefits for people (57:25)
- God gave Jesus son of Mary the Gospel (al-Injil) (57:27)
- God put compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed Jesus (57:27)
- Believers in the messenger receive a double portion (kiflayn) of God's mercy and a light to walk by (57:28)
- The People of the Book should know they have no power over God's bounty; bounty is in God's hand for whom he wills (57:29)

**Al-Mujadila: the woman who disputed, the zihar formula and its expiation; God the fourth of three; the party of God**
- God has heard the woman who argued with the prophet about her husband and complained to God (Khawla, 'she who disputes') (58:1)
- Expiation for zihar before touching again: free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor (58:3, 58:4)
- Secret counsels (najwa) for sin, aggression and disobedience are of Satan; confer rather in piety (58:8, 58:9, 58:10)
- They greet the prophet with a greeting with which God did not greet him (al-sam for al-salam) (58:8)
- When told to make room in assemblies, make room, and God will make room for you; rise when told to rise (58:11)
- Before a private consultation with the prophet give charity (sadaqa); the rule is then relaxed (58:12, 58:13)
- The party of Satan (hizb al-shaytan) are the losers; the party of God (hizb Allah) are the successful (58:19, 58:22)
- God has written: 'I will surely prevail, I and my messengers' (58:21)

**Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay'**
- God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr) (59:2)
- The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers (59:2)
- Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world (59:3)
- Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave (59:5)
- Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts (59:10)

**The hypocrites' false promises, Satan's disowning, the Quran on a mountain, and the litany of beautiful names**
- Hypocrites promise their unbelieving allies to leave or fight with them, but will not (59:11, 59:12)
- They fight only from fortified towns or behind walls; you think them united but their hearts are divided (59:13, 59:14)
- Like Satan who says to man 'Disbelieve!' and when he disbelieves says 'I am quit of you, I fear God' (59:16, 59:17)
- Let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (59:18)
- Those who forgot God, so he made them forget themselves (59:19)
- Had this Quran been sent down on a mountain you would see it humbled and split asunder for fear of God (59:21)

**Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge**
- Believers must not take God's enemies, who expelled the prophet, as allies (awliya') or secretly show them affection (60:1, 60:2, 60:9, 60:13)
- Abraham and those with him are an excellent example: they declared themselves quit of their people and their gods, with enmity until they believe (60:4, 60:6)
- Except Abraham's saying to his father 'I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you before God' (60:4)
- Believing women who emigrate are to be examined; if believers, they are not returned to the unbelievers, whose dowries are repaid (60:10)
- Do not hold on to marriage ties with unbelieving women; dowries are reckoned between the communities (60:10, 60:11)
- The women's pledge (bay'at al-nisa'): not to associate anything with God, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, bring a fabricated slander, or disobey in what is right (60:12)
- Prohibition of killing one's children (60:12)
- They despair of the hereafter as the unbelievers despair of those in the graves (60:13)

**Al-Saff: ranks like a solid structure; Moses hurt by his people; Jesus foretells Ahmad; the disciples as God's helpers**
- Jesus son of Mary confirms the Torah and announces a messenger to come after him named Ahmad (61:6)
- A trade (tijara) that saves from punishment: believe and strive in God's way with wealth and selves (61:10, 61:11)
- Goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden ('Adn) (61:12)

**Al-Jumu'a: the messenger among the unlettered, the donkey carrying books, wishing for death, and the Friday prayer**
- Those charged with the Torah who did not carry it are like a donkey carrying books (asfar) (62:5)
- Challenge to the Jews: if you claim to be God's friends apart from others, wish for death, if you are truthful; they never will (62:6, 62:7)
- When the call to prayer is made on Friday (yawm al-jumu'a), hasten to God's remembrance and leave trading; after the prayer disperse and seek God's bounty (62:9, 62:10)
- When they saw trade or amusement they rushed to it and left the prophet standing (62:11)

**Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay**
- The hypocrites testify 'You are God's messenger'; God knows he is, and testifies that the hypocrites are liars (63:1)
- It is the same whether the prophet asks forgiveness for the hypocrites or not; God will not forgive them (63:5, 63:6)
- The hypocrites say 'When we return to Medina the mightier will expel the meaner from it'; but might belongs to God, his messenger and the believers (63:8)
- Let not your wealth and children divert you from God's remembrance (63:9)
- Spend before death comes and one says 'My Lord, if only you would delay me a little, I would give charity'; God delays no soul when its term comes (63:10, 63:11)

**Al-Taghabun: forms made beautiful, the Day of Mutual Loss, enemies among wives and children, and the goodly loan**
- God created you, and among you are unbelievers and believers (64:2)
- Unbelievers rejected their messengers saying 'Shall mere humans guide us?' (64:6)
- The Day of Gathering is the Day of Mutual Dispossession / Loss and Gain (yawm al-taghabun) (64:9)
- No calamity strikes except by God's leave; whoever believes, God guides his heart (64:11)
- Among your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them; yet if you pardon and forgive, God is forgiving (64:14)
- Fear God as much as you are able (ma stata'tum) (64:16)

**Al-Talaq: divorce and the waiting period, two witnesses, nursing wages, and the seven heavens and earths**
- Divorce women at (the start of) their waiting period ('idda), count it, and do not expel them from their homes during it unless for flagrant indecency (65:1)
- At the end of the term, retain or part with them honorably, and call two just witnesses (65:2)
- Waiting period of three months for women past menses or not yet menstruating; for the pregnant, until delivery (65:4)
- House divorced wives as you live, support them while pregnant, and pay them if they nurse your child; otherwise another woman may nurse (65:6)
- God created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, the command descending between them (65:12)

**Al-Tahrim: the prohibited thing and the divulged secret; fire fed with stones; the wives of Noah and Lot, Pharaoh's wife and Mary daughter of 'Imran**
- 'O Prophet, why do you forbid what God made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives?'; God has ordained the dissolution of oaths (66:1, 66:2)
- The prophet confided a secret to one of his wives; she divulged it, and God informed him (66:3)
- If two wives back each other against him, God is his protector, and Gabriel, the righteous believers and the angels (66:4)
- If he divorced them, God might give him in exchange better wives: submitting, believing, devout, repentant, worshipping, fasting/wandering (sa'ihat), previously married and virgins (66:5)
- A Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are harsh, stern angels who never disobey God (66:6)
- Turn to God in sincere repentance (tawba nasuh) (66:8)
- The believers pray on the day: 'Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us' (66:8)
- The wives of Noah and Lot, married to righteous servants, betrayed them and are told to enter the Fire (66:10)
- Pharaoh's wife prays 'My Lord, build me a house with you in the Garden and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds' (66:11)
- Mary, daughter of 'Imran, guarded her chastity; God breathed into it of his spirit, and she believed the words of her Lord and his books (66:12)

**Al-Mulk: death and life as test, seven flawless heavens, stars as missiles against devils, hell nearly bursting with rage**
- 'Blessed is he in whose hand is the dominion (al-mulk)' (67:1)
- God created seven heavens in layers (tibaqan); look again and again, you will see no flaw or rift; your sight returns dazzled and weary (67:3, 67:4)
- God adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles (rujum) against the devils (67:5)
- As each group is thrown in, the keepers of hell ask 'Did no warner come to you?' and they admit it did (67:8, 67:9)
- The damned say: 'Had we listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze' (67:10, 67:11)
- 'Does he who created not know?' He is the Subtle, the Aware (67:14)

**The tractable earth, the one in heaven who could make it swallow you, the birds held up, and the water that could sink away**
- God made the earth tractable (dhalul) for you: walk its shoulders and eat of his provision (67:15)
- Are you secure from him who is in heaven, that he will not make the earth swallow you as it quakes, or send a stone-storm? (67:16, 67:17)
- Is one who walks prone on his face better guided than one who walks upright on a straight path? (67:22)

**Nun: by the pen; the prophet's great character; the swearer, slanderer and base-born man branded on the snout**
- The prophet is not mad; he has an unfailing reward and is of a great moral character (khuluq 'azim) (68:2, 68:3, 68:4)
- The deniers wish the prophet would compromise (tudhin) so they would compromise (68:9)
- God threatens: 'We shall brand him on the snout (khurtum)' (68:16)

**The companions of the garden who swore to harvest without 'if God wills' and to exclude the poor**
- The owners of a garden swore to harvest it in the morning without making exception ('if God wills') (68:17, 68:18)
- A visitation from God went round the garden while they slept, and by morning it was like a harvested/blackened field (68:19, 68:20)
- The owners set out whispering that no poor man (miskin) should enter the garden that day (68:23, 68:24, 68:25)
- The most moderate of them (awsatuhum) said 'Did I not tell you to glorify God?'; they blame one another, repent and hope for a better garden (68:26, 68:27, 68:28, 68:29, 68:30, 68:31, 68:32)

**Do you have a book or oaths binding God?; the shin laid bare; the companion of the fish; the evil eye**
- On the day when the shin is laid bare (yukshafu 'an saq) and they are called to prostrate but cannot (68:42, 68:43)
- God leads the deniers on step by step (istidraj) from where they do not know, and grants them respite; his plan is firm (68:44, 68:45)
- Do not be like the companion of the fish (sahib al-hut, Jonah) who cried out while choking with grief (68:48)
- Had not grace from his Lord reached him he would have been cast onto the barren shore blameworthy; but his Lord chose him and made him righteous (68:49, 68:50)
- The unbelievers almost make the prophet slip with their (evil) eyes when they hear the reminder (68:51)

**Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne**
- Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?' (69:1, 69:2, 69:3)
- Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast) (69:4, 69:5)
- 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks (69:6, 69:7, 69:8)
- When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears (69:11, 69:12)
- At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing (69:13, 69:14)
- That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them (69:17)

**The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger**
- Whoever is given his book in his right hand says 'Here, read my book!' and lives a pleasing life in a lofty garden with fruit clusters near (69:19, 69:20, 69:21, 69:22, 69:23, 69:24)
- Whoever is given his book in his left hand wishes he had never been given it and that death had been final; his wealth and power are gone (69:25, 69:26, 69:27, 69:28, 69:29)
- 'Seize him, fetter him, roast him in hellfire, then thread him on a chain seventy cubits long' (69:30, 69:31, 69:32)
- He did not believe in God the Great and did not urge the feeding of the poor (69:33, 69:34)
- The damned have no friend and no food except ghislin (foul washings/pus) (69:35, 69:36, 69:37)
- 'I swear by what you see and what you do not see' (69:38, 69:39)
- Had he fabricated sayings against God, God would have seized him by the right hand and cut his aorta (watin) (69:44, 69:45, 69:46)

**The ascending stairways: the day of fifty thousand years and the steadfast worshippers**
- A day whose measure is fifty thousand years, during which angels and the Spirit ascend to God (70:4)
- On the day the sky will be like molten metal or dregs of oil (muhl) (70:8)
- Humankind was created restless (halu'): fretful when evil touches him, grudging when good comes (70:19, 70:20, 70:21)
- The dead come out of the graves hurrying as if racing to a standing stone (nusub) (70:43)

**Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood**
- Prophet summons his people night and day, openly and in secret, yet they only flee further (71:5, 71:6, 71:8, 71:9)
- The people put their fingers in their ears and wrap their garments over their heads to avoid hearing the prophet (71:7)
- God caused humans to grow from the earth like a plant, returns them to it and will bring them out again (71:17, 71:18)
- Noah's people refuse to abandon their gods Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr (71:23)
- Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a fire (71:25)
- The flood hero prays for forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever enters his house believing, and all believers (71:28)

**The jinn hear the recitation**
- A band of jinn overhears the recitation of scripture, believes and reports it to their kind (72:1, 72:2, 72:13)
- Men used to seek refuge with male jinn, who only increased them in burden (72:6)
- Among the jinn are the righteous and the unjust, believers (muslimun) and deviators (qasitun), of different ways (72:11, 72:14, 72:15)
- The places of prostration (al-masajid) belong to God; call on no one beside him (72:18)
- God alone knows the unseen and discloses it only to a messenger he approves, sending watchers before and behind him (72:26, 72:27, 72:28)

**The enwrapped one: the night vigil**
- Night vigil prescribed in measured portions (half the night, less or more, two-thirds or a third), later lightened for the sick, travelers and fighters (73:2, 73:3, 73:4, 73:20)
- Command to recite the scripture in slow measured chant (tartil) (73:4)
- A day so terrible it turns children grey-haired (73:17)

**The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen**
- God created a man alone, gave him extended wealth and sons present at his side; yet he wants more and stubbornly opposes the signs (74:11, 74:12, 74:13, 74:14, 74:15, 74:16, 74:17)
- Over hell are nineteen; its keepers are angels whose number is made a test (74:30, 74:31)
- Every soul is held in pledge (rahina) for what it has earned (74:38)
- The people of paradise ask the damned what brought them to hell; they answer: we did not pray, feed the poor, and we denied the day (74:40, 74:41, 74:42, 74:43, 74:44, 74:45, 74:46, 74:47)
- Those who turn from the reminder are like startled wild asses fleeing from a lion (qaswara) (74:50, 74:51)
- Each of the deniers wants to be given scrolls unrolled (personally revealed) to him (74:52)

**The resurrection: bones, fingertips and the collarbone**
- Oath by the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama) (75:2)
- On that day radiant faces look upon their Lord (beatific vision) (75:23)
- At death the soul reaches the collarbones, someone asks 'who is a healer (or charmer, raq)?', leg is wrapped with leg and the drive is to the Lord (75:26, 75:27, 75:28, 75:29, 75:30)
- Does man think he will be left aimless (suda), without purpose or accountability? (75:36)

**The human: the mingled drop and the camphor cup**
- The righteous drink from a cup mixed with camphor (kafur) or ginger (zanjabil) (76:5, 76:17)
- The blessed wear green garments of fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq) and bracelets of silver (76:12, 76:21)
- Vessels of silver and goblets of crystal made of silver, measured exactly, are passed round (76:15, 76:16)
- Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate among the blessed, like scattered pearls (76:19)

**Those sent forth: the refrain of woe**
- Humans created from a despised fluid placed in a secure lodging (the womb) for a known term (77:20, 77:21, 77:22, 77:23)
- The earth is made a receptacle (kifat) that holds the living and the dead (77:25, 77:26)
- The damned are led to a shadow of three branches that gives no shade nor protects from the flame (77:30, 77:31)
- Hell throws sparks as huge as castles, like yellow (or black) camels (77:32, 77:33)
- On that day the damned do not speak and are not permitted to offer excuses (77:35, 77:36)

**The great tiding: signs of creation and the day of sorting**
- Transgressors abide in hell for ages (ahqaban) (78:23)
- On the day the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks; none speaks except whom the Merciful permits and who says what is right (78:37, 78:38)
- On the day the unbeliever says 'Would that I were dust!' (78:40)

**Those who drag forth: Moses at Tuwa, Pharaoh's claim, and the spreading of the earth**
- Oath by those who draw out (souls) violently, those who release gently, who glide, outstrip and direct affairs (79:1, 79:2, 79:3, 79:4, 79:5)
- The first quaking blast (al-rajifa) is followed by a second (al-radifa); a single shout (zajra) and they are on the open plain (al-sahira) (79:6, 79:7, 79:13, 79:14)
- One who feared standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire (hawa) will have the garden as refuge (79:40, 79:41)
- When they see the Hour it will seem they lingered (in the world or the grave) only an evening or its forenoon (79:46)

**He frowned: the blind man and the honored scrolls**
- The prophet frowns and turns away from a blind man who came seeking, while attending to a self-sufficient notable, and is rebuked (80:1, 80:2, 80:3, 80:4, 80:5, 80:6, 80:7, 80:8, 80:9, 80:10)

**The folding up: twelve signs of the end and the messenger on the horizon**
- At the end the ten-month pregnant she-camels ('ishar) are left untended (81:4)
- At the end the wild beasts are gathered together (81:5)
- At the end the souls are paired (with bodies or their like) (81:7)
- Oath by the stars (or planets) that withdraw, run their course and hide (al-khunnas, al-jawari al-kunnas) (81:15, 81:16)
- The revelation is the word of a noble messenger, powerful, secure with the Lord of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy (81:19, 81:20, 81:21)
- Opponents call the prophet mad (majnun) or possessed; scripture denies it (81:22)
- The prophet saw the heavenly messenger on the clear horizon (81:23)

**The cleaving: the noble scribes**
- Over humans are guardians, noble scribes (kiraman katibin), who know what they do (82:10, 82:11, 82:12)

**The defrauders: Sijjin and 'Illiyyun**
- Woe to the defrauders (mutaffifin) who exact full measure from others but give short measure or weight (83:1, 83:2, 83:3)
- The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, that of the righteous in 'Illiyyun, each an inscribed book (kitab marqum) witnessed by those brought near (83:7, 83:8, 83:9, 83:18, 83:19, 83:20, 83:21)
- Deniers dismiss the recited signs as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) (83:13)
- What they earned has covered their hearts with rust (rana) (83:14)
- On that day the wicked are veiled (debarred) from their Lord (83:15)
- An elite of 'those brought near' (al-muqarrabun) witness the righteous register and drink from Tasnim (83:21, 83:28)
- Sinners laughed at and winked at believers; on that day the believers laugh at the unbelievers from their couches (83:29, 83:30, 83:31, 83:32, 83:34, 83:35, 83:36)

**The splitting: the book in the right hand**
- 'You will surely ride (pass through) stage upon stage' (tabaqan 'an tabaq) (84:19)
- O man, you are toiling laboriously toward your Lord, and you will meet him (84:6)

**The constellations: the people of the ditch and the preserved tablet**
- Oath by the sky possessing the constellations or towers (dhat al-buruj) (85:1)
- The people of the ditch (ashab al-ukhdud) sit by a fire pit, watching what they do to believers, whose only offense was faith in God (85:4, 85:5, 85:6, 85:7, 85:8)
- The scripture is a glorious recitation inscribed on a preserved tablet (lawh mahfuz) in heaven (85:21, 85:22)

**The night-comer: fluid from between backbone and ribs**
- Oath by the sky and the night-comer (al-tariq), explained as the piercing star (al-najm al-thaqib) (86:1, 86:2, 86:3)
- Human created from a gushing fluid that issues from between the backbone (sulb) and the ribs or breastbones (tara'ib) (86:5, 86:6, 86:7)

**The Most High: the scrolls of Abraham and Moses**
- God will make the prophet recite so that he will not forget, except what God wills (87:6, 87:7)

**The overwhelming event: dari' and the carpets of paradise**
- The prophet is only a reminder (mudhakkir), not a controller (musaytir) over people (88:21, 88:22)

**The dawn: Iram of the pillars and the soul at peace**
- The people of 'Ad and Iram of the pillars ('imad), the like of which was never created in the lands (89:6, 89:7, 89:8)
- Thamud cut out the rock in the valley (for dwellings) (89:9)
- When God tests a man with bounty he says 'my Lord honored me'; when he restricts his provision he says 'my Lord humiliated me' (89:15, 89:16)
- On the day man remembers, too late, and says 'Would that I had sent ahead (good deeds) for my life' (89:23, 89:24)
- The soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'inna) is called to return to its Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, and enter his garden (89:27, 89:28, 89:29, 89:30)

**The night: the giver and the miser**
- To the giver who fears God, God eases the way to ease; to the miser, the way to hardship (92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10)

**The forenoon and the expansion: the orphan prophet consoled**
- God found the prophet an orphan and sheltered him, astray and guided him, needy and enriched him (93:3, 93:6, 93:7, 93:8)
- God expanded the prophet's breast, removed the burden that weighed down his back and raised his renown (94:1, 94:2, 94:3, 94:4)

**The fig and the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city**
- Humankind created in the best of forms (ahsan taqwim), then returned to the lowest of the low, except the believers (95:4, 95:5, 95:6)

**The clot: recite! and the forelock**
- A man who forbids a servant of God to pray is threatened: he will be dragged by his lying, sinful forelock (96:9, 96:10, 96:15, 96:16)
- Let the opponent call his council (nadi); God will call the guards of hell (al-zabaniya) (96:17, 96:18)

**The Night of Decree**
- Scripture sent down on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), better than a thousand months (97:1, 97:3)
- On a holy night the angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's permission with every command; it is peace until dawn (97:4, 97:5)

**The clear proof**
- The People of the Book split only after the clear proof (al-bayyina) came to them (98:1, 98:4)
- God is pleased with the saved and they are pleased with him (98:8)

**The chargers**
- Oath by charging war-horses that pant, strike sparks with their hooves, raid at dawn, raise dust and storm into the midst of a host (100:1, 100:2, 100:3, 100:4, 100:5)

**The striking day: moths, wool and the scales**
- On the striking day (al-qari'a) people will be like scattered moths (101:4)
- The one whose scales are light: 'his mother is Hawiya (the abyss)', a blazing fire (101:9, 101:10, 101:11)

**Rivalry, time and the slanderer**
- Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures (102:1, 102:2, 102:8)
- Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell (102:5, 102:6, 102:7)
- Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss (103:1, 103:2, 103:3)
- God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns (104:6, 104:7, 104:8, 104:9)

**The companions of the elephant**
- God's action against the companions of the elephant (ashab al-fil), whose plot he made go astray (105:1, 105:2)
- God sends birds in flocks (tayran ababil) that pelt an army with stones of baked clay (sijjil), leaving them like devoured straw (105:3, 105:4, 105:5)

**Quraysh, small kindnesses and al-Kawthar**
- Woe to those who pray but are heedless of their prayer, make a show, and withhold small kindnesses (al-ma'un) (107:4, 107:5, 107:6, 107:7)
- God has given the prophet al-Kawthar (abundance; in tradition a river or pool in paradise); 'pray and sacrifice' (108:1, 108:2)
- The one who hates the prophet is the one cut off (al-abtar, without posterity) (108:3)

**The disbelievers, the help, and the flame**
- Curse on Abu Lahab ('father of flame'): his hands perish, he will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife carries firewood with a rope of palm fiber (masad) on her neck (111:1, 111:3, 111:4, 111:5)

**Sincerity, daybreak and mankind: God's unity and the two refuges**
- God is al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge, the solid one who needs nothing) (112:2)
- Refuge from the evil of darkness (or the moon) when it settles (ghasiq idha waqab) (113:3)
- Refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies (evil eye) (113:5)
- Triple title: Lord of mankind, King of mankind, God of mankind (114:1, 114:2, 114:3)
- Refuge from the evil of the slinking whisperer (al-waswas al-khannas) who whispers in people's breasts, from jinn and humans (114:4, 114:5, 114:6)


## Reader hints (from memory, not from the text)

Parallels the reader recalled while tagging. They are secondary and unverified: use them as places to look, not as evidence.

**Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest** (Gen 1:1-2:3)
- Enuma Elish: Tiamat (cf. tehom), division of the waters with a heaven-half; Quran 21:30 heavens and earth were joined and split.
- Quran 50:38 'no weariness touched Us' answers divine rest; Quran 7:54 six days; 2:30 khalifa.
- Egyptian Memphite theology: creation by Ptah's word. Rabbinic: Gen R. 8 on 'let us make' as consulting angels.

**Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman** (Gen 2:4-25)
- Atrahasis/Enki: humans from clay mixed with a god's blood; Quran 15:26-29 clay and spirit breathed in; Quran 2:31 Adam taught the names.
- Sumerian Dilmun / Enki and Ninhursag: the 'lady of the rib' (Nin-ti) pun; Quran 4:1 created from a single soul and its mate.

**The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion** (Gen 3:1-24)
- Gilgamesh XI: the serpent steals the plant of rejuvenation; Adapa refuses the food of life.
- Quran 7:19-25 and 20:120-121: Iblis whispers, 'tree of immortality', both eat, leaves of the garden as covering; no blame on the woman alone.
- Pandora (Hesiod) as first woman bringing evils; Christian proto-evangelium reading of 3:15.

**Cain and Abel** (Gen 4:1-16)
- Quran 5:27-31: the two sons of Adam, the accepted offering, a raven teaches burial; Sumerian Dumuzi and Enkimdu (shepherd vs farmer).
- Targum/Midrash supply the field dispute; Hebrews 11:4 and 1 John 3:12; Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5.

**Cain's line, the first city, culture heroes and the Song of Lamech** (Gen 4:17-24)
- Mesopotamian apkallu sages bring the arts; Phoenician history of Philo of Byblos lists inventor-generations; 1 Enoch 8 Azazel teaches metalwork.
- Matthew 18:22 seventy-seven times forgiveness answers Lamech.

**Birth of Seth and Enosh; calling on the name of the LORD** (Gen 4:25-26)
- Gnostic Sethians; Life of Adam and Eve on Seth; Gen Rabbah 23:7 on Enosh's generation and idolatry.

**The book of the generations of Adam, Adam to Noah** (Gen 5:1-32)
- Sumerian King List: ten (or eight) antediluvian kings with reigns of tens of thousands of years; seventh king Enmeduranki taken to the gods, cf. Enoch.
- 1 Enoch, Jubilees 4, Quran 19:56-57 Idris raised to a high place; Hebrews 11:5.

**Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim** (Gen 6:1-4)
- 1 Enoch 6-11 Watchers led by Shemihazah; Jubilees 5; Jude 6, 2 Peter 2:4; Greek demigods (Hesiod's race of heroes); Quran 2:102 Harut and Marut.

**The Flood (full read)** (Gen 6:5-8:22)
- Gilgamesh XI (Utnapishtim): reed-hut warning, cubic boat sealed with bitumen, dove, swallow, raven that does not return, gods gather like flies at the sacrifice; Atrahasis seven-day warning.
- Quran 11:25-49, 23:27 (God's eye), 54:13 planks and nails; 1 Enoch 89; Berossus' Xisuthrus; Deucalion.

**Blessing of Noah, blood laws and the covenant of the bow** (Gen 9:1-17)
- Rabbinic Noahide laws (b. Sanh. 56a); Acts 15:20 abstain from blood; Gilgamesh/Atrahasis: Ishtar's lapis necklace as memorial; Enuma Elish: Marduk's bow set in heaven.

**Noah's vineyard, Ham's sin and the curse of Canaan; Noah's death** (Gen 9:18-29)
- b. Sanh. 70a Ham castrated or sodomized Noah; Hesiod's Kronos castrating Ouranos and Hurrian Kumarbi; Dionysus/Icarius as first wine-maker.
- Quran 29:14 Noah among his people 950 years (here his total life).

**The Table of Nations** (Gen 10:1-32)
- Nimrod as builder of Babel and persecutor of Abraham in midrash (Pirqe R. El. 24) and Islamic qisas; Ninurta or Tukulti-Ninurta as historical models.
- Deut 32:8 nations by number of the sons of God; Jubilees 8-9 division of the earth by lot; 1 Chr 1.

**The Tower of Babel** (Gen 11:1-9)
- Sumerian 'Enmerkar and the Lord of Aratta' spell of Nudimmud on the confusion of tongues; Etemenanki ziggurat; Quran 28:38 and 40:36-37 Pharaoh's tower by Haman with baked clay.
- Acts 2 Pentecost reverses Babel; 3 Baruch on the tower builders.

**Generations of Shem to Terah; Terah's family leaves Ur** (Gen 11:10-32)
- Midrash (Gen R. 38:13): Haran dies in Nimrod's furnace after Abram survives; ties to abraham.yaml thrown-into-fire and sibling-dies-in-fire; Quran 21:68-69.
- Josh 24:2 Terah served other gods; Jubilees 12; Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8.

**The call of Abram and his journey through Canaan** (Gen 12:1-9)
- Abram aged 75 leaving Harran; 'the souls they made in Harran' (12:5) read by Gen R. 39:14 as converts; Quran 29:26 and 37:99 'I am going to my Lord'.

**Abram and Sarai in Egypt (first wife-sister episode)** (Gen 12:10-20)
- Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen 19-20) Abram's dream of cedar and palm, Sarai's beauty catalogue, Pharaoh's paralysis; Sahih al-Bukhari hadith on Sarah and the tyrant whose hand withered, gift of Hagar.

**War of the four kings, rescue of Lot, Melchizedek** (Gen 14:1-24)
- Ps 110:4 priest forever after the order of Melchizedek; Hebrews 7 (without father or mother); 11QMelchizedek heavenly figure; 2 Enoch 71-72 miraculous birth of Melchizedek.
- Abram 'the Hebrew' (ha-ivri) only here; Ugaritic El qny 'rs, creator of earth.

**The covenant between the pieces** (Gen 15:1-21)
- Jer 34:18-20 passing between the calf's parts; Hittite and Mari donkey-cutting treaty rites; Paul in Romans 4 and Galatians 3 on 15:6.
- Apocalypse of Abraham 9-15 expands the sacrifice with the bird of prey as Azazel; Quran 2:260 Abraham and the four birds cut and called.

**Hagar and the birth of Ishmael** (Gen 16:1-16)
- Code of Hammurabi 144-147 and Nuzi contracts on slave-wives who claim equality; Galatians 4:21-31 allegory; Islamic tradition of Hagar as wife and mother of the Arabs.

**El Shaddai, new names and the covenant of circumcision** (Gen 17:1-27)
- Islamic khitan, tradition of Abraham's circumcision at 80 with an adze (Bukhari); Herodotus 2.104 on Egyptian circumcision; Jubilees 15; Ishmaelite age of 13 behind Muslim practice in Josephus Ant. 1.214.

**Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac** (Gen 18:1-15)
- Quran 11:69-73 and 51:24-30: guests do not eat (Abraham fears them), roasted calf, the wife laughs and strikes her face; Tob 12:19 angel only appeared to eat; Christian Trinity icon (Rublev).
- Ovid Met. 8 Baucis and Philemon (gods hosted, flood/punishment of inhospitable neighbours); Hyrieus given a son Orion by three gods.

**Abraham bargains for Sodom** (Gen 18:16-33)
- Quran 11:74-76 Abraham pleads for Lot's people; Jer 5:1 one just man; tiqqun soferim at 18:22 (originally 'YHWH still stood before Abraham').

**Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah** (Gen 19:1-29)
- Quran 11:77-83, 15:61-77, 54:33-39: Lot offers 'my daughters', attackers' eyes blotted out, city turned upside down, stones of baked clay, wife left behind; Wisdom 10:7 pillar as memorial.
- Greek Orpheus/Eurydice and Baucis-Philemon don't-look-back; Ezek 16:49 Sodom's sin as neglect of the poor; Bera king of Sodom.

**Lot's daughters and the origin of Moab and Ammon** (Gen 19:30-38)
- Parallels Noah's drunkenness after the flood (9:21); Myrrha and Cinyras (Ovid Met. 10); Ruth the Moabite as David's ancestor; Islam rejects the episode (prophetic impeccability).

**Abraham and Sarah at Gerar (second wife-sister episode)** (Gen 20:1-18)
- Abraham's 'no fear of God in this place' (20:11); hadith of Abraham's three 'lies' (Bukhari, Sarah 'my sister' in Islam); Lev 18:9 later forbids marrying a half-sister.

**Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael** (Gen 21:1-21)
- Islamic tradition (Bukhari, Ahadith al-Anbiya) Hagar runs between Safa and Marwa and Zamzam springs at Mecca; Quran 14:37 'a valley without cultivation'.
- Galatians 4:29 Ishmael 'persecuted' Isaac; Gen R. 53:11 on metsaheq as idolatry, sexual immorality or bloodshed.

**Abraham's treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba** (Gen 21:22-34)
- Gen R. 54:6 eshel as an inn for hospitality (acrostic of eating, drinking, lodging); Philistines here are anachronistic.

**The binding of Isaac (Aqedah)** (Gen 22:1-19)
- Quran 37:99-111: dream of sacrifice, the unnamed son consents, 'great sacrifice' ransom; Islamic debate whether Ishmael or Isaac; Eid al-Adha.
- Iphigenia at Aulis replaced by a deer; Phrixus and the golden ram; 2 Chr 3:1 Moriah = temple mount; Christian Isaac-carrying-wood typology (John 19:17); Pseudo-Philo LAB 32 and Targum Isaac asks to be bound.

**The children of Nahor and the birth of Rebekah** (Gen 22:20-24)
- Uz and Buz: Job's land of Uz (Job 1:1) and Elihu the Buzite (Job 32:2); twelve-tribe pattern as with Ishmael and Jacob.

**Death of Sarah and purchase of the cave of Machpelah** (Gen 23:1-20)
- Hittite land law and Neo-Babylonian dialogue documents; Gen R. 58 Ephron's name defective (Ephrn) for his greed; Haram al-Ibrahimi in Hebron; Acts 7:16 conflates with Shechem purchase.

**Abraham's servant finds Rebekah for Isaac** (Gen 24:1-67)
- Type-scene of betrothal at a well: Jacob-Rachel (Gen 29), Moses-Zipporah (Exod 2), Quran 28:23-28; John 4 Samaritan woman; Odyssey 10 / 6 water-drawing maidens.
- Gen R. 60: the servant is Eliezer; Rebekah aged three in some midrash; Laban greedy for the gold (24:30).

**Keturah's sons, the death of Abraham, and Ishmael's line** (Gen 25:1-18)
- Gen R. 61:4 Keturah = Hagar; gifts to concubines' sons as 'names of impurity' (b. Sanh. 91a, Indian magic); Kedar and Nebaioth as Arab ancestors in Islamic genealogy (Adnan).
- Testament of Abraham: Abraham resists death and is shown the world.

**Birth of Esau and Jacob; the sale of the birthright** (Gen 25:19-34)
- Twin rivalry in the womb: Acrisius and Proetus (Apollodorus 2.2.1); Iranian Ohrmazd/Ahriman twins of Zurvan, Ahriman thrusting out first; Romans 9:10-13; rabbinic Esau = Rome.

**Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty** (Gen 26:1-33)
- b. Yoma 28b: Abraham observed the whole Torah; Quran 2:135, 3:67 Abraham hanif before Torah; doublet of Gen 20 and 21:22-34.

**Jacob steals Esau's blessing** (Gen 27:1-45)
- Odysseus recognized by Eurycleia by touch (scar) vs. Isaac deceived by touch; Hebrews 12:16-17 Esau found no place for repentance; Gen R. 65 Esau's garments were Adam's/Nimrod's.
- Jacob's smell of Paradise (Gen R. 65:22) links to joseph.yaml father-smells-son and Quran 12:94.

**Jacob's dream at Bethel** (Gen 28:10-22)
- Babylonian ziggurat stairway (simmiltu) and bab-ilu 'gate of god'; John 1:51 angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man; Ladder of Jacob (pseudepigraphon); Mithraic ladder of seven gates.
- Greek baetyl (Bethel) sacred stones anointed with oil; stone of Scone legend as Jacob's pillow; Quran 3:93 Israel's self-imposed food prohibition (sinew) linked elsewhere.

**Jacob meets Rachel; Laban's substitution of Leah** (Gen 29:1-30)
- Quran 28:27 Moses serves eight or ten years for Shu'ayb's daughter; Lev 18:18 forbids marrying two sisters; Gen R. 70 Leah's eyes weak from weeping lest she marry Esau.

**Births of Jacob's children; the mandrakes** (Gen 29:31-30:24)
- Mandragora as aphrodisiac in Greek (Aphrodite Mandragoritis) and Song 7:14; Hurrian Nuzi adoption-by-knee rites; Rachel's death in childbirth follows later (Gen 35).

**Jacob's wages and the speckled flocks** (Gen 30:25-43)
- Ancient maternal-impression belief (Hippocratic, Oppian on Spartan horse-breeders, Jerome Quaest. in Gen.); Hermes the trickster herdsman.

**Jacob's flight from Laban and the theft of the teraphim** (Gen 31:1-42)
- Nuzi tablets: possession of household gods tied to inheritance; Aeneas carrying the Penates out of Troy; Code of Hammurabi 266 shepherd not liable for losses to a lion; Exod 22:12.
- Gen R. 74:5 Rachel stole the teraphim to wean her father from idolatry; Rachel's death (35:16-19) read as fulfillment of Jacob's curse.

**Covenant of Jacob and Laban at Galeed/Mizpah** (Gen 31:43-54)
- Aramaean-Israelite border at Gilead; 'God of Abraham and God of Nahor' with plural verb (31:53) suggests two deities; Kudurru boundary stones.

**Jacob wrestles at the Jabbok and becomes Israel** (Gen 32:23-33)
- Hosea 12:4-5 he strove with the angel and wept; river-demons and night spirits who flee at dawn; Gilgamesh and Enkidu wrestling; Menelaus wrestling Proteus to extract an answer; Judg 13:18 angel withholds his name.
- Gen R. 77-78: Esau's guardian angel (Samael); Prayer of Joseph: Jacob as archangel Israel; Quran 3:93 the food Israel forbade himself.

**Jacob and Esau reconcile; Jacob at Succoth and Shechem** (Gen 33:1-20)
- Josh 24:32 Joseph's bones buried in this plot; John 4:5 Jacob's well at Sychar; Esau reconciliation contrasts with Joseph's brothers (joseph.yaml hero-forgives-brothers).

**Dinah, Shechem and the massacre by Simeon and Levi** (Gen 34:1-31)
- Jubilees 30 and Judith 9:2-4 praise Simeon's zeal; Testament of Levi 5-7 has an angel commission Levi's sword.
- Compare 2 Sam 13 (Amnon and Tamar) and the abduction of maidens in Greek myth (Persephone, Europa).

**Purge of foreign gods, Bethel, Rachel's death in childbirth, Reuben and Bilhah, Isaac's death** (Gen 35:1-29)
- Gen 35:22 reported tersely with a masoretic gap (pisqa); cf. Reuben's punishment Gen 49:4 and Absalom with David's concubines 2 Sam 16:22.
- Rachel weeping for her children, Jer 31:15 / Matt 2:18.

**Generations of Esau, Horite chiefs, kings of Edom** (Gen 36:1-43)
- Rabbinic tradition (b. Pesachim 54a) makes Anah the inventor of mule-breeding; Targum Neofiti reads 'mules'.
- Eliphaz the Temanite reappears as Job's friend (Job 2:11); Uz (36:28) is Job's land.

**Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt** (Gen 37:1-36)
- Quran 12:4-20; Testaments of Zebulun and Gad. Twenty silver later read as typological for Judas's thirty (Matt 26:15).
- The Egyptian Tale of Two Brothers parallels the coming seduction episode.

**Judah and Tamar** (Gen 38:1-30)
- Perez is ancestor of David (Ruth 4:18-22) and appears in Matthew's genealogy (Matt 1:3). Testament of Judah 10-12.
- Middle Assyrian Laws A 33 and Hittite Laws 193 on levirate obligations of the father-in-law.

**Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison** (Gen 39:1-23)
- Egyptian Tale of Two Brothers (Anubis and Bata); Phaedra-Hippolytus and Bellerophon-Stheneboea (Iliad 6.155-170); Quran 12:21-35.

**The cupbearer's and baker's dreams** (Gen 40:1-23)
- Quran 12:36-42 (Joseph preaches to the prisoners first). Herod's birthday feast (Mark 6:21) is the other biblical birthday-feast execution.

**Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's elevation** (Gen 41:1-57)
- Famine Stela of Sehel (seven-year famine under Djoser, Imhotep advises); Gilgamesh VI seven years of chaff; Joseph and Aseneth expands 41:45.
- 'Whatever he tells you, do' (41:55) echoed by Mary at Cana, John 2:5. Quran 12:43-56.

**The silver cup and Judah's plea** (Gen 44:1-34)
- Quran 12:70-79 (cup/measure in Benjamin's bag; 'the penalty is the one in whose bag it is found'). Cup divination in Mesopotamian oil-omen texts.

**Joseph makes himself known; the wagons sent for Jacob** (Gen 45:1-28)
- Quran 12:89-93 (Joseph's shirt sent to restore Jacob's sight); here it is wagons, not a shirt.

**Vision at Beersheba, the seventy who went down, reunion in Goshen** (Gen 46:1-34)
- Serah bat Asher becomes in midrash the woman who tells Jacob Joseph lives, and who shows Moses Joseph's coffin (Mekhilta Beshallah). Seventy echoes the seventy nations (Gen 10) and Deut 32:8.
- Nunc dimittis (Luke 2:29) echoes 46:30.

**The Testament (Blessing) of Jacob and his death** (Gen 49:1-33)
- Gen 49:10 read messianically in Targum Onqelos, 4Q252, and Christian exegesis; 49:11 echoed in Zech 9:9 and the triumphal entry. Lion of Judah in Rev 5:5.
- Tribal blessings parallel Deut 33; zodiacal readings of the twelve tribes in Philo and Josephus.

**Embalming and burial of Jacob; Joseph's last words and death** (Gen 50:1-26)
- 110 years is the ideal Egyptian lifespan. Midrash: Joseph's coffin sunk in the Nile and raised by Moses (Mekhilta, b. Sotah 13a).

**Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons** (Exod 1:1-22)
- Quran 28:4 and 2:49 (Pharaoh slaughtering sons, sparing women). Josephus Ant. 2.205 adds a scribe's prophecy of a deliverer; Sargon, Cyrus, Krishna (Kamsa) and Herod (Matt 2:16) infanticide parallels.
- Rabbinic identification of Shiphrah and Puah with Jochebed and Miriam (b. Sotah 11b).

**Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry** (Exod 2:1-25)
- Sargon of Akkad birth legend (basket of rushes sealed with bitumen, set in the river). Quran 28:7-28 (Moses' mother inspired, the two daughters at the water of Madyan, eight or ten years' service).
- Acts 7:23-29 (Moses aged 40). Compare Jacob at the well (Gen 29) and the Egyptian Tale of Sinuhe (flight from Egypt).

**The burning bush and the divine name** (Exod 3:1-22)
- Quran 20:9-24, 27:7-12, 28:29-35 ('take off your sandals, you are in the sacred valley Tuwa'). Acts 7:30-34; Mark 12:26 (God of the living).
- Philo, Mos. 1.65-75 and LXX 'ego eimi ho on'. Compare Zoroaster's vision and theophany in fire.

**Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood** (Exod 4:1-31)
- Quran 20:17-23, 27:10-12, 28:31-32 (staff becomes a snake, hand comes out white 'without harm'); 20:25-32 (Moses asks for Aaron, 'untie the knot from my tongue').
- Exod 4:24-26 compared with Jacob at the Jabbok (Gen 32) and apotropaic blood rites; Exod Rabbah has the serpent swallowing Moses to the feet.

**First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw** (Exod 5:1-23)
- Egyptian brickmaking quotas (Papyrus Anastasi IV/V, Louvre leather roll) and the Rekhmire tomb paintings of foreign brickmakers.

**'I am YHWH': the name not known to the patriarchs; genealogy of Moses and Aaron** (Exod 6:1-30)
- Four cups of the Passover seder (y. Pesahim 10:1) keyed to 6:6-7. Quran 28:34 (Aaron more eloquent).

**Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs** (Exod 7:1-13)
- Quran 7:107-122, 20:65-70, 26:32-48 (Moses' staff swallows the magicians' illusions; the magicians fall prostrate and believe). The magicians are named Jannes and Jambres in CD 5:18-19 and 2 Tim 3:8.
- Westcar Papyrus: magician Webaoner's wax crocodile comes alive; Egyptian snake-charming wands.

**Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice** (Exod 7:14-8:15)
- Admonitions of Ipuwer ('the river is blood'). Quran 7:133 (flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood as 'distinct signs'). Luke 11:20 'finger of God'.

**Plague 7: hail and fire** (Exod 9:13-35)
- Wisdom of Solomon 16:16-22 (fire burning in water, not melting the hail). Rev 8:7, 16:21 (hail and fire).

**Plagues 8-9: locusts and darkness** (Exod 10:1-29)
- Wisdom of Solomon 17-18 elaborates the darkness (phantoms, terror) and the light for Israel. Joel 1-2 locusts.

**Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt** (Exod 12:1-51)
- John 19:36 applies 12:46 to Jesus; 1 Cor 5:7 'Christ our Passover'. Jubilees 49 (Mastema). Apotropaic doorway blood in Mesopotamian namburbi rites and Arab fidya customs; Mishnah Pesahim.
- Samaritan Pentateuch and LXX at 12:40 add 'and in the land of Canaan'; Gal 3:17 counts 430 years from Abraham.

**Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire** (Exod 13:1-22)
- Mishnah Menahot and the Qumran tefillin; Deut 6:8. Midrash (b. Sotah 13a) on Moses retrieving Joseph's coffin from the Nile with Serah's help.
- Quran 20:77; Isa 4:5 cloud by day and fire by night over Zion.

**The pursuit and the parting of the sea** (Exod 14:1-31)
- Quran 26:61-66 ('strike the sea with your staff' and it parts like a great mountain), 10:90-92 (Pharaoh's last-moment faith and preserved body), 20:77-78.
- Midrash of Nahshon entering the sea first (b. Sotah 37a); Joshua 3 (Jordan), 2 Kings 2:8 (Elijah). Ugaritic Baal vs Yam; Baal-zephon as the storm god's mountain.

**The Song of the Sea and Miriam's song** (Exod 15:1-21)
- Ugaritic Baal cycle (Baal defeats Yam, builds palace on Zaphon, kingship) maps onto 15:8-18. Rev 15:3 'song of Moses'. Mekhilta Shirata; Quran 10:90.
- 'Miriam sister of Aaron' (15:20) is the title behind Quran 19:28 'O sister of Harun' addressed to Maryam.

**Bitter water sweetened at Marah; Elim's twelve springs and seventy palms** (Exod 15:22-27)
- Elisha sweetens water with salt (2 Kgs 2:19-22). Quran 2:60 and 7:160 have twelve springs gushing from the rock struck by the staff, one per tribe.

**Manna and quail; the first Sabbath** (Exod 16:1-36)
- Quran 2:57, 7:160, 20:80 (al-mann wa-l-salwa). John 6:31-58 (bread from heaven); Heb 9:4 (golden jar of manna in the ark); Rev 2:17 (hidden manna). Wisdom 16:20-21 (manna suited to every taste); 2 Baruch 29:8 (manna returns in the messianic age).
- Tamarisk-scale honeydew of Sinai (Arabic mann).

**Battle with Amalek; Moses' raised hands** (Exod 17:8-16)
- Raised hands in prayer at battle: compare Quranic and hadith motifs of prophetic supplication at Badr; Christian typology (Barnabas 12) reads the outstretched arms as the cross.

**Jethro's visit and the appointment of judges** (Exod 18:1-27)
- Quran 28:22-28 (Moses and the Midianite elder, often identified with Shu'ayb/Jethro). Deut 1:9-18 retells the judges without Jethro.

**Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany** (Exod 19:1-25)
- Quran 7:171 and 2:63 (the mountain raised over Israel); rabbinic 'na'aseh ve-nishma'; Acts 2 Pentecost imagery (fire, sound).

**The Ten Words and the people's fear** (Exod 20:1-21)
- Quran 17:22-39 and 6:151-153 as decalogue-like lists; Egyptian Book of the Dead 125 negative confession.

**Covenant Code - homicide, injury and the goring ox** (Exod 21:12-37)
- Laws of Hammurabi 196-201 (talion), 209-214 (pregnant woman), 250-252 (goring ox); Laws of Eshnunna 53-55. Thirty pieces of silver: Zech 11:12, Matt 26:15. Quran 5:45 cites talion as in the Torah.

**Covenant Code - theft, deposits, seduction** (Exod 22:1-16)
- Laws of Eshnunna 12-13 and LH 21 (burglar killed at breach); LH 266 (lion kills animal in fold, shepherd clears himself before god).

**Covenant Code - sorceress, stranger, widow, loans, firstborn** (Exod 22:17-30)
- Quran 2:275-279 on riba; Quran 5:3 forbids flesh killed by a beast (ma akala al-sabu).

**The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest** (Exod 23:20-33)
- Rabbinic and Christian identification of the name-bearing angel with Metatron (b. Sanh 38b) or the Logos.

**Covenant ratified in blood; the elders see God** (Exod 24:1-11)
- Blood of the covenant: Mark 14:24, Heb 9:18-22. Sapphire pavement: Ezek 1:26; rabbinic tradition of the sapphire brick as a memorial of the bondage.

**Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days** (Exod 24:12-18)
- Quran 2:51 and 7:142 (forty nights appointment of Moses); Jesus' forty days, Matt 4:2.

**Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand** (Exod 25:1-40)
- Heavenly pattern: Heb 8:5; Gudea cylinders (temple plan in a dream); Wisdom 9:8. Lampstand as stylized tree: compare tree-of-life imagery; Zech 4; Rev 1:12.

**Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil** (Exod 26:1-37)
- Veil torn at the crucifixion, Matt 27:51; Heb 10:20 veil as flesh. Feminine idiom 'a woman to her sister' for joined curtains (26:3).

**The high priest's vestments** (Exod 28:1-43)
- Twelve gems: Rev 21:19-20 foundations; Ezek 28:13 king of Tyre's stones. Bells on hem: Sir 45:9; Josephus on cosmic symbolism of the vestments. Seamless robe: John 19:23.

**The daily offering and God's dwelling** (Exod 29:38-46)
- Daily offerings parallel to Islamic fixed prayer times (rabbinic derivation of shaharit and minhah from the tamid).

**Incense altar, half-shekel ransom and bronze laver** (Exod 30:1-21)
- Census danger: 2 Sam 24. Ritual washing of hands and feet before worship: compare Islamic wudu (Quran 5:6).

**Recipes of the holy anointing oil and incense** (Exod 30:22-38)
- Christian chrism; Egyptian kyphi incense recipes; Greek Magical Papyri on sacred recipes kept secret.

**Bezalel and Oholiab; Sabbath as sign; the tablets** (Exod 31:1-18)
- Quran 50:38 'no weariness touched us' reads as a rebuttal of God resting/refreshing. Bezalel and divine wisdom in craft: Ugaritic Kothar-wa-Hasis.

**The golden calf** (Exod 32:1-14)
- Quran 20:83-98 and 7:148-154: the Samiri fashions the calf that lows; Aaron pleads 'do not seize me by my beard'; Moses burns and scatters it in the sea. 1 Kgs 12:28 Jeroboam's calves use the same formula.

**Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer** (Exod 32:15-35)
- Quran 20:97 (the Samiri's calf burned and scattered in the sea); Quran 2:54 'kill yourselves' as atonement for the calf; Paul's wish to be accursed for his kin, Rom 9:3; Rev 3:5 book of life; Num 5 ordeal of drinking.

**Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back** (Exod 33:1-23)
- Quran 7:143: Moses asks 'my Lord, show yourself to me', is told 'you will not see me, but look at the mountain', which crumbles and Moses falls unconscious. 1 Kgs 19 Elijah at the cave on Horeb. Rom 9:15 quotes 33:19.

**New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue** (Exod 34:1-28)
- The thirteen attributes recited in synagogue liturgy; cf. Quranic divine names al-Rahman al-Rahim; Jonah 4:2, Joel 2:13 reuse 34:6.

**Moses' shining face and the veil** (Exod 34:29-35)
- Horned Moses of Michelangelo; 2 Cor 3:7-18 veil allegory; Matt 17:2 transfiguration; Quran 7:108 / 20:22 Moses' hand shining white (different organ).

**Sabbath fire ban and the people's donations** (Exod 35:1-29)
- Jewelry for the sanctuary versus jewelry for the calf (32:2-3): rabbinic contrast. Karaite and rabbinic dispute over Sabbath fire.

**Altar, laver of mirrors, court and the metal inventory** (Exod 38:1-31)
- Women serving at the tent door: 1 Sam 2:22. Rabbinic midrash (Tanhuma) on the mirrors the women used to arouse their husbands in Egypt.

**The tabernacle erected; cloud and glory fill it** (Exod 40:1-38)
- 1 Kgs 8:10-11 glory fills Solomon's temple; Quranic sakina (2:248) with the ark (tabut); Enuma Elish's temple-building after victory.

**The burnt offering of cattle, flock and birds** (Lev 1:1-17)
- Greek holocaust; Vedic animal sacrifice (pasubandha) with dismemberment; Luke 2:24 poor parents' offering of doves. Bird split but not divided: Gen 15:10.

**The grain offering; no leaven or honey; salt of the covenant** (Lev 2:1-16)
- Salt covenant: Num 18:19, 2 Chr 13:5; Mark 9:49; salt in Roman mola salsa and Homeric sacrifice. Honey excluded: contrast honey offerings in Mesopotamian and Vedic ritual.

**The well-being (shelamim) offering and the ban on fat and blood** (Lev 3:1-17)
- Mesopotamian extispicy focused on the liver lobe (yoteret); Greek gods' portion of fat-wrapped thigh bones (Hesiod, Prometheus at Mekone). Quran 22:37 'neither their flesh nor their blood reaches God'.

**The purification (hattat) offering for unintentional sin** (Lev 4:1-35)
- Heb 13:11-12 (Jesus suffered outside the gate as the sin-offering burned outside the camp).

**Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering** (Lev 5:1-26)
- Matt 5:23-24 reconcile with your brother before the altar; Mishnah Yoma 8:9; Islamic rule that rights of people (huquq al-'ibad) must be restored before repentance is complete.

**Priestly instructions for burnt, grain and sin offerings; the perpetual fire** (Lev 6:1-23)
- Perpetual fire: Zoroastrian Atash Behram; Roman Vestal fire; Mal 1:11. Earthen vessels absorbing holiness/impurity: Lev 11:33; rabbinic kashering of vessels; Islamic rules on vessels.

**Guilt and well-being offerings; priests' portions; fat and blood bans** (Lev 7:1-38)
- Acts 15:20, 29 (abstain from blood); Quran 2:173, 5:3, 6:145 (blood forbidden); Greek priest's perquisite of the hide (dermatikon).

**Moses ordains Aaron and his sons** (Lev 8:1-36)
- Seven-day liminal seclusion during initiation: compare rites of passage (van Gennep); Christian ordination anointing.

**The eighth day - Aaron's first offerings and the divine fire** (Lev 9:1-24)
- Compare 1Kgs 18:38 (Elijah), 2Chr 7:1 (Solomon), Judg 6:21 and 13:20; Quran 3:183 on the demand for an offering consumed by fire.

**Strange fire - death of Nadab and Abihu; priestly rules** (Lev 10:1-20)
- Rabbinic tradition links 10:9 to the brothers' drunkenness (Lev. Rab. 12). Compare Num 16:35 (Korah's 250 burned) and Greek stories of illicit fire (Prometheus).

**Clean and unclean animals; carcass impurity** (Lev 11:1-47)
- Compare Deut 14; Quran 2:173, 5:3, 6:145 (pig, carrion); Acts 10 (Peter's vision); Zoroastrian classifications of noxious creatures (khrafstra); the hoopoe in Quran 27:20.

**Impurity after childbirth** (Lev 12:1-8)
- Luke 2:22-24 cites 12:8 for Mary's offering; compare Zoroastrian and Hindu (sutaka) postpartum impurity periods; Islamic nifas (40 days).

**Diagnosis of tsara'at in skin, scalp and fabric** (Lev 13:1-59)
- Compare Num 12 (Miriam), 2Kgs 5 (Naaman), 2Chr 26:19-21 (Uzziah); Mark 1:40-44 ('show yourself to the priest'); Quran 3:49 and 5:110 (Jesus heals the leper, al-abras).

**Purification of the healed leper; plague in houses** (Lev 14:1-57)
- The bird released over the field parallels the scapegoat (Lev 16) and Mesopotamian/Hittite elimination rites carrying impurity away on a living animal; rabbinic tradition (Arakhin 16a) links tsara'at to slander.

**Impurity of bodily discharges, semen and menstruation** (Lev 15:1-33)
- The woman with an issue of blood (Mark 5:25-34) presupposes 15:25; compare Quran 2:222 on menstruation (adhan), Islamic ghusl after janaba, Zoroastrian Vendidad 16 on menstruants.

**The Day of Atonement and the goat for Azazel** (Lev 16:1-34)
- Azazel appears as a fallen angel in 1 Enoch 8-10 (Asael), Apocalypse of Abraham 13-14; Mishnah Yoma 6 (goat pushed off a cliff, scarlet thread turning white); Hebrews 9; Greek pharmakos and Hittite/Babylonian elimination rites (Ashella, akitu kuppuru with sheep carcass); Ashura fasting on the 10th of Muharram in Islamic tradition.

**Slaughter only at the tent; the blood is the life** (Lev 17:1-16)
- Acts 15:20, 29 (apostolic decree: abstain from blood and things strangled) applies these alien-binding laws to gentiles; Noahide prohibition Gen 9:4; Quran 2:173, 5:3 (blood, carrion, al-munkhaniqa); Hebrews 9:22.

**Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants** (Lev 18:1-30)
