**Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash** (2Kgs 11:1-20)
- Hidden-heir-raised-in-sanctuary pattern: compare Ion at Delphi (Euripides), Moses, and the Cyrus/Kai Khusrau hidden-child cycles; Athaliah as foreign queen is paired with Jezebel.

**Joash repairs the temple; the collection chest; assassination** (2Kgs 12:1-22)
- The temple chest anticipates the shofar-shaped collection boxes of the Second Temple (m. Sheqalim 6) and church alms boxes.

**Jehoahaz and Jehoash; Elisha's death and the miraculous bones** (2Kgs 13:1-25)
- Elisha's bones are the classic proof-text for Christian relic cults (e.g. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catech. 18.16); compare Sirach 48:13-14.
- Belomancy/arrow divination: compare Ezek 21:21 and pre-Islamic Arab azlam (Quran 5:3).

**Amaziah's war with Jehoash and the fable of the thistle; Jeroboam II** (2Kgs 14:1-29)
- The only historical anchor for the prophet of the book of Jonah (Quran's Yunus/Dhu al-Nun).
- Plant-disputation fables: compare Mesopotamian Tamarisk and Palm and Aesop's oak and reed.

**Azariah the leper; the usurper kings of Israel; Tiglath-pileser** (2Kgs 15:1-38)
- Chronicles (2Chr 26) explains the leprosy as punishment for offering incense; Josephus adds an earthquake. Compare the Quran's general theme of kings struck down for hubris.

**Fall of Samaria and the sermon on Israel's exile** (2Kgs 17:1-23)
- Origin of the 'ten lost tribes' legends (Halah, Habor, Gozan, Media), later developed in 4 Ezra 13, Eldad ha-Dani and many diaspora traditions.

**The resettled peoples, the lions and the syncretistic cult of Samaria** (2Kgs 17:24-41)
- The polemical origin of 'Cutheans' (rabbinic name for Samaritans; m. Berakhot 8:8, b. Hullin 6a 'lion converts' — gerei arayot).

**Hezekiah's reform; Sennacherib's invasion and the Rabshakeh's speech** (2Kgs 18:1-37)
- Sennacherib's own annals (Taylor/Rassam prisms) and the Lachish reliefs: Hezekiah shut up 'like a bird in a cage'; tribute of 30 talents gold matches.
- Bronze serpent: compare John 3:14 and the Mosaic serpent in later Christian iconography.

**Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter** (2Kgs 19:1-37)
- Herodotus 2.141: Sennacherib's army before Pelusium undone overnight by mice gnawing bowstrings, after the priest-king Sethos prays. Sennacherib's murder by a son is confirmed in Babylonian chronicles.
- Hook-in-nose: Assyrian reliefs (Esarhaddon's Zincirli stele) show captive kings led by nose-ropes.

**Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys** (2Kgs 20:1-21)
- Siloam tunnel inscription (8th c.) documents the conduit. Rabbinic tradition (b. Berakhot 10a) on Hezekiah turning his face to the wall; Daniel 1 sees the eunuch prophecy fulfilled.
- Fig poultices for boils appear in Ugaritic hippiatric texts and Greek medicine.

**Manasseh's apostasy and its doom-oracle; Amon's assassination** (2Kgs 21:1-26)
- Innocent blood: later tradition (Martyrdom/Ascension of Isaiah 5; b. Yevamot 49b) has Manasseh saw Isaiah in half inside a tree; compare Heb 11:37.
- Chronicles (2Chr 33) gives Manasseh a captivity and repentance; Prayer of Manasseh.

**Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle** (2Kgs 22:1-20)
- Found-book legitimation: compare Egyptian texts 'found' in temples (Book of the Dead ch. 64 found under Menkaure), the Numa books found in his tomb (Livy 40.29), and Buddhist terma (hidden treasure texts).

**Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo** (2Kgs 23:1-30)
- Sun-horses and sun-chariots: compare Helios' chariot, Shamash iconography and the Vedic Surya's horses.
- Josiah's death at Megiddo is a seed of 'Armageddon' (har megiddo, Rev 16:16) and of the lament tradition (2Chr 35:25; Zech 12:11).

**The siege and destruction of Jerusalem; Gedaliah; Jehoiachin released** (2Kgs 25:1-30)
- Babylonian ration tablets (Weidner tablets) list oil rations for 'Ya'u-kinu king of Judah' and his sons.
- The four fasts of Zech 8:19 (10th, 4th, 5th, 7th months) are tied to these dates; the Joseph-like 'lifting of the head' from prison (Gen 40:13, 20) closes the book on hope.

**Genealogy from Adam to Abraham and the table of nations** (1Chr 1:1-27)
- Compare Sumerian King List and Berossus' ten antediluvian kings; Luke 3:23-38 runs the line back to Adam in the same way.

**Sons of Ishmael, Keturah and Esau; the Seirite chiefs and kings of Edom** (1Chr 1:28-54)
- Ishmael's sons (Nebaioth, Kedar, Tema, Dumah) are Arabian tribes and oases attested in Assyrian records; Islamic genealogists trace the Prophet through Ishmael via Kedar or Nebaioth.

**Sons of Israel; the genealogy of Judah, Hezron, Jerahmeel and Caleb** (1Chr 2:1-55)
- Ethan and Heman of Zerah are the sages of 1 Kgs 5:11 and the eponyms of Psalms 88-89; Solomon's wisdom is measured against them.
- Matthew 1:3-6 uses this Judah-to-David line (Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed, Jesse).

**Sons of David and the kings of Judah to the post-exilic descendants** (1Chr 3:1-24)
- Anani (3:24), last of the line, was read messianically: Targum to 1Chr 3:24 'Anani, he is the King Messiah who is to be revealed'; cf. Dan 7:13 'with the clouds (anane) of heaven'.
- Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27 make Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, against 1Chr 3:19.

**Clans of Judah; the prayer of Jabez; craft guilds; Bithiah daughter of Pharaoh** (1Chr 4:1-23)
- Rabbinic tradition (Lev. Rabbah 1:3; b. Megillah 13a) identifies Bithiah ('daughter of YH') with the Pharaoh's daughter who rescued Moses; compare the Quran's Asiya, wife of Pharaoh (Q 28:9, 66:11).
- Jabez is identified in b. Temurah 16a with Othniel, and Jabez's prayer became a popular Christian devotion.

**The sons of Levi and the high-priestly line to the exile** (1Chr 5:27-41)
- This Zadokite list underlies the priestly genealogy in Ezra 7:1-5 and the Zadokite claims of Qumran (Damascus Document).

**Levite clans, David's singers and the Levitical cities** (1Chr 6:1-66)
- Heman, Asaph and Ethan are the eponyms of Psalm headings (Ps 50, 73-83, 88, 89).

**Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher** (1Chr 7:1-40)
- Ephraimite raid on Gath: rabbinic midrash (b. Sanhedrin 92b, Targum to Ps 78:9) makes this a premature exodus of Ephraimites who miscalculated the end of bondage and were slain; their bones are the dry bones of Ezek 37.
- Serah daughter of Asher becomes in midrash the immortal woman who told Jacob Joseph lived and who showed Moses Joseph's coffin.

**The resettlers of Jerusalem; priests, Levites, gatekeepers and their duties** (1Chr 9:1-34)
- Parallel list in Neh 11; the perpetual day-and-night praise anticipates laus perennis monasticism and Rev 4:8.

**Saul's death on Gilboa and the theological verdict** (1Chr 10:1-14)
- Head of the slain enemy displayed in a temple: compare the Assyrian display of Teumman's head and Celtic head-trophies in sanctuaries.

**David's mighty men and their exploits** (1Chr 11:10-47)
- Water poured out rather than drunk: compare Alexander refusing water in the Gedrosian desert (Arrian, Anabasis 6.26).

**Warriors who joined David at Ziklag and the stronghold; Amasai's inspired greeting** (1Chr 12:1-23)
- 'The spirit clothed Amasai' recurs for Gideon (Judg 6:34) and Zechariah son of Jehoiada (2Chr 24:20); compare the Greek notion of a god 'putting on' a mortal's form.

**Tribal contingents come to Hebron to make David king; the feast** (1Chr 12:24-41)
- Issachar 'knowing the times' was read in rabbinic tradition (Gen. Rabbah 72; b. Yoma 26a) as mastery of astronomy and intercalation of the calendar.

**The first attempt to bring up the ark; Uzza struck down** (1Chr 13:1-14)
- Danger of touching the holy object: compare the Greek and Roman taboos on touching the Palladium, and Num 4:15.

**The Levites carry the ark to Jerusalem; musicians appointed; David dances** (1Chr 15:1-29)
- Kenaniah 'in charge of the massa' (15:22, 27) — either carrying or musical 'lifting' (oracle); obscure office.
- Royal ritual dance before the god: compare Egyptian pharaohs dancing before Min and the Hittite king's festival roles.

**The ark installed in David's tent; Levite singers appointed** (1Chr 16:1-7, 1Chr 16:37-43)
- The Levitical choirs of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun are the eponyms of psalm superscriptions (Pss 50, 73-83, 88, 39, 62, 77).

**David's thanksgiving psalm (composite of Pss 105, 96, 106)** (1Chr 16:8-36)
- Ps 105:15 / 1Chr 16:22 'touch not my anointed' became a proof text in Jewish-Christian debate; Quran 2:136 lists patriarchs as recipients of revelation (prophets), cf. 'my prophets' here.

**Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer** (1Chr 17:1-27)
- Royal sonship formula: cf. Ps 2:7, Egyptian and Mesopotamian divine sonship of kings; Heb 1:5 applies 1Chr 17:13 to Christ; 4Q174 (Florilegium) interprets it messianically.
- Quran 38:26 'O David, we have made you a vicegerent (khalifa) in the earth'.

**Satan incites the census; plague, the angel over Jerusalem and Ornan's threshing floor** (1Chr 21:1-30)
- 2Chr 3:1 identifies Ornan's threshing floor with Mount Moriah (Gen 22). Quran 38:21-25 has David's repentance; rabbinic Satan; Zoroastrian Ahriman as the source of evil, often invoked to explain the YHWH-to-Satan shift.

**David prepares materials and charges Solomon to build the temple** (1Chr 22:1-19)
- The bloodshed ban parallels the rabbinic rule that iron (instrument of war) may not touch the altar (m. Middot 3:4) and Quran-exegetical traditions that David began and Solomon completed Bayt al-Maqdis with jinn labor (cf. Quran 34:12-13).

**The twenty-four priestly courses by lot; remaining Levites** (1Chr 24:1-31)
- Luke 1:5 places Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, in the course of Abijah (24:10); 1Macc 2:1 derives the Hasmoneans from Joarib (24:7). The 24 courses underlie Qumran calendar texts (4Q320-330 Mishmarot), the Caesarea inscription and synagogue piyyutim; Rev 4:4's 24 elders have been linked to them.

**The twenty-four courses of temple musicians who 'prophesy' with lyres** (1Chr 25:1-31)
- Music as prophecy: cf. Elisha's minstrel (2Kgs 3:15), Greek mantic poetry and the Muses, Sufi sama'. The name-poem in 25:4 resembles acrostic and onomastic games in Mesopotamian scholarship.

**David's assembly speech and the written pattern of the temple** (1Chr 28:1-21)
- 28:18 is the earliest text naming the cherub throne 'merkavah', the term that gives Jewish Merkavah mysticism (Ezek 1, Hekhalot literature) its name; Sir 49:8 uses it of Ezekiel's vision.
- Divine blueprint for a temple: cf. Gudea of Lagash receiving the plan of Eninnu in a dream (Cylinder A).

**Free-will gifts, David's doxology, Solomon enthroned again, David's death** (1Chr 29:1-30)
- 29:11 is the source of the doxology appended to the Lord's Prayer ('for thine is the kingdom, the power and the glory', Matt 6:13 in later manuscripts, Didache 8.2) and of the kabbalistic sefirot names Gedullah, Gevurah, Tif'eret, Netsah, Hod, Malkhut.
- 29:14 'all things come of thee' is used at the Anglican offertory; 29:10-13 recited in the daily Jewish morning service (Vayevarekh David).

**Solomon at Gibeon asks for wisdom; his chariots, wealth and horse trade** (2Chr 1:1-18)
- Solomon's choice of wisdom: Quran 27:15-16 and 38:35 (Solomon asks for a kingdom none after him will have); Wisdom of Solomon 7-9; cf. the 'choice of Heracles'.

**The temple built on Mount Moriah; holy of holies, cherubim, veil and pillars** (2Chr 3:1-17)
- Moriah = temple mount underlies Josephus Ant. 1.226, Jubilees 18:13, rabbinic tradition and the Dome of the Rock's Foundation Stone; Islamic tradition locates the binding variously at Mina.

**Bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, lavers, lampstands and tables** (2Chr 4:1-22)
- Molten sea as the cosmic waters (Apsu basins in Mesopotamian temples); 12 oxen as zodiac/months in Josephus and Philo; rabbinic debate on 30 vs pi (Mishnat ha-Middot).

**The ark brought into the holy of holies; the cloud fills the house at the singing** (2Chr 5:1-14)
- Rabbinic tradition (b. Yoma 52b) has Josiah hide the ark; 2 Macc 2:4-8 has Jeremiah hide it on Mount Nebo. The poles 'to this day' fuel legends of the ark's survival.

**Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform** (2Chr 6:1-42)
- Prayer toward Jerusalem: Dan 6:10, Tob 3:11; the Muslim first qibla toward Jerusalem and Quran 2:142-144; synagogue orientation (b. Ber. 30a cites 1Kgs 8).
- 6:37 confession formula is used in the Yom Kippur vidui.

**Fire from heaven, the dedication feast and God's night reply** (2Chr 7:1-22)
- Fire from heaven on a dedication: Lev 9:24; 1Kgs 18:38; 2 Macc 1:18-36 (Nehemiah's naphtha fire) and 2:10 links Solomon's fire to the Hanukkah story.

**The Queen of Sheba tests Solomon; his gold, ivory throne, ships and death** (2Chr 9:1-31)
- Queen of Sheba: Quran 27:20-44 (Bilqis, the hoopoe, the glass floor); Targum Sheni to Esther and the Alphabet of Ben Sira (riddles); Ethiopian Kebra Nagast (Menelik); Matt 12:42.
- Solomon's throne with lions: elaborated in Targum Sheni and Islamic qisas (mechanical lions and eagles); Byzantine Throne of Solomon at the Magnaura.
- 666 recurs as the number of the beast (Rev 13:18).

**Rehoboam rejects the elders' counsel; the northern tribes secede** (2Chr 10:1-19)
- Rehoboam's counsel scene parallels Greek tyrant tales; Quran has no parallel but the elder/young counsellor topos appears in Ahiqar and Persian mirrors for princes.

**Rehoboam forsakes the Torah; Shishak's invasion; repentance and partial reprieve** (2Chr 12:1-16)
- Sheshonq I's Karnak relief lists conquered Palestinian towns. Retribution within one's lifetime as a Chronicler principle parallels Quranic punishment-narratives (e.g. Q 7, 11).

**Azariah son of Oded's oracle; Asa's covenant oath and the deposing of Maacah** (2Chr 15:1-19)
- The covenant oath in the third month was read by Jubilees and Qumran (1QS) as a Shavuot covenant-renewal festival.

**Asa bribes Ben-hadad, imprisons Hanani the seer, seeks physicians and is buried with spices** (2Chr 16:1-14)
- Zech 4:10 'the eyes of YHWH which range through all the earth'; cf. the Persian 'eyes and ears of the king' and Mesopotamian Shamash who sees all. Rabbinic sources debate the legitimacy of physicians (b. Ber. 60a; Sir 38).

**Jehoshaphat's piety, itinerant Torah teachers, tribute and army** (2Chr 17:1-19)
- Jehoshaphat's Torah teachers are cited in rabbinic tradition as a model of public instruction; compare Ezra's Levites (Neh 8:7-9) and the Islamic dispatch of Qur'an teachers by Muhammad (Mu'adh to Yemen).

**Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death** (2Chr 18:1-34)
- Lying spirit in the heavenly court: Job 1-2; 1 Enoch's watchers; the Quranic Iblis who volunteers to mislead (Q 7:16-17, 15:39); Zoroastrian druj (the Lie).
- Disguised king and the stray arrow: cf. Josiah's death (2Chr 35:22), and Greek tales of fated deaths despite disguise (Codrus).

**Jehoshaphat's fast and prayer; the Levite oracle; enemies destroy one another as the choir sings** (2Chr 20:1-37)
- Abraham as God's friend: Isa 41:8; James 2:23; Quran 4:125 (Abraham khalil Allah); the Hebron name al-Khalil.
- Victory through praise rather than fighting: cf. Joshua at Jericho; Byzantine and crusader processions with relics; 1QM (War Scroll) Levites and trumpets lead the battle.

**Jehoram kills his brothers; Elijah's letter; death by bowel disease, unlamented** (2Chr 21:1-20)
- Death by bowel disease/worms of a wicked ruler: Antiochus IV (2 Macc 9:5-9), Herod (Josephus Ant. 17.168-9), Herod Agrippa (Acts 12:23), Judas (Acts 1:18), Arius in Christian polemic; Lactantius' De mortibus persecutorum.
- Elijah's letter after his ascension was used in rabbinic tradition (Seder Olam 17) as a sign Elijah still acts after being taken up, cf. Elijah's return (Mal 3:23).

**Ahaziah counselled by his mother, killed by Jehu; Athaliah's purge and Joash hidden** (2Chr 22:1-12)
- The hidden royal infant raised in a temple: Moses, Cyrus (Herodotus 1.108-113), Zeus hidden from Kronos, the Mahdi/hidden imam topos; Ion raised at Delphi (Euripides).

**Joash repairs the temple with the collection chest; after Jehoiada's death he stones Zechariah** (2Chr 24:1-27)
- Matt 23:35 / Luke 11:51 'from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah ... between the sanctuary and the altar' (Matthew confuses him with Zechariah son of Berechiah). Rabbinic legend: Zechariah's blood seethed in the temple until Nebuzaradan slew thousands (b. Git. 57b; Lam. Rab. proem 23); Islamic tradition conflates him with Zakariyya father of Yahya, also martyred.

**Amaziah spares the assassins' sons, dismisses mercenaries, worships Edom's gods and is humbled** (2Chr 25:1-28)
- Plant fable of thistle and cedar: Jotham's fable (Judg 9), Aesop, Mesopotamian disputation poems (Tamarisk and Palm).

**Uzziah's prosperity, war machines and agriculture; struck with leprosy for offering incense** (2Chr 26:1-23)
- Josephus Ant. 9.225 adds an earthquake splitting the temple roof and a sunbeam striking Uzziah's face (cf. Amos 1:1, Zech 14:5). Incense usurpation and divine punishment parallels Korah (Num 16) and Nadab and Abihu.

**Ahaz's child sacrifice and defeats; Oded and the Ephraimites release and tend the captives** (2Chr 28:1-27)
- 28:15 is widely recognized as the model of the Good Samaritan parable (Luke 10:30-35): Samarians clothe, anoint, feed and set the wounded on donkeys and bring them to Jericho.

**Hezekiah reopens and purifies the temple** (2Chr 29:1-36)
- Compare 2Kgs 18:1-4 (no temple cleansing there) and Mishnah Pesahim 4:9 on Hezekiah's acts.

**Sennacherib's invasion, blasphemy and the angel's slaughter** (2Chr 32:1-23)
- Herodotus 2.141: Sennacherib's army undone by mice at Pelusium; Sennacherib's annals ('like a bird in a cage'); Esarhaddon's account of his father's murder.

**Hezekiah's illness and sign, pride, wealth, tunnel, Babylonian envoys and burial** (2Chr 32:24-33)
- Siloam tunnel inscription; 2Kgs 20:8-11 shadow on the steps; Babylonian Talmud Berakhot 10a on Hezekiah hiding the book of remedies.

**Manasseh's apostasy, captivity in Babylon, repentance and restoration** (2Chr 33:1-20)
- The apocryphal Prayer of Manasseh; rabbinic legend (Targum Chronicles, y. Sanhedrin 10) of Manasseh in a bronze mule heated by fire, crying to his idols and then to God; Ascension of Isaiah: Isaiah sawn asunder under Manasseh.

**Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant** (2Chr 34:8-33)
- Compare 2Kgs 22-23; finding of foundation texts by Nabonidus; the Egyptian 'book found in the temple' topos (Book of the Dead chapter 64 found under Menkaure).

**Josiah's great Passover** (2Chr 35:1-19)
- Compare 2Kgs 23:21-23; 1 Esdras 1 retells this Passover; Mishnah Pesahim 5 on Passover slaughter in three groups.

**Josiah ignores Necho's divine warning and dies at Megiddo; Jeremiah's lament** (2Chr 35:20-27)
- Zech 12:11 mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo; Lamentations attributed to Jeremiah (Targum, Josephus Ant. 10.78); Herodotus 2.159 Necho at 'Magdolus'; the Megiddo = Armageddon link in Rev 16:16.

**Last kings of Judah, burning of the temple, exile and seventy years** (2Chr 36:1-21)
- Lev 26:34-35 sabbaths of the land; Jer 25:11; 29:10; Dan 9:2 reinterprets the seventy years; Babylonian ration tablets naming Jehoiachin.

**The edict of Cyrus closes the Hebrew canon** (2Chr 36:22-23)
- Cyrus Cylinder (Marduk chose Cyrus, restoration of gods and peoples); Isa 44:28; 45:1 (Cyrus 'my anointed').

**Cyrus's decree and the return of the temple vessels** (Ezra 1:1-11)
- Cyrus Cylinder lines 30-34 on returning gods to their sanctuaries; Exod 3:21-22; 12:35-36 despoiling Egypt; 1 Esdras 2.

**List of the returnees with Zerubbabel** (Ezra 2:1-70)
- Parallel list Neh 7:6-72 with differing figures; 1 Esdras 5; rabbinic 'ten genealogical classes' that came up from Babylon (m. Qiddushin 4:1).

**Altar rebuilt, Sukkot kept, foundation of the second temple laid amid weeping and shouting** (Ezra 3:1-13)
- Hag 2:3 'who among you saw this house in its former glory?'; Mesopotamian kalû lamentations sung at laying of temple foundations (Akkadian kalu rituals).

**Offer of help from the deportee peoples rejected; opposition and accusations** (Ezra 4:1-7)
- Origin of the Samaritan schism as read by Josephus Ant. 11.84-88 and 2Kgs 17:24-41; the Samaritan counter-tradition.

**Rehum and Shimshai's letter to Artaxerxes and the king's stop order** (Ezra 4:8-24)
- Elephantine papyri for Aramaic chancery style (e.g. TAD A4.7 petition about rebuilding the Yahu temple); Persian 'eating salt' as covenant of loyalty (cf. Arabic milh, Num 18:19 covenant of salt).

**Cyrus's memorandum found at Ecbatana; Darius's decree; temple completed and dedicated** (Ezra 6:1-18)
- Behistun and Persepolis inscriptions' curse formulas on anyone who alters a decree; Herodotus 3.159 Darius impales 3,000 Babylonians; the Persian dahyu archives; Dan 6:9 law of the Medes and Persians.

**Ezra's priestly lineage and journey to Jerusalem** (Ezra 7:1-11)
- Rabbinic 'Ezra was worthy that the Torah be given through him had Moses not preceded him' (t. Sanhedrin 4:7); Quran 9:30 'Uzayr son of God'; 4 Ezra 14 Ezra restores the burnt scriptures.

**Artaxerxes' rescript to Ezra** (Ezra 7:12-26)
- Persian imperial 'authorization' theory; Udjahorresnet inscription (Darius restores Egyptian temple scribes); Demotic Chronicle on Darius codifying Egyptian law.

**Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders** (Ezra 10:1-44)
- Compare Deut 7:3; Neh 13:23-27; Malachi 2:11-16 (divorce 'hated'); Quran 60:10 on separation from unbelieving wives; 1 Esdras 9.

**News from Jerusalem and Nehemiah's prayer at Susa** (Neh 1:1-11)
- Ahiqar as cupbearer and seal-bearer of Esarhaddon (Tob 1:22); Herodotus 3.34 on the Persian royal cupbearer.

**The king's question, Nehemiah's commission and the night inspection of the walls** (Neh 2:1-20)
- Elephantine letter TAD A4.7 names 'Delaiah and Shelemiah sons of Sanballat governor of Samaria'; Qedarite king Geshem on a silver bowl from Tell el-Maskhuta; Herodotus 9.110 on Persian royal favors at a banquet.

**The builders of the wall and gates, section by section** (Neh 3:1-32)
- Akkadian building inscriptions apportioning wall sections; Josephus Ant. 11.174-183.

**Conspiracy against Jerusalem; builders work with a weapon in one hand** (Neh 4:1-17)
- Zionist and Israeli 'builder with a sword' imagery; Josephus Ant. 11.177; compare Arrian on Alexander's soldiers building under arms.

**Outcry over debt slavery; Nehemiah's remission and his refusal of the governor's allowance** (Neh 5:1-19)
- Solon's seisachtheia (shaking off of debts) in Athens; Mesopotamian misharum/andurarum edicts; Lev 25:35-43; Matt 10:14 shaking dust off; Acts 18:6 shaking out garments.

**Plots against Nehemiah, the open letter, the hired prophet and the wall completed in 52 days** (Neh 6:1-19)
- Josephus Ant. 11.179 gives two years and four months; Ben Sira 49:13 praises Nehemiah raising the walls.

**Ezra reads the Torah at the Water Gate; the day declared holy; Sukkot restored** (Neh 8:1-18)
- b. Megillah 3a: 'read distinctly' = Targum, 'gave the sense' = verse division and accents; Lev 23:40 four species; Jewish synagogue reading practice (standing, Amen) traced here; Esth 9:19 mishloah manot.

**Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession** (Neh 9:1-37)
- Prototype of penitential prayers (Dan 9; Baruch 1-3; Prayer of Azariah); Acts 7 Stephen's recital; Matt 23:31-37 Israel kills the prophets; Psalm 106.

**The sealed pledge (amanah) and its stipulations** (Neh 10:1-40)
- Mishnah Taanit 4:5 lists nine wood-offering days by family; Qumran Temple Scroll wood festival; Matt 17:24 temple tax; m. Hallah on the dough offering.

**Lists of priests and Levites; the high-priestly succession** (Neh 12:1-26)
- Josephus Ant. 11.302-347: Jaddua meets Alexander the Great; Elephantine papyri name Johanan as high priest c. 410 BCE.

**Dedication of the wall with two thanksgiving choirs processing on the wall** (Neh 12:27-47)
- Ritual circumambulation of city walls (Josh 6; Ps 48:13 'walk about Zion'); Roman lustratio and pomerium processions; Babylonian akitu procession.

**Ammonites and Moabites excluded; Tobiah expelled from the temple; Levites' portions, Sabbath and mixed marriages** (Neh 13:1-31)
- Josephus Ant. 11.302-312: Manasseh, brother of Jaddua, marries Nikaso daughter of Sanballat and becomes priest of the Samaritan temple on Gerizim; Jubilees 50 and Damascus Document on Sabbath commerce; Mal 2:4-8 covenant of Levi.

**Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal** (Esth 1:1-22)
- Herodotus 1.8-12 Candaules shows his wife's beauty to Gyges; Herodotus 9.108-113 Xerxes and Amestris; Herodotus 3.31 the royal judges; Josephus Ant. 11.191; b. Megillah 12b (Vashti to appear naked).

**The search for virgins, Esther made queen, and Mordecai foils the eunuchs' plot** (Esth 2:1-23)
- Thousand and One Nights frame (Shahriyar's nightly bride, Scheherazade); Herodotus 3.84 Persian king chooses wives from seven families; Herodotus 3.140, 8.85 'benefactors of the king' recorded; Tobit and Ahiqar on Jewish courtiers; Joseph's rise at a foreign court.

**Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; the lot is cast and the decree of extermination issued** (Esth 3:1-15)
- Akkadian puru 'lot' (die of Iahali, vizier of Shalmaneser III); 3 Maccabees (Ptolemy's decree against the Jews); Quran 28:6 and 40:24-36 Haman as Pharaoh's minister; rabbinic Haman as descendant of Agag and Amalek (Targum Sheni); Esarhaddon-era Ahiqar slandered at court.

**Mordecai's mourning and Esther's resolve to approach the king** (Esth 4:1-17)
- Mordecai's silence-or-act speech is the hinge for LXX Additions C (prayers of Mordecai and Esther) which supply the missing God-language.
- Esther's fast is the basis of Ta'anit Esther; compare Judith 8-9 (fast and prayer before entering the enemy camp).

**Esther before the king; first banquet; Haman's gallows** (Esth 5:1-14)
- Up to half the kingdom: Herod's oath to Salome's mother's daughter in Mark 6:23.
- Zeresh as wicked counselor wife: compare Jezebel (1 Kgs 21) and Job's wife (Job 2:9).

**The king's sleepless night and Mordecai's parade** (Esth 6:1-14)
- Herodotus 3.140 and 8.85: Persian kings recorded benefactors (orosangai) in royal registers and rewarded them.
- Rabbinic midrash (Megillah 16a) has Haman's daughter throw refuse on his head mistaking him for Mordecai.

**Second banquet; Haman exposed and hanged** (Esth 7:1-10)
- Hoist with his own petard: Ps 7:16-17 and 9:16, Prov 26:27 (who digs a pit falls in it); Perillus and the brazen bull of Phalaris.
- Covering the face of the condemned: Roman practice (caput obnubito) and Q. Curtius 6.8.22 on Macedonians.

**Mordecai elevated; the counter-decree** (Esth 8:1-17)
- Irrevocable law of the Medes and Persians: Dan 6:9,13,16.
- Persian royal post (angareion), Herodotus 8.98, Xenophon Cyropaedia 8.6.17.
- Esth 8:16 is recited at Havdalah.

**The thirteenth of Adar; Haman's ten sons** (Esth 9:1-19)
- Numbers: 500 and 300 in Shushan, 75,000 in the provinces; LXX gives 15,000.
- Haman's sons' names are chanted in one breath in synagogue; Targum Sheni and Talmud (Megillah 16b) discuss their layout.

**Letters instituting Purim** (Esth 9:20-32)
- Akkadian puru 'lot'; an inscribed lot-die of Iahali (Assyria, 9th c. BCE) is a physical pur.
- Comparisons of Purim with the Babylonian New Year (Marduk/Ishtar ~ Mordecai/Esther) and the Persian Farvardigan festival of the dead (Lagarde, Zimmern).
- 2 Macc 15:36 names 'Mordecai's day' on 14 Adar.

**Coda on Ahasuerus and Mordecai** (Esth 10:1-3)
- Joseph (Gen 41:43) and Daniel (Dan 2:48) as Jewish viziers; the Ahiqar romance.

**Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test** (Job 1:1-22)
- Testament of Job; Quran 21:83-84 and 38:41-44 (Ayyub afflicted, calls on God, strikes the ground with his foot for a spring).
- Heavenly wager: Goethe's Faust, Prologue in Heaven; the Babylonian Ludlul bel nemeqi and 'Babylonian Theodicy'; Indian Harishchandra tested by Vishvamitra after a wager among the gods (Markandeya Purana).
- Zech 3:1-2 (the Satan accusing the high priest) and 1 Chr 21:1.
- Ezek 14:14,20 pairs Job with Noah and Danel as proverbially righteous ancients.

**The second test; Job's wife; the three friends** (Job 2:1-13)
- LXX expands Job's wife's speech (she wanders as a servant); Testament of Job names her Sitis and has her sell her hair to Satan for bread.
- Quran 38:44: Ayyub told to strike (his wife?) with a bundle of grass so as not to break his oath.
- Shiva custom: comforters do not speak until the mourner speaks (Moed Qatan 28b), derived from this verse.

**Job curses the day of his birth** (Job 3:1-26)
- Jer 20:14-18 (curse on his birthday) is the closest parallel; Sophocles OC 1224 'not to be born is best' and the Silenus wisdom (Theognis 425-428).
- Rousing Leviathan by spell-casters: Ugaritic Lotan; Aramaic incantation bowls bind Leviathan.

**Eliphaz's first speech, the night vision** (Job 4:1-21)
- Demamah vaqol: Elijah's 'still small voice' (1 Kgs 19:12). Teman (Edom) was proverbial for wisdom (Jer 49:7, Obad 8).
- Mesopotamian night-apparitions and dream revelations (Ludlul tablet III).

**Eliphaz continues - seek God, accept discipline** (Job 5:1-27)
- Resheph: Canaanite plague/fire god (Ugaritic rsp), equated with Nergal and Apollo; cf. Hab 3:5, Deut 32:24.
- Covenant with wild beasts: Hos 2:20; Isa 11:6-9; Hesiod's golden age.

**Job's reply - the weight of grief and the treacherous wadi** (Job 6:1-30)
- Arrows of the god as plague: Apollo's arrows (Iliad 1), Resheph 'lord of the arrow' at Kition.

**Job - human life as hard service; 'Am I Sea or Dragon?'** (Job 7:1-21)
- Guard over Sea: Enuma Elish IV.139-140 (Marduk posts guards so Tiamat's waters do not escape); Ugaritic Yamm and Tunnanu bound by Anat.
- Land of no return: Akkadian 'erset la tari' (Descent of Ishtar).

**Bildad's first speech - the papyrus and the spider's web** (Job 8:1-22)
- Spider's house as image of flimsy trust: Quran 29:41 (the parable of the spider, al-Ankabut).

**Job - cosmic power of God and the impossible lawsuit** (Job 9:1-35)
- Rahab's helpers: Enuma Elish IV.105-120 (Tiamat's allies captured by Marduk); Isa 51:9, Ps 89:11.
- God treading on the back of Sea: Ugaritic and Akkadian 'treading on the back' as conquest; Mesoamerican earth-monster.
- No umpire: Christian readings of the mediator (1 Tim 2:5); Ludlul's search for an intercessor.

**Job - 'Your hands fashioned me'; land of darkness** (Job 10:1-22)
- Embryo as curdled milk: Aristotle, Generation of Animals 2.4 (semen as rennet); Quran 23:14 and 22:5 (nutfa, alaqa, mudgha); Wisdom of Solomon 7:2; Charaka Samhita.

**Zophar's first speech - the unsearchable depth of God** (Job 11:1-20)
- Four-dimension measure of God: Eph 3:18 (breadth, length, height, depth); Ps 139:8-9; Sirach 1:3.

**Job - ask the beasts; God's sovereign overturnings** (Job 12:1-25)
- Ask the beasts: Quran's signs (ayat) in animals (16:66-69); Francis of Assisi; Jainism. Job 12:9 echoes Isa 41:20 verbatim.

**Job - worthless physicians; 'though he slay me'** (Job 13:1-28)
- Talmud Bava Batra 16a: Rava reads 'Job sought to turn the dish upside down'; Sotah 27b debates the ketiv/qere of 13:15 to decide whether Job served from love.

**Job - 'man born of woman'; the tree has hope** (Job 14:1-22)
- Iliad 6.146-149 (generations of men like leaves); Mimnermus fr. 2; 'man born of woman' recited in the Anglican burial service.
- Bag of sins: Mesopotamian sealed tablets of guilt; 1 Sam 25:29 'bundle of the living' (tseror hachayyim).

**Eliphaz's second speech - the first man and the fate of the wicked** (Job 15:1-35)
- First man born before the hills: Ezek 28:12-17 (primal man in Eden full of wisdom), Prov 8:25 (Wisdom born before the hills); Iranian Gayomart; Adam Qadmon.
- Eavesdropping on the divine council: Jer 23:18,22; Prometheus; Mesopotamian apkallu sages.
- Ps 7:15 and Isa 59:4 'conceive mischief, bear iniquity'.

**Job - God the assailant; a witness in heaven** (Job 16:1-22)
- Blood crying from the ground: Gen 4:10 (Abel); Isa 26:21; Ezek 24:7-8.
- Heavenly advocate: Christian paraclete (1 John 2:1); the personal god of Mesopotamian laments; Zoroastrian Mithra/Rashnu as judges and witnesses.

**Job - a pledge with God; the grave as home** (Job 17:1-16)
- Kinship with the grave and worm: Sirach 10:11; Buddhist cemetery contemplations; Ecclesiastes.

**Bildad's second speech - the king of terrors** (Job 18:1-21)
- Ugaritic Mot (Death) as a devouring god; Nergal as king of the underworld; Greek Thanatos; the 'king of terrors' read in rabbinic and Christian tradition as the angel of death.
- Firstborn of Death: possibly a plague-demon, cf. Namtar, vizier of Ereshkigal.

**Job - abandoned by all; 'I know my redeemer lives'** (Job 19:1-29)
- 19:25-26 read as bodily resurrection in Christian tradition (Handel's Messiah; Vulgate 'in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum'); Clement of Rome 1 Clem 26.
- Rock inscription with iron stylus and lead-filled letters: Behistun inscription of Darius.

**Zophar's second speech - the portion of the wicked** (Job 20:1-29)
- Rivers of honey and milk: Quran 47:15 (rivers of water, milk, wine and honey in paradise); Ovid Met. 1.111 (golden age streams of milk and nectar).

**Job - why do the wicked prosper?** (Job 21:1-34)
- Jer 12:1; Ps 73; Mal 3:15; Babylonian Theodicy XXIII-XXVI; Plato Republic 2.364.
- Contrast Ezek 18 and Deut 24:16 against punishing sons for fathers.

**Eliphaz's third speech - Job accused of social crimes** (Job 22:1-30)
- Social-crime list echoes Egyptian Book of the Dead 125 (Negative Confession: 'I have not let anyone hunger') and Matt 25:35-45.
- 22:16 read in rabbinic midrash (Gen Rabbah) as the generation of the Flood.

**Job - 'Oh that I knew where I might find him'** (Job 23:1-17)
- Refining like gold: Zech 13:9, Mal 3:3, 1 Pet 1:7, Quran 29:2-3 (people will be tested).

**Job - the oppressed poor and the rebels against light** (Job 24:1-25)
- Loving darkness rather than light: John 3:19-20; Zoroastrian opposition of light (asha) and the deceivers of darkness.
- Placement of 24:18-24 is disputed; many assign it to Zophar's missing third speech.

**Bildad's third speech - man a worm** (Job 25:1-6)
- 25:2 'oseh shalom bimromav' became the closing line of the Kaddish and Amidah; rabbinic exegesis: peace between Michael (water) and Gabriel (fire).

**Job - the earth hung on nothing; Rahab smitten** (Job 26:1-14)
- Fleeing serpent: Isa 27:1 and Ugaritic KTU 1.5 I 1-3 'Lotan the fleeing serpent (btn brh), the twisting serpent, the mighty one with seven heads'.
- Earth suspended on nothing: Anaximander (earth floating unsupported); Quran 13:2 and 31:10 (heavens raised without visible pillars); Zaphon as Baal's mountain (Jebel Aqra).
- Abaddon personified: Rev 9:11 (angel of the abyss, Apollyon).

**Job's oath of integrity; the wicked man's portion** (Job 27:1-23)
- Wealth of the wicked inherited by the righteous: Prov 13:22, Eccl 2:26.

**The hymn to hidden wisdom** (Job 28:1-28)
- Ancient mining: Sinai turquoise and Timna copper mines; Agatharchides on Egyptian gold mines; Pliny NH 33.70-78 on Spanish mines.
- Hidden wisdom: Baruch 3:15-37; 1 Enoch 42 (Wisdom found no dwelling and returned to heaven); Sirach 24; Prov 3:14-15, 8:11.
- Gilgamesh's journey to the ends of the earth for life/wisdom.

**Job remembers his former glory** (Job 29:1-25)
- Phoenix (chol): Herodotus 2.73, Ovid Met. 15.391-407, 1 Clement 25, 2 Enoch 15; Egyptian Bennu bird.
- Testament of Job 9-15 expands Job's charity (doors open on four sides for travelers).

**Job's present humiliation** (Job 30:1-31)
- Despised troglodyte outcasts: Herodotus 4.183 (Ethiopian troglodytes); Agatharchides on root-eaters (rhizophagi).
- Ps 102:7 (pelican of the wilderness, owl of the ruins) as companions of the lamenter; Mic 1:8.

**Job's oath of innocence** (Job 31:1-40)
- Closest parallel: Egyptian Book of the Dead ch. 125 'Negative Confession' before the 42 judges, with the heart weighed on scales (cf. 31:6).
- Covenant with the eyes: Matt 5:28; Sirach 9:5,8. Kissing the hand to the moon: Pliny NH 28.25, Lucian De saltatione 17.
- Ps 81 and Ps 137:5-6 self-curse form; Assyrian loyalty-oath curses.
- Psalm 7:4-6, the Ezek 18 righteous man's list.

**Elihu is introduced and explains his intervention** (Job 32:1-22)
- New wine bursting old/new wineskins: Mark 2:22. Jewish tradition (Seder Olam; Bava Batra 15b) counts Elihu among the seven prophets to the gentiles, with Balaam, Job and Job's friends.
- The young sage who outwits elders: Daniel in Susanna; the boy Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2:46-47).

**Elihu - warning dreams and the interceding angel** (Job 33:1-33)
- Pinched off from clay: Akkadian karatsu tita 'to nip off clay' used of Aruru creating Enkidu (Gilgamesh I) and of Mami creating humans (Atrahasis I).
- Interceding angel: Michael as advocate; Talmud Shabbat 32a (a man's merits as paraclete, 'one in a thousand'); the kofer ransom echoes the Christian ransom theory.
- Naaman's flesh restored 'like a little child's' (2 Kgs 5:14).

**Elihu - God cannot do wrong** (Job 34:1-37)
- Ps 104:29-30 (God takes away their breath and they die); Quran 32:9 and 15:29 (God breathes his spirit into man).
- Midnight death of the mighty recalls the slaying of the firstborn (Exod 12:29).

**Elihu - human righteousness does not affect God** (Job 35:1-16)
- God's self-sufficiency: Quran 35:15 ('you are the poor ones in need of God, and God is the Rich'); Hadith qudsi 'O my servants, you cannot harm me nor benefit me' (Muslim, Birr 55); Epicurean impassible gods.

**Elihu on God's justice and suffering as discipline** (Job 36:1-25)
- Elihu's 'pedagogy of suffering' recalls Prov 3:11-12 and Heb 12:5-11; rabbinic yissurin shel ahavah (afflictions of love), b. Ber. 5a.

**Elihu's hymn on rain, thunder, snow and the storm** (Job 36:26-37:24)
- Cloud-gathering storm god (Baal 'rider of clouds', Zeus nephelegereta); 'gold from the north' has been linked to Zaphon, Baal's mountain.

**God's first speech from the whirlwind - foundations of earth, sea, light and the heavens** (Job 38:1-38)
- Sekhvi interpreted as rooster in rabbinic tradition (b. Ber. 60b; the morning blessing 'who gave the rooster understanding'); Egyptian ibis (Thoth) proposed for tuhot.
- Cornerstone and measuring line of the cosmos: Enuma Elish IV-V (Marduk measuring Apsu); Prov 8:27-29; Quran 79:27-33 rhetorical 'are you harder to create or the heaven?'

**God's first speech from the whirlwind - the wild animals** (Job 38:39-39:30)
- The ostrich's neglect of its eggs is also in Lam 4:3 and in Physiologus/medieval bestiaries; the raven fed by God: Ps 147:9, Luke 12:24.

**Behemoth** (Job 40:15-24)
- Behemoth and Leviathan as the paired primordial monsters kept for the eschatological banquet: 1 Enoch 60:7-9, 4 Ezra 6:49-52, 2 Baruch 29:4, b. B. Bat. 74b-75a; Behemoth paired with Ziz in Midrash.

**Leviathan** (Job 40:25-41:26)
- Ugaritic Ltn (Lotan) 'the twisting serpent' (KTU 1.5 I 1-3); Isa 27:1; Ps 74:14; Tiamat; the Indic Vrtra; Rev 12-13 dragon; rabbinic Leviathan banquet (b. B. Bat. 74b).

**Epilogue - the friends rebuked, Job's intercession and restoration** (Job 42:7-17)
- Testament of Job 46-52: the three daughters inherit magical sashes and speak in angelic tongues. LXX adds an ending identifying Job with Jobab king of Edom. Quran 38:41-44 (Ayyub restored, family given back 'and the like with them').

**Psalm 1 - the two ways** (Ps 1)
- Jer 17:5-8; Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope ch. 4 (the hot man vs the silent man as trees); Didache 1-6 and Barnabas 18-20 (two ways); Dhammapada 1-2 twin verses.

**Psalm 2 - the nations rage; the king as God's son** (Ps 2)
- Acts 4:25-27, 13:33; Heb 1:5; Rev 2:27, 12:5, 19:15 (rod of iron); Egyptian royal ideology of the pharaoh as son of the god; 4QFlorilegium; b. Sukkah 52a applies to messiah son of David.

**Psalm 4 - evening prayer of trust** (Ps 4)
- Eph 4:26 quotes 4:5 LXX 'be angry and sin not'.

**Psalm 5 - morning prayer against the deceitful** (Ps 5)
- Rom 3:13 quotes 5:10. Ps 5:8 is recited on entering the synagogue (Mah tovu sequence).

**Psalm 6 - plea of the sick sufferer** (Ps 6)
- First of the seven Christian penitential psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143); Ps 6:9 quoted Matt 7:23. Recited in Jewish Tahanun.

**Psalm 8 - what is man** (Ps 8)
- Matt 21:16 (babes), Heb 2:6-9, 1 Cor 15:27; rabbinic legend of the angels objecting to the creation of man / giving of Torah quoting 'what is man' (b. Sanh. 38b, b. Shabb. 88b); cf. Job 7:17 parody.

**Psalm 10 - why do you stand far off** (Ps 10)
- Ps 9-10 is one psalm in LXX and Vulgate, which is why Greek/Latin psalm numbering lags by one through Ps 147. Rom 3:14 quotes 10:7.

**Psalm 14 - the fool says there is no God** (Ps 14)
- Near duplicate of Ps 53 (Elohistic version). Rom 3:10-12 quotes 14:1-3.

**Psalm 15 - who may dwell on your holy mountain** (Ps 15)
- b. Makkot 24a: David reduced the 613 commandments to eleven (Ps 15). Egyptian temple-door inscriptions of purity requirements; Book of the Dead 125 negative confession.

**Psalm 16 - YHWH my portion; not abandoned to Sheol** (Ps 16)
- Acts 2:25-31 and 13:35 read 16:8-11 of the resurrection of Jesus. Levites' portion is YHWH (Num 18:20).

**Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany** (Ps 18)
- Duplicate of 2 Sam 22. Storm-god descent: Baal 'rider of the clouds' at Ugarit, Adad/Hadad and Teshub; Indra wielding the vajra against Vrtra; Zeus' thunderbolt.

**Psalm 19 - the heavens declare; the Torah is perfect** (Ps 19)
- Sun as judge seeing all (Shamash; Helios 'who sees all'); Rom 10:18 quotes 19:5; 19:15 closes the Amidah. Quran 17:44 'the seven heavens glorify him, but you do not understand their praise.'

**Psalm 20 - may YHWH answer you in the day of trouble** (Ps 20)
- A close parallel prayer in Aramaic written in Demotic script in Papyrus Amherst 63 (col. XI), addressed to Horus/YHW, often compared with Ps 20.

**Psalm 22 - my God, my God, why have you forsaken me** (Ps 22)
- Mark 15:34 / Matt 27:46 (Jesus' cry in Aramaic), John 19:24 (lots for garments), Matt 27:39-43 (head-wagging). Rabbinic: read of Esther (b. Megillah 15b; Ayelet ha-Shahar = Esther). Quran 4:157 denies the crucifixion.

**Psalm 23 - YHWH is my shepherd** (Ps 23)
- Shepherd-king epithet of Mesopotamian kings (Hammurabi 're'um') and of Shamash; John 10:11; Hermes Kriophoros iconography.

**Psalm 24 - lift up your heads, O gates** (Ps 24)
- Christian Harrowing of Hell tradition (Gospel of Nicodemus/Descensus 21) uses 24:7-10 at the gates of Hades; ark procession; Ugaritic 'lift up your heads, O gods' (KTU 1.2 I 27-29).

**Psalm 26 - judge me, for I have walked in integrity** (Ps 26)
- Hand-washing of innocence: Deut 21:6; Matt 27:24 (Pilate). Recited by priests at the lavabo in the Latin Mass.

**Psalm 27 - YHWH is my light; one thing I ask** (Ps 27)
- Recited daily in Jewish liturgy from Elul to Hoshana Rabbah; the sukkah of 27:5 links it to Sukkot.

**Psalm 29 - the voice of YHWH over the waters** (Ps 29)
- Widely considered an adapted Canaanite Baal hymn: Baal's thunder voice (qlh qdsh) shaking the earth in KTU 1.4 VII 29-35; Lebanon and Sirion as Baal's cedar mountains. Ugaritic 'bn ilm' = sons of El. Also the basis of the seven blessings of the Amidah (b. Ber. 28b).

**Psalm 30 - song at the dedication of the house** (Ps 30)
- Read at Hanukkah (Soferim 18:2) and in the daily morning service before Pesukei de-Zimra.

**Psalm 31 - into your hand I commit my spirit** (Ps 31)
- Luke 23:46 (Jesus' last words); Jewish bedtime prayer and Adon Olam 'beyado afqid ruhi'; Christian Compline.

**Psalm 32 - happy is he whose sin is forgiven** (Ps 32)
- Rom 4:7-8 quotes 32:1-2. Augustine's favorite psalm (Possidius); a Christian penitential psalm.

**Psalm 33 - by the word of YHWH the heavens were made** (Ps 33)
- Creation by divine word: Memphite Theology (Ptah creating by heart and tongue); John 1:1-3; Quran 36:82 'Be, and it is' (kun fa-yakun).

**Psalm 34 - acrostic when David feigned madness before Abimelech** (Ps 34)
- John 19:36 (no bone broken; cf. paschal lamb Exod 12:46); 1 Pet 2:3 and 3:10-12; Christian communion chant 'taste and see'. Abimelech as a royal title of Philistine kings (Gen 20, 26).

**Psalm 35 - contend, YHWH, with those who contend with me** (Ps 35)
- John 15:25 'they hated me without cause' quotes 35:19 or 69:5.

**Psalm 36 - transgression's oracle and the fountain of life** (Ps 36)
- Rom 3:18 quotes 36:2. 'In your light we see light' is the Nicene 'light from light' prooftext and the motto of Columbia University; Quran 24:35 (light upon light).

**Psalm 37 - acrostic: do not fret; the meek shall inherit the land** (Ps 37)
- Matt 5:5 'the meek shall inherit the earth'; Quran 21:105 'my righteous servants shall inherit the earth' explicitly cites the Zabur (Psalms) = Ps 37:29. Qumran Pesher on Psalms (4Q171) applies it to the Teacher of Righteousness.

**Psalm 38 - the sick penitent abandoned by friends** (Ps 38)
- Penitential psalm; sickness as punishment for sin as in Mesopotamian incantation-prayers (shuilla) and the Babylonian 'Ludlul bel nemeqi'.

**Psalm 39 - my days a handbreadth; I am a sojourner** (Ps 39)
- Hevel as in Qohelet; Heb 11:13 strangers and sojourners; Islamic hadith 'be in the world as a stranger' (Bukhari 6416).

**Psalm 40 - out of the miry pit; sacrifice you did not desire** (Ps 40)
- Heb 10:5-10 reads 40:7-9 LXX of Christ's body replacing sacrifices; prophetic critique of sacrifice (1 Sam 15:22, Hos 6:6, Ps 50, 51).

**Psalm 41 - happy who considers the poor; the friend who lifted his heel** (Ps 41)
- John 13:18 applies 41:10 to Judas; Ahithophel in rabbinic reading. Five-book Psalter mirrors the Torah (Midrash Tehillim 1:2).

**Psalm 42 - as the hart longs for water brooks** (Ps 42)
- Deer-at-water iconography in early Christian baptisteries; Ps 42-43 likely one poem with a triple refrain.

**Psalm 43 - send out your light and your truth** (Ps 43)
- 'Introibo ad altare Dei' (43:4 Vulgate) opened the Tridentine Mass.

**Psalm 44 - national lament; why do you sleep, O Lord** (Ps 44)
- Rom 8:36 quotes 44:23; rabbinic martyrology applies it to kiddush ha-shem (Gittin 57b, the mother and seven sons). b. Sotah 48a: the Levites' 'awakeners' (me'orerim) chanting 44:24 daily were abolished by John Hyrcanus. Sleeping god: Baal in 1 Kgs 18:27.

**Psalm 45 - royal wedding song** (Ps 45)
- Heb 1:8-9 applies 45:7-8 to Christ; Targum renders the king as the Messiah; Christian Marian reading of the queen. Often linked with Ahab and the Tyrian Jezebel.

**Psalm 46 - God is our refuge; a river makes glad the city** (Ps 46)
- Ezek 47:1-12, Joel 4:18, Zech 14:8, Rev 22:1-2 (river from the temple); Ugaritic El's dwelling 'at the source of the two rivers'. Luther's 'Ein feste Burg' paraphrases Ps 46.

**Psalm 47 - God has gone up with a shout** (Ps 47)
- Recited seven times before the shofar on Rosh Hashanah; Christian Ascension-day psalm. Mowinckel's hypothesized autumn enthronement festival, compared with the Babylonian Akitu.

**Psalm 48 - Mount Zion, the recesses of the north** (Ps 48)
- Zaphon (Jebel Aqra), Baal's mountain at Ugarit, transferred to Zion; Isa 14:13 'mount of assembly in the recesses of the north'; Mount Meru / Olympus as world-mountains. Sung as the Monday Levitical psalm (m. Tamid 7:4).

**Psalm 49 - no man can ransom his brother** (Ps 49)
- Luke 12:16-21 (rich fool); Quran 102 and 104:2-3 (he thinks his wealth will make him immortal); Egyptian Harper's Songs ('none takes his goods with him'). Personified Death as shepherd: Ugaritic Mot.

**Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls** (Ps 50)
- Mesopotamian care-and-feeding of the gods contrasted (Atrahasis: gods gather like flies over the sacrifice). Quran 22:37 'their flesh and blood do not reach God, but your piety reaches him.' Rabbinic Ziz bird (b. B. Bat. 73b) from 50:11, paired with Behemoth and Leviathan.

**Psalm 51, David's confession after Bathsheba (Miserere)** (Ps 51:1-21)
- Ps 51 is the Christian Miserere; v.7 is a proof text for original sin (Augustine). Compare Mesopotamian penitential prayers (eršahunga) and the Egyptian negative confession inverted.

**Psalm 53, the fool says there is no God (Elohistic doublet of Ps 14)** (Ps 53:1-7)
- Quoted in Romans 3:10-12. Compare Quran 45:24 on those who deny resurrection and divine agency.

**Psalm 55, wings of a dove and the treacherous friend** (Ps 55:1-24)
- Three daily prayer times: Dan 6:11; rabbinic shaharit/minhah/arvit; contrast the five Islamic salat. 1 Pet 5:7 echoes v.23. Judas traditions read vv.13-15 of the betrayer.

**Psalm 56, when the Philistines seized David in Gath** (Ps 56:1-14)
- Tear-flask: later lachrymatory bottles; Quran/hadith on God recording deeds; Mandaean and Zoroastrian books of deeds.

**Psalm 57, in the shadow of your wings (in the cave)** (Ps 57:1-12)
- Talmud Berakhot 3b: David's harp hung over his bed and the north wind played it at midnight, waking him (from v.9).

**Psalm 58, do you gods truly speak justice?** (Ps 58:1-12)
- Snake-charming: Egyptian and Mesopotamian snake spells; Jer 8:17; Eccl 10:11.

**Psalm 60, God has rejected us; Moab my washpot** (Ps 60:1-14)
- Sandal as symbol of acquiring land: Ruth 4:7, Deut 25:9; Nuzi texts on transfer by the foot/shoe.

**Psalm 62, for God alone my soul waits in silence** (Ps 62:1-13)
- Weighing image recalls the Egyptian weighing of the heart and the Quranic mizan (Q 7:8-9, 101:6-9). Rom 2:6 quotes v.13.

**Psalm 65, praise in Zion; God crowns the year with bounty** (Ps 65:1-14)
- Baal as rain-giver and rider of clouds in Ugaritic texts; Mesopotamian hymns to Adad. Rabbinic: rain blessings.

**Psalm 67, may God be gracious and bless us; let the peoples praise you** (Ps 67:1-8)
- Recited during the counting of the Omer; in Kabbalistic tradition written in the shape of a menorah (seven verses, 49 words).

**Psalm 68, let God arise; the rider of the clouds marches from Sinai to his mountain** (Ps 68:1-36)
- v.19 quoted in Eph 4:8 (Christ ascending). v.32 central to Ethiopian Christian self-understanding. Ugaritic Baal cycle: rider of clouds, Bashan/btn serpent, mountain Zaphon envied by others. Midrash: mountains competing to host the Torah (Tabor, Carmel vs Sinai) derives from vv.16-17.

**Psalm 69, the waters have come up to my neck; gall and vinegar** (Ps 69:1-37)
- Most-quoted lament in the NT passion narratives: v.10 (John 2:17), v.22 (Matt 27:34,48), v.23 (Rom 11:9), v.26 (Acts 1:20 of Judas). Compare Jonah 2.

**Psalm 70, O God, hasten to deliver me (doublet of Ps 40:14-18)** (Ps 70:1-6)
- v.2 'Deus in adiutorium meum intende' opens every hour of the monastic Divine Office (Cassian, Conferences 10.10).

**Psalm 72, for Solomon; the ideal king; end of Book II** (Ps 72:1-20)
- b. Sanhedrin 98b: one of the Messiah's names is Yinnon (from v.17). v.10-11 shaped the Christian Magi tradition (kings bearing gifts). Compare Mesopotamian royal hymns (Shulgi) and Egyptian royal ideology of the king as bringer of Ma'at and Nile flood.

**Psalm 73, Asaph on the prosperity of the wicked; afterward you will take me to glory** (Ps 73:1-28)
- Compare Job 21, Jeremiah 12:1, Babylonian Theodicy and Ludlul bel nemeqi. v.24 is a key text for afterlife in the Psalms.

**Psalm 74, the burned sanctuary and God who crushed the heads of Leviathan** (Ps 74:1-23)
- Combat myth: Baal defeats Yam and Lotan (KTU 1.5 I 1-3; 1.3 III 38-42); Marduk splits Tiamat (Enuma Elish IV); Indra slays Vritra and frees the rivers. Leviathan as eschatological food for the righteous: 2 Baruch 29:4, 1 Enoch 60:7-9, b. Bava Batra 74b-75a.

**Psalm 76, God's lair in Salem where he broke the flaming arrows** (Ps 76:1-13)
- LXX heading adds 'concerning the Assyrian': read of Sennacherib's army struck in its sleep (2Kgs 19:35; Herodotus 2.141 on mice gnawing the Assyrian bows).

**Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David** (Ps 78:1-72)
- v.2 quoted in Matt 13:35. 'Table in the wilderness' parallels the Quran's ma'ida (Q 5:112-115), where the disciples ask whether God can send down a table from heaven. Bread of angels: Wis 16:20, John 6:31. Compare plague lists in Ps 105 and in Artapanus.

**Psalm 79, the nations have come into your inheritance** (Ps 79:1-13)
- vv.6-7 are recited at the Passover Seder when the door is opened for Elijah (Shefokh hamatkha). 1 Macc 7:17 quotes vv.2-3 of the Hasideans' murder.

**Psalm 80, Shepherd of Israel enthroned on the cherubim; the vine from Egypt** (Ps 80:1-20)
- Rabbinic: the boar of the forest = Rome/Edom (Lev. Rabbah 13.5). Vine of Israel: Isa 5, Hos 10:1; John 15 (true vine). Son of man: Dan 7:13.

**Psalm 81, blow the shofar at the new moon; O that my people would listen** (Ps 81:1-17)
- v.4-5 is the Rosh Hashanah proof text (b. Rosh Hashanah 8a-b: keseh = the day the moon is covered). Thursday psalm of the Levites (m. Tamid 7:4). Rom 1:24 on God handing people over to their desires.

**Psalm 82, God judges in the council of El; you are gods, yet you shall die** (Ps 82:1-8)
- Quoted by Jesus in John 10:34. Rabbinic readings take the 'gods' as Israel at Sinai who lost immortality through the calf (b. Avodah Zarah 5a). Ugaritic assembly of El ('dt ilm, bn il); fall of the Watchers in 1 Enoch; Isa 24:21-22. Compare Hesiod's Theogony on gods deposed.

**Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar** (Ps 84:1-13)
- Birds nesting at temples as inviolable: Herodotus 1.159 (Aristodicus and the sparrows of Branchidae); Aelian. Solar epithet: Mesopotamian Shamash as judge; Mal 3:20 sun of righteousness.

**Psalm 85, steadfast love and truth meet; righteousness and peace kiss** (Ps 85:1-14)
- Medieval Christian 'Four Daughters of God' allegory (Mercy, Truth, Justice, Peace debating man's redemption) grew from v.11 via Midrash (Gen. Rabbah 8.5: at man's creation Hesed and Tsedeq favored, Emet and Shalom opposed, and God cast Truth to earth - from v.12).

**Psalm 87, Zion mother of nations; this one was born there** (Ps 87:1-7)
- LXX 'Mother Zion' (meter Sion) behind Gal 4:26 (Jerusalem above is our mother). Compare Mesopotamian Babylon/Esagila as navel of the world and Delphi as omphalos.

**Psalm 88, Heman's lament from the pit; darkness my companion** (Ps 88:1-19)
- Rephaim also in Ugaritic funerary texts (rpum) and Phoenician tomb inscriptions (Tabnit, Eshmunazar). Mesopotamian 'land of no return' (Descent of Ishtar). Rev 9:11 Abaddon as angel of the abyss.

**Psalm 89, Ethan's hymn of the divine council, Rahab crushed, and the broken Davidic covenant** (Ps 89:1-53)
- Baal cycle: Baal defeats Yam (Sea) and Nahar (River); Ps 89:26 transfers this to the Davidic king, as Assyrian kings 'wash weapons in the sea'. Moon as witness: cf. ancient treaty witness lists of celestial deities. 'My firstborn' (v.28) read messianically (Heb 1:6).

**Psalm 90, prayer of Moses; a thousand years as yesterday** (Ps 90:1-17)
- v.4: 2 Pet 3:8; Jubilees 4:30 (Adam died at 930, short of a 'day' of 1000 years); Quran 22:47 and 32:5 ('a day with your Lord is as a thousand years'), 70:4 (fifty thousand). Mountains 'born': cf. Hesiod's Gaia bearing the mountains (Theogony 129).

**Psalm 91, shelter of the Most High; the noonday demon; angels bear you up** (Ps 91:1-16)
- Satan quotes vv.11-12 in the temptation of Jesus (Matt 4:6). 11QApocryphal Psalms (11Q11) pairs it with anti-demonic songs; rabbis call it shir shel pega'im (y. Shabbat 6:2; b. Shevuot 15b). Qeteb meriri as noonday demon (Num. Rabbah 12.3); LXX daimonion mesembrinon -> the monastic 'noonday demon' of acedia (Evagrius). Used on Jewish, Christian and Coptic amulets.

**Psalm 92, a song for the Sabbath day; the righteous flourish like the palm** (Ps 92:1-16)
- Levitical psalm for the Sabbath (m. Tamid 7:4); rabbinic tradition ascribes it to Adam on the first Sabbath (Gen. Rabbah 22.13). Mishnah calls it a song 'for the world to come, a day wholly Sabbath'.

**Psalm 93, YHWH reigns; the floods have lifted up their voice** (Ps 93:1-5)
- Friday Levitical psalm (m. Tamid 7:4). Ugaritic Baal's kingship follows his defeat of Prince Yam and Judge Nahar (KTU 1.2 IV).

**Psalm 94, God of vengeance; he who planted the ear** (Ps 94:1-23)
- Wednesday Levitical psalm. Argument of v.9 recurs in Philo and in Islamic kalam on divine hearing and seeing (Q 58:1).

**Psalm 95, come let us sing; today if you hear his voice (Venite)** (Ps 95:1-11)
- Opens Kabbalat Shabbat (Lekhu neranenah) and the Christian Invitatory (Venite). Heb 3:7-4:11 builds a theology of Sabbath rest on v.11.

**Psalm 96, sing a new song; the gods of the nations are nothings** (Ps 96:1-13)
- Justin Martyr (Dial. 73) accused Jews of removing 'reigned from the tree' from v.10.

**Psalm 97, YHWH reigns; clouds and thick darkness; all gods bow down** (Ps 97:1-12)
- Heb 1:6 quotes v.7 (LXX) of angels worshipping the Son. 'Or zarua' recited before Kol Nidre; Kabbalah's hidden primordial light sown for the righteous (b. Hagigah 12a).

**Psalm 99, YHWH reigns enthroned on cherubim; holy is he** (Ps 99:1-9)
- Threefold 'holy' parallels Isa 6:3 and the Christian Trisagion/Sanctus. Jer 15:1 likewise pairs Moses and Samuel as intercessors.

**Psalm 101, the king's vow of integrity** (Ps 101:1-8)
- Compare Egyptian royal instructions (Merikare) and the Mesopotamian 'Advice to a Prince'; Luther called it 'David's mirror for princes'.

**Psalm 102, prayer of the afflicted; the heavens wear out like a garment** (Ps 102:1-29)
- vv.26-28 applied to the Son in Heb 1:10-12. Cf. Isa 51:6; Stoic ekpyrosis; Iranian frashokereti renewal of the world.

**Psalm 103, bless YHWH, O my soul; youth renewed like the eagle** (Ps 103:1-22)
- Eagle renewal: Rashi and Saadia cite the eagle that flies near the sun, plunges into the sea and is renewed; links to the Physiologus eagle and the phoenix legend; cf. Isa 40:31.

**Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten)** (Ps 104:1-35)
- Close parallels with Akhenaten's Great Hymn to the Aten: night when lions come out of their dens and snakes bite / at dawn they retire and men go to work (vv.20-23); ships sailing upstream and downstream and fish in the river (vv.25-26); 'How manifold are your works' (v.24); the creatures live when the god rises and die when he sets (vv.27-30). Leviathan as God's plaything: b. Avodah Zarah 3b (God plays with Leviathan in the last three hours of the day). Rabbinic Rosh Hodesh psalm; Christian Pentecost text (v.30 'Emitte spiritum tuum').

**Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus** (Ps 105:1-45)
- The iron collar of v.18 underlies later Joseph legends (Targum, Jubilees, Quran 12:42 years in prison). Plague lists: compare Ps 78:44-51, Wis 16-19, Artapanus, and Quran 7:133 (flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood) and 17:101 (nine signs).

**Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile** (Ps 106:1-48)
- Ps 106:47-48 is quoted in 1Chr 16:35-36. Compare Acts 7 (Stephen's sin-history) and Neh 9.
- Rom 1:23 echoes 106:20 (glory exchanged for an image).

**Psalm 107, thanksgiving of the redeemed (wanderers, prisoners, sick, seafarers)** (Ps 107:1-43)
- Inverted nun signs in 107:23-28 in the Masoretic tradition. Talmud (Ber 54b) derives from the four groups the obligation of the thanksgiving blessing (birkat ha-gomel).
- Compare Jonah 1 and Mark 4:35-41 (Jesus stilling the storm); Isa 45:2 (bronze doors, iron bars); 1 Pet 3:19 / harrowing of hell imagery.

**Psalm 109, curses on the accuser** (Ps 109:1-31)
- Acts 1:20 applies 109:8 ('let another take his office') to Judas. Compare curse tablets (defixiones) and Mesopotamian curse formulae binding offspring.

**Psalm 110, the lord at God's right hand, priest after Melchizedek** (Ps 110:1-7)
- Most-quoted psalm in the New Testament (Mark 12:36, Acts 2:34, Heb 1:13, 5-7). Qumran 11QMelchizedek makes Melchizedek a heavenly redeemer. Compare Egyptian iconography of the pharaoh enthroned at the god's right with enemies as footstool (Tutankhamun's footstool).

**Psalm 111, acrostic hymn on God's works** (Ps 111:1-10)
- Twin of Ps 112: phrases of God in 111 (his righteousness endures forever, gracious and compassionate) are transferred to the righteous man in 112.

**Psalm 112, acrostic on the blessed God-fearer** (Ps 112:1-10)
- 2 Cor 9:9 quotes 112:9. Compare Matt 8:12 'gnashing of teeth' of the excluded wicked.

**Psalm 113, God on high raises the poor and the barren** (Ps 113:1-9)
- Opens the Hallel (Ps 113-118) of the festivals and Passover Seder. Compare Luke 1:46-55 (Magnificat) and Mal 1:11.

**Psalm 114, when Israel went out of Egypt the sea fled** (Ps 114:1-8)
- Dante, Purgatorio 2:46 (In exitu Israel sung by souls arriving at Purgatory). Compare Ugaritic Yamm and Nahar (Sea and River) as paired chaos foes of Baal.

**Psalm 115, not to us, polemic against idols** (Ps 115:1-18)
- 'Those who fear YHWH' (115:11) later read as God-fearers/proselytes. Compare Jer 10, Isa 44, Epistle of Jeremiah, and Quran 7:195 on idols with feet that cannot walk.

**Psalm 116, thanksgiving after rescue from death** (Ps 116:1-19)
- Rom 3:4 cites 116:11 ('let every man be a liar'). Cup of salvation linked to the Seder cups and the eucharistic cup (Roman canon 'calicem salutaris').

**Psalm 117, all nations praise** (Ps 117:1-2)
- Rom 15:11 quotes it for the gentiles' inclusion.

**Psalm 118, festal thanksgiving, the rejected stone and hosanna** (Ps 118:1-29)
- Mark 11:9-10 and 12:10-11 (triumphal entry; the rejected stone); Acts 4:11; 1 Pet 2:7. Hoshana rituals of Sukkot circle the altar with willows (m. Sukkah 4:5).

**Psalm 119, stanzas alef to he** (Ps 119:1-40)
- Ps 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible (176 verses). Compare the Avestan/Vedic litanies built on fixed sacred terms, and Mesopotamian acrostics like the Babylonian Theodicy.

**Psalm 119, stanzas vav to kaf** (Ps 119:41-88)
- Midnight prayer (119:62) underlies Tikkun Hatzot and the monastic night office (Benedict, Rule 16, cites 119:62 and 119:164).

**Psalm 119, stanzas lamed to ayin** (Ps 119:89-128)
- 119:126 is read in m. Berakhot 9:5 as permitting the use of God's name in greetings; later used to justify writing down the Oral Torah.

**Psalm 119, stanzas pe to tav** (Ps 119:129-176)
- 119:164 is the basis of the seven canonical hours. Compare Luke 15:4-7 (lost sheep) and the Islamic five daily prayers.

**Psalm 120, song of ascents against the lying tongue** (Ps 120:1-7)
- Rabbinic tradition links the fifteen Songs of Ascents to the fifteen steps between the Women's and Israelites' courts (m. Middot 2:5; b. Sukkah 51b) and to David calming the abyss when digging the temple foundations.

**Psalm 121, the keeper who does not sleep** (Ps 121:1-8)
- Contrast 1Kgs 18:27 (Elijah mocks Baal as asleep) and the Egyptian/Mesopotamian sleeping gods. Moonstroke belief: Matt 4:24 seleniazomai. Ps 121 is the classic shir ha-ma'alot amulet over the birthing bed against Lilith.

**Psalm 122, pilgrim's song, pray for the peace of Jerusalem** (Ps 122:1-9)
- b. Taanit 5a reads 122:3 as an earthly Jerusalem joined to a heavenly one; compare Gal 4:26 and Rev 21 (Jerusalem above).

**Psalm 126, restoration of Zion, sowing in tears** (Ps 126:1-6)
- Sung before Grace after Meals on Sabbaths and festivals. The legend of Honi the Circle-Drawer's seventy-year sleep is generated from 126:1 (b. Taanit 23a). Compare the Egyptian/Adonis lament over the sown seed.

**Psalm 127, unless YHWH builds the house; sons as arrows** (Ps 127:1-5)
- Motto 'Nisi Dominus' of many city coats of arms. Compare Hesiod, Works and Days on toil, and Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope on fate and labor.

**Psalm 128, blessing of the God-fearer's household** (Ps 128:1-6)
- Used in Jewish and Christian wedding liturgies.

**Psalm 130, out of the depths** (Ps 130:1-8)
- One of the seven Penitential Psalms; Luther's hymn 'Aus tiefer Not'. Recited in the Ten Days of Repentance.

**Psalm 131, a soul like a weaned child** (Ps 131:1-3)
- Compare Ben Sira 3:21-22 'seek not what is too wonderful for you' (quoted in b. Hagigah 13a against esoteric speculation).

**Psalm 132, David's vow, the ark and the oath to David** (Ps 132:1-18)
- Luke 1:69 ('horn of salvation in the house of David'); Acts 2:30 (oath and fruit of loins). Compare Mesopotamian royal temple-building vows (Gudea's sleepless dedication).

**Psalm 133, brothers dwelling together, oil and dew** (Ps 133:1-3)
- Hinneh ma tov; motto of fraternal orders. Compare the Ugaritic dew-and-oil blessings (dew of heaven, oil of earth) of Baal's daughters Tallay and Pidray.

**Psalm 135, hymn on God's power, election and the idols** (Ps 135:1-21)
- 135:7 = Jer 10:13; compare the Babylonian/Ugaritic storm god's storehouses and Quran 15:21-22 (winds as fertilizers, treasuries of all things).

**Psalm 136, litany 'for his steadfast love is forever' (Great Hallel)** (Ps 136:1-26)
- Rabbinic tradition of the sea divided into twelve paths (one per tribe) is drawn from gozer lig'zarim. Compare Quran 26:63 (sea split, each part like a great mountain) and Quran 55 (Surat al-Rahman), whose refrain 'Which of your Lord's favors will you deny?' structures a creation-and-favors litany.

**Psalm 137, by the rivers of Babylon** (Ps 137:1-9)
- 137:5-6 recited at Jewish weddings (breaking the glass). Compare Hos 14:1, Nah 3:10, 2Kgs 8:12 for dashing infants as a war atrocity, and Homer, Iliad 22:63-64 (Priam foresees his grandsons dashed down).

**Psalm 138, thanksgiving before the gods** (Ps 138:1-8)
- Compare Dan 6:11 and 1Kgs 8:35 (prayer toward the temple) and the qibla in Islam.

**Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo** (Ps 139:1-24)
- Amos 9:2-3 (no escape to Sheol, heaven, Carmel or sea); Quran 50:16 (closer than the jugular vein) and 57:4. 'Golem' here is the source of the later term for the artificial man; compare the earth-born first man of Gen 2:7 and Mesopotamian tablets of destiny.

**Psalm 140, deliverance from violent men with serpent tongues** (Ps 140:1-14)
- Rom 3:13 cites 140:4 in a catena on universal sin.

**Psalm 141, prayer as incense, guard on the mouth** (Ps 141:1-10)
- Evening psalm of Byzantine Vespers ('Lord, I have cried'); Rev 5:8 and 8:3-4 (prayers as incense).

**Psalm 143, enter not into judgment** (Ps 143:1-12)
- Rom 3:20 and Gal 2:16 echo 143:2 ('no flesh justified'). Last of the seven Penitential Psalms.

**Psalm 144, royal prayer for victory and prosperity** (Ps 144:1-15)
- Largely a reworking of Ps 18 (2Sam 22). Compare Greek caryatids for daughters as carved pillars.

**Psalm 145, acrostic praise of the King (Ashrei)** (Ps 145:1-21)
- b. Berakhot 4b: whoever recites it three times daily is assured the world to come; the missing nun explained as avoiding 'Fallen is the virgin Israel' (Amos 5:2). Compare Quran 2:186 ('I am near; I answer the caller').

**Psalm 146, do not trust in princes** (Ps 146:1-10)
- Compare Isa 61:1 and Luke 4:18, 7:22 (blind see, captives freed); the morning blessings 'who opens the eyes of the blind... frees the captive'.

**Psalm 147, builder of Jerusalem, counter of stars, giver of snow** (Ps 147:1-20)
- Isa 40:26 (calls the stars by name); Job 38:41 and Luke 12:24 (ravens fed). Compare Quran 67:5 and Babylonian star catalogues.

**Psalm 148, praise from heaven and earth** (Ps 148:1-14)
- Expanded in the Prayer of Azariah / Song of the Three Young Men (Benedicite, Dan 3:57-90 LXX) and Francis of Assisi's Canticle of the Creatures. Compare Quran 17:44 and 24:41 (all in heaven and earth glorify God).

**Psalm 149, new song, dance, and the sword of the faithful** (Ps 149:1-9)
- Read by Thomas Müntzer in the Peasants' War; compare Qumran War Scroll (1QM) where the faithful execute eschatological judgment, and Rev 1:16 (two-edged sword from the mouth).

**Psalm 150, everything that breathes, praise Yah** (Ps 150:1-6)
- Tenfold 'hallelu' linked in b. Rosh Hashanah 32a to the ten utterances of creation. LXX adds Ps 151 (David and Goliath), found in Hebrew at Qumran 11QPs-a.

**Proverbs 1:1-7, title and purpose; fear of YHWH** (Prov 1:1-7)
- Compare Egyptian instruction prologues (Ptahhotep, Amenemope ch. 1) and the Sumerian Instructions of Shuruppak.

**Proverbs 1:8-19, warning against the gang of robbers** (Prov 1:8-19)
- Compare Mot (Death) with open gullet in Ugaritic myth swallowing Baal, and Isa 5:14.

**Proverbs 1:20-33, Lady Wisdom's speech in the streets** (Prov 1:20-33)
- Wisdom speaks like a prophet (cf. Jer 7:13). Compare 1 Enoch 42 (Wisdom finds no dwelling among men and returns to heaven), Sir 24, Wis 7-9, Matt 23:34-37 / Luke 11:49, and the Gnostic Sophia.

**Proverbs 2, seeking wisdom as treasure; the strange woman** (Prov 2:1-22)
- Compare Matt 5:5 (meek inherit the earth) and Ps 37. The 'land of no return' is a stock name for the Mesopotamian underworld (Descent of Ishtar).

**Proverbs 3:1-12, trust in YHWH, firstfruits, the Lord's discipline** (Prov 3:1-12)
- Heb 12:5-6 quotes 3:11-12 (LXX). Compare Jer 31:33 (law written on the heart) and 2 Cor 3:3.

**Proverbs 3:13-35, wisdom a tree of life; creation by wisdom; neighbor ethics** (Prov 3:13-35)
- Prov 3:17-18 sung when the Torah scroll is returned to the ark ('Etz hayyim hi'); the scroll's rollers are called atsei hayyim. Jas 4:6 and 1 Pet 5:5 quote 3:34 (LXX). Egyptian Maat iconography: the goddess holding the ankh (life) in one hand and a scepter in the other.

**Proverbs 4, a father's father's teaching; the two paths** (Prov 4:1-27)
- Compare Didache 1-6 and Barnabas 18-20 (Two Ways), Qumran Two Spirits (1QS 3-4), and the Pythagorean Y.

**Proverbs 5, the strange woman versus the wife of one's youth** (Prov 5:1-23)
- Compare Song 4:12-15 (bride as sealed fountain) and Eccl 9:9. Egyptian Instruction of Any warns against 'the woman from abroad, not known in her town'.

**Proverbs 6:1-19, surety, the ant, the scoundrel, six things God hates** (Prov 6:1-19)
- Quran 27:18 (the ant in Solomon's valley) and the Arabic proverbial wisdom of the ant; Aesop's Ant and Grasshopper. Compare Ahiqar sayings on surety.

**Proverbs 7, the youth and the seductress at twilight** (Prov 7:1-27)
- Compare the 'woman at the window' ivories (Astarte/Kilili 'who leans from the window') and Ishtar as the goddess of the tavern who seduces passers-by; Gilgamesh VI (Ishtar's lovers destroyed). The Qumran 'Wiles of the Wicked Woman' (4Q184) develops this figure as a demonic seductress.

**Proverbs 8:1-21, Wisdom's public speech, by me kings reign** (Prov 8:1-21)
- Compare Matt 7:7 (seek and you will find) and Wis 8:2-3 (Solomon sought Wisdom as bride). Isis aretalogies use the same 'I am' self-praise ('I gave laws to men').

**Proverbs 8:22-31, Wisdom before and at creation** (Prov 8:22-31)
- Central text for the Arian controversy (LXX ektisen 'created me') and for Logos/Christ as pre-existent Wisdom (John 1:1-3, Col 1:15-17, Heb 1:2-3). Sir 24 identifies Wisdom with Torah; Gen. Rabbah 1:1 and m. Avot 3:14 make Torah the instrument of creation; 'reshit' links to Targum Neofiti Gen 1:1 'in wisdom God created'.
- Compare Egyptian Maat, daughter of Re, present with him at creation; Mesopotamian apkallu/ummanu sages; Avestan Spenta Mainyu and the Amesha Spentas; Philo's Sophia as mother of the Logos; Gnostic Sophia; Kabbalistic Hokhmah as the second sefirah; Quran 2:30-33 and the pre-existent 'preserved tablet' (85:22).

**Proverbs 8:32-36, happy who watch at Wisdom's doors** (Prov 8:32-36)
- Compare John 10:9 (I am the door) and Sir 14:23-24 (one who peers through Wisdom's windows and camps by her house).

**Lady Wisdom's house and banquet versus Woman Folly** (Prov 9:1-18)
- Sirach 24:19-21 and John 6:35 (bread of life) echo Wisdom's banquet; rabbinic exegesis read the seven pillars as seven days of creation or seven books of Torah (Lev. Rab. 11).
- Compare Wisdom 'building a house' with the Quranic invitation to the 'abode of peace' (Q 10:25).

**First Solomonic collection begins (antithetic sayings on righteous and wicked)** (Prov 10:1-32)
- 10:12 is quoted in James 5:20 and 1 Peter 4:8 ('love covers a multitude of sins').
- 10:7 'zekher tsaddiq livrakhah' became the standard Jewish formula for the dead (z"l).

**Sayings on honest scales, generosity and the fate of the wicked** (Prov 11:1-31)
- 11:31 is quoted from the LXX in 1 Peter 4:18; 11:24 parallels the Quranic theme that spending in charity multiplies (Q 2:261).
- Egyptian Amenemope ch. 16 and the Babylonian Shamash hymn condemn the false balance.

**Sayings on the capable wife, speech and diligence** (Prov 12:1-28)
- 12:10 is a basis of the rabbinic principle tsa'ar ba'alei hayyim (animal suffering); cf. hadith on the woman punished for a cat.

**Sayings on discipline, hope and companions** (Prov 13:1-25)
- 13:20 parallels the hadith of the perfume-seller and the blacksmith (good and bad companions) and Menander 'bad company corrupts' (1 Cor 15:33).
- 13:24 compare Ahiqar: 'Spare not your son the rod'.

**Sayings on the soft answer, prayer and better-than proverbs** (Prov 15:1-33)
- 15:16-17 better-than sayings parallel Amenemope ch. 6 ('better is bread with a happy heart than riches with sorrow').

**YHWH sayings and royal sayings (man plans, God disposes)** (Prov 16:1-33)
- 16:2 'YHWH weighs the spirits' recalls the Egyptian weighing of the heart before Thoth/Osiris (Book of the Dead 125) and Quran 21:47 (scales of justice).
- 16:9 resembles Amenemope 19 ('the words men say are one thing, what the god does is another') and the proverb homo proponit, Deus disponit.
- 16:32 parallels the hadith 'the strong man is not the wrestler but the one who controls himself in anger' and Pirqe Avot 4:1.

**Sayings on strife, bribes, friends and the silent fool** (Prov 17:1-28)
- 17:28 parallels the Latin 'si tacuisses, philosophus mansisses' and the hadith 'whoever believes in God... let him speak good or keep silent'.
- 17:2 the wise slave inheriting resembles Ahiqar's adopted heir and Gen 15:3 (Eliezer).

**Sayings on the tongue, the strong tower and the lot** (Prov 18:1-24)
- 18:21 is central to Jewish laws of lashon hara and parallels the hadith on the tongue casting people into the Fire; cf. James 3:5-10.

**Sayings on the poor, the king's wrath and the sluggard** (Prov 19:1-29)
- 19:17 'lending to God' parallels Quran 2:245 and 57:11 ('who will lend God a goodly loan?') and Matt 25:40.

**Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH** (Prov 20:1-30)
- 20:27 'the soul of man is the lamp of YHWH' became a key prooftext in Jewish mysticism and the custom of searching for leaven by candlelight (b. Pesah. 7b-8a); cf. the 'light' of Quran 24:35.
- 20:22 compare Rom 12:17-19 and Amenemope ch. 21/22 ('sit in the arms of the god').

**Sayings on the king's heart, justice over sacrifice, and the contentious wife** (Prov 21:1-31)
- 21:1 parallels the Egyptian image of the god guiding the king's heart, and the hadith that hearts are between two fingers of the Merciful, who turns them as he wills.
- 21:3 compare Hos 6:6, 1 Sam 15:22, Quran 22:37 (neither their flesh nor blood reaches God, but piety).

**End of the first Solomonic collection (good name, training a child)** (Prov 22:1-16)
- 22:1 parallels Eccl 7:1 and the Egyptian concern for a lasting name; 22:9 'good eye/evil eye' is the basis of rabbinic 'ayin tovah / 'ayin ra'ah (m. Avot 2:9; 5:19).

**Words of the Wise begin (Amenemope parallel), introduction and first sayings** (Prov 22:17-29)
- Instruction of Amenemope (Egypt, c. 1100 BCE): parallels identified by Erman (1924). 22:21 'to return true words to those who sent you' matches Amenemope's prologue.

**Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel), dining with rulers, winged riches, the orphan's field** (Prov 23:1-14)
- 23:13-14 matches Ahiqar (Aramaic, saying 81-82): 'if I strike you, my son, you will not die'.
- 23:7 'as he reckons in his soul, so is he' is the source of the popular 'as a man thinketh'.

**Father's appeal, the harlot as pit, and the drunkard's woes** (Prov 23:15-35)
- 23:29-35 compare the Egyptian Instruction of Any on beer drinking and Quran 5:90-91 on wine (khamr) as Satan's work sowing enmity.

**End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section)** (Prov 24:1-22)
- 24:17 is recited in the Passover tradition of spilling wine for the drowned Egyptians (cf. b. Meg. 10b) and recalls Pirqe Avot 4:19 (Samuel the Small).
- 24:21 is cited in 1 Peter 2:17 ('fear God, honor the king').

**'These also are of the wise': judgment, retaliation and the sluggard's field** (Prov 24:23-34)
- 24:29 contrasts with the lex talionis and parallels Matt 5:38-39 and the 'golden rule' traditions (Hillel, b. Shabb. 31a).
- 24:30-34 the first-person observed example (exemplum) is like the Egyptian Instruction of Any and Qohelet's 'I saw'.

**Proverbs of Solomon copied by Hezekiah's men (king, speech, enemies)** (Prov 25:1-28)
- 25:6-7 is the basis of Jesus' parable of the wedding seats (Luke 14:8-10); 25:21-22 is quoted in Rom 12:20.
- 'Coals on the head' has been linked to an Egyptian penitential rite of carrying a basin of burning coals on the head (Demotic Tale of Khamuas).

**Sayings on the fool (the 'book of fools')** (Prov 26:1-12)
- 26:4-5 contradiction is discussed in b. Shabb. 30b (one concerns Torah matters, the other worldly matters); 26:11 is quoted in 2 Pet 2:22.

**Sayings on the sluggard, the meddler, the whisperer and the hypocrite** (Prov 26:13-28)
- 26:23 'silver dross on potsherd' is illuminated by Ugaritic spsg ('glaze'): 'like glaze over earthenware'. Compare Matt 23:27 (whitewashed tombs).

**Sayings on tomorrow, friends and the care of flocks** (Prov 27:1-27)
- 27:1 parallels James 4:13-14 and Quran 31:34 / 18:23-24 (say not 'I shall do it tomorrow' without 'if God wills').
- 27:20 compare the hadith 'if the son of Adam had a valley of gold he would want a second; only dust fills his mouth'.

**Sayings on torah, rulers, usury and confession** (Prov 28:1-28)
- 28:13 is a classic prooftext for teshuvah (confession plus abandonment of sin; Maimonides, Hilkhot Teshuvah 2) and parallels 1 John 1:9.
- 28:24 resembles Mark 7:11-12 (corban, depriving parents).

**Last Hezekian sayings (vision, rulers, discipline)** (Prov 29:1-27)
- 29:18 'where there is no vision the people perish' (KJV) is widely quoted; the Hebrew pairs prophetic vision with torah-keeping.

**Words of Agur son of Yakeh, confession of ignorance and prayer** (Prov 30:1-9)
- 30:4 compare John 3:13 ('no one has ascended into heaven except he who descended'), Deut 30:12, and Mesopotamian 'who can go up to heaven?' (Gilgamesh, Ludlul). Christian exegesis read 'his son' christologically.
- 30:8 'lehem huqqi' parallels the Lord's Prayer 'daily bread' (Matt 6:11).

**Agur's numerical sayings (leech, four wonders, four small wise creatures)** (Prov 30:10-33)
- Numerical sayings occur in Ugaritic poetry, Ahiqar ('two things are good, a third pleases Shamash') and Sir 25-26; Amos 1-2 uses the same form.
- 30:25 ants compare Quran 27:18 (the ant of Solomon) and Aesop's Ant and Grasshopper.

**Words of King Lemuel taught by his mother** (Prov 31:1-9)
- Rabbinic tradition identifies Lemuel with Solomon and his mother with Bathsheba (Num. Rab. 10:4). 31:6 is the basis of offering wine to the condemned (b. Sanh. 43a; cf. Mark 15:23).
- Royal instructions from a parent compare the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemhat and Merikare.

**The woman of valor (alphabetic acrostic)** (Prov 31:10-31)
- Sung at the Sabbath table (Eshet Hayil); midrash reads it of Sarah, Torah, the Shekhinah or the soul. Compare the ideal wife in Egyptian and Mesopotamian household texts.

**Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature** (Eccl 1:1-11)
