- Cyclical cosmos compares Heraclitus and Stoic eternal recurrence; 'nothing new' resembles Marcus Aurelius (Meditations 2.14, 7.1). Rabbinic tradition ascribes the book to Solomon in old age (Song Rab. 1:1).
- Hevel ('breath') compare Quran 57:20 (worldly life is play and amusement) and Buddhist anicca.

**Qohelet the king searches out all things by wisdom** (Eccl 1:12-18)
- The legend that Solomon was dethroned by Ashmedai and wandered saying 'I, Qohelet, was king' (b. Git. 68b) builds on 1:12.

**The royal experiment with pleasure, wealth and great works** (Eccl 2:1-11)
- Compare the royal self-presentation in Assyrian building inscriptions and the Egyptian Harper's Songs; the 'paradise' gardens recall Achaemenid royal parks.

**Wise and fool share one fate; hatred of toil; eat and drink** (Eccl 2:12-26)
- 2:24 'eat and drink' closely parallels Siduri's advice to Gilgamesh (OB version, Meissner tablet) and Egyptian Harper's Songs.

**A time for everything; eternity in the heart** (Eccl 3:1-15)
- 3:1-8 compare the Stoic kairos doctrine and Bhagavad Gita on acting according to the occasion; the merism catalogue resembles Egyptian onomastica.

**Injustice, divine judgment, and humans no better than beasts** (Eccl 3:16-22)
- 3:21 parallels Greek debates on the soul's ascent (Pythagorean, Platonic) and contrasts with Quran 17:85 ('the spirit is of my Lord's command').

**Oppression, envy, the lonely miser, and 'two are better than one'** (Eccl 4:1-12)
- 4:2-3 'best never to have been born' is Theognis 425-428 and Sophocles, Oedipus at Colonus 1224-1227 (Silenus' wisdom).
- 4:12 the threefold cord appears in Gilgamesh (Sumerian 'Gilgamesh and Huwawa': 'a triple-ply rope cannot be cut').

**The poor wise youth and the old king; caution at the house of God** (Eccl 4:13-17)
- The prisoner who becomes king recalls Joseph (Gen 41) and the Midrash (Eccl. Rab. 4) reading it of Abraham vs Nimrod or the good and evil inclinations.

**Few words before God and paying vows** (Eccl 5:1-6)
- 5:3-4 closely echoes Deut 23:22-24; compare Quran 2:225 and 5:89 on unintentional oaths and the hadith on fulfilling vows.

**Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes** (Eccl 5:7-19)
- 5:14 compare Job 1:21, 1 Tim 6:7 and the hadith 'the son of Adam says my wealth, my wealth...' (what you ate, wore out or gave in charity).

**Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing)** (Eccl 7:1-14)
- 7:1b 'day of death better than day of birth' compares Herodotus 1.31 (Cleobis and Biton) and 5.4 (Thracians mourning births).

**Do not be overly righteous; the search for the sum of things; the snaring woman** (Eccl 7:15-29)
- 7:16-18 parallels the Greek meden agan and Aristotle's mean; also the hadith 'the best of affairs is the middle course'. 7:20 is cited in Rom 3:10 (with Ps 14).
- 7:26-28 compare misogynist sayings in Ankhsheshonq and Hesiod's Pandora (Works and Days).

**Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution** (Eccl 8:1-17)
- 8:2 'the oath of God' to the king compares loyalty oaths to Persian/Hellenistic kings and Egyptian courtier instructions.

**One fate for all; the living dog; eat your bread with joy** (Eccl 9:1-10)
- 9:7-9 closely parallels Siduri's speech to Gilgamesh (OB Gilgamesh, Meissner fragment iii): eat, make merry, wear clean clothes, wash, let your wife delight in your embrace.
- 9:4 cf. Achilles in Odyssey 11.489-491 (better a living serf than king of the dead).

**Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city** (Eccl 9:11-18)
- The poor wise man has been compared with Archimedes at Syracuse and with the wise woman of Abel-beth-maacah (2 Sam 20).

**Sayings on folly, rulers and hazards (dead flies, slaves on horses)** (Eccl 10:1-20)
- 10:20 'a little bird told me': compare Aristophanes, Birds 601 and the Ahiqar saying 'a word is a bird; once released no one can recapture it'.
- 10:16 was applied to young kings (Ptolemy V?) and recalls Isa 3:4,12.

**Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth** (Eccl 11:1-10)
- 11:1 parallels the Egyptian Instruction of Ankhsheshonq ('do a good deed and throw it in the river; when it dries you will find it') and a similar Arabic proverb; also John 3:8 for 11:5.

**Remember your Creator; the allegory of old age; dust and spirit return** (Eccl 12:1-8)
- The old-age allegory is read anatomically in b. Shabb. 151b-152a; compare the Egyptian Instruction of Ptahhotep's prologue on old age (eyes dim, ears deaf, the heart forgets).
- 12:7 contrasts with 3:21; compare the Zoroastrian and Platonic return of the soul and Quran 2:156 ('to Him we return').

**Epilogue on Qohelet, many books, and the whole duty of man** (Eccl 12:9-14)
- The epilogue's orthodox ending is cited in the rabbinic debate on Qohelet's canonicity (m. Yad. 3:5; b. Shabb. 30b). 12:12 compare Callimachus 'big book, big evil'.

**Title; 'let him kiss me'; black and beautiful; the shepherd** (Song 1:1-8)
- Rabbinic allegory (Targum, Song Rab.) reads the lovers as God and Israel; Origen and Bernard of Clairvaux as Christ and the Church or soul. R. Akiva called it the Holy of Holies (m. Yad. 3:5).
- Egyptian love songs (Papyrus Harris 500, Chester Beatty I) use 'sister/brother' and similar flower and perfume imagery; Sufi poetry (Ibn Arabi, Tarjuman al-Ashwaq) shares the mystical-erotic register.

**Mare among chariots, nard and myrrh, lily of the valleys, lovesick under the apple tree** (Song 1:9-2:7)
- Lovesickness as illness compares Egyptian Chester Beatty love song 37 ('seven days I have not seen my sister, sickness invades me') and the Arabic 'Udhri love tradition (Majnun Layla).

**The lover like a gazelle; spring song 'Arise, come away'; little foxes** (Song 2:8-17)
- The Song is read at Passover because of the spring song 2:10-13; compare the Sumerian Inanna-Dumuzi love songs and the Greek Anacreontic spring lyric.

**Night search through the city and the mother's house** (Song 3:1-5)
- The goddess searching for the lost lover (Inanna/Ishtar for Dumuzi, Isis for Osiris, Anat for Baal) has been compared; also Mary Magdalene seeking Jesus in John 20 (liturgically paired).

**Procession of Solomon's litter on his wedding day** (Song 3:6-11)
- Rabbinic readings take the litter as the Tabernacle or Temple and 'the day of his wedding' as Sinai (m. Ta'an. 4:8). Wedding crowns for grooms were abolished after 70 CE (m. Sotah 9:14).

**Descriptive song of the bride's beauty** (Song 4:1-7)
- The term wasf comes from Syrian Arab wedding songs (Wetzstein 1873). Compare Egyptian love-song descriptions of the beloved's hair, teeth and breasts (Chester Beatty I, first stanza).

**Come from Lebanon; sister-bride; the locked garden and its consummation** (Song 4:8-5:1)
- The 'hortus conclusus' and 'fons signatus' became Marian titles in Latin Christianity; rabbinic readings apply 4:12 to Israel's chastity in Egypt (Song Rab. 4:12).
- 'Sister' for the bride parallels Egyptian snt ('sister') in love songs and Ugaritic usage.

**The knock at night, the vanished lover and the watchmen's blows** (Song 5:2-8)
- The paraklausithyron (lover locked out at the door) is a Greek and Latin love-poetry genre (Theocritus 3, Propertius 1.16); Egyptian love songs also stage the lover at the door. Rev 3:20 echoes the knock.
- Inanna's stripping as she descends to the underworld has been compared with 5:7.

**Descriptive song of the beloved man ('radiant and ruddy')** (Song 5:9-16)
- The man described as a statue of gold, ivory and lapis matches cult-image descriptions of gods (Egyptian gods with gold flesh and lapis hair); the Shi'ur Qomah mystical tradition measures God's body from this wasf.

**Where has your beloved gone; the beloved unique among queens** (Song 6:1-12)
- Rev 12:1 (woman clothed with the sun, moon under her feet); Mariological use of Song 6:10 ('pulchra ut luna, electa ut sol').
- Egyptian love songs (Chester Beatty I) describe the beloved as unique ('the One, the sister without peer') and use body-catalogue.

**The Shulammite's dance and the palm tree** (Song 7:1-14)
- Song 7:11 'his desire is for me' (teshuqato) inverts Gen 3:16; rabbinic and patristic readings of the Shulammite as Israel/Church.

**Seal on the heart; love strong as death; the little sister; Solomon's vineyard** (Song 8:1-14)
- Love vs. Death (Mot) and Sea (many waters) evoke Ugaritic Baal cycle; Resheph is a Canaanite plague/fire god.
- Mishnah Yadayim 3:5 (R. Akiva: Song is holy of holies); Christian bridal mysticism (Bernard of Clairvaux).

**Hear, O heavens; the great indictment, sacrifice rejected, the faithful city** (Isa 1:1-31)
- Isa 1:3 ox and ass underlie the ox and ass at the manger in Christian nativity iconography (Pseudo-Matthew 14).
- Isa 1:18 is a key text on forgiveness in Jewish Yom Kippur liturgy and Christian preaching; cf. Quran on deeds exchanged (25:70).

**The mountain of the Lord's house; the Day of YHWH against all that is proud** (Isa 2:1-22)
- Isa 2:2-4 doublet in Mic 4:1-3; 'swords into plowshares' at the UN; Rev 6:15-16 (kings hide in caves and call on rocks to fall).

**Removal of stay and staff; children rule; the finery of the daughters of Zion; seven women and one man** (Isa 3:1-4:1)
- Crescent ornaments (saharonim) also on Midianite camels (Judg 8:21).

**The branch of YHWH and the canopy over Zion** (Isa 4:2-6)
- Targum renders 'branch of YHWH' as 'the Messiah of YHWH'.

**Song of the vineyard; six woes; the nation from afar** (Isa 5:1-30)
- Mark 12:1-9 / Matt 21:33 parable of the wicked tenants builds on Isa 5:1-2; Sheol's open mouth recalls Ugaritic Mot with one lip to earth, one to heaven.

**The throne vision and the call of Isaiah** (Isa 6:1-13)
- Trisagion: Kedushah in Jewish liturgy, Sanctus in Christian mass; seraph/saraph = fiery serpent (Num 21), winged uraeus serpents in Egyptian iconography.
- Isa 6:9-10 quoted in Matt 13:14-15, John 12:40, Acts 28:26; Quran 2:7 (God sealed their hearts and hearing).
- Mouth-purification of a prophet: Jer 1:9, Ezek 3; Mesopotamian mis pi (mouth-washing) rite; Muhammad's chest-opening (sharh al-sadr).

**Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign** (Isa 7:1-25)
- Matt 1:23 reads LXX parthenos ('virgin'); Justin Martyr's Dialogue with Trypho debates 'almah; Quran 19 (Maryam) virgin birth.
- Isa 7:9 LXX 'if you do not believe you will not understand' -> Augustine's 'crede ut intelligas'.

**Maher-shalal-hash-baz; waters of Shiloah; the stone of stumbling; ghosts that chirp** (Isa 8:1-23)
- Isa 8:14 with 28:16 in Rom 9:33 and 1 Pet 2:8; Isa 8:17-18 in Heb 2:13; Isa 8:23-9:1 in Matt 4:15-16. Chirping shades: Homer Od. 24.5 (ghosts squeak like bats).

**Great light; a child is born to us; the outstretched hand against Ephraim** (Isa 9:1-20, Isa 10:1-4)
- Egyptian coronation throne-names (fivefold titulary) for the five-part name in Isa 9:5; Handel's Messiah; rabbinic tradition (Sanhedrin 94a) on the closed mem and Hezekiah as nearly messiah.

**Woe to Assyria, rod of my anger; a remnant will return; the invader's march on Jerusalem** (Isa 10:5-34)
- God using a pagan empire as unwitting instrument: Quran 17:4-7 (servants of great might sent against Israel twice); Rom 9:27-28 quotes Isa 10:22-23.

**Shoot from the stump of Jesse; the peaceable kingdom; second exodus** (Isa 11:1-16)
- Seven gifts of the Holy Spirit (Vulgate); netser and Nazarene (Matt 2:23); 2 Thess 2:8 (lawless one slain by breath of his mouth); Virgil Eclogue 4 and Iranian Frashokereti golden-age animal peace; Hindu Satya Yuga.

**Song of thanksgiving 'on that day'** (Isa 12:1-6)
- Isa 12:3 sung at Havdalah and associated with the Simhat Beit ha-Sho'evah water-drawing at Sukkot (m. Sukkah 5); John 7:37-38.

**Oracle against Babylon; the Day of YHWH darkens the heavens** (Isa 13:1-22)
- Mark 13:24-25 / Matt 24:29 and Rev 6:12-13 reuse Isa 13:10; satyrs (se'irim) as goat-demons in Lev 17:7; Greek satyrs.

**Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn)** (Isa 14:1-23)
- Helel ben Shahar -> Vulgate 'Lucifer'; Christian fall of Satan (Luke 10:18, Rev 12); Quran 7:12-13 and 2:34 (Iblis's pride and fall); 2 Enoch 29 (Satanail wants his throne above the clouds).
- Ugaritic: Shahar (Dawn) and Shalim; Athtar who tries Baal's throne on Zaphon but is too small; Greek Phaethon; Ezek 28 (king of Tyre in Eden).
- Underworld welcome of a new arrival: Gilgamesh/Enkidu's dream of the house of dust; Odyssey 11.

**God's oath against Assyria; oracle against Philistia in the year Ahaz died** (Isa 14:24-32)
- Flying serpents of Arabia in Herodotus 2.75 and 3.107; winged uraei on Judean seals.

**Oracle concerning Moab; lament, plea for refuge, the vine of Sibmah** (Isa 15:1-16:14)
- Jer 48 reuses much of Isa 15-16; Mesha Stele toponyms (Dibon, Nebo, Medeba, Jahaz, Kir-hareseth).

**Oracle on Damascus and Ephraim; gardens of the pleasant one; the roaring of the nations** (Isa 17:1-14)
- Na'aman as epithet of Adonis/Tammuz; Greek 'gardens of Adonis' (Plato Phaedrus 276b) quickly sprouting and withering.

**Oracle to the land of whirring wings beyond the rivers of Cush** (Isa 18:1-7)
- Herodotus 3.20 on the Ethiopians as tallest and most beautiful of men; Kushite 25th dynasty diplomacy.

**Oracle on Egypt; the drying Nile; an altar to YHWH in Egypt; 'Blessed be Egypt my people'** (Isa 19:1-25)
- Onias IV's temple at Leontopolis justified from Isa 19:19 (Josephus Ant. 13.62-68); Egyptian 'Admonitions of Ipuwer' and 'Prophecy of Neferti' on the Nile drying and social chaos.

**Isaiah walks naked and barefoot as a sign against Egypt and Cush** (Isa 20:1-6)
- Diogenes the Cynic and Indian naked ascetics (gymnosophists, Digambara Jains) as other naked holy men; Sargon II's annals record the Ashdod campaign of 711 BCE.

**Wilderness of the sea; the watchman; Dumah; Arabia** (Isa 21:1-17)
- Rev 14:8 and 18:2 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great'; the riders on donkey and camel were read in medieval Jewish and Muslim polemic as Jesus and Muhammad (e.g. Saadia, Ibn Qayyim).

**Valley of vision; let us eat and drink; Shebna deposed, Eliakim given the key of David** (Isa 22:1-25)
- Rev 3:7 (the one who has the key of David); Matt 16:19 keys of the kingdom given to Peter; 1 Cor 15:32 'let us eat and drink'; Siloam tomb inscription of '...yahu who is over the house'.

**Oracle on Tyre; seventy years forgotten; the harlot's song** (Isa 23:1-18)
- Ezek 26-28 and Rev 18 (merchants and ships lament the great city); seventy years as in Jer 25:11 and Esarhaddon's Babylon inscription (70 years decreed, reversed to 11).

**The earth laid waste; the host of heaven imprisoned; YHWH reigns on Zion** (Isa 24:1-23)
- Imprisoned host: 1 Enoch 10 and 18-21 (Watchers bound in a pit until judgment), 2 Pet 2:4, Jude 6, Rev 20:1-3; Rabbinic 'razi li' read as mystical secret (b. Sanhedrin 94a).

**Thanksgiving; the feast on the mountain; death swallowed forever** (Isa 25:1-12)
- 1 Cor 15:54 'Death is swallowed up in victory'; Rev 7:17 and 21:4 (God wipes away every tear); messianic banquet with Leviathan's flesh (2 Bar 29, b. Bava Batra 75a); Ugaritic Mot's devouring jaws.

**Song of the strong city; your dead shall live** (Isa 26:1-21)
- Dew of resurrection in rabbinic lore (b. Shabbat 88b, y. Berakhot 5:2; the 'tal' prayer); Dan 12:2; Zoroastrian resurrection (Bundahishn 34); Isa 26:20 echoes Passover night (Exod 12:22-23).

**Leviathan slain; the vineyard of delight; the great shofar** (Isa 27:1-13)
- Ugaritic KTU 1.5 I 1-3: Baal smote 'Lotan the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent, the mighty one with seven heads' - nearly verbatim; Rev 12:9 and 20:2; Zoroastrian Azhi Dahaka; Vritra slain by Indra; Typhon.
- The great shofar of Isa 27:13 enters the Amidah's tenth blessing (teqa be-shofar gadol) and 1 Thess 4:16 / Matt 24:31 (last trumpet).

**Ephraim's drunkards; tsav la-tsav; covenant with death; the cornerstone; the farmer's wisdom** (Isa 28:1-29)
- 1 Cor 14:21 quotes Isa 28:11 on tongues; Isa 28:16 in Rom 9:33, 1 Pet 2:6, Eph 2:20; Qumran (1QS 8:7) calls the community the tested wall and precious cornerstone; covenant with Mot evokes Canaanite death-god.

**Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay** (Isa 29:1-24)
- Mark 7:6-7 / Matt 15:8-9 quote Isa 29:13; 1 Cor 1:19 quotes 29:14; Rom 9:20 (potter); Mesha Stele 'r'l (altar-hearth); midrash of Abraham saved from Nimrod's furnace read from 29:22 (Gen Rabbah 38); Quran 21:68-69.
- Sealed book given to one who 'cannot read' is invoked in Muslim polemic for the unlettered prophet (Quran 96:1, 'Read!').

**Woe to the rebellious children going down to Egypt; returning and rest; the Teacher; Topheth prepared** (Isa 30:1-33)
- Sevenfold light of the sun in the world to come: b. Pesahim 68a, b. Sanhedrin 91b; Topheth -> Gehenna (Valley of Hinnom) and the lake of fire and brimstone in Rev 19:20; 'Teacher of Righteousness' at Qumran (moreh).

**Woe to those who go down to Egypt; YHWH like a lion and hovering birds over Zion** (Isa 31:1-9)
- Passover verb pasah used for God's protection of the city (Isa 31:5; cf. Exod 12:13); Matt 23:37 (hen gathering chicks).

**A king will reign in righteousness; complacent women; the spirit poured from on high** (Isa 32:1-20)
- Spirit poured out: Joel 3:1-2, Acts 2:17; Isa 32:17 is a common inscription text.

**Woe to the destroyer; who can dwell with devouring fire; the king in his beauty; Zion's broad rivers** (Isa 33:1-24)
- Ps 15 and 24 (entrance liturgies); b. Makkot 24a counts six principles in Isa 33:15; er'elam as weeping angels at the binding of Isaac (Gen Rabbah 56).

**Judgment on the nations and Edom; heavens rolled up like a scroll; Lilith in the ruins** (Isa 34:1-17)
- Lilith: Mesopotamian lilitu wind-demons; Talmud (b. Shabbat 151b), Alphabet of Ben Sira (Adam's first wife), Aramaic incantation bowls; Rev 6:13-14 (sky rolled up like a scroll); Rev 14:11 (smoke goes up forever).

**The desert blossoms; the blind see and the lame leap; the Way of Holiness** (Isa 35:1-10)
- Matt 11:5 / Luke 7:22 (Jesus' answer to John: the blind see, the lame walk); 4Q521 messianic apocalypse; Heb 12:12.

**Sennacherib's invasion; the Rabshakeh's speech at the conduit** (Isa 36:1-22)
- Parallel 2 Kgs 18:13-37 (omits Hezekiah's tribute); Sennacherib's annals (Taylor Prism): Hezekiah shut up 'like a bird in a cage'.

**Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter** (Isa 37:1-38)
- Herodotus 2.141: mice gnaw Sennacherib's bowstrings at Pelusium; Byron's 'Destruction of Sennacherib'; Babylonian Chronicle on Sennacherib's murder by his son.

**Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm** (Isa 38:1-22)
- Thread of life cut from the loom: Greek Moirai (Atropos), Norse Norns; Quran 2:259 and 13:39 on extended terms; b. Berakhot 10a (Hezekiah turned to the wall).

**Merodach-baladan's envoys and the prophecy of the Babylonian exile** (Isa 39:1-8)
- Dan 1:3 (royal youths in Babylon's palace) read as fulfilment; b. Sanhedrin 93b identifies Daniel and companions as these eunuchs.

**Comfort my people; a voice in the wilderness; to whom will you liken God** (Isa 40:1-31)
- Mark 1:3 and John 1:23 (John the Baptist); 1QS 8:13-14 (Qumran withdraws to the desert to prepare the way); 1 Pet 1:24-25; Ps 147:4 (God counts stars); Quran 2:255 (neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes him).
- Isa 40:12-14 (God without counselor) answers Babylonian Enuma Elish where Ea advises Marduk; Haftarah of consolation (Nahamu) after Tisha b'Av.

**Trial of the nations; the one from the east; Israel my servant, fear not; gods challenged to foretell** (Isa 41:1-29)
- Abraham khalil Allah (Quran 4:125); James 2:23; Rev 1:8 and 22:13 (Alpha and Omega); Quran 57:3 (the First and the Last).

**First servant song; light to the nations; a new song; God as warrior and as woman in labor; the blind servant** (Isa 42:1-25)
- Matt 12:18-21 applies Isa 42:1-4 to Jesus; Luke 2:32 (light to the nations); Muslim polemic reads 42:11 (Kedar, Sela) as foretelling Muhammad and Medina (Ibn Rabban, Ibn Qutayba).

**I have called you by name; you are my witnesses; behold I do a new thing** (Isa 43:1-28)
- Isa 43:10 'you are my witnesses' read in Sifre Deut 346 ('if you are my witnesses I am God'); Dan 3 (three youths unburned in the furnace) and Quran 21:69 (fire cool for Abraham); Rom 5:12 and the 'first father' (Adam or Jacob).

**Spirit on your offspring; the idol made from half a log; Cyrus my shepherd** (Isa 44:1-28)
- Wisdom of Solomon 13:11-19 and Epistle of Jeremiah expand the half-log satire; Horace Satires 1.8 (fig-wood Priapus: 'the carpenter wondered whether to make a bench or a god'); Abraham smashing idols (Gen Rabbah 38, Quran 21:57-67).

**Cyrus the anointed; I form light and create darkness; the potter; every knee shall bow** (Isa 45:1-25)
- Cyrus Cylinder: Marduk 'pronounced his name', took his hand and made him go to Babylon; Josephus Ant. 11.5-6 says Cyrus read Isaiah's prophecy; Ezra 1:1-4.
- Isa 45:7 against Zoroastrian dualism of Ahura Mazda and Angra Mainyu; liturgy changes 'creates evil' to 'creates all' (Yotser prayer, b. Berakhot 11b); Phil 2:10-11 and Rom 14:11 (every knee); Pascal's Deus absconditus (45:15).

**Bel and Nebo carried off; God who carries Israel** (Isa 46:1-13)
- Bel = Marduk, Nebo = Nabu, whose statues were carried in the Babylonian Akitu procession; compare the Cyrus Cylinder on returning gods to their shrines.

**Taunt over the virgin daughter Babylon** (Isa 47:1-15)
- Revelation 18:7-8 reuses 'I sit as a queen, I am no widow' and 'in one day' for Babylon/Rome; Zeph 2:15 has the same boast of Nineveh.

**Obstinate Israel, former and new things, flee from Babylon** (Isa 48:1-22)
- Isa 48:16 was read by early Christian writers (e.g. Origen) as a triadic text: Lord God, his Spirit, and the one sent.

**Second servant song - called from the womb, a light to the nations** (Isa 49:1-13)
- Luke 2:32 and Acts 13:47 cite 'light to the nations'; Rev 1:16 the sharp sword from the mouth; Gal 1:15 Paul's call 'from my mother's womb'.
- Sinim was long read as China (Sinae); modern scholars favor Syene (Aswan), cf. 1QIsaa swnyym.

**Zion not forgotten; her children return** (Isa 49:14-26)
- Mark 3:27 / Matt 12:29 (binding the strong man) echoes 49:24-25. The divine mother image compares with rabbinic and Sufi images of divine rahma (womb-mercy).

**No bill of divorce; third servant song** (Isa 50:1-11)
- Gospel passion narratives (Mark 14:65; 15:19; Luke 9:51 'set his face') echo 50:6-7; Rom 8:33-34 echoes 50:8-9.

**Look to the rock you were hewn from** (Isa 51:1-8)
- Matt 3:9 'God can raise children for Abraham from these stones' plays on the quarry image; Mark 13:31 / Ps 102:26-27 on heaven passing away.

**Awake, arm of YHWH - Rahab and the dragon** (Isa 51:9-11)
- Ugaritic Baal cycle (KTU 1.3 III 38-42): Anat smites Yam, the tunnanu, the twisting serpent; Enuma Elish: Marduk splits Tiamat. Ps 74:13-14 and 89:11 also fuse Rahab with the exodus.

**I am your comforter; the cup of staggering** (Isa 51:12-23)
- Cup of wrath recurs in Jer 25, Rev 14:10 and 16:19; compare Gethsemane 'let this cup pass' (Mark 14:36).

**Awake, Zion; the feet of the herald** (Isa 52:1-12)
- Rom 10:15 cites 52:7 for apostolic preaching; 2 Cor 6:17 cites 52:11; 'mevasser' underlies the Greek euangelion. Rom 2:24 cites 52:5.

**Fourth servant song - the suffering servant** (Isa 52:13-53:12)
- Acts 8:32-35 (Ethiopian eunuch), Mark 15:28, Luke 22:37, 1 Pet 2:22-25, Matt 8:17 apply the song to Jesus; Jewish interpretation (Rashi, Ibn Ezra) reads the servant as Israel; Targum Jonathan applies it to the Messiah but transfers the suffering.
- Compare the Babylonian substitute-king ritual (sar puhi) and the Mesopotamian 'Ludlul bel nemeqi'; also 4 Macc 6:28-29 and 17:22 on martyrs' blood as ransom.

**Sing, barren one; covenant of peace; city of jewels** (Isa 54:1-17)
- Gal 4:27 cites 54:1 for the Jerusalem above; Rev 21:18-21 and Tobit 13:16-17 expand the jeweled city; John 6:45 cites 54:13. Berakhot 64a puns banayikh 'your children' / bonayikh 'your builders'.

**Ho, everyone who thirsts; the word that does not return empty** (Isa 55:1-13)
- Wisdom's banquet (Prov 9:5), Sirach 24:19-21 and 51:23-25, and John 7:37 echo 55:1; Acts 13:34 cites 55:3. Compare Quran 2:186 'I am near'.

**Eunuchs and foreigners in God's house of prayer** (Isa 56:1-8)
- Mark 11:17 cites 56:7 at the temple cleansing; Acts 8:27-39 the Ethiopian eunuch; Yad Vashem takes its name from 56:5; Matt 19:12 on eunuchs for the kingdom.

**Blind watchmen, mute dogs; the righteous taken away** (Isa 56:9-57:2)
- Rabbinic tradition (b. Bava Qamma 60a; Sanhedrin 113b) cites 57:1: the righteous are taken away before calamity; compare the death of Josiah and Wis 4:7-14.

**Sons of the sorceress - cult under every green tree** (Isa 57:3-13)
- Cultic necromancy and Molech worship; compare Ugaritic rpum/Malik cult of the dead kings and the stone-cults (betyls) of Arabia, cf. ansab in Quran 5:90.

**The high and lofty One dwells with the contrite** (Isa 57:14-21)
- Eph 2:13-17 applies 'peace to far and near' to Jews and gentiles; Jude 13 'wild waves casting up their shame'; 57:15 a favorite of Jewish and Christian mysticism on divine immanence.

**The fast that God chooses; the Sabbath a delight** (Isa 58:1-14)
- Read as the haftarah of Yom Kippur morning. Compare Zech 7:5-10, Matt 6:16-18, Quran 2:177 and 90:11-16 (freeing a neck, feeding on a day of hunger).

**Your sins have separated you; God arms himself** (Isa 59:1-21)
- Eph 6:14-17 and 1 Thess 5:8 (armor of God), Wis 5:17-20; Rom 3:15-17 quotes 59:7-8; Rom 11:26-27 quotes 59:20-21. 59:20-21 begins the Jewish 'Uva le-Tsiyon' prayer.

**Arise, shine - the nations come to Zion's light** (Isa 60:1-22)
- Matt 2:11 (magi's gold and frankincense) and Rev 21:23-26 (no sun, open gates, glory of nations); b. Sanhedrin 98a harmonizes 'in its time' and 'I will hasten it'.

**The spirit of the Lord is upon me** (Isa 61:1-11)
- Luke 4:16-21: Jesus reads 61:1-2 in the Nazareth synagogue, stopping before 'day of vengeance'; 11QMelchizedek applies it to a heavenly Melchizedek; 4Q521 links it to raising the dead.

**Hephzibah and Beulah - Zion's new name** (Isa 62:1-12)
- Rev 2:17 and 3:12 (a new name), Rev 22:12 ('my reward is with me'); Hephzibah is also the name of Hezekiah's wife (2 Kgs 21:1).

**Who is this coming from Edom? The winepress of wrath** (Isa 63:1-6)
- Rev 14:19-20 and 19:13-15 (robe dipped in blood, treading the winepress); compare Anat wading in the blood of warriors (KTU 1.3 II).

**Remembering the days of Moses - O that you would rend the heavens** (Isa 63:7-64:11)
- 1 Cor 2:9 'what no eye has seen' adapts 64:3; Eph 4:30 'do not grieve the holy spirit' echoes 63:10; Mark 1:10 (heavens torn, schizomenous) echoes 63:19; Quran 15:26 on humans from clay.

**Found by those who did not seek; rebels and servants** (Isa 65:1-16)
- Rom 10:20-21 quotes 65:1-2; Rev 3:14 'the Amen'. Gad = Tyche/Fortuna (cf. Gen 30:11, Baal-gad); Meni a fate deity, compare Arabian Manat (Quran 53:20). Mark 5:2-5 demoniac dwelling among tombs.

**New heavens and a new earth** (Isa 65:17-25)
- Rev 21:1-4; 2 Pet 3:13; 1 Enoch 10:17-19 (long life); Zoroastrian frashokereti (renovation of the world); Virgil Eclogue 4 peaceful animals; Quran 6:165 vs. hadith on paradise.

**Heaven is my throne; sacrifice as abomination** (Isa 66:1-6)
- Acts 7:49-50 (Stephen) quotes 66:1-2; Matt 5:34-35; 1 Kgs 8:27. 'Haredim' is the source of the modern name for ultra-Orthodox Jews.

**Zion gives birth in a day; comforted like a child by its mother** (Isa 66:7-14)
- Rev 12:1-5 (woman gives birth to a male child); John 16:21; rabbinic 'birth pangs of the Messiah' (hevlei mashiah).

**Judgment by fire, ingathering of nations, the undying worm** (Isa 66:15-24)
- Mark 9:48 Gehenna 'where their worm does not die'; Judith 16:17; Paul's mission to Spain (Tarshish?) in Rom 15 has been read against 66:19.

**Jeremiah's call - known before the womb, words in his mouth** (Jer 1:1-10)
- Compare Isa 6:6-7 (coal on lips), Ezek 2:8-3:3 (scroll eaten), Muhammad's first revelation (Quran 96:1-5; Bukhari's iqra' narrative with the squeezing angel), Gal 1:15.

**Visions of the almond branch and the boiling pot** (Jer 1:11-19)
- Amos 7:8 and 8:1-2 (plumb line, summer fruit pun); the Scythian hypothesis for the northern foe (Herodotus 1.103-106).

**The bride of the wilderness; broken cisterns** (Jer 2:1-13)
- Hosea 2:16-17 (wilderness honeymoon); Song 8:5; John 4:10-14 and 7:38 (living water); Quran 67:30.

**Degenerate vine, she-camel in heat, gods of wood and stone** (Jer 2:14-37)
- Isa 5:1-7 vineyard song; John 15 true vine. Matt 23:37 / Luke 13:34 and Quran 2:61, 3:112 on killing prophets.

**Can a divorced wife return? Faithless Israel, treacherous Judah** (Jer 3:1-25)
- Ezek 23 (Oholah and Oholibah); 2 Macc 2:4-8 says Jeremiah hid the ark on Mount Nebo, cf. 3:16. Teshuvah theology (b. Yoma 86a cites 3:22).

**If you return - circumcise your hearts** (Jer 4:1-4)
- Rom 2:29; Deut 10:16; Hos 10:12; Jubilees 1:23.

**Alarm - disaster from the north** (Jer 4:5-18)
- Compare 1 Kgs 22:20-23 (God's lying spirit) and Ezek 14:9 on God deceiving prophets.

**My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation** (Jer 4:19-31)
- A reversal of Gen 1 creation order (earth, light, mountains, humans, birds). Compare Babylonian flood imagery in Atrahasis and Zoroastrian end-of-world catastrophes; Joel 2:10.

**Search Jerusalem for one just man** (Jer 5:1-9)
- Gen 18:23-32 (Abraham's bargaining for Sodom); Diogenes searching with a lamp for an honest man; Hos 13:7-8 and Dan 7 (beasts).

**Strip her vines - a nation whose tongue you do not know** (Jer 5:10-19)
- Measure-for-measure punishment pattern; compare Deut 28:49-51.

**The sea's sand boundary; houses full of deceit** (Jer 5:20-31)
- Job 38:8-11, Ps 104:9, Prov 8:29 on the sea's bound; Mark 8:18 'having eyes do you not see'; Quran 7:179.

**Sanctify war against her - the siege** (Jer 6:1-8)
- Holy war ideology (cf. Joel 4:9 'sanctify war'); Deut 20:19-20 on cutting trees in siege.

**Glean the remnant; peace, peace, when there is no peace** (Jer 6:9-15)
- 1 Thess 5:3 'when they say peace and security'; Ezek 13:10 whitewash.

**Ask for the ancient paths; incense from Sheba rejected** (Jer 6:16-21)
- Matt 11:29 'you will find rest for your souls' quotes 6:16.

**A cruel people from the north; the prophet as assayer** (Jer 6:22-30)
- Ezek 22:18-22 dross; Mal 3:2-3 refiner's fire; Zech 12:10 mourning for an only son.

**The temple sermon - a den of robbers; remember Shiloh** (Jer 7:1-15)
- Mark 11:17 / Matt 21:13 combine Isa 56:7 and Jer 7:11 at the temple cleansing; Jer 26 narrates the same sermon and the trial.

**Do not pray for this people; cakes for the Queen of Heaven** (Jer 7:16-20)
- Queen of Heaven = Ishtar/Astarte (cf. Jer 44:15-19; Ishtar's kamanu-cakes); Epiphanius on the Collyridians offering cakes to Mary.

**Obedience not sacrifice; the Topheth becomes the Valley of Slaughter** (Jer 7:21-8:3)
- Amos 5:25 makes a similar claim about no sacrifice in the wilderness; Maimonides (Guide 3.32) and the Epistle of Barnabas 2 use Jer 7:22. 'Gehenna' as hell derives from Ben-hinnom; the 'voice of bride and groom' is sung in the Jewish wedding blessings (Jer 33:11).

**The stork knows its seasons; the lying pen of the scribes** (Jer 8:4-13)
- The 'lying pen of the scribes' is cited in Muslim polemic for tahrif (alteration of scripture), cf. Quran 2:79 'woe to those who write the book with their hands'. Isa 1:3 ox knows its owner; Mark 11:13 fig tree without fruit.

**Is there no balm in Gilead? The prophet's tears** (Jer 8:14-23)
- Jeremiah as 'the weeping prophet' (also tradition of authorship of Lamentations); 'There is a Balm in Gilead' African-American spiritual; Num 21:6 fiery serpents.

**Every brother a Jacob - tongues like bows** (Jer 9:1-8)
- Mic 7:5-6 (trust no friend); Gen 27:36 Esau's pun on Jacob 'aqav.

**Summon the keening women - death has climbed in at our windows** (Jer 9:9-21)
- In the Ugaritic Baal cycle (KTU 1.4 V-VII) Baal at first refuses a window in his palace, apparently for fear of Mot (Death); compare Lamashtu entering through windows. Professional mourners: Egyptian and Greek threnody, Arab nadiba.

**Let not the wise boast; circumcised yet uncircumcised** (Jer 9:22-25)
- 1 Cor 1:31 and 2 Cor 10:17 cite 9:23; Herodotus 3.8 says Arabs shave their temples in a ring; Herodotus 2.104 on circumcising peoples (Egyptians, Colchians, Phoenicians).

**Idols like scarecrows in a cucumber field** (Jer 10:1-10)
- The Letter of Jeremiah (Baruch 6), esp. v. 70 'like a scarecrow in a cucumber bed', expands this chapter; compare Isa 44:9-20, Ps 115:4-8, Abraham's idol-smashing (Quran 21:51-67; Genesis Rabbah 38:13) and Wis 13-15.

**The Aramaic verse - gods who did not make heaven and earth** (Jer 10:11)
- The only Aramaic verse in Jeremiah, apparently a ready-made formula for exiles to say to Aramaic-speaking neighbors; compare Abraham's argument from creation in Quran 6:74-79 and 21:56, and Apocalypse of Abraham 1-8.

**He made the earth by his power - the Portion of Jacob** (Jer 10:12-16)
- Prov 3:19-20 and 8:22-31 (wisdom at creation); Ps 135:7; Quran 2:164.

**Pack your bundle; my tent is destroyed; a man cannot direct his steps** (Jer 10:17-25)
- Prov 16:9 and 20:24 on man's steps; Ps 79:6-7 is recited at the Passover seder ('Shefokh hamatkha').

**Cursed is the man who does not hear this covenant** (Jer 11:1-17)
- Often linked to Josiah's covenant (2 Kgs 23:1-3); Rom 11:17-24 (olive tree whose branches are broken off).

**First confession - a gentle lamb led to slaughter; the men of Anathoth** (Jer 11:18-23)
- Compare Isa 53:7-8 (lamb to slaughter, cut off from land of the living); Luke 4:24-29 (no prophet accepted in his hometown; Nazarenes try to kill Jesus).

**Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Running with horses** (Jer 12:1-6)
- Theodicy question also in Job 21:7, Hab 1:13, Ps 73, Mal 3:15; Mark 3:21 and Mic 7:6 on family hostility.

**I have forsaken my house; the speckled bird of prey** (Jer 12:7-17)
- Futility curse as in Deut 28:38 and Hag 1:6; the nations' conversion parallels Zech 8:20-23.

**Symbolic act - the ruined linen loincloth** (Jer 13:1-11)
- Compare Isaiah walking naked (Isa 20), Ezekiel's brick and lying on his side (Ezek 4), Agabus binding himself with Paul's belt (Acts 21:11).

**Every jar shall be filled with wine** (Jer 13:12-14)
- Prelude to the cup of wrath of Jer 25:15-29.

**Before darkness comes; can the Cushite change his skin?** (Jer 13:15-27)
- 13:23 became a proverb ('a leopard cannot change its spots'); compare Aesop's 'Washing the Ethiopian white' and Lucian, Adversus Indoctum 28.

**The drought - the doe forsakes her fawn; lying prophets** (Jer 14:1-16)
- Jewish fast-day liturgy draws on Jer 14 (Mishnah Ta'anit). 'Mikveh Israel' (14:8) is punned in m. Yoma 8:9 by Rabbi Akiva as the ritual bath.

**Let my eyes run with tears; do not spurn us** (Jer 14:17-22)
- Compare 1 Kgs 18 (Baal and rain) and the Ugaritic Baal as rain-giver.

**Though Moses and Samuel stood before me** (Jer 15:1-9)
- Ezek 14:14 (Noah, Daniel, Job); 2 Macc 7 mother of seven martyred sons; Ps 99:6 Moses and Samuel; Amos 8:9 sunset at noon.

**Second confession - woe that my mother bore me; your words I ate** (Jer 15:10-21)
- Ezek 2:8-3:3 and Rev 10:9-10 (eating the scroll); Ps 1:1 (not sitting with scoffers); Job 6:15 friends as a deceitful wadi; Job 3.

**Symbolic acts - no wife, no mourning, no feasting** (Jer 16:1-13)
- The marzeah is attested at Ugarit (mrzh, KTU 1.114 El's drunken feast), in Phoenician and Nabataean texts, and in Amos 6:7. Jewish mourning meal (se'udat havra'ah) and the cup of consolation (b. Ketubot 8b); Paul on celibacy in view of crisis (1 Cor 7:26).

**A new exodus from the north; fishers and hunters** (Jer 16:14-21)
- Mark 1:17 'fishers of men'; Amos 4:2 hooks; Quran 2:170 and 43:22 (we follow what we found our fathers doing).

**Sin engraved with an iron pen** (Jer 17:1-4)
- Contrast Jer 31:33 (law written on the heart). The shamir becomes in rabbinic legend the stone-cutting worm used for the temple (m. Avot 5:6; b. Gittin 68a).

**Cursed who trusts in man, blessed who trusts in YHWH; the deceitful heart** (Jer 17:5-13)
- Ps 1 (two ways, the tree); b. Pesahim 54a lists the Throne of Glory among things created before the world, citing 17:12; John 8:6-8 Jesus writes in the ground; Amenemope 4 (the hot man vs the silent man like a tree).

**Third confession - heal me and I shall be healed** (Jer 17:14-18)
- 17:14 is the basis of the eighth blessing of the Amidah (Refa'enu); 2 Pet 3:4 'where is the promise of his coming?'

**Carry no burden on the Sabbath day** (Jer 17:19-27)
- Basis of the rabbinic category of carrying (hotsa'ah) between domains, m. Shabbat 1:1; compare Neh 13:15-22.

**At the potter's house - conditional prophecy** (Jer 18:1-12)
- Rom 9:20-21 (potter's right over the clay); Jonah 3:10 (Nineveh repents, God relents); Egyptian Khnum shaping humans on the potter's wheel; Quran 55:14.

**Does the snow leave Lebanon? A land for hissing** (Jer 18:13-17)
- Compare Jer 2:27 where the people show God their back not face (measure for measure).

**Fourth confession - let us smite him with the tongue** (Jer 18:18-23)
- The three-fold division of religious authority (priest, sage, prophet) parallels Ezek 7:26; compare imprecatory psalms 35 and 109, and Muhammad's qunut against Ri'l and Dhakwan.

**Symbolic act - the shattered flask at the Topheth** (Jer 19:1-15)
- Egyptian execration texts: names of enemies written on pots that are smashed; Matt 27:7-10 (potter's field, attributed to Jeremiah).

**Pashhur puts Jeremiah in the stocks - Terror on Every Side** (Jer 20:1-6)
- Acts 16:24 (feet in the stocks); 2 Chr 16:10 (Hanani in the stocks).

**Fifth confession - you enticed me; fire shut up in my bones** (Jer 20:7-13)
- Amos 3:8 'the lord has spoken, who can but prophesy?'; Muhammad's distress at the start of revelation; Ps 31:14 'terror on every side' (also 1QH).

**Cursed be the day I was born** (Jer 20:14-18)
- Job 3 develops the same curse; Sophocles, Oedipus at Colonus 1224 ('not to be born is best'); Theognis 425-428.

**Zedekiah's inquiry - the way of life and the way of death** (Jer 21:1-10)
- Didache 1:1 and Barnabas 18 'two ways'; Josephus (War 5.391-393) uses Jeremiah to urge Jerusalem's surrender to Rome.

**To the house of David - judge in the morning** (Jer 21:11-14)
- Ps 101:8 (morning judgment); the king as judge at dawn in Egyptian and Mesopotamian royal ideology (Shamash).

**Go down to the king's house - justice or ruin** (Jer 22:1-9)
- Deut 29:23-25 and 1 Kgs 9:8-9 have the same question-and-answer schema, also attested in Assyrian annals (Ashurbanipal on Arabia).

**Weep for the one who goes away - Shallum** (Jer 22:10-12)
- Do not weep for the dead (Josiah) but for the exile; compare Ovid's Tristia on exile as a living death.

**Woe to him who builds his house by injustice - Jehoiakim** (Jer 22:13-19)
- Mishnah-era 'hoy' lament formulas; compare 1 Kgs 13:30 'alas my brother'; Jesus on the worker's wage (Luke 10:7); the palace at Ramat Rahel with window balustrades.

**Cry from Lebanon; Coniah the signet ring torn off** (Jer 22:20-30)
- Hag 2:23 reverses the curse for Zerubbabel ('I will make you like a signet ring'); Matt 1:11-12 includes Jechoniah in Jesus' line, which Christian apologists connect to the virgin birth; rabbis (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 24) say his repentance annulled the decree.

**Woe to the shepherds; the righteous Branch** (Jer 23:1-8)
- Ezek 34; John 10 (good shepherd); Zech 3:8 and 6:12 'Branch' (Tsemah) as messianic title; Targum renders 'messiah'; 4QFlorilegium 'Branch of David'; Lam. Rabbah 1:51 lists 'YHWH our righteousness' as a name of the Messiah.

**Concerning the prophets - who has stood in the council of YHWH?** (Jer 23:9-22)
- 1 Kgs 22:19-23 (Micaiah in the council), Amos 3:7; Deut 18:20-22 tests for false prophets; Quran 69:44-47 on one who fabricates revelation.

**A God near and far; dreams versus the word like a hammer** (Jer 23:23-32)
- b. Sanhedrin 34a: 'as a hammer splits rock into many fragments, so one verse yields many meanings'; Ps 139:7-12 and Quran 50:16 ('closer than the jugular vein'), 57:4.

**What is the burden of YHWH?** (Jer 23:33-40)
- A rare biblical ban on a religious formula; compare Zech 13:2-6 on the end of prophecy and Quran 2:104 (forbidding the word ra'ina).

**Vision of the two baskets of figs** (Jer 24:1-10)
- Amos 8:1-2 (basket of summer fruit); compare Matt 7:16-20 good and bad fruit and the barren fig tree (Mark 11:13; Luke 13:6-9).

**Twenty-three years of warning; seventy years of servitude** (Jer 25:1-14)
- Dan 9:2 reinterprets the seventy years as seventy weeks of years; 2 Chr 36:21 links them to sabbatical years; Esarhaddon's Babylon inscription: Marduk decrees 70 years of desolation, reversed to 11. Rev 18:22-23 (millstone, lamp, bride and groom).

**The cup of the wine of wrath for all nations; Sheshach** (Jer 25:15-29)
- Rev 14:10 and 16:19 (cup of the wine of God's wrath); 1 Pet 4:17 'judgment begins with the household of God'; atbash also in Jer 51:1 (Leb-qamai = Kasdim) and in kabbalistic exegesis; Ugaritic and Greek images of drinking a god's cup.

**YHWH roars from on high; the shepherds wail** (Jer 25:30-38)
- Amos 1:2 and Joel 4:16 (YHWH roars from Zion); Isa 63:1-6 treading the winepress; Revelation 19:15.

**Jeremiah tried for prophesying the temple will become like Shiloh; Uriah executed** (Jer 26:1-24)
- Compare Socrates' trial; Jesus' temple saying and trial (Mark 14:58); Quran 2:61/3:21 on Israel killing prophets.

**Jeremiah wears yoke bars and sends them to the envoys of five kings** (Jer 27:1-22)
- Compare the temple vessels' fate in Dan 5, Ezra 1:7-11 and legends of hidden vessels (2 Macc 2).

**Hananiah breaks the wooden yoke and dies within the year** (Jer 28:1-17)
- Deut 18:20-22 test of a prophet; compare Ahab's prophets and Micaiah (1Kgs 22).

**Letter to the exiles; seventy years; Ahab and Zedekiah roasted; Shemaiah's counter-letter** (Jer 29:1-32)
- Jer 29:7 is foundational for diaspora ethics (Mishnah Avot 3:2 'pray for the welfare of the government'). Ahab and Zedekiah become the elders of Susanna in rabbinic tradition (b. Sanh. 93a).

**Return of Ephraim, Rachel weeping in Ramah, sour grapes, the new covenant and the measured city** (Jer 31:1-40)
- Jer 31:15 is quoted in Matt 2:18 (massacre of innocents); 31:31-34 in Heb 8:8-12 and the Last Supper 'new covenant' (Luke 22:20); 'ruh' of Rachel's tomb tradition. Jer 31:22 read messianically in Christian exegesis (virgin birth).

**Jeremiah buys his cousin's field at Anathoth during the siege** (Jer 32:1-44)
- Double documents (Doppelurkunde) are known from Elephantine and Babylonian practice; jar storage recalls the Dead Sea Scrolls.

**Healing of the city, the Righteous Branch and the covenant with day and night** (Jer 33:1-26)
- Jer 33:14-26 is absent from the Septuagint. 'Branch' (tsemah) is a messianic title (Zech 3:8; 6:12; Qumran 4Q252).

**Zedekiah's fate and the revoked release of slaves; the calf cut in two** (Jer 34:1-22)
- Self-curse treaty ritual: Sefire treaty (lamb cut), Mari 'killing a donkey' (hayaram qatalum); Gen 15. Lachish ostraca mention signal fires of Azekah.

**The Rechabites refuse wine and are held up as a model of obedience** (Jer 35:1-19)
- Compare Nazirite vows (Num 6), Nabataean prohibition of wine, houses and sowing (Diodorus 19.94); the 'History of the Rechabites' apocryphon (blessed ones on an island); Muslim abstinence.

**Baruch reads the scroll; Jehoiakim cuts it with a penknife and burns it; it is rewritten** (Jer 36:1-32)
- Compare Ezra re-dictating the burned scriptures (4 Ezra 14), rabbinic laws on burned Torah scrolls; Caliph Uthman burning variant Quran codices (inverse); 2 Kgs 22 (Josiah).

**Jeremiah sunk in the muddy cistern and rescued by Ebed-melech the Cushite** (Jer 38:1-28)
- Compare Joseph cast into a waterless pit (Gen 37:24) and Ps 69:2-3 (sinking in mire); Ebed-melech in rabbinic legend is identified with Zedekiah's Cushite and enters paradise alive; in 4 Baruch (Paralipomena of Jeremiah) Abimelech sleeps 66 years.

**Ishmael murders Gedaliah at table and slaughters eighty pilgrims into Asa's cistern** (Jer 41:1-18)
- The murder of Gedaliah is commemorated by the Fast of Gedaliah (3 Tishri; Zech 7:5, 8:19).

**The remnant asks for an oracle, rejects it and drags Jeremiah to Tahpanhes; stones hidden in the pavement** (Jer 42:1-43:13)
- Flinders Petrie identified a brick platform at Tell Defenneh (Tahpanhes) with 'the house of Pharaoh'. Jewish tradition (Lives of the Prophets) says Jeremiah was stoned in Egypt.

**The Judeans in Egypt defend their cult of the Queen of Heaven** (Jer 44:1-30)
- Elephantine papyri attest a Jewish colony in Egypt with Anat-Yahu; Ishtar 'Queen of Heaven' (sharrat shame) cakes (kamanu) in Akkadian ritual; compare Collyridians (Epiphanius) offering cakes to Mary as Queen of Heaven.

**Oracle to Baruch: do not seek great things; your life as booty** (Jer 45:1-5)
- Baruch is the pseudonymous author of 1-3 Baruch and 4 Baruch; in Jewish legend he is denied prophecy (Mekhilta Bo) and in some Islamic and Christian traditions identified with figures who sleep or ascend.

**Oracle against Moab: wine settled on its lees, Chemosh into exile** (Jer 48:1-47)
- Much of Jer 48 parallels Isa 15-16. The Mesha Stele names Nebo, Kiriathaim, Dibon, Aroer, Beth-diblathaim and Chemosh.

**Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, and Elam** (Jer 49:1-39)
- Jer 49:7-22 closely parallels Obadiah. Elam's archers are famous in Assyrian reliefs and Isa 22:6.

**Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken** (Jer 50:1-46)
- Compare Rev 18 (fall of Babylon the great, 'come out of her, my people'); Cyrus Cylinder on Marduk's abandonment of Nabonidus.

**Oracle against Babylon (II): golden cup, destroying mountain, Sheshach, the scroll sunk in the Euphrates** (Jer 51:1-64)
- Rev 18:21 (an angel throws a millstone into the sea: so Babylon falls); Rev 17:1 'sits on many waters'; Bel and the Dragon (Daniel additions) where Bel's food is eaten; Atbash in Kabbalah.

**Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release** (Jer 52:1-34)
- Babylonian ration tablets (Weidner) list oil rations for 'Ya'ukinu king of Yahudu' and his sons. Compare Joseph lifting the head of the cupbearer (Gen 40:13).

**Lamentations 1: 'How lonely sits the city', Zion as a widow with no comforter** (Lam 1:1-22)
- Read on Tisha b'Av. Compare Mesopotamian city laments (Lament over Ur, Lament for Sumer and Ur) with the weeping city goddess; Lam 1:12 applied to Christ's passion in Good Friday liturgy (O vos omnes).

**Lamentations 2: the Lord became like an enemy; children faint in the streets** (Lam 2:1-22)
- Lam 2:20 (priest and prophet slain in the sanctuary) is linked in the Talmud (b. Git. 57b; y. Taan. 4:5) to the blood of Zechariah son of Jehoiada bubbling in the temple; compare Matt 23:35.

**Lamentations 3: 'I am the man who has seen affliction'; mercies new every morning** (Lam 3:1-66)
- Jewish tradition reads the 'geber' as Jeremiah in the pit (Jer 38). Lam 3:30 echoed in Matt 5:39; Lam 3:22-23 in hymnody ('Great is thy faithfulness'). Compare Babylonian 'Ludlul bel nemeqi' (righteous sufferer).

**Lamentations 4: gold grown dim, ostrich-cruel mothers, the anointed captured** (Lam 4:1-22)
- Lam 4:20 'the anointed of YHWH' was applied to Christ by Christian Fathers (Justin, Irenaeus: 'Christ the Lord, the breath of our face'). Edom in Uz links to Job 1:1.

**Lamentations 5: communal prayer 'Remember, O LORD', renew our days as of old** (Lam 5:1-22)
- Lam 5:18 foxes on Zion: Rabbi Akiva laughs at seeing a fox emerge from the Holy of Holies (b. Makkot 24b). 'Hashivenu' (5:21) sung at the Torah's return to the ark.

**Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory** (Ezek 1:1-28)
- Basis of ma'aseh merkavah mysticism and Hekhalot literature; read as haftarah on Shavuot. Four faces become the four Evangelists' symbols (Irenaeus, Jerome) and Rev 4:6-8. Compare Assyrian lamassu, Mesopotamian winged genii supporting the sky, Hindu vahanas, and Mithraic or Vedic solar chariots; Quran 69:17 (eight bearing the Throne).

**Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey** (Ezek 2:1-3:15)
- Rev 10:9-10 (John eats a little scroll sweet in the mouth, bitter in the belly); Jer 15:16; Hekhalot and Kedushah liturgy (Isa 6:3 + Ezek 3:12). Compare the Islamic tradition of the Prophet's chest opened and filled, and the Iranian Arda Viraf.

**Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house** (Ezek 3:16-27)
- Ezekiel's muteness ends at 33:22; compare Zechariah struck dumb (Luke 1:20) and Quran 19:10 (Zechariah's three nights' silence).

**Sign-acts of the siege: the brick, the iron griddle, lying on his sides, rationed bread baked on dung** (Ezek 4:1-17)
- Day-for-a-year reckoning (Num 14:34) underlies Daniel's weeks and Christian/Millerite and Baha'i prophetic chronologies. Compare Peter's vision refusing unclean food (Acts 10:14) and Daniel 1:8.

**The shaven hair divided in thirds; Jerusalem in the midst of the nations** (Ezek 5:1-17)
- Hair-cutting and dividing as a symbolic act; compare Mesopotamian prophetic letters (Mari) in which a prophet's hair and garment hem are sent to the king as tokens.
- Jerusalem at the center of the nations underlies the rabbinic and medieval 'navel of the world' idea (Tanhuma Kedoshim 10; Jubilees 8:19; medieval mappae mundi).

**The end has come upon the four corners of the land** (Ezek 7:1-27)
- Compare Amos 8:2 ('the end has come upon my people') and the Qumran and apocalyptic 'time of the end' (Dan 8:17).

**Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship** (Ezek 8:1-18)
- Tammuz = Sumerian Dumuzi, the shepherd-lover of Inanna/Ishtar mourned annually in the month Tammuz; compare Adonis laments (Byblos) and Jerome's note on Bethlehem's Adonis grotto.
- Prophet carried by the hair: Bel and the Dragon 36 (angel carries Habakkuk by his hair to Babylon).
- Mishnah Sukkah 5:4: at the Water-Drawing the priests turned westward and said 'our fathers in this place had their backs to the temple and faces east, bowing to the sun; we are for God.'

**The six executioners and the man in linen who marks the foreheads** (Ezek 9:1-11)
- The tav in the old script was an X/cross; Tertullian (Adv. Marc. 3.22) and other Fathers read it as the sign of the cross; b. Shabbat 55a: tav for tihyeh/tamut (live/die) and the 'seal of God is truth'; Rev 7:3-4 and 9:4 (sealing the servants of God on the forehead); CD 19:12 cites the verse.
- The seven heavenly figures (six plus a scribe) recall the Mesopotamian seven sages/demons and the scribal god Nabu.

**Coals from between the cherubim; the wheels full of eyes; the glory leaves the temple** (Ezek 10:1-22)
- The merkavah tradition (m. Hagigah 2:1 forbids expounding it publicly); ofannim become an angelic class (1 Enoch 61:10, 71:7; Hekhalot literature; Christian 'thrones'). Four faces underlie the four evangelist symbols (Irenaeus, Adv. Haer. 3.11.8) and Rev 4:6-8.

**The cauldron saying, death of Pelatiah, God as little sanctuary, the new heart, the glory on the Mount of Olives** (Ezek 11:1-25)
- b. Megillah 29a: the 'little sanctuary' is the synagogue and house of study in Babylon.
- Rabbinic tradition (Lam. Rabbah proem 25) has the Shekhinah wait on the Mount of Olives for three and a half years; compare Acts 1:11-12 and Zech 14:4.

**The exile's baggage, eating with trembling, and the end of delayed visions** (Ezek 12:1-28)
- Josephus (Ant. 10.106-107) says Zedekiah disbelieved because Jeremiah said he would be taken to Babylon and Ezekiel said he would not see it; both came true.

**Against the false prophets and the women who hunt souls** (Ezek 13:1-23)
- Kesatot have been compared with Mesopotamian binding magic (Maqlu) and with wrist-amulets; soul-trapping as birds has parallels in Egyptian ba-birds and in later Jewish and folk soul-catching.
- The whitewashed wall is taken up in CD 8:12 and 19:24-25 ('builders of the wall ... daubers of whitewash') and in Acts 23:3 / Matt 23:27.

**Idols in the heart; Noah, Daniel and Job could not save the land** (Ezek 14:1-23)
- Dan'el is the righteous judge-king of the Ugaritic Aqhat epic (KTU 1.17-19); compare also Ezek 28:3. Abraham's bargaining for Sodom (Gen 18) is the inverse principle; Jer 15:1 names Moses and Samuel.

**Parable of the useless vine-wood** (Ezek 15:1-8)
- Compare the Israel-as-vine image (Ps 80, Isa 5) and John 15:6 (branches gathered and burned).

**Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot** (Ezek 16:1-43)
- Infant exposure and rescue: Sargon of Akkad legend, Moses (Exod 2), Romulus and Remus, Oedipus; Arabian pre-Islamic burial of infant girls (Quran 81:8-9).
- Neonatal salting: b. Shabbat 129b; Galen on rubbing newborns with salt.
- m. Megillah 4:10 lists Ezek 16 as a chapter not to be read as haftarah (R. Eliezer).

**Like mother like daughter; Sodom and Samaria her sisters; the everlasting covenant** (Ezek 16:44-63)
- The social sin of Sodom recurs in rabbinic lore (m. Avot 5:10 'what is mine is mine'; b. Sanhedrin 109a-b, the bed of Sodom and the girl punished for feeding the poor).

**Riddle of the two eagles, the cedar and the vine; the messianic cedar shoot** (Ezek 17:1-24)
- The tree in which birds nest: Dan 4:9-18 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree), Matt 13:31-32 (mustard seed). Eagle-and-tree fable: the Etana myth (eagle and serpent in the tree); Aesop's eagle and fox. Eagle allegory reused in 4 Ezra 11-12.

**Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance** (Ezek 18:1-32)
- Jer 31:29-30 has the same proverb. Quran 6:164, 17:15, 35:18 ('no bearer of burdens bears another's burden'). Contrast Exod 20:5. Ezek 18:23/32 underlies 1 Tim 2:4 and 2 Pet 3:9 and the Yom Kippur liturgy.

**Dirge for the princes of Israel - the lioness and her cubs, the uprooted vine** (Ezek 19:1-14)
- Lion-capture imagery (cage, pit, net) matches Assyrian royal lion hunts and the caged-king image in Ashurbanipal's inscriptions; compare Gen 49:9 (Judah as lion's whelp).

**Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt; the second exodus into the wilderness of the peoples** (Ezek 20:1-44)
- The 'laws that were not good' troubled later readers: compare Justin Martyr and the Didascalia on the 'second legislation' as punishment for the calf, and Quran 4:160 (good things forbidden to the Jews for their wrongdoing).
- Ezek 20:32-33 ('I will be king over you') is cited in b. Rosh Hashanah 32b among the Malkhuyot verses.

**Fire in the southern forest; the song of the sword; Babylon's divination at the crossroads; against Ammon** (Ezek 21:1-37)
- Babylonian hepatoscopy (barutu) is amply documented in clay liver models; arrow-divination (istiqsam bi-l-azlam) is condemned in Quran 5:3 and 5:90 and was practiced at the Kaaba before Hubal.

**The city of blood; the dross in the furnace; no man in the breach** (Ezek 22:1-31)
- Zeph 3:3-4 has the same sequence of princes as lions, judges as wolves, prophets and priests; Ps 106:23 has Moses 'standing in the breach'.

**Oholah and Oholibah, the two harlot sisters** (Ezek 23:1-49)
- Nose-and-ear mutilation of adulteresses is attested in Middle Assyrian Laws A 15 and in Egyptian practice (Diodorus 1.78).
- Pekod (Puqudu), Shoa (Sutu) and Koa (Qutu) are Aramean and Mesopotamian peoples in Assyrian records.

**The rusted cauldron; death of the prophet's wife without mourning** (Ezek 24:1-27)
- The 'bread of men' and the covering of the upper lip are the basis of halakhic mourning customs (se'udat havra'ah; b. Moed Qatan 15a-b, 27b, derive many avelut laws from this chapter).
- Blood that cries until covered: Gen 4:10; Job 16:18; the Zechariah blood legend (b. Gittin 57b) in which the priest's blood bubbles in the temple court.

**Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia** (Ezek 25:1-17)
- Moabite towns Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and Kiriathaim appear also in the Mesha Stele.

**Oracle on the fall of Tyre and the princes of the sea** (Ezek 26:1-21)
- The later failure of Nebuchadnezzar's 13-year siege is acknowledged in Ezek 29:17-20; Alexander's causeway (332 BCE) was later read as fulfilment (Jerome). Rev 18 reuses the lament of kings and merchants over Babylon.

**Lament over Tyre the great merchant ship** (Ezek 27:1-36)
- Rev 18:11-19 copies the merchant cargo list and the lament of shipmasters and sailors standing far off; compare the ship-of-state allegory (Alcaeus, Horace Odes 1.14).

**The prince of Tyre who said 'I am a god'** (Ezek 28:1-10)
- Ruler claiming divinity and seated on the waters: Quran 28:38 and 79:24 (Pharaoh 'I am your lord most high'); Isa 14:13-14; Acts 12:21-23 (Herod Agrippa). Rabbinic lore (Gen. Rabbah 9:5; Tanhuma Bereshit 7) lists Hiram among those who made themselves gods and had seven heavens built on the sea.

**Lament over the king of Tyre - the gem-covered cherub in Eden cast from God's mountain** (Ezek 28:11-19)
- Read by Origen (De Principiis 1.5.4), Tertullian and later Christian tradition, together with Isa 14:12, as the fall of Satan/Lucifer; compare the Quranic Iblis (proud of being made of fire, 7:12; expelled from the garden, 7:13) and 2 Enoch 29:4-5.
- A different primal-man version of Eden (Adam on the mountain, robed in glory/gems) appears in Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 12 and in the Syriac Cave of Treasures; Mesopotamian jewel-garden of Gilgamesh XI (garden of gem-trees).

**Pharaoh the great dragon of the Nile; Egypt as a reed; Egypt given as Nebuchadnezzar's wages** (Ezek 29:1-21)
- Pharaoh as crocodile/dragon: Isa 27:1, 51:9 (Rahab), Ps 74:13-14; Egyptian Sobek and Apophis; the Ugaritic tnn bound by Anat. Quran 10:90-92 (Pharaoh's body cast out as a sign) and 28:38-39 for Pharaoh's hubris.

**The day of YHWH on Egypt; the cities of Egypt; Pharaoh's broken arms** (Ezek 30:1-26)
- Egyptian royal ideology of the pharaoh's 'strong arm' (khopesh) - Hophra's epithet; compare Exod 6:6. Aven/On = Heliopolis, Pi-beseth = Bubastis of Bastet.

**The great cedar of Eden felled and sent down to Sheol** (Ezek 31:1-18)
- World-tree imagery: Dan 4 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree), the Mesopotamian kiskanu tree of Eridu with roots in the Apsu, the Norse Yggdrasil, the Gilgamesh cedar forest of Humbaba.

**Dirge over Pharaoh the sea dragon caught in God's net** (Ezek 32:1-16)
- Monster netted by a god: Marduk catches Tiamat in a net (Enuma Elish IV 95) and makes heaven and earth from her body; Ninurta and Anzu. Carcass on the mountains recalls 1 Enoch 60:7-9 and 4 Ezra 6:49-52 (Leviathan and Behemoth as food for the righteous).

**Egypt's descent to the Pit among the uncircumcised nations** (Ezek 32:17-32)
- Stratified underworld with ranks of the dead: Isa 14:9-20; Gilgamesh XII and the Descent of Ishtar; Odyssey 11 (the nekyia with heroes); 1 Enoch 22 (compartments of the dead). Burial with weapons under the head matches warrior burials and 1 Macc 13:29.

**The watchman; turn and live; the fugitive's news; Abraham was one; the prophet as love-singer** (Ezek 33:1-33)
- Watchman passage cited in rabbinic discussions of the duty of rebuke (b. Shabbat 54b-55a) and in Christian pastoral tradition (Gregory the Great, Regula Pastoralis); compare Quran 5:105 and 6:69 on not bearing another's guilt once warned.
- Abraham as 'one' (ehad): Isa 51:2; Mal 2:15; Quran 16:120 ('Abraham was a nation (umma)').

**The bad shepherds; God the shepherd; one shepherd David; the covenant of peace** (Ezek 34:1-31)
- John 10:1-16 (the good shepherd, one flock one shepherd); Luke 15:4-7 (seeking the lost sheep); Matt 25:31-46 (separating sheep from goats). b. Yevamot 61a reads 'you are adam' (34:31) to say only Israel is called adam. Mesopotamian kings as 'shepherd' (re'u), e.g. Hammurabi's prologue.

**Against Mount Seir** (Ezek 35:1-15)
- Edom becomes the rabbinic cipher for Rome (Gen. Rabbah 65:21); compare Obadiah and Ps 137:7.

**For my holy name - clean water, new heart, my spirit within; the land like Eden** (Ezek 36:16-38)
- 36:25 is read in m. Yoma 8:9 (R. Akiva: God as the mikveh of Israel) and in Christian baptismal theology (John 3:5); 1QS 4:20-21 (God sprinkles the spirit of truth like waters of purification); Jer 31:31-34 (new covenant on the heart).

**The valley of dry bones** (Ezek 37:1-14)
- b. Sanhedrin 92b debates whether the dead revived were Ephraimites who left Egypt early, and says they married and had children ('a parable' says another view); the Dura-Europos synagogue paints the scene. Zoroastrian Bundahishn 34 (bones reassembled at the frashokereti); Quran 2:259 (the man and his donkey: 'look at the bones, how we raise them and clothe them with flesh') and 2:243 (thousands who died and were revived).

**The two sticks joined - one kingdom under David, an everlasting covenant and sanctuary** (Ezek 37:15-28)
- Rev 21:3 ('the dwelling of God is with men') quotes 37:27; the Joseph/Ephraim stick fed later Messiah ben Joseph traditions and, in Latter-day Saint reading, the Bible and Book of Mormon.

**Gog of Magog invades the land dwelling at the navel of the earth** (Ezek 38:1-23)
- Gog and Magog: Rev 20:8; Quran 18:94-98 and 21:96 (Ya'juj and Ma'juj walled in by Dhu'l-Qarnayn, released at the end); Alexander Romance (Alexander's gate against the unclean nations); rabbinic war of Gog and Magog before the messianic age (b. Berakhot 7b, Sanhedrin 97b). Gog has been linked to Gyges (Gugu) of Lydia.
- Tabbur ha-arets: Judg 9:37; Jubilees 8:19; Tanhuma Kedoshim 10 (Jerusalem the navel, the Foundation Stone); Greek omphalos at Delphi.

**Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds** (Ezek 39:1-29)
- Rev 19:17-18 (the angel calls the birds to 'the great supper of God' to eat the flesh of kings, horses and riders); Joel 3:1 (outpoured spirit). The bone-marker (tsiyyun) underlies the halakhic practice of marking graves to warn priests (m. Shekalim 1:1, m. Moed Qatan 1:2; b. Moed Qatan 5a derives it from 39:15).

**The new temple vision begins - the man of bronze with the measuring reed on a very high mountain** (Ezek 40:1-4)
- The angelic guide with a measuring rod: Zech 2:5-6; Rev 11:1 and 21:15-17 (gold measuring reed of the New Jerusalem on a great high mountain, Rev 21:10); 11QTemple and the Qumran New Jerusalem texts (4Q554). 'Rosh ha-shanah on the tenth' coincides with the jubilee date (Lev 25:9-10); 25 years is half a jubilee.

**Measuring the gates and courts of the visionary temple** (Ezek 40:5-37)
- The three-chambered gate plan matches excavated Iron Age gates at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer. Middot (Mishnah tractate) and 11QTemple build their temple plans in dialogue with these measurements.

**Slaughtering tables, the priests' chambers, the Zadokites, the inner court and the porch** (Ezek 40:38-49)
- Zadokite exclusivity is the root of the Qumran 'sons of Zadok' self-designation (CD 3:21-4:4 quotes Ezek 44:15) and of the Sadducee name. Compare the two pillars Jachin and Boaz (1 Kgs 7:21).

**The river from the temple and the healing of the sea** (Ezek 47:1-12)
- Compare Rev 22:1-2 (river of the water of life, tree bearing twelve fruits monthly, leaves for healing), Joel 4:18, Zech 14:8.

**Borders and tribal allotment of the land; the city 'YHWH is there'** (Ezek 47:13-48:35)
- Compare Rev 21:12-13 (twelve gates named for the tribes) and the New Jerusalem text from Qumran.

**The statue of four metals and the stone cut without hands** (Dan 2:24-49)
- Compare Hesiod, Works and Days 106-201 (gold, silver, bronze, heroic, iron races) and the Zoroastrian Bahman Yasht tree of four metal branches.

**The golden image and the fiery furnace** (Dan 3:1-30)
- Compare Abraham in Nimrod's furnace (Gen. Rab. 38:13; Quran 21:68-69), the Greek Additions (Prayer of Azariah, Song of the Three) and the Quranic People of the Ditch (85:4-8).

**Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness** (Dan 3:31-4:34)
- Compare the Qumran Prayer of Nabonidus (4Q242), Nabonidus' sojourn at Teima, and Ezek 31 (the cosmic cedar).

**Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall** (Dan 5:1-30)
- Compare Herodotus 1.191 and Xenophon Cyropaedia 7.5 (Babylon taken during a festival).

**Daniel in the lions' den** (Dan 6:1-29)
- Compare Bel and the Dragon 31-42 (Habakkuk carried to the den), and Islamic qibla and fixed daily prayers.

**The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man** (Dan 7:1-28)
- Compare 1 Enoch 14 and 46-48 (Head of Days and Son of Man), Mark 14:62, Rev 1:13-14, 13:1-2, 20:12 and the Ugaritic El/Baal enthronement.

**Daniel's penitential prayer and the seventy weeks** (Dan 9:1-27)
- Compare Mark 13:14 / Matt 24:15 and Christian messianic computations; 1 Macc 1:54; Baruch 1:15-3:8 penitential prayer.

**The vision by the Tigris and the angelic princes of the nations** (Dan 10:1-21)
- Compare Rev 1:13-16, the Zoroastrian yazatas, and the seventy angels of the nations in 1 Enoch 89 and rabbinic sarim.

**Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book** (Dan 12:1-13)
- Compare Rev 10:5-6 (angel swears with raised hand), 1 Enoch 104:2 (righteous shine like stars), Zoroastrian frashokereti and Quranic resurrection from the earth.

**Judgment on priests and kings; 'on the third day he will raise us'** (Hos 5:1-6:11)
- Hos 6:6 is quoted in Matt 9:13 and 12:7; Hos 6:2 is read with the third-day resurrection in Christian and rabbinic tradition.

**The luxuriant vine, the calves of Beth-aven, sow righteousness** (Hos 10:1-15)
- Hos 10:8 is echoed in Luke 23:30 and Rev 6:16.

**'Out of Egypt I called my son'; God's compassion overturns his anger** (Hos 11:1-11)
- Matt 2:15 applies Hos 11:1 to the flight to Egypt.

**Ephraim's idols, God as predator, 'O Death, where are your plagues?'** (Hos 13:1-14:1)
- Hos 13:14 is quoted in 1 Cor 15:55.

**'Return, O Israel'; God as dew and evergreen** (Hos 14:2-10)
- Hos 14:2-10 is the haftarah of Shabbat Shuvah; compare rabbinic teshuvah doctrine (b. Yoma 86a-b).

**The locust army of the Day of YHWH; 'rend your hearts'; restoration** (Joel 2:1-27)
- The phrase moreh li-tsdaqah (Joel 2:23) is linked to the Qumran 'Teacher of Righteousness' (moreh ha-tsedeq).

**The spirit poured on all flesh and signs before the Day** (Joel 3:1-5)
- Quoted at Pentecost in Acts 2:17-21 and in Rom 10:13; compare Num 11:29 ('would that all YHWH's people were prophets').

**Judgment of the nations in the Valley of Jehoshaphat; the fountain from the temple** (Joel 4:1-21)
- Reverses Isa 2:4 / Mic 4:3; compare Rev 14:14-20 (sickle and winepress). The Kidron valley has been identified with Jehoshaphat in Jewish, Christian and Islamic burial tradition.

**Lament for virgin Israel; seek me and live; the Day of YHWH is darkness** (Amos 5:1-27)
- Amos 5:25-27 is quoted (LXX form) in Acts 7:42-43; compare Babylonian Kayamanu (Saturn).

**Woe to the complacent; the marzeah ends; the plague-house** (Amos 6:1-14)
- The marzeah is attested in Ugaritic texts as a feast-association linked with the dead.

**The Lord at the altar, no escape, the sieve, and the fallen booth of David** (Amos 9:1-15)
- Amos 9:11-12 (LXX) is quoted by James in Acts 15:16-17; the 'fallen booth of David' gives the rabbinic messianic epithet bar niflei (b. Sanh. 96b). Compare Ps 139:7-12 on no escape from God.

**Obadiah's vision against Edom's pride** (Obad 1:1-9)
- Obad 1-9 is closely paralleled by Jer 49:7-22. The fall of the star-high proud one recalls Isa 14:12-15 (Helel ben Shahar).
- Rabbinic tradition identifies Edom/Esau with Rome; Obadiah was said (b. Sanh. 39b) to be an Edomite proselyte.

**Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH** (Obad 1:10-21)
- Ps 137:7 also condemns Edom for the day of Jerusalem. Medieval Jewish naming of Spain (Sefarad) and France (Tsarfat) derives from Obad 20.

**Jonah flees to Tarshish and is thrown into the sea** (Jonah 1:1-16)
- Quran 37:139-141: Yunus 'fled (abaqa) to the laden ship', cast lots (sahama) and was among the losers. Quran 21:87: Dhu'l-Nun 'went off in anger' thinking God would not constrain him.
- Mark 4:35-41 (Jesus asleep in the boat in the storm; the sea stilled). Cf. Greek tales of jettisoning a guilty passenger (Arion; Antiphon on the shipwreck as evidence of guilt).

**Jonah swallowed by the great fish and his psalm** (Jonah 2:1-11)
- Quran 21:87-88: in the darknesses he called 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; I have been among the wrongdoers', and God saved him from distress. Quran 37:142-145: the fish swallowed him while blameworthy; had he not glorified God he would have stayed in its belly until the Day of Resurrection; he was cast onto the bare shore, sick. Quran 68:48-49: 'the companion of the fish' who called out while choked with grief (makzum).
- Matt 12:40 (sign of Jonah: three days and nights in the heart of the earth). Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 10 (Jonah sees the sea floor and Leviathan from inside the fish). Greek: Heracles swallowed by the sea monster at Troy; Perseus-Andromeda localized at Joppa.

**Jonah preaches and Nineveh repents down to its animals** (Jonah 3:1-10)
- Quran 10:98: of all towns only the people of Yunus believed and their punishment of disgrace was lifted. Quran 37:147-148: sent to a hundred thousand or more, who believed. Mishnah Taanit 2:1 cites Jonah 3:10 for public fasts; Jonah is read on Yom Kippur afternoon.
- Herodotus 9.24 (Persians shear their horses in mourning for Masistius); Judith 4:10 (cattle in sackcloth).

**Jonah's anger, the qiqayon plant and God's question** (Jonah 4:1-11)
- Quran 37:146: 'We caused a gourd plant (shajaratan min yaqtin) to grow over him'; the Quran sets the plant after the fish, as shelter for the sick prophet, not as a lesson. Quran 21:87 'went off in anger' (mughadiban) parallels Jonah 4:1.
- Jerome's cucurbita/hedera dispute with Augustine over qiqayon. Matt 12:41 (men of Nineveh will rise in judgment).

**YHWH comes down against Samaria; the prophet wails naked** (Mic 1:1-9)
- Isa 20:2-4 (Isaiah walks naked and barefoot three years). Ps 97:5 (mountains melt like wax).

**Punning lament over the towns of the Shephelah** (Mic 1:10-16)
- Isa 10:28-32 is a similar town-by-town march poem. Assyrian annals of Sennacherib's 701 campaign and the Lachish reliefs.

**Woe to those who seize fields; the breaker goes before the flock** (Mic 2:1-13)
- Gen. Rab. 85 and later midrash read ha-porets (Mic 2:13) as the Messiah descended from Perez. Isa 5:8 (woe to those who join house to house).

**Cannibal rulers, hireling prophets and Zion plowed as a field** (Mic 3:1-12)
- Jer 26:18 quotes Mic 3:12 as said in Hezekiah's days. Lev 13:45 (leper covers his upper lip). Ezek 22:27 (officials like wolves).

**Nations stream to Zion; swords into plowshares** (Mic 4:1-8)
- Near-verbatim in Isa 2:2-4; reversed in Joel 4:10 (plowshares into swords). Targum Ps.-Jonathan Gen 35:21: the Messiah will be revealed at Migdal Eder.

**Daughter Zion in labor, exiled to Babylon, threshing the nations** (Mic 4:9-14)
- Rev 12:1-6 (woman in labor). Mark 14:65 / Matt 26:67 (Jesus struck); Lam 3:30.

**The ruler from Bethlehem and the remnant among the nations** (Mic 5:1-8)
- Matt 2:5-6 cites Mic 5:1 for the Messiah's birthplace. b. Sukkah 52b names the seven shepherds (David with Adam, Seth, Methuselah; Abraham, Jacob, Moses) and eight princes (Jesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephaniah, Zedekiah, Elijah, the Messiah).

**YHWH's lawsuit with his people; what YHWH requires** (Mic 6:1-8)
- The Good Friday Improperia ('Popule meus, quid feci tibi?') build on Mic 6:3. b. Makkot 24a: Micah reduced the 613 commandments to three.

**False scales and futility curses** (Mic 6:9-16)
- Deut 28:38-40 and Amos 5:11 (futility curses); Assyrian treaty curses (Esarhaddon's succession treaty) have the same form.

**No godly man left; who is a God like you?** (Mic 7:1-20)
- Matt 10:35-36 / Luke 12:53 quote Mic 7:6. Mishnah Sotah 9:15 applies it to the generation before the Messiah. The Tashlikh rite on Rosh Hashanah recites Mic 7:18-20 at water.

**The jealous and avenging God against Nineveh** (Nah 1:1-14)
- The Nineveh of Jonah repents; Nahum's Nineveh is destroyed (612 BCE). Tobit 14:4 (Nahum's prophecy against Nineveh).

**The herald of peace and the sack of Nineveh** (Nah 2:1-14)
- Isa 52:7 has the same herald line. Diodorus 2.26-27 and Xenophon (Anabasis 3.4) tell of Nineveh/Larisa falling when the river broke the wall. Assyrian royal lion-hunt reliefs from Nineveh.

**Woe to the bloody city, harlot and sorceress** (Nah 3:1-19)
- Thebes was sacked by Ashurbanipal in 663 BCE. Rev 17-18 (Babylon the harlot and sorceress). Isa 47 (virgin Babylon stripped).

**Habakkuk's complaint and the Chaldean fisherman** (Hab 1:1-17)
- Acts 13:41 quotes Hab 1:5 (LXX). The Qumran Pesher Habakkuk (1QpHab) reads the Chaldeans as the Kittim (Romans) and notes they sacrifice to their standards. Mesopotamian 'net of the god' imagery (Stele of the Vultures; Ninurta's net).

**The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes** (Hab 2:1-20)
- Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:37-38 quote Hab 2:3-4. b. Makkot 24a: Habakkuk based all the commandments on one, 'the righteous shall live by his faith'. b. Sanh. 97b reads Hab 2:3 on calculating the end; Maimonides' twelfth principle: 'though he tarry, I will wait for him'. Luke 19:40 (the stones would cry out). Isa 11:9 has the waters-cover-the-sea line.

**Habakkuk's prayer; God marches from Teman** (Hab 3:1-19)
- Ugaritic Baal versus Yamm and Nahar ('Prince Sea, Judge River'); Resheph as a Canaanite plague and war god. Deut 33:2 and Judg 5:4 (God from Seir/Teman). Exod 34:29 qaran (Moses' face 'horned'). Hab 3 is the haftarah for the second day of Shavuot.

**Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah** (Zeph 1:1-18)
- The Latin sequence 'Dies irae, dies illa' is built on Zeph 1:15 (Vulgate). b. Pesahim 7b derives searching for leaven by candlelight from Zeph 1:12. Ezek 7:19 repeats the silver-and-gold line.

**Seek humility; oracles on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush and Assyria** (Zeph 2:1-15)
- Isa 47:8,10 (Babylon: 'I am, and none besides me'), a phrase otherwise used by God (Isa 45:5-6). Isa 34:11 (owl and hedgehog in ruined Edom).

**The oppressing city, a pure speech for the peoples and God's song over Zion** (Zeph 3:1-20)
- Maimonides (Mishneh Torah, Kings 11) cites Zeph 3:9 for the messianic age. Ethiopian Christian and Beta Israel tradition reads 'beyond the rivers of Cush' (3:10) as their own. Luke 1:28 (rejoice, daughter Zion) echoes 3:14.

**Haggai rouses Zerubbabel and Joshua to rebuild** (Hag 1:1-15)
- Ezra 5:1-2 and 6:14 (Haggai and Zechariah encourage the builders). Mesopotamian temple-rebuilding texts (Gudea cylinders) also link fertility to the temple.

**The glory of this latter house** (Hag 2:1-9)
- Heb 12:26-27 quotes Hag 2:6. Vulgate 'veniet desideratus cunctis gentibus' (2:7) was read as the Messiah. b. Yoma 21b lists five things missing from the second temple.

**A priestly ruling on holiness and impurity; blessing from this day** (Hag 2:10-19)
- Amos 4:9 (blight and mildew 'yet you did not return'). Mishnaic degrees of impurity (rishon, sheni) and m. Hagigah 2 develop this kind of ruling.

**Zerubbabel as God's signet ring** (Hag 2:20-23)
- Reverses Jer 22:24, where Zerubbabel's grandfather Jehoiachin is a signet torn off God's hand. Sir 49:11 praises Zerubbabel 'like a signet on the right hand'.

**Zechariah's call to return** (Zech 1:1-6)
- Mal 3:7 repeats 'Return to me and I will return to you'. Lam 5:21; Quran 2:160 (God turns to those who turn).

**First night vision, the horsemen among the myrtles** (Zech 1:7-17)
- Rev 6:1-8 (four horsemen of different colors). b. Sanh. 93a reads the myrtles as the righteous (Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah) and the rider as Gabriel; Esther's name Hadassah (myrtle). Job 1:7 (the satan roams the earth).

**Second night vision, four horns and four craftsmen** (Zech 2:1-4)
- b. Sukkah 52b: the four craftsmen are Messiah son of David, Messiah son of Joseph, Elijah and the Righteous Priest (Melchizedek). Dan 7-8 (horns as kings); 1 Enoch 90.

**Third night vision, the measuring line and the wall of fire** (Zech 2:5-17)
- Ezek 40-42 and Rev 11:1 and 21:15-17 (measuring the temple/city); Rev 21 (city of God). 'Admat ha-qodesh' is the source of the later term 'Holy Land' (terra sancta).

**Fourth vision, the high priest, the satan and the Branch** (Zech 3:1-10)
- Jude 9 ('The Lord rebuke you' to the devil disputing over Moses' body); Rev 12:10 (the accuser cast down). Job 1-2 (the satan in the court). Amos 4:11 (brand plucked from burning). Zoroastrian heavenly-trial imagery; Iranian 'adversary' figures. Rabbinic midrash (b. Sanh. 93a) explains Joshua's soiled clothes by his sons' foreign marriages.

**Fifth vision, the lampstand, the two olive trees and Zerubbabel** (Zech 4:1-14)
- Rev 11:4 (the two witnesses are the two olive trees and two lampstands). Qumran messianism of two anointed (Aaron and Israel), 1QS 9:11. Zech 2:14-4:7 is the haftarah of Shabbat Hanukkah. Iranian seven Amesha Spentas and Mesopotamian seven-eyed imagery have been compared to the seven eyes.

**Sixth vision, the flying scroll** (Zech 5:1-4)
- Twenty by ten cubits are the dimensions of Solomon's temple porch (1Kgs 6:3). Ezek 2:9-3:3 (scroll written front and back). Greek and Near Eastern curse tablets (defixiones) that 'go out' against thieves and perjurers.

**Seventh vision, the woman in the ephah carried to Shinar** (Zech 5:5-11)
- Rev 17-18 (the woman Babylon). Gen 11:2 (Shinar, the plain of Babel). Commentators compare winged female genii in Assyrian art and the removal of a goddess image (Asherah/Queen of Heaven) to Babylon. 1 Enoch's binding of sin under stones.

**Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains** (Zech 6:1-8)
- Shamash rises between twin mountains on Mesopotamian cylinder seals; Mashu twin-peaked mountain in Gilgamesh IX. Rev 6:1-8; 2Kgs 23:11 (horses of the sun).

**Crowns for Joshua; the man named Branch** (Zech 6:9-15)
- Jer 23:5 and 33:15 (righteous Branch of David). Targum renders Tsemah as 'Messiah'. Heb 7 (priest-king); Qumran priestly and royal messiahs. Christian 'Ecce homo' readings of 6:12 (LXX Anatole, 'Dawn', later a name for Christ).

**The Bethel delegation's question about fasting** (Zech 7:1-14)
- Isa 58:3-7 (the fast God chooses). Shamir is, in rabbinic legend (m. Avot 5:6; b. Gittin 68a), the stone-cutting creature Solomon used to build the temple without iron tools; Ezek 3:9 and Jer 17:1 use shamir for adamant.

**Ten promises for Zion; fasts become feasts; ten men grasp a Jew's garment** (Zech 8:1-23)
- The four fasts are traditionally 17 Tammuz, 9 Av, the Fast of Gedaliah and 10 Tevet (b. Rosh Hashanah 18b). Zech 8:16 is cited in m. Avot 1:18 (truth, judgment and peace). Zech 8:23 and the kanaf (tassel corner) of Num 15:38; Matt 9:20 (the woman touches the hem of Jesus' garment).

**Oracle against Hadrach, Tyre and Philistia** (Zech 9:1-8)
- Often linked to Alexander's march (332 BCE) and siege of Tyre (Arrian, Anabasis 2.15-24). Ezek 28 (wisdom and wealth of Tyre).

**Zion's humble king on a donkey; sons of Zion against Javan** (Zech 9:9-17)
- Matt 21:5 and John 12:15 quote Zech 9:9 for the entry into Jerusalem (Matthew has two animals). b. Sanh. 98a: if Israel is worthy the Messiah comes on the clouds (Dan 7), if not, poor and riding on a donkey. Hellenistic-era reading of 'Javan'.

**Rain from YHWH, false teraphim and the regathering of Judah and Joseph** (Zech 10:1-12)
